Abstraction: This is used to hide background details or any unnecessary implementation about the data so that users only see the required information. It is one of the most important and essential features of object-oriented programming

API: Application Programming Interface. A software intermediary that allows two applications to interact with each other. Each time we use an app like Facebook, send an instant message, or check the weather on our smart device, we are using an API
Business Logic: The custom rules or algorithms that handle the exchange of information between a database and user interface

Business Rules: Business Rules provide a true abstraction level and separation from the user interface. The business rule is not actively selecting user interface elements to collect input values, which allows flexible modification of the presentation and the rule itself. The same business rule can service any number of data controller views regardless of the view types
Class: This is a blueprint that defines the variables and the methods common to all objects of a certain kind
Commit: A command that is used for storing changes performed by a transaction

Deprecated: This is the process of taking older code and marking it as no longer being useful within the codebase, usually because it has been replaced by newer code. The deprecated code is not immediately removed from the codebase because doing so may cause regression errors
Entity: An entity is a real time object that is different from others. An entity can be defined using its attributes. They are a part of an entity
Entity set: It is a collection of similar entities

Flush Current Transaction: Flushing is the process of synchronising the underlying persistent store with persistable state held in memory. It will update or insert into your tables in the running transaction, but it may not commit those changes
Getter: A getter is often associated with a setter. Together they are known as accessors. Getter returns the value of the private member variable
kloBroker: KloBroker is also known as Middleware/ MW. It is a broker in between tenants, clients, and external systems
kloTuner: It is an application used for configuration of and maintaining data under the object types. It maintains the number of users, number of roles as well as Business partners
kloIDE: It is an integrated development environment for kloBase for developing applications and websites

Lisp: Lisp is the second-oldest high-level programming language after Fortran and has changed a great deal since its early days, and a number of dialects have existed over its history. Today, the most widely known general-purpose Lisp dialects are Common Lisp and Scheme

Method: A method in object-oriented programming (OOP) is a procedure associated with a message and an object. An object consists of data and behaviour; these compose an interface, which specifies how the object may be utilised by any of its various consumers
Multi-Tenant Cloud: This is a cloud computing architecture that allows customers to share computing resources in a public or private cloud

Meta Model: A metamodel or surrogate model is a model of a model, and metamodeling is the process of generating such metamodels. Thus metamodeling or meta-modelling is the analysis, construction and development of the frames, rules, constraints, models and theories applicable and useful for modelling a predefined class of problems
Object: An entity that contains both attributes and actions is its object. It is defined by its life span, name and object identifier. Every object has two components: State and Behaviour
ORM: Object Relational Mapping is a computer programming technique for converting data between incompatible type systems (Object to Relational), using object-oriented programming language

Pagination: A storage allocation technique in which programs or data are divided into fixed length blocks called pages, main storage/memory is divided into blocks of the same length called page frames, and pages are stored in page frames, not necessarily contiguously or in logical order, and pages are transferred between main and auxiliary storage as needed
Property: A property is a special class member, intermediate in functionality between a field (or data member) and a method
Query: A query is a request for data or information from a database table or combination of tables

Query tree: It is an internal representation of an SQL statement where the single parts that it is built from are stored separately. These query trees can be shown in the server log if you set the configuration parameters debug_print_parse, debug_print_rewritten, or debug_print_plan
Rollback: A transactional control language that is used to undo the transactions that have not been saved in the database
Schema: A representation of a plan or theory in the form of an outline or model
Setter: Setter is a method to set the value of any property of a private member variable. It is accompanied by Getter

Stateless Model: In simple terms, a client program makes a request to an application server, which sends data back to the client. The server treats all client connections equally and saves no information from prior requests or sessions. A website that serves up a simple static web page is a good example of the stateless model
UTC: Coordinated United Time. Prior to 1972, this time was called Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)

Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5112027 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5112027. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process

Every attempt to create, update, or delete an entity takes place in the context of a transaction. A single transaction can include any number of such operations. To maintain the consistency of the data, the transaction ensures that all of the operations it contains are applied to KloBase Datastore as a unit or, if any of the operations fails, that none of them are applied. Furthermore, all strongly-consistent reads (ancestor queries or gets) performed within the same transaction observe a consistent snapshot of the data.

documents.t: By following the above instructions, you will ensure that dialogs opened using the KloController.openDialog API are closed consistently and correctly with the KloController.closeDialog API. This approach helps avoid potential issues and improves the stability and maintainability of the application.
Screenshot
Screenshot

Dialogs opened via the KloController.openDialog API should be closed using the KloController.closeDialog API, not the sap.m.Dialog's close method. The sap.m.Dialog's close method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the sap.m.Dialog.open() method.

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API.

Notification is an alert message like SMS, email and notification in an app. Notification can be sent whenever it is required. This will work similarly to an endpoint resolver (it can send notifications to multiple receivers). The notifications sharing service is done by a third-party service (fcm) provider to clients. However, the data storage, the notification body, and the channel types are all configured by us.

The Callbacks tab is available within a notification template in the Notification Editor. It allows you to register server-side callback methods that run when the notification is being processed, enabling you to attach files dynamically to outgoing emails. Each callback method is defined by a name and a sequence number that controls the order in which it is executed.

The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

The Page area is the next level in the page hierarchy after the Page Layout. Page areas are embedded with the pagelayout. The detail of the page Area that needs to be rendered for the page area will be maintained in the Page Layout’s Layout Data section.

PageLayout is the topmost layer embedded with the page. At runtime, only one pageLayout will be picked based on the device type. The detail of which pageLayout needs to be picked is maintained in the page’s properties (screencontainerdefault, screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screenontainertab). If the property for a specific device type is not maintained then the default pageLayout will be rendered.

Row wise authorization is a security feature provided by a framework with which access to entity data can be restricted to selective row items on user level. By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens.

Name Type Default Description channel ChannelType filter on qualified endpoint to narrow down the receivers. dependentEntity @@@ addition entities alnog with BO endPointID string this can be single ID as per specified type or array of IDS ass per specified types. endPointType EndpointType endPointType and endPointID togather determines set of endpoint to send the message entityObject KloEntity BO to send as message onlyRootEntity boolean if true only the root object will be in message else its child also will be in Message onlydirtyobject boolean if true builds only dirty object in message else loads the complete entity object

addDependantEntities(entity): KloEntity[] Parameters​ Name Type Description entity KloEntity The KloEntity instance to add as a dependent entity Returns​ KloEntity[] - Array of all dependent entities including the newly added one Description​ Adds a dependent entity to be included in the data message sent to endpoints. Dependent entities are additional entities that should be sent along with the main entity object. This is useful when you need to send related data that may not be directly linked but is contextually important. Example​ let endpointBean = eventContext.addEndpoint("USER001", EndpointType.USER, ChannelType.DEVICE, orderEntity); let customerEntity = await txn.loadEntityP("d_customer", customerKey); endpointBean.addDependantEntities(customerEntity); // Customer info sent along with order See​ getDependantEntities to retrieve the list of dependent entities

getDependantEntities(): KloEntity[] Returns​ KloEntity[] - Array of KloEntity instances that are configured as dependent entities Description​ Gets the list of dependent entities that have been added to this endpoint bean. Dependent entities are additional entities that will be included in the data message along with the primary entity object when the message is sent to endpoints. Example​ let endpointBean = eventContext.addEndpoint("USER001", EndpointType.USER, ChannelType.DEVICE, orderEntity); endpointBean.addDependantEntities(customerEntity); endpointBean.addDependantEntities(productEntity); let dependents = endpointBean.getDependantEntities(); console.log("Number of dependent entities:", dependents.length); See​ addDependantEntities to add dependent entities

Q: Why is my application not working, and why isn't the private node screen in VS Code displaying as expected? A: If you encounter issues with the application not working, follow these steps: Open Command Prompt and type ipconfig to check your current IP address. Compare the IP address displayed with the one maintained in the hosts file. If the IP address in the hosts file does not match the current IP, update the hosts file with the correct IP address. After saving the changes, restart the application and check if the issue is resolved. This will help ensure that the correct IP address is mapped for proper application functionality.

documents.t: FAQs on Private Node Date of Issue: March 2025 Target Audience: Application Developers Prepared by: RINCY MERIN ROBINSON Platform Version: 7.0

Q: I'm getting a "JavaScript heap out of memory" / "FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit" error when running tsc -w in Private Node. What's causing this and how do I fix it? A: This typically happens when your system doesn't have enough free RAM left for the TypeScript watcher to allocate memory — often because browsers (Chrome/Edge) or other applications are already consuming most of the available memory. On an 8GB machine, it's common to see 7GB+ already in use before the compiler even starts. Immediate fix: Close unused browser tabs/windows and other memory-heavy applications before starting a tsc -w session. Alternatively, give Node a defined heap budget so it fails more gracefully or succeeds where the default limit was too aggressive: set NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 tsc -w If the issue persists or recurs frequently: A RAM upgrade (16GB recommended) is advised for machines regularly running Private Node builds alongside browsers/IDEs. Check that tsconfig.json includes incremental: true and skipLibCheck: true to reduce the compiler's memory footprint per rebuild. Use cmd terminal to start the typescript watcher (tsc -w).

documents.t: Q: Why is it important for the port number in the private node server to match the port number in the private URL when opening the application in the browser? A: It is crucial for the port number in the private node server to match the port number in the private URL because: The port number in the URL defines which specific service or application on the server is being accessed. If the port numbers don't match, the browser will attempt to connect to the wrong service, potentially resulting in an error or failure to load the application correctly. Ensuring that both the server configuration and the private URL use the same port number guarantees proper communication and accessibility between the client (browser) and the server. Mismatched port numbers can lead to incorrect routing or connection failures, preventing the application from loading as expected after selecting the "Open Application in Browser" option. Note: Always verify that the port number shown in the URL matches the one configured on the server to avoid connectivity issues.

This is a screen that helps the users search for the frequently asked questions and read the details. It can also be used as a guide on the process of performing certain activities in the application.
App to be assigned: faqs_1 faqs_1 app should be assigned to the user.

Go to the Help Center menu and click on the sub-menu named Help Center to open it. The screen will be initially loaded with the FAQ groups based on their sequence in ascending order. Users can search for the FAQs based on their group title, question, key ID and key description. Users need to input the search text and click on the OK button to perform the search. Users can clear the search criteria by clicking on the cross Button in the Search Bar. Users can Expand Any Group To See the List of Questions Associated with that Group. Users Can Click On the Question Link To Open The Answer Detail Section. Users Can Also See the Answer in Full-Screen Mode by Clicking on the Expand Button at the Bottom Right Hand Side of the Answer Section. Users can close the full-screen answer by clicking on the collapse button at the bottom right-hand side. Users can close the answer detail by clicking on the close button on the top right-hand side of the answer detail.
This can be used to: Search for the user-relevant FAQs and to read their answers in detail.

documents.t: The installation screen is used to install or update external apps. This includes the app’s folder that will be saved in the closedmodules folder and its zip will be extracted in cdn_app. Apart from this, the installation screen does the following tasks in the background: Update madm_app table. Update the Flavor folder in the closedmodules folder. Update the Flavor zip in the cdn_app folder. Create/Update Tables for that App and its dependent app. Install Config for that App. The screen will have a table which contains all information relevant to the app. Following is a list of columns in the app installation screen like the App name. Components Description App Name of the app. BOL Version BOL version used by the app. Version A version of the app. Is External It is a component of the app. If is_external is marked as false then the app is in closedmodules, if marked as true then the app is in cdn_app. Dependant App Shows the dependent app information of a particular app with the dependent app name and version. Created On Shows the date app was created. Landscape The landscape where the apps are present.

documents.t: To install an app follow the following steps: Click the Upload App button on the top left of the screen to select the zip file and press OK. Note: zip name should be proper for eg:- app_version.zip. Then a popup screen will appear that will give relevant details related to the app, if the app is already there in the madm_app table then it will ask for an install. If it's not there then it will ask for an update. On click of install or update, madm_app will be updated, tables for that app will be generated and the app zip will be placed inside closed modules with extracted files.

documents.t: Open site - https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html Enter your domain name in the input box labeled "Hostname" and wait for the web application to display the result. Under Server key and Certificate and additional certificates section look for Pin SHA256 label There will be 4 such labels. Collect all their values and store them temporarily. Values are marked in yellow as shown in the image. Now Open folder - platforms/android/app/src/main/res/xml Create on file in that folder with name network_security_config.xml Copy and paste the following content into that file: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <network-security-config> <domain-config> <domain includeSubdomains="true">procify.com</domain> <pin-set> <pin digest="SHA-256">VZbCxPHWEHQfBSK5uCQZqIbQ57dTkQCbY0SHQAAoI+M=</pin> <pin digest="SHA-256">JSMzqOOrtyOT1kmau6zKhgT676hGgczD5VMdRMyJZFA=</pin> <pin digest="SHA-256">++MBgDH5WGvL9Bcn5Be30cRcL0f5O+NyoXuWtQdX1aI=</pin> <pin digest="SHA-256">KwccWaCgrnaw6tsrrSO61FgLacNgG2MMLq8GE6+oP5I=</pin> </pin-set> </domain-config> </network-security-config> "procify.com" is the package name, which can be found in the google-services.json file In the previous 3 or 4 steps, you have collected three values for the SHA256 Pin. Replace collected values in four <pin digest=”SHA-256”> </pin> tags respectively. documents.t: When the server environment moves to a newer Klobase (Procify Framework) version, your existing Private Node workspace can now be updated in place. Note: The feature is available post klobase 7-2-365 and later version and Procifynow IDE 7.0.25 and later versions, Working on an older version will not allow the feature
documents.s: 8.2. Klobase Update in the Same Workspace

documents.t: When a new Klobase version is detected, the Klobase Update Required tab opens in VS Code. It shows the Current Workspace, the Previous Klobase Version and the New Klobase Version. (Figure 1) Any app changes that came with the update are listed under Application changes in this update. They are grouped as Updated, Added, Removed, Write access granted and Write access removed. Each group expands and collapses, and long lists scroll. Click Update in This Workspace (the recommended option). The button shows Updating... while it runs. The Private Node restarts once, automatically. Keep VS Code open until it finishes. A notification confirms the new version, for example “Procify Framework updated from 7-2-364 to 7-2-365 in this workspace.”, and the tab closes. (Figure 2) You can also start it from the Command Palette: Update Procify Framework in This Workspace. What Is Kept: checked-out apps, uncommitted changes under src (the notification says how many were left untouched), and pending-change tracking.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Installation Guide/Private Node Setup Developer Guide/Extension Features

documents.t: Message What happened What to do Framework update failed: ... restored to its previous version It failed before the new version was applied. The workspace and node are back on the previous version. Retry, or use Start in a new workspace. Framework updated to X, but the app list could not be refreshed ... The new version is applied and the node is running on it. Only the app refresh failed. Run Update Apps once the node is up. This workspace runs Klobase X, which cannot be updated in place ... This workspace’s Klobase build doesn’t support in-place updates. Use Start in a new workspace, as before. Note: Start in a new workspace (Continue in New Workspace) is still available. Uncommitted changes stay in the old folder and have to be copied across by hand. Note: In-place updates require the matching Procify IDE extension build.

documents.t: If you encounter issues with the application not opening in the browser, follow these steps: Open Command Prompt and type ipconfig to check your current IP address. Compare the IP address displayed with the one maintained in the hosts file. If the IP address in the hosts file does not match the current IP, update the hosts file with the correct IP address. After saving the changes, refresh the application and check if the issue is resolved. This will help ensure that the correct IP address is mapped for proper application functionality. Note: Maintaining a host file entry for procifynowide.com is required in order to open the private node’s url in the Browser. IP addresses change upon changing networks.Only one entry should be present. E.g.: 10.1.1.101 procifynowide.com and 10.1.1.152 procifynowide.com are present, then only one needs to be maintained for the current IP address. Path: system hosts file (common) Format per line: IP_address <whitespace> hostname [aliases...] Example: 10.1.1.101 procifynowide.com

documents.t: Date of Issue: Feb 2025 Target Audience: Application Developer, Consultants, Trainees. A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.

The purpose of this document is to help you understand all the terms that are to be understood after you install the Procifynow IDE - Private Node in your system. There will be various fields and terms present inside the setup which will be relatively unknown to you. This document will help you clear your doubts and make your workflow smooth.

VS Code ≥ 1.95 (alway work on a latest version of vs code unless a particular version is asked to be used) Node.js v22.20.0(LTS) (Windows/Mac ) Git (latest) TypeScript ≥ 4.9.5 (dev dependency) **Install TypeScript (v4.9.5 or later): **npm install -g typescript@^4.9.5 TypeScript is required to compile the App’s .ts files. If you aren’t installing packages globally (i.e. you’re relying on a Local packages installation), you need to install TypeScript globally so you can run tsc -w to compile your code. In order to execute ProcifynowIDE, the workspace folder has to be opened and it has to be updated as a trusted workspace. Application user url: https://<domain_Name>/p6/<Landscape>/index.html Example: https://dev.procifynow.com/p6/Training/index.html Note: URL should be applied according to the server in which the Procify IDE will be set up. URL must be accessible in your browser with a valid SSL certificate. [If not, contact the Admin Team] Git Integration User Guide

In VS Code, open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P/ Cmd+Shift+P) Execute: Run Environment Setup Select required setups from the options provided "Environment Variables" : For maintaining environment variables when packages are installed globally. (Windows only) "Global Package Installation" : Install required packages globally. (Windows only) "Host File Entry" : For maintaining host file entry. "Certificate Installation" : Install certificates. Note: The above needs to be done only after the first installation, Users will be notified if these steps are further required. When prompted for the admin password—please request it from the Infra team. Setup on Mac : Setup on Windows :

documents.t: What is sudo -s: It is used to get the root privileges ( read and write any files on the system, perform operations as any user, change system configuration, install and remove software, and upgrade the operating system and/or firmware ). What is cordova platforms: It will give you the list of platforms added to your project. What is cordova platform rm ios: It is used to remove the ios platform from the current project. What is the cordova platform add ios@7: It is used to add an ios platform from the current project. And @7 is nothing but the iOS platform version. What is chmod -R 777 . : It is used to give the full read/write/execute access; absolute permission to do whatever you need to do. What is the cordova plugin add cordova-plugin-fcm-with-dependecy-updated: It is used to add a plugin to a project and cordova-plugin-fcm-with-dependecy-updated is an fcm plugin. What is --force: It is used to add a plugin to a project by force. What is --allow-root: It is used to run cocoapods as root user. What is pod install: It is used to install cocoapods based upon Podfile configuration.

documents.t: A .certSigningRequest file is a critical part of the certificate generation process in iOS development. It is used to create a code-signing certificate, which is necessary for signing your iOS apps for distribution via In-House or Ad Hoc methods. The CSR file contains information about the developer or the organization, including the public key, which is used by Apple to generate the appropriate signing certificate.If you want to create a new Certificate, then follow the steps below. Open the keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Request a Certificate From a Certificate Authority as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Fill the below details as shown in the below screenshot. The user's email address plays an indirect role in the code-signing process since it is linked to your Apple Developer account and included in the signing certificate's metadata. While the Keychain holds the signing certificate and private key, it does not store the email address in plain text. Instead, the email is embedded within the certificate's metadata, which identifies the developer or organization. In short: Email is used to identify the developer in the signing certificate. Keychain stores the certificate and private key needed for signing the app, enabling secure app distribution and code signing. The CA Email Address is a part of the Issuer information within a certificate and provides a way to contact the Certificate Authority that issued the certificate. It serves as a point of contact for issues related to the certificate, such as validation, renewal, or revocation. You can find the CA's email address in the certificate metadata, which can be inspected in various tools like Keychain Access on macOS or by viewing the certificate details in a web browser. Save the certificate as shown in the below screenshot. Now you can see the certificate as shown in the below screenshot.

documents.t: Certificates ensure your app is properly authorized for development, testing, and distribution. They act as a security mechanism to ensure that only authorized developers and apps can interact with Apple devices. Without these certificates, your app cannot be installed on devices or distributed via the App Store. If you want to create a new Certificate, then follow the steps below. Open your Apple developer account. Click on Certificates as shown in the below screenshot Click on the create ( + ) button as shown below. Select the In-House and Ad Hoc check box and click on continue. In-House: Choose this if you need to distribute apps internally within a company, especially if the app is for internal use and will be installed on many devices within your organization. This is the best choice for enterprise-level apps and internal tools. Ad Hoc: Choose Ad Hoc distribution if you have a small group of testers or specific clients who need to test or review your app before release. This is the best choice for beta testing or distributing an app to a limited number of users. Both methods are critical for scenarios where an app is not intended for public release via the App Store but needs to be tested or used by a controlled group. In the next screen select the certificate request file (a file with a .certSigningRequest file extension), then click Choose and click on continue. Now you can see the Certificate in the list as shown below,

documents.t: The Bundle ID is a unique identifier for your iOS app, and its uses in app development and distribution are crucial for various processes: App Identification: Differentiates your app from others in the Apple ecosystem and App Store. Code Signing and Provisioning Profiles: Ties the app to provisioning profiles for code signing. Enabling Services: Used to enable services like Push Notifications, iCloud, In-App Purchases, Game Center, and more. Managing Versions: Helps to manage different versions of the app, such as production and staging. App Group and Keychain Sharing: Facilitates data sharing between multiple apps. App Distribution: Ensures correct signing and submission for App Store or TestFlight. App Extensions: Ties extensions (e.g., widgets, share extensions) to the main app. Security: Ensures app integrity during installation and distribution. documents.t: Identifiers play a central role in iOS app development, as they are used to uniquely identify different components and services across the Apple ecosystem. They are essential for ensuring proper code signing, testing, distribution, and enabling services like Push Notifications, In-App Purchases, and iCloud.If you want to create new Identifiers, then follow the steps below. Click on ( + ) button as shown in the below screenshot. In the Apple Developer Portal, App IDs are essential for associating your iOS app with Apple's developer services. By creating either Explicit App IDs or Wildcard App IDs, you ensure that your app is properly configured for code signing, provisioning profiles, and services such as Push Notifications and In-App Purchases. It's critical to select the right type of App ID based on your app’s needs and how you intend to distribute it (via App Store, Ad Hoc, or In-House). Select App IDs as shown in the below screenshot. Provide the details and scroll down The Description field in the Identifiers & Profiles section of the Apple Developer Portal is a valuable tool for organizing, managing, and tracking your app development and distribution assets. It improves clarity and helps developers and teams keep track of multiple configurations, ensuring smooth app development and distribution workflows. The Bundle ID is a critical part of the iOS development and distribution process. It uniquely identifies your app, associates it with your developer account, and enables it to interact with various Apple services. Properly setting and managing your Bundle ID is essential for a smooth app development workflow, particularly when managing app versions, provisioning profiles, and services like push notifications and in-app purchase Click on the Push Notification check box and click on continue. Push notifications are an incredibly powerful tool for engaging users, delivering timely information, and enhancing user retention. By leveraging Apple Push Notification Service (APNs), iOS developers can integrate push notifications into their apps to send personalized, real-time updates to users. However, it's important to use push notifications thoughtfully, respecting user preferences and ensuring the content is relevant and non-intrusive. When implemented properly, push notifications can significantly improve user experience, drive engagement, and increase the overall success of an app. Click on register and check the identifier is present in the identifier list.

Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-15475 UI Editor: On rename of any page element, select the existing text(so that user can start typing new value directly) Tools:UI Editor No UI Editor: When renaming a page element, the existing text is selected, enabling the user to start typing the new value right away. After the rename dialog box is opened the text inside the input box is automatically selected. PROC-9723 Message Monitor - Endpoint information on popover Tools: Message monitor No On hovering over the endpoint, the details will be displayed in a popover. End point Details like Registration date, last active date ,Last transaction, device type and status will be shown. The popover functionality has been added to show the endpoint details when hovered over. PROC-15240 BOL Editor -Add validation to restrict changing the primary keys in the child flavor Tools: Bol Editor No The primary key cannot be modified in entities passed from the parent app to the child app, nor in entities created using an older flavor version. These restrictions are in place to maintain data integrity and consistency across different versions and flavors. PROC-16164 Validation while adding and saving in App Hierarchy Detail Section Tools -System Admin No App Hierarchy Detail Section added Validation. A validation is now in place to prevent creating cyclic JSON structures when assigning a parent to a flavor, ensuring no crashes occur. Additionally, if a flavor version is deleted and a new version of the same flavor is assigned immediately, it won't work. The user must save changes before adding the new version. Details: App Hierarchy
No features are developed as a part of the release in this module.

documents.t: Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-18584 UI Editor: Device need to be added in "Preview In" and existing needs correction No Tools - UI Editor Enhanced preview functionality by adding new device options to "Preview In" feature and corrected existing device preview settings for better responsive design testing. Status: **Tested** PROC-20605 UI Editor: Coping a existing page to a different App, changes the id of the controls copied to previous id+"_copy01" No Tools - UI Editor Fixed issue where copying pages between apps resulted in incorrect control ID naming convention. Controls now maintain proper unique IDs when copied across applications. Status: **Tested** PROC-20474 Wizard: Update through wizard is not working for child entity No Tools - UI Editor Resolved wizard update functionality for child entities. Updates to child entities through wizard interface now work correctly. Status: **Tested** PROC-19513 Primary key update should be restricted (UI editor) No Tools - UI Editor Implemented restrictions on primary key updates in UI editor to prevent data integrity issues and maintain referential consistency. Status: **Tested** PROC-21284 Please update the package.json "libphonenumber-js": "^1.12.9" to the vsix No BOL - Private Node (VS Code) Updated libphonenumber-js package to version 1.12.9 in VSIX package for improved phone number validation and formatting capabilities. Status: **Tested** PROC-19721 Feature Request – Read-Only Code Checkout for a User No BOL - Private Node (VS Code) Developers can access and analyze the application's code and structure to debug or investigate issues. However, code modifications are restricted unless the app is explicitly assigned to them. Only developers have permission to save files within the app. While referencing logic is allowed during custom development, existing workflows can be explored safely without the risk of unintended changes. Status: **Tested**

Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-20598 $Variable needed to know the screen size No Tools - UI Editor Introduced screen size variables to enable responsive design capabilities. Controls can now dynamically adjust based on device screen dimensions for improved mobile experience. Status: **Tested** PROC-20499 Feature to Select Desired loading image in kloAttachment - Type: Image (PNG/JPEG) No Tools - UI Editor Enhanced kloAttachment control with customizable loading image selection. Users can now specify custom loading images for better visual feedback during image loading. Status: **Tested** PROC-20530 Grid with auto height(fit to area), empty space height should be reduced / removed in the footer(end) No KloTouch Optimized grid layout by reducing/removing empty footer space when using auto height (fit to area) setting, improving visual appearance and space utilization. Status: **Tested** PROC-19928 KloInput(Combo Box) on down arrow from keyboard suggestions items should get loaded No KloTouch Enhanced KloInput combo box to load suggestion items when down arrow key is pressed, improving keyboard navigation and accessibility. Status: **Tested**

Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-18928 Transport : check should be added to confirm the klobase version in config No BOL - Transport Added version validation checks in transport configuration to ensure Klobase version compatibility during transport operations. Status: **Done - Closed** PROC-20336 VH :- Unable to add deleted values again in vhc, throwing error "Cannot read properties of null (reading '_pm')" No BOL Deleted VH entries with the same key can now be re-added, even if the key differs only by case. Status: **Tested** PROC-20067 Excel upload and download for object type and rollup status in BOL editor No BOL Implemented Excel import/export functionality for object type and rollup status configurations in BOL editor, enabling bulk data management. Status: **Tested** PROC-19104 If build is taking very long time, then it should be marked as FAILED No BOL - Flavor Build Added timeout mechanism for build processes. Builds exceeding specified time limits (e.g., 20 minutes) are now automatically marked as FAILED. Status: **Tested** PROC-20917 Bol Editor: Where used List, if no data found show it in a messageBox No BOL Editor Enhanced user experience by displaying an informative message box when "Where Used" functionality finds no references instead of showing empty tables. Status: **Tested** PROC-20748 VH Config: Adding duplicate keys(id) should be supported No BOL Enhanced Value Help configuration to allow duplicate key IDs when business requirements necessitate multiple entries with same identifier. Status: **Tested** PROC-19496 BOL Editor :- If we are creating or copying any status or config entity and navigating to any other entity it is getting removed from where we added No BOL Editor Fixed data persistence issue where newly created or copied status/config entities were lost when navigating between entities in BOL Editor. Status: **Tested** PROC-20281 Column Sort with loadAll true needs to be handled No BOL Enhanced column sorting functionality to properly handle scenarios where loadAll property is set to true, ensuring consistent data ordering. Status: **Tested** PROC-20265 Column Filter is not working based on the Key-ID No BOL, KloTouch Fixed column filtering functionality to work correctly with Key-ID based filtering, improving data search and display capabilities. Status: **Tested** PROC-20821 oData - Error Handling is not proper No BOL Improved oData error handling mechanisms to provide better error messages and graceful failure recovery for data service operations. Status: **Tested** PROC-21117 Addition of VH Config Item: Please add "KloRemarks" as key and text in base_control propertytype p_vh_id value help No BOL Added "KloRemarks" configuration item to base_control property type value help for enhanced control documentation and metadata management. Status: **Tested** PROC-17273 In app notification No BOL Implemented in-app notification system for real-time user communication and system status updates within the application interface. Status: **Tested**

Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-9574 DEEP LINK / UNIVERSAL LINK: Runtime No KloTouch Implemented deep linking and universal link functionality for mobile runtime, enabling direct navigation to specific app screens from external sources.Universal Link release is only for desktop. Universal Link for apk and ipa will be handled in subsequent release. Status: **Done - Closed** PROC-9248 Side by Side view - Open & Close of right hand side section is not smooth No KloTouch Improved animation and transition effects for side-by-side view panel opening and closing operations for smoother user experience. Status: **Tested** PROC-20438 In case of any dirty object if users navigates to different screen using menu item, Dirty object popup should appear No KloTouch Enhanced data protection by implementing dirty object detection and confirmation popup when users navigate away from screens with unsaved changes. Status: **Tested** PROC-20283 Advanced search: tokens to be displayed if query parameter is set No KloTouch Enhanced advanced search functionality to display search tokens when query parameters are provided, improving search visibility and user experience. Status: **Tested**

Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-20595 POC : UWL and Workflow :Timeline screen alignment in mobile view No BOL - Workflow Enhanced timeline screen layout and alignment for mobile view in Universal Work List, improving mobile user experience and readability. Status: **Tested** PROC-20594 POC : UWL and Workflow : Search Section on Desktop No BOL - Workflow Added search functionality section to desktop version of UWL for improved filtering and navigation capabilities. Status: **Tested** PROC-20593 POC : UWL and Workflow : Status Mismatch in History Tab No BOL - Workflow Resolved status inconsistency issues in History tab where mobile and desktop versions showed different status values for the same requests. Status: **Tested** PROC-20591 POC : UWL and Workflow : Column Width Adjustments No BOL - Workflow Optimized column width settings to eliminate horizontal scrolling and improve data visibility across different screen sizes. Status: **Tested** PROC-20589 POC : UWL and Workflow : Grid Column Order No BOL - Workflow Implemented column reordering functionality for UWL grid, allowing users to customize column arrangement based on their preferences. Status: **Tested** PROC-20588 POC : UWL and Workflow : Mandatory Rejection Reason No BOL - Workflow Enforced mandatory rejection reason input for workflow rejection actions, ensuring proper documentation of rejection decisions. Status: **Tested** PROC-20403 FSFM : Require the ability to pass query parameters to the UWL No BOL - Workflow Enhanced UWL to accept and process query parameters for filtered views and pre-configured search states. Status: **Tested** PROC-20075 POC : UWL and Workflow : New Actor Assignment Screen No BOL - Workflow Implemented new actor assignment interface for improved workflow task delegation and assignment management. Status: **Tested**

Status: **Tested** PROC-19957 Landscape Editor: After changing data from Source Server Config dialog, the updated data are not reflecting in config.json file No Tools - Other Fixed data synchronization issue in Landscape Editor where changes made through Source Server Config dialog were not properly saved to config.json file. Status: **Tested** PROC-19726 Msg monitoring flavor should not extend adm No Tools - Other Refactored message monitoring flavor architecture to remove dependency on ADM extension, improving modularity and reducing coupling. PATCH Klobase Release Note Version 7-2-326 · Sprint 26/19-22 Klobase Version 7-2-326 Version Type Minor Version Release Type Sprint Release — 26/19-22 Sprint 5059 (26/19-22) Sprint Lead Yenuga Siva Narendra Reddy Update Branch release/QA Release Approved by Santhosh H R Regression Run by Abhijit kuanr and Team Test Landscapes EAM, EAM_QA_R, ATTACH, PRC Testing Platform WildFly Server Restart Yes api.json Change Yes — WildFly restart required APK / IPA Change Yes — PROC-24144 VSIX Change No NestJS Update No Shared App Changes No Build Reference PROC-26843 1. Overview 1.1 What are the changes? This release contains the below tested items across BOL Editor, UI Editor, kloReact runtime, BOL Node server infrastructure, mobile (APK/IPA), Account Console, server-side Pivot/Report/Chart, and Business AI modules. Area Has Changed? Adoption Required? Dev Tools (BOL Editor, UI Editor, Online Code Editor, Menu, App Cache-Control) Yes No Dev Config Tools No No UI Controls Yes No BOL Yes No KloTouch / Mobile Runtime Yes No ADM No No Account Console Yes No System Admin / Message Monitoring Yes No Index.html No No 2. Module: BOL Editor / Dev Tools Below are the new features, improvements, and bug fixes delivered in this release for BOL Editor and Dev Tools. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-25909 BOL Editor: Auto Number Behaviour Is Not Consistent Fixed an inconsistency in the Auto Number field where generated numbers occasionally started from 1001 instead of the expected sequence. The auto-number generator now produces a reliable, consistent sequence. N/A PROC-25839 Show Warning / Error If Two Properties Use the Same Label in the Same Entity BOL Editor now raises a warning when two properties within the same entity share an identical label, preventing ambiguity at runtime and improving data quality during schema design. User Guide: Data Studio- User Guide 7.0 N/A PROC-26051 Entity Creation via Excel Sheet: Support for Config VH Creation (s_status etc.) The Excel-based entity creation utility now supports creation of config-type value helps (e.g. s_status) in addition to regular entities, significantly reducing manual setup steps for new entities. User Guide: Data Studio- User Guide 7.0 N/A PROC-23549 Training: Incorrect Automatic Import When Typecasting Using Private Node Suggestion Fixed the code editor's auto-import logic when accepting a typecast suggestion from Private Node. The incorrect import statement is no longer inserted; the correct module path is used. N/A 3. Module: UI Editor / Wizard Below are the improvements and bug fixes delivered in this release for UI Editor and Notification Modeler. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-24424 UI Editor Wizard: Integer/Decimal Column Headers and Cell Content Should Be Right-Aligned in Grid and Tree In the UI Editor Wizard, columns configured with Integer or Decimal property types now correctly right-align both header text and cell content in Grid and Tree screen types, matching standard numerical display conventions. Reference document : Page Builder- User Guide 7.0 N/A PROC-26821 Add Validation to Restrict Template ID Length to 25 Characters in Notification Modeler The Notification Modeler now enforces a maximum length of 25 characters for Template IDs at validation time, preventing downstream processing errors caused by oversized template identifiers. N/A 4. Module: kloReact / React Runtime Below are the bug fixes and improvements delivered in this release for the kloReact / React runtime, covering both web and mobile UI issues. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-26727 kloReact APK/IPA: Notification Red Dot Not Removed After Marking All Notifications as Read Fixed a defect in kloReact APK and IPA builds where the notification red dot badge persisted even after all notifications were marked as read, causing confusion for mobile users. N/A PROC-26726 kloReact BOL Editor: Change Icon on VH Screen Does Not Open Icon Dialog Resolved a bug where clicking the 'Change' icon button on the VH (Value Help) screen in the BOL Editor under a kloReact environment did not open the icon picker dialog. N/A PROC-26725 kloReact: UI-Type VH Is Not Editable in Specific Scenario Fixed a scenario in kloReact where a Value Help of UI type was rendered as read-only when it should have been editable, preventing users from updating the VH value. N/A PROC-26719 kloReact: Upgrade Banner Click Throws Error as Alert Resolved an issue where clicking the upgrade banner in kloReact displayed a JavaScript error as a browser alert popup instead of handling it gracefully. N/A PROC-26718 kloReact: Menu Became Blank on Desktop During Parallel Mobile Testing with Same User Fixed a race condition in kloReact where the desktop menu became blank when the same user account was simultaneously active in a mobile session, caused by conflicting menu state updates. N/A PROC-26716 kloReact: Create Button Alignment and Checkbox Size Mismatch in User Collections Corrected a CSS mismatch between kloTouch and kloReact runtime in the User Collections screen — the Create button alignment and individual check/tick-box size are now consistent. N/A PROC-26714 kloReact: User Details Not Showing After Navigating to About Page Then Logging Out Fixed an issue where navigating to the About page and then logging out caused user details to be absent on the next login, due to stale session state not being cleared. N/A PROC-26713 kloReact: Incorrect Alignment on Login Page Corrected layout alignment issues on the kloReact login page, ensuring consistent positioning across screen sizes and device types. N/A PROC-26158 React Phase 01: SAP Icons Should Not Be Shown for React Flavors in Any Tool SAP-specific icon sets are no longer displayed in Dev Tools for React-type flavors, as SAP icons are not applicable to React runtime environments. N/A PROC-25987 React Phase 01: Delay Should Not Be Used for Loading kloTouch Files Removed artificial delays used when loading kloTouch files in the React runtime. Files are now loaded via a proper event-driven mechanism, improving startup performance and reliability. N/A PROC-21063 No Internet Connection Banner: UI Improvement Improved icons, responsiveness and alignment of No Internet Connection and Upgrade banners for better display across mobile and desktop resolutions. N/A PROC-23390 navByQuery Not Working in Mobile Application When Navigating with kloGuid Control Fixed a bug preventing navByQuery from functioning correctly on mobile applications when navigation was triggered via a kloGuid control, restoring expected deep-navigation behaviour. N/A 5. Module: BOL Node / Server / Middleware Below are the improvements and bug fixes delivered in this release for BOL Node 512 MB, server-side message processing, and middleware. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-24595 BOL Node 512 MB: Middleware Message Dispatch Messages are now correctly excluded from dispatch to dedicated nodes and master node for processing when running in the 512 MB BOL Node configuration, preventing unnecessary processing overhead. N/A PROC-24592 BOL Node 512 MB: Server-Side Query Streaming (Rules / Scheduler / AppService) Implemented server-side query streaming for Rules, Scheduler, and AppService executions in the 512 MB BOL Node environment, enabling efficient processing of large result sets without memory overflow. N/A PROC-25937 Message Monitoring: Queries Need to Be Optimised Optimised the server queue monitor queries that were causing slowdowns due to 3.1 million records in the ma_tenant_log_q table. Indexes and query refactoring significantly reduce monitor execution time. N/A PROC-26584 More Than One Master Found: Service cacheMaster Fixed a parallel election race condition in middleware where multiple nodes started simultaneously and each declared itself master. The election protocol now correctly ensures a single master is elected. N/A 6. Module: Mobile (APK / IPA) Below are the bug fixes delivered in this release for the mobile APK and IPA builds. Note: an APK/IPA rebuild is required for PROC-24144. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-24144 Unnecessary Permission Requests in APK for KloRemark and Document Upload Removed spurious permission prompts in the Android APK: KloRemark no longer requests microphone permission on screen load without user interaction, and Document Upload no longer triggers unnecessary storage permissions. Both now request permissions only at the point of use. APK/IPA rebuild required 7. Module: Account Console / Permissions / Notifications Below are the improvements delivered in this release for Account Console role management and push notifications. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-26524 Enhancement: Enforce Default Permissions and Validation for New Roles At DEV Systems, after a new role creation, a warning box will be shown on the screen, to inform the developers about maintaining the permissions for that new role, to avoid Access Denied scenario for the respective users belonging to that role. Document: LINK . N/A PROC-25592 Push Notification: Improvements When a notification is clicked by a different user, the app shows a Switch User message with notification user details and switch information about switching accounts and possible unsaved data loss. If there are unsaved changes, an additional warning note is also displayed. Also, once the intended user logs back in, missed notifications can be reviewed anytime from the Notification Centre (🔔). Document: LINK . N/A 8. Module: Server-Side Pivot / Report / Chart Below are the new features delivered in this release for PIVOT, REPORT, and CHART screen types. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-25423 Phase 01 Runtime: Server-Side Pivoting for PIVOT / REPORT / CHART Screens Pivoting operations for PIVOT, REPORT, and CHART screen types are now executed server-side rather than on the client, significantly improving performance for large datasets and reducing browser memory usage. N/A 9. Module: Business AI Below are the new features delivered in this release for the Business AI module. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-26816 Business AI: Application Workflow Context Implementation — POC and Phase 1 Completed POC and Phase 1 implementation of application workflow context for Business AI. The AI assistant can now understand and reason about the workflow state of the current application, enabling context-aware suggestions. N/A PROC-26745 Business AI: VH Query Suggestion Display to User Business AI now surfaces Value Help query suggestions to the user during data entry. When a VH Query field requires idata, the AI fires a query matching on key or description and presents the best matches for user selection. N/A 10. Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-27362 OData BO Support – Deep Update (Header + Child updates in a single call) No BOL Extended OData support to allow deep update operations where both header and child entity data can be updated in a single API call. Previously, multi-level updates required sequential requests, increasing round trips. Clients can send nested JSON payloads containing parent entity properties along with child entity arrays. Child entities are automatically matched by parent key - existing children are updated, and new children are created.All operations are committed in a single transaction with full validation support. This significantly reduces overhead for complex entity hierarchies. Document Link Status: Tested PROC-27343 BOL Node 512 MB Stability Verification & Issue Resolution No BOL Verified stability of the BOL Node running under a 512 MB memory constraint and resolved all identified issues. Ensures the platform operates reliably within constrained memory environments for applicable deployments. Status: Done - Closed PROC-27366 Middleware: 1000 messages with no_sequence=0 took 17 minutes to process No BOL - Middleware Resolved a middleware throughput issue where 1000 messages with no_sequence=0 took 17 minutes to complete against only 1 minute of actual processing time (16 minutes idle). Queuing and dispatch logic has been optimized to eliminate idle wait between message batches. Status: Tested PROC-26465 Middleware: Default retry delay for deadlock/lock wait should be increased No BOL - Middleware For the middleware retry settings for Inbound Messages, the RetryDelaySeconds default value has been changed to 1 second in the config.json file. If it’s already overridden, then that value is not changed. Document Link Status: Tested PROC-25080 Transport log showing source and target landscape as "undefined" No BOL - Transport Fixed a transport logging defect where source and target landscape names appeared as "undefined" in the transport log. Landscape identifiers are now correctly resolved and displayed in all transport log entries. Status: Tested PROC-26541 Indexing required on Users Permissions table – madm_user_permissions No BOL Added a composite index on the r_user_id & r_landscape column in the madm_user_permissions table to improve query performance for user-based permission lookups. Status: Tested PROC-26503 Remove deprecated entity reference button or handle logic in BOL / BOL Editor No BOL / BOL Editor Removed the deprecated entity reference-based condition button from the BOL Editor UI. Updated the underlying logic to prevent duplicate condition generation and to ignore deprecated backward-compatibility paths, eliminating developer confusion caused by legacy UI artifacts. Status: Tested PROC-26994 Custom template should be enabled for OTP Services No BOL OTP notification services can now use custom message templates. Previously OTP messages were fixed to a system template. Developers can now configure custom templates for OTP emails and SMS channels, enabling branded OTP communications per application. Status: Tested Reference Document : Notification Developer Guide PROC-26106 Attachment: setAttachmentP() not working on server side No BOL Fixed a bug where setAttachmentP() called from server-side logic (entity callbacks or controllers) threw a "File Write Failed" error. The server-side attachment API now correctly processes and persists file data. Status: Tested PROC-25752 Phase 02 Runtime – PIVOT/REPORT/CHART: Server-side pivoting No BOL Implemented Phase 2 of server-side data pivoting. Pivot, Report, and Chart data transformations are now computed on the server instead of the client browser, reducing client-side load and significantly improving performance for large datasets. Status: Tested User Guide link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oNQqNsgTLLFqtPn7914ggasXzJTDXc-oSo6QBYq9T6Y/edit?tab=t.0 PROC-22355 API Versioning Behavior Creates Misleading User Experience No BOL Corrected API URL versioning behaviour that was ignoring explicitly requested patch versions and automatically redirecting to the latest patch. API version resolution now honours the requested version, giving developers predictable and accurate versioning. Status: Done - Closed PROC-25409 BOL Editor: Excel-uploaded entry not present after refreshing (Rollup status and Status Config) No BOL Editor Fixed a persistence bug in BOL Editor where entries added via Excel upload were not retained after a page refresh in the Rollup Status and Status Config views. Uploaded entries now correctly persist to the database and reload on refresh. Status: Tested PROC-24593 BOL Node 512 MB – OData GET Services No BOL Validated and ensured OData GET service functionality is fully operational in the BOL Node 512 MB memory configuration. Addressed compatibility issues specific to this constrained memory deployment scenario. Status: Tested PROC-25001 BOL/Metadata: adding vh to query parameter not updating query generation No BOL Fixed a metadata query generation bug where adding a value help (vh) to a query parameter did not correctly update the generated query. The query generator now correctly incorporates vh-based parameters, ensuring accurate data retrieval. Status: Tested PROC-24749 Training: get$Role() returning empty object {} in controller and console No BOL Resolved an issue where get$Role() returned {} instead of the user's role data when called from a controller. The function now correctly retrieves and returns the active user role, consistent with $SYSTEM.roleId behaviour. Status: Tested PROC-27146 Safeguards to prevent recursive invocation between entity callback and CommitP API No BOL Added runtime safeguards to detect and break recursive call loops that occur when an entity callback triggers a CommitP API call, which in turn re-invokes the entity callback. Prevents infinite recursion and stack overflow in server-side business logic. Validation added in case the same transaction is being used for commitP() from callbacks throwing error as “Transaction commit is already in progress. Please wait for the current commit to finish before calling commit again.“. e.g., Developers should not use commitP() by using the same transaction at the rules callbacks - get the transaction from oEvent (function parameter) and use that for commitP() later on in the rules callback. Document Link 1, Document Link 2 Status: Tested PROC-26611 SEAM4: error_code missing in kloerror when commitP fails No BOL Fixed a bug where the error_code field was absent in the kloerror response object when a commitP operation failed. The error_code is now correctly populated, enabling downstream error handling to distinguish and respond to specific failure types. Status: Tested

This phase integrates kloQuery callbacks and additional AI context scenarios, enabling Business AI to generate queries and responses with richer, application-aware data. Status: Tested Reference Guide - Business_AI_User_Guide PROC-26607 Developer AI – User/App level token limits and usage metrics No Developer AI Implemented configurable token limit enforcement and usage tracking at user and application level for Developer AI. Administrators can now set per-user and per-app token quotas; usage metrics are tracked for governance and cost control. Status: Tested PROC-27240 Developer AI – All LLM calls properly logged in LangSmith No Developer AI All LLM calls from Developer AI are now captured in LangSmith with proper, searchable names. Previously generic entries made it impossible to isolate individual AI call chains. Each call now appears with a meaningful identifier. Status: Tested PROC-27215 Developer AI – Early return on dependency failure in agents No Developer AI Added early-exit logic across RuleAgent, SchedulerAgent, NotificationAgent, and SampleDataAgent. If any upstream dependency fails mid-execution, the agent immediately returns a clear error instead of continuing with partial or misleading output. Status: Tested PROC-26921 Developer AI – Code files fetched from actual repository No Developer AI Developer AI now fetches existing code files directly from the version-controlled source repository instead of the local file system, ensuring AI modifications are based on the live codebase rather than potentially stale copies. Status: Tested PROC-27598 Developer AI – Qdrant not supporting 3072 dimensions No Developer AI Fixed a vector storage compatibility issue where Qdrant rejected 3072-dimension embeddings. The Qdrant collection is now correctly configured to support the required dimensionality for the AI embedding model in use. Status: Tested PROC-27565 Developer AI – Incorrect accountId in payload causing metadata save error No Developer AI Corrected a payload bug where an incorrect accountId caused AI metadata save operations to fail. The payload now correctly resolves and includes the authenticated user's accountId before submission. Status: Tested PROC-27214 Developer AI – Run-only-jobs includes screen creation in response No Developer AI Fixed a response scoping issue where selecting "run only jobs" in Developer AI still returned screen creation results. The agent now correctly restricts execution and response to the selected job types only. Status: Tested PROC-27128 Developer AI – Errors in Google Cloud logs during normal operation No Developer AI Resolved error-level log entries in Google Cloud logs triggered by normal Developer AI operations. Log levels have been corrected and error handling improved to eliminate false-alarm log noise. Status: Tested PROC-27034 Developer AI – Handle transient fields in SampleDataAgent/RuleAgents/NotificationAgent No Developer AI Updated agents to correctly differentiate Regular, Transient, and Calculated property types. Previously transient fields were incorrectly included in insert operations, causing errors and invalid data generation. Status: Tested PROC-27024 Developer AI – getEntitiesDetails API returning all properties as Regular No Developer AI Fixed a logic bug where getEntitiesDetails returned all properties as "Regular" regardless of actual type. Property types are now correctly derived from entity configuration (Transient, Calculated, Regular). Status: Tested PROC-27021 Developer AI – Attachment and GeoLocation must be transient, not regular No Developer AI Corrected property type classification for Attachment and GeoLocation to Transient, as these are not persisted directly in the entity table. Ensures correct handling by all AI agents. Status: Tested PROC-26309 Developer AI – Clear message when requested App is not found No Developer AI Improved error handling so Developer AI returns a clear, actionable message when a requested application does not exist, instead of a generic failure. Status: Tested PROC-26281 Developer AI – Handle concurrent multi-user requests No Developer AI Implemented concurrency handling for simultaneous multi-user Developer AI requests. Each user's workflow now executes in full isolation, preventing session cross-contamination. Status: Tested PROC-26278 Developer AI – Use incremental IDs for screens, remove datekey No Developer AI Replaced timestamp-based datekeys in AI-generated screen IDs with deterministic incremental IDs. Added duplicate ID checks. Produces cleaner, predictable identifiers for AI-generated screens. Status: Tested PROC-26277 Developer AI – Multiple subscreen layouts incorrectly added to one subscreen No Developer AI Fixed a screen generation defect where multiple subscreen layout definitions were attached to the same subscreen. Each subscreen now receives only its designated layout. Status: Tested PROC-26271 Developer AI – Validate each metadata item created for screen No Developer AI Added per-metadata validation during AI screen generation. Each generated metadata item is individually validated before persistence, allowing errors to be caught granularly. Status: Tested PROC-25033 React Phase 01 – Playwright automation No React UI Implemented Playwright-based automated test coverage for React Phase 01 deliverables. Establishes a regression test baseline for the React UI track. Status: Tested

Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-27915 UI Editor : Vinable optimization and improvement No Page Builder: Optimized the performance of the Vienable TreeTable by reducing rendering overhead, removing unnecessary formatters and dynamic style processing, and simplifying read-only handling, resulting in improved tab loading time and reduced browser resource consumption. Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-27719 Manthan : Inconsistency on data over downloading excel No BOL / KloTouch While downloading the reports data is missing in excel. Status: Tested. PROC-27570 Created saved query not available in VH No BOL Editor: Addressed an issue causing the Data Browser to fail to display data for value helps created from saved queries. PROC-27379 Attachment download: No error thrown when trying to download a attachment but is not downloading No BOL When trying to download attachment using downloadAttachP, If it fails to fetch the data or fails once For the next time if downloadAttachP is triggerd it does’t throw any error. This is due to the client side table gets the entry and for the next time the attachmentDownloadPromise stays as a unresolved promise and doesn’t throw any error Status: Tested. PROC-27170 Row auth :- Data access recalculation is failing No BOL Data Access Keys will also support for Entities having names in uppercase during search or recalculate operations in the screen under Access Management. Status: Tested. PROC-26700 Upgrade Cordova Projects to Android 15 and iOS 8 No Upgraded procifyapp-generic to cordova-android 15 (targetSdk 36) and cordova-ios 8 (SPM migration, new hooks, deprecated API fixes) — app version 3.2.12, backward compatible across iOS/Android/Desktop/Tablet with no known issues. Full details: Cordova_Upgrade_Guide_Android15_iOS8. PROC-26043 BOL VH:- vh is inherited from parent flavor even after deleting from child flavor No BOL Even after removing the value help (VH) in the child flavor It is still appearing in the UI. If VH is removed or overridden in the child flavor, there shouldn’t be any need to make changes in the parent flavors. Status: Done - Closed. PROC-26017 oData service : Missing confirmation for relational (child) data save in oData response No BOL When sending relational (child) data within the parent entity JSON, the oData response only returns the parent entity data. The response does not include any details or confirmation regarding whether the relational (child) data has been successfully saved. $expand and its relation names need to be maintained in the URL to show the relational entities data in the response. $expand is for response purpose only, it does not affect the update process. Explained this behavior in the document: ODATA SERVICES User Guide 6.0 - Important Point No. 6. Status: Not an Issue - Closed. PROC-25979 Production Excel Upload Error - Precison should be 2 No Updated the setter to automatically format/round the value based on the configured precision before storing it, ensuring that the value always conforms to the defined precision. Note: This change is applicable only to new entries. Existing entries will not be affected. If this change is required for existing entries, build will be required for the flavor. Status: Tested. PROC-25942 PVT Node: Folders are coming in new but throwing error while committing No BOL - Private Node PVT Node: Folders are coming in new but throwing error while committing. Status: Tested. PROC-25486 App Merge: Deleting a property deletes the config of the property but modifying only the property is not considering the config. No BOL When merging a branch to a version. If in version, a property is deleted(which had a config) and the same property is modified in branch and then merged, the property’s conflict gets resolved via app merge but the property’s config is not considered. Status: Tested. PROC-25447 Transport tool update is not completing in a single trigger. No BOL - Transport The update is not completing through the screen, and even though the tool update is automated via the terminal It remains in **in_progress** status. Status: Tested. PROC-25129 App Merge : during merge of newly created app_service the system fields are not filled for app service file in m_file. No BOL Fixed an App Merge defect where system fields were not populated for a newly created app_service entry in m_file during merge, which caused issues in private node checkout when validating s_modified_on. Status: Tested. PROC-23429 Relation Data not shown when creating parent's data No BOL Fixed a defect where related child data was not displayed while creating a parent record. Status: Tested.

Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-28028 Press Event needs to be added for card grey color font needs to be added No KloTouch Press Event needs to be added for card grey color font needs to be added. Status: Tested. PROC-26470 getSelectedIndices() returns an empty array when called on a transnode used inside a dialog, as dialog sections are not included in active node filtering. No KloTouch When `getSelectedIndices()` is called on a transnode used within a dialog It returns an empty array. This occurs because the current implementation filters sections only from the screen’s active nodes, excluding sections rendered inside dialogs. Status: Tested. PROC-26174 Separate Key and Description Columns for Selected Properties in Excel Download No The vhDownloadFormat property lets developers configure how individual Value Help (VH) fields are exported during the standard Excel download by specifying key, description, or key + description for each VH field (for example: [{"my_key":"key"},{"country_code":"desc"},{"state_code":"key-desc"}]). Only the VH fields listed in this property follow the configured format, while all other VH fields use the default download behavior. If a non-VH field is included in the property, the download continues with the normal field value without errors, although a console warning/error may be logged. This configuration applies only to the standard Excel Download button and does not affect the ShowDownloadExcelOptions button, which already allows users to choose the VH export format for all column KloSectionXLSX. Status: Tested. PROC-25576 Need to support kloBarCodeReader Control in toolbar of dialog page area. No KloTouch Need to support kloBarCodeReader Control in toolbar of dialog page area. Status: Tested. PROC-25420 sap.m.ObjectNumber control's dsrc binding is getting mapped to state property instead of number property. No KloTouch sap.m.ObjectNumber control's dsrc binding is getting mapped to state property instead of number property. Status: Tested. PROC-23925 KloTouch : Excel Download Fails to Export VH Column Values Using sap controls such as sap.m.ObjectStatus No KloTouch Fixed Excel export failing to include value-help column values for fields using SAP controls such as sap.m.ObjectStatus.
