Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand the three types of Value Helps (VH Config, VH Query, VH Transaction) and when to use each. Create a VH Config for priority (Low / Medium / High / Critical) and nature_of_complaint, complaint_type fields. Create VH Query types that fetch data from d_customers and d_resp_team entities as picker suggestions. Understand what a KloQuery is and how it differs from a Runtime Entity query. Create two Saved Queries for the complaint list: My Complaints (filtered by assigned_to = current user) and All Open Complaints (filtered by s_status = OPEN). Assign Value Helps to entity properties in the BOL Editor. Update the UI — wire VH pickers and query-driven TransNodes into the p_complaints search and detail sections. 📘 What This Session Builds On Session 3 configured Relations, Object Types, Status, and ID Series on d_complaints — the structural foundation. Session 4 makes the user experience intelligent: instead of typing raw IDs, users get dropdowns and pickers. priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint → VH Config (fixed, app-managed lists). customer_id, responsible_team → VH Query (dynamic, fetched from d_customers / d_resp_team). Saved Queries → drive the different list views per role (My Complaints for Employee, All Open for Manager). Part A — Understanding Value Helps​ A.1 — What Is a Value Help?​ A Value Help (VH) is a platform-level component that provides a controlled list of choices for an entity property. When a VH is assigned to a property, the corresponding input field in the UI automatically renders as a dropdown (ComboBox), auto-complete field, or picker dialog (F4) — without any additional coding. The VH also validates that the entered value exists in the list when 'Is Restricted' is enabled. 📘 Three VH Types in Klobase (VH User Guide — Section 1.1) VH Config: Values are maintained in the metadata (config) DB. App-managed, flavor-dependent. Can be overridden by child apps. Requires a build after creation/update. Use for fixed classification lists (priority, complaint_type, etc.). VH Query: Values are fetched from a transactional or modelled query at runtime. Use for dynamic master data pickers (customer_id, responsible_team). The query determines what data appears in the picker. VH Transaction (DEPRECATED): Older type. Internally still supported for legacy apps. New development should use VH Config or VH Query instead. VH Type Source Naming Use Case for This App VH Config Metadata / Config DB vhc_<name> priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint VH Query Transactional / Modelled Query vhq_<name> customer_id → d_customers, responsible_team → d_resp_team A.2 — Value Helps to Create in This Session​ VH ID Type Property to Assign Description vhc_priority VH Config priority Low / Medium / High / Very High vhc_complaint_type VH Config complaint_type Software vhc_nature_of_complaint VH Config nature_of_complaint Hardware : Battery not charging vhq_customer VH Query customer_id Fetches from d_customers — key: customer_id, display: customer_name vhq_resp_team VH Query responsible_team Fetches from d_resp_team — key: emp_id, display: name Part B — Creating VH Config Value Helps​ B.1 — What Is VH Config and When to Use It?​ VH Config stores its values in the metadata database — the same database that stores entity definitions, page structures, and app metadata. These values are part of the application definition itself, not the transaction data. Use VH Config for lists that are defined once by the developer and rarely change: priority levels, complaint categories, nature classifications. B.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating vhc_priority​ Follow these steps to create the priority VH Config. Repeat the process for vhc_complaint_type and vhc_nature. # Action Detail 1 Open Data Studio Navigate to Design Studio → Data Studio. Select your application customer_complaints_<prid> from the dropdown. 2 Click + → Value Help Select entity. Click the Add icon (+) in the toolbar. A menu appears — select Value Help. The Value Help creation dialog opens. 3 Fill VH ID and Type Value Help ID: vhc_priority 5 Fill VH detail fields Description: Priority levels for customer complaints 6 Add VH Config items Click the Add (+) icon in the VH Config Items section. Add Row 1: Key: LOW 7 Save Click Save. vhc_priority is saved. Note: a build is required for this to appear in the UI — proceed to create all VH Configs first, then the trainer will trigger the build. B.3 — Assign VH Config to Entity Properties​ After creating all three VH Configs, assign each to the corresponding property in d_complaints. This is done in the Properties tab of the entity. # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints In the Data Studio tree, click d_complaints. 2 Go to Properties tab Click the Properties tab. Locate the priority property row. 3 Set Value Help for priority Click the Value Help column cell for the priority row. A value help picker opens — type vhc_priority and select it. The VH ID is now assigned to the property. 5 Repeat for complaint_type and nature_of_complaint Assign vhc_complaint_type to complaint_type property. Assign vhc_nature to nature_of_complaint property. 6 Save Click Save. All three properties now have VH Config assignments. ✔ VH Config Checkpoint vhc_priority created — 4 items: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL. vhc_complaint_type created — 5 items matching the Object Types from Session 3. vhc_nature created — 4 items: TECHNICAL, LOGISTICS, COMMERCIAL, GENERAL. All 3 VH Configs assigned to their respective d_complaints properties. Save confirmed for all. Part C — Creating VH Query Value Helps​ C.1 — What Is VH Query?​ A VH Query fetches its suggestion items from a live entity or modelled query at runtime. Unlike VH Config (which is static metadata), VH Query shows records that are currently in the transactional database. This is the right choice for master entity pickers — where the data comes from d_customers, d_resp_team, or any other entity that can be searched and selected. 📘 VH Query Fields (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 2.2.3 Value Help Detail) Entity/Query: The entity name or modelled query ID that returns the list of suggestions. Key Property: The property whose value gets STORED in the parent entity when the user selects an item. For d_customers → customer_id. Display Text: The property shown to the user in the dropdown/picker. For d_customers → customer_name. Desc Format: How the display appears. Example: :customer_id--:customer_name shows ID followed by Name. Icon: Optional — entity property that holds an icon URL to show alongside each suggestion item. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating vhq_customer​ # Action Detail 1 Click + → Value Help Select entity and In the Data Studio toolbar, click + → Value Help. Value Help ID: vhq_customer 2 Open vhq_customer Click vhq_customer in the tree. The Detail panel shows the VH Query configuration fields. 3 Set Entity/Query In the Entity/Query field, select d_customers. This means the VH will execute a runtime query against d_customers to fetch suggestion rows. 4 Set Key Property Key Property: customer_id. This is the value that gets written into d_complaints.customer_id when the user picks a customer. 5 Set Display Text Display Text: customer_name. This is what the user sees in the dropdown list. 6 Set Desc Format Desc Format: :customer_id--:customer_name. This renders as 'CUST-001 -- Acme Corp' in the picker field once a value is selected. 7 Save Click Save. vhq_customer is ready. Perform the same for vhq\_res\_team C.4 — Assign VH Query to Entity Properties​ # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints → Properties tab Click on d_complaints in the tree and go to Properties. 2 Assign vhq_customer to customer_id Click the Value Help cell for customer_id. Select vhq_customer from the picker. Optionally mark Is Restricted = true to enforce that only valid customer records can be entered. 3 Assign vhq_resp_team to responsible_team Click the Value Help cell for responsible_team. Select vhq_resp_team. 4 Save Click Save. 💡 VH Type in the UI Control (KloControls 7.0 User Guide — KloInput) After assigning a VH to a property, the KloInput control in the UI renders differently based on the vhType setting in the Page Data Model or the control's properties panel. F4: Shows a full picker dialog when the user clicks the input — best for large datasets (d_customers with many records). ComboBox: Shows a dropdown list — best for small fixed lists (priority, complaint_type). AutoComplete: Shows suggestions as the user types — best for name-search scenarios. The platform automatically uses the appropriate type based on the VH type. You can override it in the Page Data Model or the control properties. Part D — Understanding and Creating KloQueries​ D.1 — What Is a KloQuery?​ A KloQuery is the Klobase equivalent of a SQL SELECT statement. It lets you define — within the Data Studio — exactly what records to fetch, from which entity, with which filters, joins, and sort order. Unlike a Runtime Entity Query (which simply fetches all records of an entity), a Modelled Query gives you full control over the WHERE clause, JOIN entities, and sort order — and is reusable across multiple pages. Query Type When to Use Runtime Query (Entity Query) Fetch all records of a single entity. No WHERE clause in the definition. Filters applied at runtime via the TransNode. Use for simple list screens. Modelled Query (Dynamic Query) Define custom WHERE conditions, joins, sort order in the BOL Editor. Reusable, entity-independent. Use for role-filtered lists (My Complaints), VH Queries backed by joins, aggregated results. Native Query (Advanced Query) Raw SQL. Database-specific. Use only for special cases not achievable with modelled queries. Avoid training. 📘 KloQuery Fields Reference (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.2) Return Entity: The entity whose properties appear in the result set. Query Type: Runtime Entities And Join: Add the root entity and any joined entities (LEFT JOIN, INNER JOIN, etc.). Select Properties: Choose which properties from the entities appear in the result. Parameters: Define input parameters the query accepts at runtime (e.g., user_id filter passed from the TransNode). Where: Define filter conditions: entity.property = :parameter or entity.property = 'fixed_value'. Sort Order: Set the default sorting column and direction (ASC / DESC). Naming convention: Query IDs must start with q_. All lowercase. D.2 — Queries to Create in This Session​ Query ID Type Purpose q_complaints Modelled Employee: shows only complaints assigned to the logged-in user D.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating q_my_complaints​ # Action Detail 1 Click + → Query Select d_complaints entity and click + → Query. Fill : q_complaints and click create then save. 2 Open q_complaints Click q_my_complaints in the tree. The Detail panel shows the query configuration tabs. 4 Select Properties tab Click the Select Properties tab. By default, all d_complaints properties are included. Remove any you do not need to reduce payload. Keep it all for now. 5 Add Parameter Click the Parameters tab. Click Add. Parameter ID: current_user 6 Add WHERE clause Click the Where tab. Click Add. Fill: Entity Property: d_complaints.assigned_to 7 Add Sort Order Click the Sort Order tab. Click Add. Field: d_complaints.created_on 8 Save Click Save. q_my_complaints is ready. Part E — Saved Queries​ E.1 — What Is a Saved Query?​ A Saved Query is a named combination of a base query and a specific set of pre-filled search parameters. Where a Modelled Query defines the structure, a Saved Query defines a pre-configured instance of that query — ready to execute with one click in the search bar. Saved Queries appear as quick-filter options in the search TransNode of the UI. 📘 Saved Query vs Modelled Query (Basic Training Guide — Section 2.1) Modelled Query: The definition — entity, properties, parameters, WHERE logic. Reusable structure. Saved Query: A named configuration of a modelled query with preset parameter values. Stored per entity. In the UI, a Saved Query appears as a quick-filter button or dropdown in the search bar section. Saved Queries are created from the Data Browser (Advanced Search), not directly in the query detail tab. Naming convention for Saved Query IDs: Begin with sq_ by convention. E.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Saved Query from Data Browser​ # Action Detail 1 Open Data Browser Select d_complaints in the Data Studio tree. Click the data browser in the toolbar. The Data Browser opens. 2 Open Advanced Search In the Data Browser toolbar, click the Advance Search button. A search configuration dialog opens. 3 Select Base Query In the Query field of the Advance click + 4 Set parameter values Select customer_id in the left input and like in the middle input. Enter: $SYSTEM.userID as the parameter value. This means the saved query will always use the logged-in user's ID at runtime. 5 Save as Saved Query Click the Save Query button (or the Save icon in the Advance Search toolbar). Enter Saved Query ID: sq_my_complaints 6 Verify Click search. The Data Browser should show only complaints where assigned_to matches the current user (or empty if no matches). The saved query is now available. Part F — Updating the UI to Use Value Helps and Queries​ With all Value Helps and Queries configured in the BOL Editor, the p_complaints page now needs to be updated to use them. In this part you will: Update the search TransNode to use q_complaints_list as its data source. Add the quick-filter Saved Query buttons (sq_my_complaints, sq_all_open) to the search section. Verify that priority, complaint_type, customer_id, and responsible_team fields in the form render as dropdowns/pickers automatically. Set the vhType on customer_id and responsible_team controls to F4 (full picker dialog). F.1 — Update the TransNode to Use q_complaints_list instead d_complaints​ Currently the search TransNode uses the default entity fetch. Switching it to q_complaints_list gives you control over sort order and allows future WHERE customisation. # Action Detail 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. Select your app. Click the Edit icon. 2 Select p_complaints → Page Data Model Click p_complaints in the tree. Open the Page Data Model panel (right-side tab). 3 Update the search TransNode Delete the existing transnode (search → list → detail) and create the same with q_complaints instead of d_complaints and verify bindings once more. 4 Save Click Save. F.2 — Verify VH Controls Render Correctly in Full Preview​ After the build is triggered by the trainer (required for VH Config changes), verify the following in Full Preview: # Action Detail 1 Click Show Full Preview Click Show Full Preview in the Page Builder toolbar. 2 Verify priority dropdown In the search filter bar, click the Priority field. It should render as a dropdown (ComboBox) showing: Low, Medium, High, . 3 Verify complaint_type dropdown Click the Complaint Type field in search. Should show: Product Issue, Billing Issue, Delivery Issue, Service Issue, General. 4 Verify customer_id picker Click a complaint row to load the details. In the detail form, click the customer_id (Employee ID) field. An F4 picker dialog should open listing all d_customers records with their names. 5 Verify responsible_team picker In the detail form, click the responsible_team field. The picker should show d_resp_team records (name + emp_id). 6 Test a selection Select a customer from the customer_id picker. Save the complaint. Verify the customer_id value is stored correctly (the KEY, not the display text) by checking the Data Browser. 💡 VH Type (F4 / ComboBox / AutoComplete) Override The Page Data Model assigns a default vhType to each property with a VH. You can override it per control in the Page Builder. To change vhType on a specific control: Click the control in the tree → Detail panel → find vhType property → change to F4, ComboBox, or AutoComplete. For customer_id and responsible_team: use F4 (full picker with search) since the lists may grow large. For priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint: ComboBox is ideal (small fixed list, no search needed). ✔ UI Wiring Checkpoint — Verify Before Session 4 Assignment search TransNode on p_complaints updated to q_complaints_list (Modelled Query). s_search section has 2 Saved Query quick-filters: 'My Complaints' and 'All Open'. Full Preview (post-build): priority dropdown shows Low/Medium/High/Critical. Full Preview: complaint_type dropdown shows 5 type options. Full Preview: customer_id field opens F4 picker with d_customers records. Full Preview: responsible_team field opens F4 picker with d_resp_team records. Full Preview: 'My Complaints' button filters list to current user's complaints.

Concept What It Does Naming / Config VH Config Static lists in metadata DB. Needs build after changes. For developer-managed fixed classifications. vhc_ prefix, CONFIG type VH Query Dynamic pickers from entity/query. Fetches live transactional data. For master data selection. vhq_ prefix, QUERY type Key Property The value stored in the entity when a VH item is selected. Internal ID. Set in VH Detail — Key Property field Display Text What the user sees in the dropdown. Human-readable label. Set in VH Detail — Display Text field Desc Format Controls how the selected value appears in the input field after selection. ':key--:display' pattern Is Restricted Enforces VH validation — only known keys accepted. No free-text bypass. Independent of DBMS. q_ prefix, Modelled Query type Saved Query Named pre-configured instance of a query. 📘 Session 5: BOL Logic & Validations With VH and Queries in place, Session 5 introduces server-side business logic via the Private Node TypeScript environment. Entity Lifecycle Hooks: onCreate, onValidate, onAfterSave, onDelete callbacks in the entity .ts file. Validations: Mandatory field checks, custom error messages, business rule enforcement (e.g. planned_resolution_date must be after created_on). Role-based logic: Using hasPermission() and hasCRUDPermission() to enforce who can transition complaint status. Setting default values: Auto-setting s_status = 'OPEN' on complaint creation, auto-populating created_by from $SYSTEM.userID. Query Rules: beforeQ/afterQ callbacks on the query file — role-based row filtering and post-fetch computed fields.

Naming Convention Summary​ Item Convention Example VH Config ID vhc_<name> vhc_priority VH Query ID vhq_<name> vhq_customer Modelled Query ID q_<name> q_my_complaints Saved Query ID sq_<name> sq_my_complaints Query parameter lowercase, descriptive current_user Desc Format :<key>--:<display> :customer_id--:customer_name Documentation Sources​ Topic Reference VH Types Overview VH User Guide — Section 1.1 Create VH Config BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.3 Create VH Config Create VH Query BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.3 Create Value Help (QUERY type) KloQuery / Modelled Query BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Sections 2.2.2, 3.0.2 Saved Queries Basic Training Guide — Section SAVED_QUERY KloInput VH Types kloControls 7.0 User Guide — Section 8.0 KloInput Jira — VH multiple dependents PROC-26625 (Enable Support for Multiple Dependent Properties in VH) Jira — VH Query display data PROC-26243 (Issue while displaying data of manual value help — Closed) API Help https://apihelp.procifynow.com/bol/index.html

By the end of this session, you will be able to: Set up the Private Node development environment and understand the TypeScript entity file structure. Understand the entity lifecycle and all hook methods: onAfterCreate, OnValidate, onDelete. Write and test server-side default value logic: auto-set s_status = OPEN and assigned_to = current user on complaint creation. Implement property-level Getter and Setter overrides to compute derived fields (actual_tat, full customer display). Write business rule validations in OnValidate: mandatory field checks, date constraints, role-based restriction. Implement query-level beforeQ / afterQ callbacks: enforce row-level, role-based visibility before a query runs, and reshape/compute values across the result set after it returns. Apply the landing page concept: prepare the p_complaints page to function as the application's primary home screen post-login. 📘 What This Session Builds On Sessions 1–4 built the data model, page structure, VH pickers, and queries — all through the low-code tools (Data Studio, Page Builder). Session 5 crosses the threshold into code: you will write TypeScript in the entity .ts file, running server-side in the Klobase Node.js runtime. The entity file is the ONLY place business logic belongs. Never write business rules in the controller file. Session 5 follows the core platform principle: Business logic → Entity file. UI orchestration → Controller file. Reference: PROC-23582 (Validation Logic to Be Maintained in Entity Callback onValidate Methods instead of Controller files). Part A — Setting Up the Private Node Environment​ Reference: Private Node setup Guide The Private Node is a local Node.js server running on your laptop that acts as the workspace server for your development session. Instead of your browser talking to the shared landscape server, it talks to your VS Code instance — giving you full debugging capability and instant iteration on server-side code. Pre-requisites​ Requirement How to verify VS Code installed Open VS Code — if it opens, you are good. Procify VSIX extension installed Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X) → search 'Procifynow'. If not installed, ask the trainer for the VSIX file. Network access to the landscape Open your landscape URL in a browser. If the login page loads, connectivity is confirmed. Node.js installed Open a terminal: node --version. You should see v22+. Setting the Private Node in VS Code​ 1 Create Your Workspace Folder Create a new folder on your laptop: Documents/PrivateNode/srm_<your_prid>. All application server-side files will be downloaded here. 2 Open the Folder in VS Code File > Open Folder > navigate to your new folder > click Open. 3 Open the Command Palette Press Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+P (Mac). 4 Run Procify Version Selection Type: Procifynow: Procify IDE Setup and press Enter. A WebView panel opens on the right. 5 Enter Your Landscape URL In the WebView, enter your app URL — e.g. https://dev.procify38.com/p6/srm_pr0045/index.html. Click Next. 6 Enter Developer Credentials Enter your developer username and password. Click Start Setup. 7 Wait for Initialisation The VS Code file explorer will populate with folders (entity stubs, controller stubs, kloconfig, etc.). A confirmation message appears when complete. 8 Checkout application The VS Code will open a webview to checkout the assigned apps. Select the created app and perform checkout A.2 — Entity File Location and Structure​ The entity .ts file for d_complaints is located in the Private Node workspace at the path: workspace/apps/<your_app_id>/d_complaints.ts If the file does not exist yet, the private node can generate it. The base structure looks like this: import { KloEntity, ValidationError, ErrorType } from 'klobase'; export class d_complaints extends KloEntity { // ── Getters & Setters ────────────────────────────────────────── // ── Lifecycle Hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────── public async onAfterCreate(): Promise<any> { // Called after a new complaint record is created } public async OnValidate(): Promise<any> { // Called during navigation if transnode setActiveIf = Valid } public async onDelete(): Promise<any> { // Called after the record is deleted } } 💡 Architecture Principle: Business Logic Belongs Here The entity file is the authoritative location for all business logic. Period. Controller file → UI orchestration only (navigation, formatter functions, show/hide decisions). Entity file → field defaults, cross-field computations, validations, role enforcement. Never duplicate validation logic in the controller. If the controller calls commitP(), OnValidate() fires automatically on the server — that is your safety net. Reference: kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide — Section 7.5 Best Practice Do's and Don'ts (Entity File). Part B — Entity Lifecycle Hooks​ B.1 — The Three Hook Methods​ Klobase provides three entity lifecycle hook methods that you override in the entity .ts file. These run on the server and are triggered automatically by the platform at the appropriate point in the entity's lifecycle. Method When Called Trigger Condition Primary Use onAfterCreate() After entity is created in DB On every new entity save Set defaults, auto-populate audit fields, initialise related records OnValidate() During navigation / on save / validateP function TransNode setActiveIf = 'Valid' Validate field values, enforce business rules, push errors onDelete() After entity is deleted On every delete operation Cascade cleanup, logging, send notifications 📘 OnValidate — Important Details OnValidate is triggered ONLY when the TransNode's 'setActiveIf' property is set to 'Valid' in the Page Builder. If setActiveIf is not set, OnValidate does NOT fire — the platform skips validation on navigation. Inside OnValidate, push errors using: this.errors.push(new ValidationError(this, propertyId, errorCode, message, ErrorType.ERROR)); The method must NOT return the errors array — it pushes to this.errors and the platform reads it. (PROC-24075 fixed this for proper return type.) ErrorType.ERROR blocks save. ErrorType.WARNING allows save but shows a warning toast. After your OnValidate runs, the platform ALSO runs its own mandatory-field validation based on key attributes — you don't need to repeat those. B.2 — Configuring TransNode setActiveIf for Validation​ Before OnValidate can fire, the TransNode that holds the complaint detail must be configured with setActiveIf = Valid in the Page Builder. # Action Detail / Code 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. Select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit icon. 2 Select the detail TransNode Click p_complaints in the tree. Open the Page Data Model panel. Click on the 'detail' TransNode row. 3 Set setActiveIf = Valid In the TransNode detail section (right side), find the 'setActiveIf' property. Change from the default (Always) to 'Valid'. This means: when the user tries to navigate away from the detail form, the platform will call OnValidate first. If errors exist, navigation is blocked. 4 Save Click Save. Part C — Entity Rules​ C.1 — What are Entity Rules?​ Rules contain business logic codes. It works with the event bus, any change in the entity will trigger the event, and all the rules hooked with the event will be executed sequentially. Rules are reusable objects across client, server and middleware. EX: When a complaint is created by an employee then status should be OPEN and assigned_to should be the same user. A responsible team/manager/assigned_to can be assigned by the manager only. An employee or manager can delete the complaint but not the responsible team Field Default Value Logic s_status 'OPEN' — every new complaint starts in OPEN status assigned_to this.txn.getUserID() — auto-set to the logged-in user who created the complaint created_on this.s_created_on — already auto-set by system field, no action needed created_by this.s_created_by — already auto-set by system field, no action needed C.2 — How to create an Entity Rule?​ Step 1: Go to the Rule tab and click on the add icon(+). Field Description Event type Select the event type. Based on the type of event you choose, the rule will be executed. Type Select the channel type, based on this the transaction will be performed. Exit ID is an ID you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Clazz This will be the rule file name. Invocation Method The method needs to be called. Step 2: Select the Event Type from the drop-down. The event type will mention when the rules will be executed. Event types: On Create ( rule will be executed on create of an entity) On Delete (rule will be executed on delete of an entity) On Update (rule will be executed on update of an entity) Rest of the types will be covered in future. Step 3: Select the channel type(there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule). Channel Type: Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on the client Endpoint / Device on Klarion server Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on server(current focus) Endpoint / Device to Server/ Client -Network Context Switch Legacy on Klarion server Klarion server to Klarion offline server Klarion server to Klarion Server Step 4: Fill in the value for Exit ID. Exit ID: It's an ID that you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Step 5: In the Clazz field provide the rule file name (example: rules/<file_name>) and in the invocation method provide an event name. You will be using that event to write your business logic codes. NOTE: If you are creating a Rule for the same entity you can fill this inside the Clazz field. Step 6: Click on the save button to save the newly created rule. C.3 — Implementing onCreateRule for default values​ As mentioned above, create a rule for onCreate with channel type as ALWAYS_ON_SERVER with class as this. Create Entity Folder and d_complaints.ts file | public async onCreateComplaint(oEvent:any): Promise<any> { // Auto-set status to OPEN on every new complaint let complaint = oEvent.getObject(); complaint.s_status = 'OPEN'; // Auto-set assigned_to to the creating user's login ID const currentUser = this.txn.getUserID(); complaint.assigned_to = currentUser; // Log for debugging (visible in Private Node terminal) this.info('Complaint created by:', currentUser, '| Status set to OPEN'); } | | :---- | 📘 this.txn — The Transaction Object (BOL API Reference) Inside entity hooks, oEvent.getTxn() gives you access to the KloTransaction object — the server-side context for the current request. oEvent.getTxn().getUserID() → returns the login ID of the user who triggered the save. Use for audit fields. oEvent.getTxn().getValueBag() → a key-value store local to the current transaction. Good for passing data between hooks. this.info(), this.warn(), this.error() → server-side logging methods. Output appears in the Private Node terminal and the Google Cloud logs. C.4 — Testing onCreate​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Typescript compilation Run tsc -w in one terminal 2 Save d_complaints.ts In VS Code, save the file. The Private Node auto-reloads — watch the terminal for 'server restarted' or similar message. 3 Create a new complaint in the UI Open the browser, navigate to p_complaints. Click the Add button in the section_toolbar of the detail area. The new record form opens. 4 Fill minimal fields and save Enter complaint_desc: 'Test Create logic'. Select priority = HIGH. Click Save (commitP from the Save button). 5 Verify in Data Browser Open Data Studio → d_complaints → Test → Data Browser. The latest record should show: s_status = OPEN, assigned_to = your login ID (e.g. PR0045). C.5 — Implementing onUpdate for assignee​ As mentioned above, create a rule for onUpdate with channel type as ALWAYS_ON_SERVER with class as this. Create Entity Folder and d_complaints.ts file if not available public async onUpdateComplaint (oEvent:any): Promise<any> { // Auto-set status to OPEN on every new complaint Let complaint = oEvent.getObject(); Const = previousState = await complaint.fromP() if((previousState.assigned_to != complaint.assigned_to)&& oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID != ‘EMPLOYEE_MANAGER’){ Throw Error (‘team assignment should be done by manager’)//Make “T” in to a //lowercase } } C.6 — Implementing onDelete for validation​ As mentioned above, create a rule for onUpdate with channel type as ALWAYS_ON_SERVER with class as this. Create Entity Folder and d_complaints.ts file if not available public async onDeleteComplaint (oEvent:any): Promise<any> { if(oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID == ‘IT_TEAM’){//Change ’ ’ to “ ”this Throw Error (‘it_team cannot delete complaint’)//Make “T” in to a lowercase } } Part D — Property Setters and Getters​ D.1 — What Are Setters and Getters?​ TypeScript property accessors let you intercept reads and writes of entity properties. In Klobase, setters and getters in the entity .ts file are the correct place for computed/derived field logic — not the controller. Pattern Purpose Setter (set propertyId) Called every time the property value changes. Use to: compute a derived field when an input changes, enforce value formatting, trigger side-effects. Getter (get propertyId) Called every time the property value is read. Use to: return a computed / formatted value instead of the raw stored value. ⚠ Critical Setter Pattern — Always Call this.s() Inside a setter, you MUST call this.s('propertyId', new_value, 'dataType', false, false) to actually persist the new value into the entity's internal state. Without this.s(), the new_value is accepted by TypeScript but never written to the entity data — the save will ignore your change. Pattern: if(new_value == this.propertyId) return; // guard to avoid infinite loop Then: this.s('propertyId', new_value, 'dataType', false, false); D.2 — Setter: Auto-Compute actual_tat When closed_on Changes​ When a complaint is closed (closed_on is set), actual_tat should be computed as: (closed_on - created_on) in days. public set closed_on(new_value: Date) { if (new_value == this.closed_on) return; this.s('closed_on', new_value, 'date', false, false); // Compute actual_tat when closed_on is set if (new_value && this.s_created_on) { const msPerDay = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24; const diffMs = new Date(new_value).getTime() - new Date(this.s_created_on).getTime(); this.actual_tat = parseFloat((diffMs / msPerDay).toFixed(1)); } } D.3 — Getter: Display complaint_id with Priority Badge​ A getter can return a formatted composite string. For example, a display_title getter that combines complaint_id and priority: // t_ prefix = transient property (not stored in DB) // Define t_display_title as a Transient property in the BOL Editor first public get t_display_title(): string { return `${this.complaint_id} [${this.priority || 'UNSET'}]`; } 📘 Transient Properties (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Entity Property Qualifier) Transient properties (t_ prefix) are computed at runtime and NOT stored in the database. They must still be defined as entity properties in the BOL Editor with qualifier = Transient. Once defined, they can be added to sections and controls in the Page Builder like any other property. The getter in the .ts file provides the value — the platform reads the getter whenever the control renders. Use transient properties for: display labels, formatted dates, computed totals, role-based display logic. Part E — Writing Business Rule Validations in OnValidate​ E.1 — Validation Rules for the Customer Complaints App​ Based on the BRD from Session 1, the following validations must be enforced when a complaint is saved: Rule ID Field(s) Condition Message V001 complaint_desc Empty or length < 10 chars Complaint description must be at least 10 characters. V002 priority Empty (null or blank) Priority is required. Please select Low / Medium / High / Critical. V003 planned_resolution_date Set AND is before today's date The planned resolution date cannot be in the past. V004 planned_resolution_date Set AND is before created_on The planned resolution date cannot be before the complaint creation date. V005 s_status Attempt to set CLOSED but role is Employee Employees cannot close a complaint. Only the manager can close. E.2 — Implementing OnValidate​ | public async OnValidate(): Promise<any> { // V001 — complaint_desc minimum length if (!this.complaint_desc || this.complaint_desc.trim().length < 10) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'complaint_desc', 'V001', 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } // V002 — priority is required if (!this.priority) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'priority', 'V002', 'Priority is required.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } // V003 — planned_resolution_date not in the past if (this.planned_resolution_date) { const today = new Date(); today.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0); if (new Date(this.planned_resolution_date) < today) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'planned_resolution_date', 'V003', 'Planned resolution date cannot be in the past.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } } // V004 — planned_resolution_date not before created_on if (this.planned_resolution_date && this.s_created_on) { if (new Date(this.planned_resolution_date) < new Date(this.s_created_on)) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'planned_resolution_date', 'V004', 'Planned resolution date cannot be before the complaint creation date.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } } } | | :---- | 📘 Role Rollup Values (Training Guide Beginner — Session 1 Part A) s_role_rollup is the numeric role hierarchy value assigned to application roles. Owner (Employee role) → s_role_rollup = 10 Supervisor (Manager role) → s_role_rollup = 20 Reviewer (ResponsibleTeam role) → s_role_rollup = 30 Lower number = higher priority. Manager (20) overrides Employee (10). You can also use this.txn.hasPermission('permission_id') for custom permission checks. See Permissions User Guide. E.4 — Testing OnValidate​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Save d_complaints.ts Save the file. Private Node restarts automatically. 2 Test V001 — short description In the UI, open a complaint detail. Clear the complaint_desc field or enter only 3 characters. Click Save. The platform should block navigation and highlight complaint_desc with the error message 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters'. 3 Test V002 — missing priority Clear the priority field. Click Save. Priority field should be highlighted with the V002 error message. 4 Test V003 — past date Set planned_resolution_date to yesterday. Click Save. Should show V003 error on the date field. 5 Test V005 — Employee closing complaint Log in as emp_<prid> (Employee role). Open a complaint. Change s_status to CLOSED. Try to Save. Should see V005 error. Log in as mgr_<prid> (Manager) — same operation should succeed. 6 Verify valid record saves Fill all required fields correctly with a future resolution date. Click Save. Record should commit without errors. Check Private Node terminal — no error logs. Part E — Query Rules E.1 — What are Query Rules? `Query rules are similar to Entity rules but are triggered before and after a query execution rather than around a create/update/delete. They are the correct place to answer two very different questions: Before the database is asked anything — “what should this user even be allowed to see?” (row-level filtering, defaulting search criteria). After the database has answered — “does the raw result need reshaping before it reaches the client?” (adding computed fields, merging data from a second query, masking sensitive values, sorting/aggregating in ways the query modeller can’t express. Both callbacks receive an EventContext (commonly named oEvent) and give access to the query instance itself via oEvent.getObject(). E.1 — How to Create Query Rules? Creating query rules is the same as creating entity rules, except the event type you subscribe to is one of: Event types: Before Query (beforeQ) — executes before the query is fired against the database. Anything set on the query object here becomes part of the WHERE condition. After Query (afterQ) — executes after results come back from the database, before they are returned to the client. The raw result set can be read and replaced here. Query Rule Event Reference (BOL API) Event.getObject() — returns the KloQueryForRule instance being executed. Set properties on it to add filter conditions (beforeQ), or call getResults() / setResults() on it to read/replace the raw result rows (afterQ). Event.getTxn() — returns the KloTransaction for the current user; use it to read $SYSTEM.roleID, call this.txn.get$User(), or check permissions. Event.getEventType() — returns which event fired, e.g. BEFORE_QUERY or AFTER_QUERY. Useful if one method is wired to handle both events. queryInstance.getResults() / setResults() — read or replace the raw JSON array of result rows in an afterQ callback. These are plain objects, not KloEntity instances — they cannot be saved back. E.3 — Implementing before Query on q_complaints​ As we already know from the BRD document complaints page behaviour will be different based on role. In case of employee only complaints raised by him should be visible In case of manager all the complaints should be visible In case of it_team only assigned tickets should be visible Create query folder and q_complaints.ts public async beforeQ(oEvent: EventContext) { let obj : any = oEvent.getObject(); let role = oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID; if(role === 'EMPLOYEE'){ obj.customer_id = (await this.txn.get$User()).login_id; obj.s_created_by = (await this.txn.get$User()).login_id; // Added for Business AI }else if( role == "IT_TEAM"){ obj.assigned_to = (await this.txn.get$User()).login_id; } if(obj.description) { obj.description = `%${obj.description}%`; } } E.3 — validate before query implementation​ Validate both the screen and data browser that data should be filtered based on role. E.4 — Testing beforeQ​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Save q_complaints.ts Private Node restarts automatically. 2 Test as Employee Log in as emp_<prid>. Open the complaints list screen. Only complaints where customer_id equals this employee’s login ID should appear, even though no filter was set from the UI. 3 Test as Manager Log in as mgr_<prid>. The full, unfiltered list should be visible — confirming the if block only narrows the query for EMPLOYEE and IT_TEAM roles. 4 Test as IT Team Log in as it_team_<prid>. Only complaints where assigned_to equals this user should appear. 5 Test in Data Browser Repeat the same three logins in the Data Browser (not just the app screen) against q_complaints. The same role-based filtering must hold — beforeQ applies at the query level, so it protects every entry point, not just one screen. Part E.1 — Implementing after Query on q_complaints​ Scenario​ The Manager’s complaint list needs a column showing how many days a complaint has been open — days_open — without storing it on the entity (it changes every day, so persisting it would immediately go stale). This is a textbook afterQ use case: compute it once, on the way out, from data already in the result set.​ Implementing afterQ​ public async afterQ(oEvent: EventContext) { let queryInstance = oEvent.getObject(); let results = await queryInstance.getResults(); let today = new Date(); let newResults = results.map((row: any) => { if (row.s_created_on) { let created = new Date(row.s_created_on); let diffMs = today.getTime() - created.getTime(); row.days_open = Math.floor(diffMs / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24)); } else { row.days_open = 0; } return row; }); queryInstance.setResults(newResults); } Wiring days_open into the UI​ Add days_open as a transient property (Session 5, Part D) on d_complaints so the Page Builder can bind a column to it, then add that column to s_complaints (Session 2, Part B.9.2). Because the value arrives already computed on the result row, no additional binding logic is needed on the client.​ Testing afterQ​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Save q_complaints.ts Confirm no errors in the Private Node terminal on restart. 2 Open the complaints list as Manager The new days_open column should show a whole number for every row. 3 Create a fresh complaint Its days_open should read 0 on the day it is created. 4 Cross-check one row against Data Browser Compare s_created_on for that record against today’s date manually — the displayed days_open should match. Part F — Preparing the Landing Page​ F.1 — What Is a Landing Page?​ The landing page is the first screen a user sees after logging into the application. In the Customer Complaints Application, p_complaints_dash will serve as the landing page — the list of complaints filtered by role will be immediately visible after login. There are two things needed to make p_complaints_dash the effective landing page: Create a dashboard screen. Configure it as landing page The screen we are going to create will be as mentioned below. F.1 — create dashboard screen?​ Dashboard also follows p_complaints page with limited changes # Action Detail / Code 1 Create dashboard page Navigate to the page builder screen and select customer_complaints application. And create a blank page. Fill id : p_complaint_dashboar 2 Create page layout Create page layout pl_desktop and mark screen type as default 3 Create page_area Create page area pa_dashborad and mark screen type as default 4 Create section Create section s_dashboard and mark screen type as card 5 Add title Add m.Text control and fill text : Status Wise Count 6 Add control 1 Add m.VBox control with properties alignitems : center 2. Add items aggregation 3. Expand and right click on items:<control-id> new → control → m.Text → text: New 4. Expand and right click on items:<control-id> new → control → m.Text → text: 0 7 Repeat steps Repeat step 6 for closed,onhold,escalated,inprocess,backlog,reopen 8 Create page data model Create search and list transnodes using q_complaints.ts Model the card with modeler as mentioned below After this you might have noticed the screen contains 0 rather than actual count for this controller is required which will be covered later and at that time we will update the dashboard as well. F.2 — configure landing page​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Navigate Navigate to Landing Page Settings and select the app from dropdown → click edit then add 2 Select page Select page from vh 3 roles Select roles for which dashboard should be visible 4 Tab Text Dashboard 5 Title Dashboard 8 Save sae F.1 — Verification​ Login with employee and check whether dashboard is available Repeat the same with manager and it_team as well

documents.t: Concept What It Does Where Implemented Private Node Local server instance. Routes browser endpoint's server calls to your VS Code for live debugging. Account Console → Endpoints → Node ID Entity .ts file TypeScript class that extends KloEntity. The ONLY place for business logic. workspace/apps/<app>/d_complaints.ts onAfterCreate() Server-side hook — fires after every new record is created. Used for auto-setting defaults. d_complaints.ts OnValidate() Server-side hook — fires on navigation when TransNode setActiveIf = Valid. Blocks save on error. d_complaints.ts + Page Builder TransNode onDelete() Server-side hook — fires after a record is deleted. Used for cascade cleanup. d_complaints.ts Setter (set property) Interceptor for property writes. Computes derived fields. Must call this.s() to persist. d_complaints.ts Getter (get property) Interceptor for property reads. Returns computed/formatted value. Used with transient properties. d_complaints.ts ValidationError Error object pushed to this.errors array. ErrorType.ERROR blocks. WARNING allows with message. OnValidate in d_complaints.ts this.txn KloTransaction — server context. Provides getUserID(), hasPermission(), hasCRUDPermisson(). Inside any entity hook or rule onPageModelReady Controller hook that fires before data is fetched. Best for applying default search filters. p_complaints.controller.ts beforeQ (Query Rule) Server-side hook — fires before a query hits the database. Used for row-level, role-based filtering. q_complaints.ts afterQ (Query Rule) Server-side hook — fires after results return from the database. Used to reshape/compute values across the result set via getResults()/setResults(). . q_complaints.ts Team Group (User Group) Bundle of users assigned in one action to an App Collection, instead of assigning users one at a time. Workspace Hub → User Groups

documents.t: ⚠ Complete ALL mandatory tasks before Session 6 Session 6 (Bindings, Navigation & Styling) builds the visual layer on top of the logic implemented today. All entity hooks must be working before styling is applied. Mandatory Tasks​ Perform all the tasks performed in session 05 # Action Detail / Code 1 Verify onAfterCreate Create a new complaint from the UI. In Data Browser, confirm: s_status = OPEN, assigned_to = your login ID. Private Node terminal shows the info log. 2 Verify V001 Try to save a complaint with complaint_desc = 'Short'. UI must show the V001 error on the complaint_desc field. Fix and save successfully with 10+ char descriptions. 3 Verify V002 Save a complaint without selecting priority. V002 error must appear. Select priority and save again — should succeed. 4 Verify V003/V004 Set planned_resolution_date to yesterday. V003 must fire. Set to tomorrow — should pass. Set to a date before today's session — V004 must fire if it's before created_on. 5 Verify V005 Log in as emp_<prid>. Try to change s_status to CLOSED and save. V005 error must appear. Log in as mgr_<prid>, make the same change — it must succeed. 6 Verify closed_on setter Log in as mgr_<prid>. Set s_status to CLOSED and set closed_on to today. After saving, check actual_tat in Data Browser — should be the computed number of days since complaint creation. 7 Verify landing page default filter Log in as emp_<prid>. On page load, the list should automatically show only that user's complaints (sq_my_complaints applied). Log in as mgr_<prid> — list should show all OPEN complaints (sq_all_open applied). 8 Verify beforeQ row-level filtering Repeat the role-based checks from E.4: Employee sees only their own complaints, IT Team sees only assigned ones, Manager sees everything. 9 Verify afterQ computed field Confirm days_open renders correctly for at least one old and one newly-created complaint. Exploration Task (Optional — Bonus)​ Add a V006 validation: if is_escalated = true and responsible_team is empty, block save with message: 'Escalated complaints must have a responsible team assigned.' Implement onDelete hook: log a message 'Complaint deleted: {complaint_id} by {user}' and push an entry into d_complaint_voices as an audit trail before deletion.

📘 Session 6: Bindings, Navigation & Styling With business logic in place, Session 6 focuses on the presentation layer — making the application look and navigate well. Bindings: Connecting controls to properties and formula expressions (binding a label text to computed values). Navigation: Implementing the complaint_id navigation link — clicking a complaint ID in the list loads the detail screen for that specific complaint. Styling: Applying predefined style classes (status badge colours — OPEN=blue, INPROCESS=orange, etc.) and custom CSS classes to sections and controls. By end of Session 6, the application will look and feel production-ready at the complaint list and detail level.

Entity Hook Summary​ Hook / Method Signature Called When onAfterCreate async onAfterCreate(): Promise<any> After new entity record created in DB OnValidate async OnValidate(): Promise<any> On navigation if TransNode setActiveIf = Valid onDelete async onDelete(): Promise<any> After entity record deleted set property set propId(new_value: Type) When property value is changed (client or server) get property get propId(): Type When property value is read (returns computed value) Documentation Sources​ Topic Reference Entity hooks (onAfterCreate, OnValidate, onDelete) BOL API Reference — KloEntity class Setter & Getter pattern kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide — Section 7.5 (Entity File Do's) ValidationError / ErrorType BOL API Reference — ValidationError class this.txn (KloTransaction) BOL API Reference — KloTransaction — getUserID(), hasPermission(), hasCRUDPermission() Private Node Setup Endpoint Redirection to Private Node User Guide TransNode setActiveIf kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide — Section 9.1 SetActive onPageModelReady (controller) UI Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 14.1 Hook Methods Jira — OnValidate return type fix PROC-24075 (Fix OnValidate() Function to Return ValidationError[] Instead of Undefined) — Tested Jira — Validation in entity files PROC-23582 (Validation Logic to Be Maintained in Entity Callback onValidate Methods) API Help https://apihelp.procifynow.com/bol/index.html Topics covered in Session 5 Entity-level callback methods: OnCreate, OnValidate, OnAfterSave. Writing TypeScript logic in entity files via private node. Applying mandatory field validations. Role-based logic and permission checks.

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand and apply all four binding modes in Klobase: Value, Path, Parts (with formatter), and Expression. Write expression bindings for visibility, enabled state, and dynamic text. Write and wire formatter functions in the controller. Implement all navigation scenarios using navTo: section nav, page nav, key-based nav, query-param nav. Apply pre-defined and user-defined style classes to controls, sections, page areas, and layouts. Part A — Data Bindings In Depth​ Every control on a Klobase screen reads and writes data through the Transaction Model ($M). The model is a JSON model object. All bindings use the prefix $M to reference it. Without a binding, a control shows a static value or nothing at all — it is disconnected from the live data. A.1 — The $M Model Path Structure​ The Transaction Model is organized as a tree. Each TransNode in the Page Data Model corresponds to a branch in the $M tree. The full path to any property follows this pattern: {$M>/transNodeRelationId/propertyId} For a list TransNode with relationId = list, the first row's complaint_desc is: {\$M\>/list/0/complaint\_desc} For the detail TransNode with relationId = detail: {\$M\>/detail/complaint\_desc} The leading / after > is mandatory. Omitting it causes a silent bind failure. A.2 — The Four Binding Modes​ Mode When to Use Syntax / Where to Set Example Value Static, hardcoded value — no model connection. Control always shows this literal text regardless of data. Properties tab → Value field text = 'Complaint ID' — always shows that label. Path Bind to exactly ONE model property. Two-way binding by default: changes in UI write back to model. Properties tab → DSRC field {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} — shows and edits the complaint description. Parts Combine MULTIPLE paths into one display value via a formatter function. Always one-way (read only). Properties tab → dsrc field (add each path as a part) + Formatter Function field Parts: {$M>/detail/first_name} + {$M>/detail/last_name} → formatter returns full name string. Expression Inline calculated value. No formatter function needed. Supports ternary operators and comparisons. Always one-way. Properties tab → dsrc field (starts with {= ...}) {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? 'Escalated' : 'Normal'} ⚠ Path and Parts are mutually exclusive on the same property — you cannot use both at once. If you need multiple values combined, always use Parts. A.3 — Path Binding: Step-by-Step​ Path binding wires one control property to one model property. This is the most common binding type for form fields. # Action Detail 1 Select the control in the tree Example: select the complaint_desc m.Input control inside s_complaint_details section. 2 Open Properties tab Detail panel (right side) → Properties tab. 4 Enter the binding in dsrc Type: {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} — the detail TransNode relationId followed by the property ID. 5 Save and verify in Full Preview The field loads with the active complaint's description. Edit it and save — the new value persists in the database. 📘 The TransNode relationId is set in the Page Data Model, not the entity name. If your detail TransNode's relationId is complaints_detail, the path is {$M>/complaints_detail/complaint_desc}. A.4 — Parts Binding with Formatter Function​ Use Parts when you need to combine or transform multiple model values into a single display string. Parts binding is one-way only — it cannot write back to the model. Value:​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path:​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind. Parts:​ In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding. (Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value) Formatter Functions​ Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field. Type:​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options:​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint:​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Example: displaying TAT status as a composite string from actual_tat and standard_tat. // Controller function — formatTAT public formatTAT(actual: number, standard: number): string { if (!actual || !standard) return '—'; const diff = actual - standard; if (diff <= 0) return `✅ On Time (${actual} days)`; return `⚠ Overdue by ${diff} day(s) — Actual: ${actual}, SLA: ${standard}`; } ⚠ The formatter function receives Part values in the exact order they appear in the Parts list. If you add actual_tat first and standard_tat second, the function signature must be formatTAT(actual, standard). Part B — Expression Bindings​ Expression binding lets you write a JavaScript ternary expression directly inside a binding path string. It starts with {= and ends with }. It is evaluated live at runtime whenever the bound model values change. B.1 — Syntax Rules​ Rule Detail Starts with {= The expression must begin with {= (curly brace, equals). Without the =, it is treated as a plain path, not an expression. Reference model paths with ${} Inside an expression, wrap every $M path in ${}: ${$M>/detail/s_status}. This dereferences the path to its current value. Must return a value The expression must evaluate to a value matching the property type. visible expects boolean. text expects string. enabled expects boolean. Ternary only for simple cases Use condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. Complex multi-branch logic belongs in a formatter function, not in expression binding. No function calls You cannot call controller functions from expression binding. Use Parts + formatter for that. B.2 — Expression Binding Examples (Customer Complaints App)​ Use Case Property Expression Explanation Show Save/Cancel only in EDIT or CREATE mode visible {= ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'EDIT' Make Edit button invisible in EDIT mode visible {= ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'DISPLAY' ? true : false} Edit button should disappear the moment the user clicks it and mode switches to EDIT. Show escalation badge only when escalated visible {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? true : false} is_escalated is a Boolean property. Bind to the is_escalated path directly. Dynamic text: 'Escalated' vs empty text {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? 'ESCALATED' : ''} Shows ESCALATED label text conditionally. Returns empty string otherwise. Disable complaint_desc when not OPEN enabled {= ${$M>/detail/s_status} === 'OPEN' ? true : false} The complaint description should only be editable when the complaint is in OPEN status. Dynamic placeholder label for priority text {= ${$M>/detail/priority} === 'VERY_HIGH' ? '🚨 Critical' : ${$M>/detail/priority}} Shows emoji label for critical priority, falls back to raw value for others. TAT warning color class {= ${$M>/detail/actual_tat} > ${$M>/detail/standard_tat} ? 'tat-overdue' : 'tat-ok'} Applies different CSS class depending on whether actual exceeds standard TAT. ⚠ Expression binding is evaluated once per model change event. For heavy computation (e.g. comparing arrays or doing date math), use a formatter function instead — expression binding performance degrades with complex logic. Part C — Formatter Functions​ A formatter function is a TypeScript method in the controller file that takes one or more raw model values as input and returns a formatted display value. It is the right tool whenever expression binding would become too long, needs multi-step logic, or needs to look up external data. C.1 — Where Formatter Functions Live​ Formatter functions are public methods on the controller class. They must be public — the framework calls them reflectively from the Page Builder binding. export class p_complaints extends KloController { // Formatter functions — called from Parts binding in Page Builder public formatPriority(priority: string): string { const map: Record<string,string> = { 'LOW': '🟢 Low', 'MEDIUM': '🟡 Medium', 'HIGH': '🔴 High', 'VERY_HIGH': '🚨 Very High' }; return map[priority] || priority || '—'; } } C.2 — Formatter Function Examples for the Complaints App​ Function Name Input Parts Return Example Output formatPriority(priority) {$M>/detail/priority} string 🔴 High formatTAT(actual, standard) {$M>/detail/actual_tat}, {$M>/detail/standard_tat} string ⚠ Overdue by 3 day(s) formatStatusLabel(status) {$M>/detail/s_status} string 🟠 IN PROCESS formatFullName(first, last) {$M>/detail/created_by_first}, {$M>/detail/created_by_last} string John Doe formatEscalationText(isEsc, type) {$M>/detail/is_escalated}, {$M>/detail/complaint_type} string ESCALATED — BILLING formatDateAge(createdOn) {$M>/detail/created_on} string 3 days ago C.3 — Wiring a Formatter Function: Complete Steps​ # Action Detail 1 Write the function in controller.ts Open the controller file in Online Code Editor. Add a public method with the formatter logic. Ensure it takes the exact number of parameters as the number of Parts you will add. 2 Select the target control Page Builder → select the control whose display property you want to format (e.g. m.Text for priority display). 3 Delete existing Path binding If a Path binding exists on the property, clear it first — Parts and Path cannot coexist. 4 Switch to Parts Properties tab → click Parts radio button. 5 Add each Part in order Click + for each model path. Order matters: Part 1 = first function argument, Part 2 = second argument, etc. 6 Set Formatter Function field Type the exact function name as it appears in the controller. No parentheses, no 'this.' prefix. 7 Private Node must be running Formatter function calls go to the running Private Node. Start your Private Node before testing. Without it, the binding silently returns undefined. 8 Save and Full Preview The control should now render formatted output. Open Chrome DevTools Sources to debug if the output is wrong. ⚠ Formatter functions must be PURE — they should not modify model state, call APIs, or have side effects. They are called repeatedly on every model refresh. Side effects cause unpredictable behavior and performance issues. Part D — Navigation In Depth​ Navigation in Klobase is handled exclusively through the navTo() controller API. All legacy navigation methods (navToS, navToByEvent, navToScreenByKeyScreen) are deprecated — always use navTo. It is defined on KloController and is available in every page controller via this.navTo(). D.1 — navTo Parameter Reference​ Parameter Type Purpose Example SS string Navigate to a section (PageArea or Section) WITHIN the same page. Used for list-to-detail navigation on the same screen. SS: 'pa_complaint_details' S string Navigate to a DIFFERENT page by page ID. S: 'p_customers' D string Navigate to a page AND set a specific record as active by its primary key. Format: entity@@key@@suffix. D: 'd_complaints@@CMP-00012@@F' QP object Navigate to a page AND apply a query parameter filter on the target page's search TransNode. QP: { complaint_type: 'BILLING' } F string Navigate to a specific flavor (application variant). F: 'flavor_prod' Mode string Set the page mode on the target page when navigating. Values: DISPLAY, EDIT, CREATE. Mode: 'CREATE' AppData object Pass arbitrary data to the target page. Read from controller using this.getAppData(). AppData: { source: 'dashboard' } D.2 — Navigation Scenarios with Code​ Scenario 1 — List row click navigates to detail section on the same page: // Press event on ticket_id m.Link control: await this.navTo({ SS: 'pa_complaint_details' }, oEvent); // oEvent is required for SS nav — it carries the row index for setActive Scenario 2 — Navigate to a different page: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_customers' }); Scenario 3 — Navigate to a different page AND a specific section within it: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_customers', SS: 'pa_customer_details' }, oEvent); Scenario 4 — Navigate to a page and load a specific record by key (requires navbykey on target TransNode): const key = this.tm.getTN('list').getProperty(`${idx}/complaint_id`); await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', SS: 'pa_complaint_details', D: `d_complaints@@${key}@@F` }); // Target page's detail TransNode must have navbykey: {"sourcePath": "list"} Scenario 5 — Navigate and pre-filter with query parameters (requires navbyquery on target TransNode): const type = this.tm.getTN('detail').getProperty('complaint_type'); await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', SS: 'pa_complaints', QP: { complaint_type: type } }); // Target page's search TransNode must have navbyquery: {"sourcePath": "search"} Scenario 6 — Navigate to Create mode on a different page: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', Mode: 'CREATE' }); D.3 — navbykey and navbyquery Configuration​ Config Field Where to Set Value Format When Required navbykey Target page's detail/list TransNode → Properties → navbykey field {"sourcePath": "list"} — the list TransNode relationId of the TARGET page Required when using D: parameter in navTo. It tells the target page which TransNode to activate. navbyquery Target page's search TransNode → Properties → navbyquery field {"sourcePath": "search"} — the search TransNode relationId of the TARGET page Required when using QP: parameter in navTo. It tells the target page to filter using the passed query params. Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts​ The Style Classes tab in the Page Builder is the single place to control all visual formatting. It has two modes: QuickAdd (pre-built bundles) and Manual (full control). Different QuickAdd bundles are available depending on what is selected in the tree: a Section, a PageArea/PageLayout, or a Control. E.1 — QuickAdd for Sections​ QuickAdd Style Applied On What It Does When to Use Card Sections (form/detail type) Adds a white background, rounded corners, drop shadow, and inner padding. Renders the section as a card floating above the page. Detail form sections (s_detail_header, s_complaint_details). Makes key information stand out. Grid Sections (grid type) Adds alternating row colors, column borders, header background, and hover highlight. Improves readability for dense tabular data. List sections (s_complaints). Always apply Grid QuickAdd to any grid-type section. Transparent Sections Removes background and border. Content sits directly on the page background. Dashboard tile sections where background should show through. E.2 — QuickAdd for Controls​ QuickAdd Style Applied On What It Does Font Size (S/M/L/XL) m.Text, m.Label, m.Input Applies a pre-defined font size class. Use L for emphasis, S for secondary information in grid cells. Text Colour Any text control Applies a branded color from the platform color palette. Includes: primary (blue), success (green), warning (orange), danger (red). Bold m.Text, m.Label Applies font-weight: bold. Use for headers, primary identifiers (complaint_id), and totals. Italic m.Text Applies font-style: italic. Use for secondary metadata (timestamps, remarks). Background Color Any control Applies a background highlight. Useful for dashboard tiles and key metrics. Color Combination Any control Pre-defined foreground + background pairs ensuring WCAG contrast compliance. Safer than picking colors individually. E.3 — Format Rules (Conditional Styling)​ Format Rules apply a style class conditionally based on the control's current value. This is how status badge colors work. Configure via Style Classes tab → Category + Style Class + Format Rule + Format Value. Field What It Does Example Category What CSS property the rule affects: Background, Text, or Icon. Background Style Class The CSS class name to apply when the condition is true. status-open Format Rule The condition type: Text Contains, Text Equals, Text Starts With, etc. Text Contains Format Value The value of the control's text must match for the class to apply. OPEN Full Row When checked, the style applies to the entire grid row instead of just the cell. Checked for critical priority rows that need full-row coloring. Status badge rules for the complaints app — apply to s_status control in both s_complaints grid and s_detail_header: Status Value Category Style Class Format Rule Format Value OPEN Background status-open Text Contains OPEN REOPEN Background status-reopen Text Contains REOPEN INPROCESS Background status-inprocess Text Contains INPROCESS ON_HOLD Background status-onhold Text Contains ON_HOLD RESOLVED Background status-resolved Text Contains RESOLVED CLOSED Background status-completed Text Contains CLOSED E.4 — User-Defined CSS Classes​ When QuickAdd and Format Rules are not sufficient, create custom CSS classes in the Settings Editor. # Action Detail 1 category Select category as user defined 2 Style class Provide your own style class 3 Add css file Maintain css file in css folder 4 Load file in controller FileLoaderUtils.loadCSSFile(this.getFlavor(), this.getFlavorVersion(), "myStyleSheet"); "myStyleSheet" this is the style sheet has been created CSS Usage — Do's & Don'ts​ ✓ Do​ Recommendation ✓ ✓ Use Style Classes first. Use Category + Style Class + Format Rule (Quick Add ) before creating a custom CSS file(user defined). ✓ ✓ Scope custom CSS to the flavor. Wrap CSS rules in .procify__<app_id> { ... }, using the flavor name without the version. ✓ ✓ Load CSS in onpageInit(). Use FileLoaderUtils.loadCSSFile(this.getFlavor(), this.getFlavorVersion(), "myStyleSheet");. ✓ ✓ Use SAPUI5/OpenUI5 classes. Target classes such as .sapMIBar, .sapUiTableRow, .sapMTB, and .KloTabContainerHeaderToolbar. ✓ ✓ Test across supported platforms. Verify custom CSS on APK, IPA, Safari, and Chrome before releasing it. ✓ ✓ Use :has() for whole-grid-cell styling. Add a User Defined class to the control and use td:has(.yourClassName) { ... } when the entire cell must be styled. ✓ ✓ Check layout configuration first. For height, spacing, or positioning issues, check screenType options such as fit_to_area, hsplitter, vsplitter, and grid_layout before overriding CSS. ✓ ✓ Order Format Rules carefully. Place general rules first and more-specific rules later when values can overlap. ✗ Don’t​ Avoid ✗ ✗ Don’t use unsupported Format Rule types. Only Always, Text Contains, and Formula are supported. ✗ ✗ Don’t use overlapping Text Contains values without checking the order. For example, OPEN also matches REOPEN. ✗ ✗ Don’t expect CSS to inherit between flavors. A child flavor must load its own stylesheet. ✗ ✗ Don’t assume embedded screens inherit CSS. Each screen must load the CSS it requires. ✗ ✗ Don’t modify Shared flavor CSS without checking the current access policy. Confirm with the platform team before making changes. ✗ ✗ Don’t use Style Class alone to color an entire grid cell. It styles the control inside the cell, not the <td>. ✗ ✗ Don’t leave the Style Class field empty. An empty Style Class prevents the style from being applied. ✗ ✗ Don’t hardcode custom class names in multiple places. Once loaded, the class is available under Category: User Defined in the Style Class UI. Reuse that class instead. F — Implement binding in application​ As you might have already seen that we already used bindings to attach data to control. G — Implement styling​ As you can see the customer complaints showed and the one we are developing functionality might be looking the same at this point but ui is looking different which is due to styling difference. Let's implement styling. G.1 — list screen​ Add formatting to complaint_id to change it to bold. Add font color to s_status based on value Add font and background color for status in detail header Style all the form sections in pa_comp_details. Concepts Recap — What You Learned in Session 6​ Concept What It Does Config Location $M path binding Binds a control to a TransNode property value. Properties tab → Path field: {$M>/detail/prop} Expression binding Inline ternary for conditional visible/enabled. Path field: {= condition ? true : false} navTo (Events tab / press event) Navigates to a section or page on control interaction. Events tab → press → NavTo function Layout type = header Pins s_detail_header at top of pa_complaint_details. Detail panel → type = header Layout type = section Sets pa_comp_details as scrollable body area. Detail panel → type = section saveTransaction Controller function. Saves dirty data, triggers OnValidate, resets to DISPLAY. press event inline function refreshTransnode Controller function. Reverts unsaved changes, resets mode to DISPLAY. press event inline function Status Group badge Format Rule Text Contains using group-level IDs: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED. Style Classes tab → Format Rule Quick Add style Pre-defined style bundle for Grid or Card sections. Style Classes tab → QuickAdd

Mandatory Tasks​ Practice all the steps performed in the session Navigate to a screen using QP to filter the data of the target Use Expression Binding and Formatter functions.
