Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Configure Vienable for all four dimensions: Screen Size, Page Mode, Role Rollup, and Status Group. Understand and correctly use all five controller page lifecycle hooks. Use the full TransNode and TransModel controller API set. Implement client-side validation using expression binding and OnValidate controller integration. Apply Procify coding standards for controller and entity files.

Vienable (Visible + Enable) is the declarative system for controlling control visibility and editability across four independent dimensions. The final result for any control is the intersection of all configured dimensions: a control is visible only if ALL applicable dimension rules say it should be visible. A.1 — The Four Vienable Dimensions​ Dimension What It Controls Values Configuration Location Page Size Visibility/enable by device screen resolution. Evaluated based on the PARENT section's resolved size. S (phone), M (tablet), L (desktop), XL (wide desktop) Vienable Dashboard → Page Size columns: S, M, L, XL Page Mode Visibility/enable by current screen interaction mode. Default mode is DISPLAY. Display, Edit, Create, Review Vienable Dashboard → Page Mode columns Role Visibility/enable by the logged-in user's s_role_rollup value. Config must be maintained in BOL Editor → Object Type tab. Owner (10), Supervisor (20), Reviewer (30), Overlooker (40). In this app: EMPLOYEE=10, EMPLOYEE_MANAGER=20, IT_TEAM=30 Vienable Dashboard → Role column Status Group Visibility/enable by the bound entity's current s_status_group value. Config must be maintained in BOL Editor → Status tab. The Status Groups you defined in Session 3. In this app: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED Vienable Dashboard → Status Group column ⚠ Entity must be set to TRUE for the control row in the Vienable Dashboard. If Entity = false, Role and Status Group dimensions are ignored — the control will always be visible/enabled regardless of role or status. A.2 — Screen Size Vienable (Responsive Layout)​ Screen size Vienable controls which columns/fields appear on small vs large screens. This is how the platform supports mobile without a separate build. Page Size Approx. Viewport Recommended for Complaints App S Up to ~600px (phone) Show only: ticket_id (link), priority, s_status. Hide: complaint_desc, customer_id, dates, responsible_team. M 601–1024px (tablet) Show: ticket_id, priority, s_status, complaint_type. Still hide verbose date columns. L 1025–1440px (desktop) Show all columns. Standard desktop experience. XL Above 1440px (wide desktop) Same as L. Use for additional panel layout or expanded detail. Steps to configure phone layout for s_complaints grid: # Action Detail 1 Open Vienable Dashboard Page Builder → p_complaints page → Vienable tab → Vienable Dashboard sub-tab. 2 Set Entity = true for each grid column control Find complaint_desc, customer_id, first_response_date, responsible_team in the Control ID column. Toggle Entity to true. 3 Set S column = Hidden for verbose columns For each verbose column: click the S (phone) cell → set to Hidden (🚫 icon). 4 Keep S = Visible for essential columns ticket_id, priority, s_status: ensure S is set to Visible (👁 icon). 5 Test with Preview In → Phone Toolbar → Preview In → Phone. Grid should show only the essential 3 columns. 6 Verify desktop unaffected Preview In → Desktop. All columns must still show. A.3 — Page Mode Vienable​ Control Display Mode Edit Mode Create Mode Rationale Edit button Visible Hidden Hidden Edit disappears when clicked (mode switches to EDIT). Save button Hidden Visible Visible Only meaningful when there is something to save. Cancel button Hidden Visible Visible Only meaningful when there is something to discard. Delete button Visible Hidden Hidden Deletion is a display-mode action (select then delete). complaint_desc input Show As Label Depends on Role Editable Read-only in display, role-controlled in edit. responsible_team input Show As Label Depends on Role Editable for MANAGER only Only manager assigns team. A.4 — Role Rollup Vienable​ Role-based Vienable uses the s_role_rollup value of the logged-in user. This value is set in BOL Editor → Object Type tab → role configuration table (KloTuner config). The mapping for this is: Application Role Procify Role s_role_rollup Vienable Role ID Employee Owner 10 EMPLOYEE Manager Supervisor 20 EMPLOYEE_MANAGER Responsible Team Reviewer 30 IT_TEAM Role-based Vienable rules for p_complaints — key controls: Control EMPLOYEE EMPLOYEE_MANAGER IT_TEAM Delete button (toolbar) Hidden Visible (OPEN group only) Hidden responsible_team field (EDIT) Show As Label Editable Show As Label complaint_desc field (EDIT) Editable (OPEN group only) Show As Label Show As Label assigned_to field (EDIT) Show As Label Editable Show As Label remark field (EDIT) Hidden Editable Editable A.5 — Status Group Vienable​ Status Group maps a set of s_status values to a group name. The configuration is in BOL Editor → Status tab. Vienable evaluates the group of the entity's CURRENT s_status to decide visibility. Status Group Name Statuses It Covers Typical Vienable Use OPEN OPEN, REOPEN Edit button visible. complaint_desc editable for EMPLOYEE. INPROCESS INPROCESS, ON_HOLD Edit button visible. Assign team button available for MANAGER. ACCEPTED RESOLVED Edit button hidden — complaint resolved, no edits allowed. COMPLETED CLOSED Edit button hidden — complaint closed. Only the Reopen button is shown. ⚠ Status Group Vienable requires Entity = true on the control row AND the entity's Status tab must have the groups configured in BOL Editor. Missing group config causes the status group column to be ignored — the control remains visible regardless of status. A.6 — Apply vienability for application.​ s_complaint_details should not be editable in display mode Desc and priority should be editable for OPEN/REOPEN status only For closed complaints nothing should be editable. s_timeline_details Time line details should be editable in edit mode only. Timeline details should be editable by manager only. Actual tat should not be editable at any time. s_assigment_details Assignment details should be editable in both edit and create mode Assignment details should be editable by manager only S_admin_details Admin details should not be editable S_complaints_list should not be editable in display mode s_voices_list should not be editable in display mode S_attachment_list should not be editable in display mode

documents.t: The Klobase framework calls lifecycle hook methods on your controller class at specific points in the page's life. Understanding WHEN each fires is essential — using the wrong hook causes bugs that are hard to trace because they appear intermittently depending on navigation order. B.1 — Hook Execution Order​ On first page load: onPageInit → onPageModelReady → onPageEnter On forward navigation back to same page: onPageEnter (only) On backward navigation away from page: onPageExit (source page), onPageEnter (target page) On back-navigation that destroys the page: onPageExit → onPageDestroy B.2 — Lifecycle Hook Reference​ Hook When It Fires Model Data Available? Primary Use Cases Common Mistakes onPageInit Once, when controller class loads. UI, model, and TransNodes do NOT exist yet. No Rare: one-time non-model setup like subscribing to a global service. Trying to access this.tm or TransNodes — they are null at this point. onPageModelReady Once (per page lifecycle), after TransNodes are initialized but BEFORE data is fetched. No (TransNodes exist but have no data) Call this.tm.getTN('search').skipModelPreparation() to skip auto-query execution and manually control data load. Reading TransNode data — getData() returns null or empty. The fetch hasn't happened yet. onPageEnter Every time the page becomes visible — forward nav, backward nav, and initial load. Yes Dashboard count calculations. Resetting UI state. Refreshing summaries. Setting default filter values. Putting logic that should only run ONCE here — it re-runs on every navigation. Use _initialized flag for one-time logic. onPageExit When the user navigates AWAY to a different page. Yes Auto-save draft, log exit event, clear unsaved state. Not called for within-page section navigation (SS). Only fires on cross-page navigation. onPageDestroy Once, when the page is removed from memory (back-nav that exits the page history). Partially Unsubscribe event listeners. Release resources. Not needed for most standard screens. Using it as a reliable 'save on exit' hook — the page may be destroyed without user navigation (memory pressure, app backgrounding). B.3 — onPageEnter: The Most Important Hook​ onPageEnter is the page lifecycle hook. It fires with data already loaded, on every navigation — making it perfect for dashboard counts, summaries, and state resets. This event will be called whenever the screen enters the visible area by means of navigation (Both front and back navigation). public async onPageEnter(): Promise<void> { // ── 1. One-time initialization guard ────────────────────────────────── if (!this._initialized) { this.\_initialized \= true; // Logic that must run only ONCE goes here } // ── 2. Dashboard count computation (server-side aggregate) ──────────── // "status_count_query" = a query-type transnode configured with: // SELECT s_status, COUNT(k_ticket_id) AS count_of_status // FROM <entity> WHERE <same filters as before> GROUP BY s_status const countQueryTN = this.tm.getTN('status_count_query').getData(); const aggregateResult = await countQueryTN.executeP(); const rows = aggregateResult; const counts: Record<string, number> = { OPEN: 0, REOPEN: 0, INPROCESS: 0, ON\_HOLD: 0, RESOLVED: 0, CLOSED: 0 }; rows.forEach((row: any) => { const st \= row.s\_status || ''; const c \= Number(row.count\_of\_status) || 0; if (counts.hasOwnProperty(st)) counts\[st\] \= c; }); // Build the derived object once, then set it on a dedicated // "other"-type transnode used purely for binding — no full row payload involved. const statusCount = { t\_open\_count: counts.OPEN \+ counts.REOPEN, t\_inprocess\_count: counts.INPROCESS \+ counts.ON\_HOLD, t\_resolved\_count: counts.RESOLVED, t\_closed\_count: counts.CLOSED }; await this.tm.getTN('status_count').setData(statusCount); }

documents.t: C.1 — TransModel APIs (this.tm.*)​ API Signature Returns Description getTN() this.tm.getTN(relationId: string) TransNode Get a TransNode by its relationId (as configured in Page Data Model). The gateway to all TransNode operations. commitP() this.tm.commitP(success, failure, validate, isDisplayMode) Promise<any> Save all dirty objects in the Transaction Model to the database. validate=true triggers OnValidate. isDisplayMode=true resets to DISPLAY after save. rollBackTxn() this.tm.rollBackTxn() Promise<void> Revert ALL unsaved changes across all TransNodes back to last commit state. Used by Cancel button. getAllTransNodes() this.tm.getAllTransNodes() TransNode[] Get all TransNodes on the page. Useful for bulk operations. getTransactionFromTransnodeData() this.tm.getTransactionFromTransnodeData(tn) any Get the raw transaction object from a TransNode. Advanced use only. C.2 — TransNode APIs (this.tm.getTN('id').*)​ API Signature Returns Description & Example getData() .getData() KloEntitySet / KloEntity / KloQuery Get all data from the TransNode. For list TransNodes returns the full entity set. Call .toArray() on the result to iterate. data = this.tm.getTN('list').getData(); getActiveData() .getActiveData() KloEntity Get only the currently active (selected/highlighted) entity. data = this.tm.getTN('detail').getActiveData(); getProperty() .getProperty(path: string) any Get a single property value from the TransNode model. For list rows: getProperty('0/complaint_id') — index/propertyId format. For detail: getProperty('complaint_desc'). setProperty() .setProperty(path, value) TransNode Set a property value — triggers immediate UI re-render. For transient/display properties. setProperty('t_open_count', '5'). setData() .setData(val, index?) Promise<void> Set the entire dataset for a TransNode. Replaces current data. Used after manual data fetch. this.tm.getTN('list').setData(entitySet); setActive() .setActive(index) Promise<bool> Set the active row by index. Triggers onArrive and updates all child TransNodes. await this.tm.getTN('list').setActive(0); getActiveIndex() .getActiveIndex() number Get the current active row index. Useful before navigating away. idx = this.tm.getTN('list').getActiveIndex(); getSelectedEntities() .getSelectedEntities(ssID?) KloEntity[] Get all checked rows in a grid section (multi-select). selected = this.tm.getTN('list').getSelectedEntities(); executeP() .executeP() Promise<void> Re-execute the query associated with a query-type TransNode. Use to refresh data without full page reload. await this.tm.getTN('search').executeP(); applySortP() .applySortP(property, order) Promise<void> Sort the TransNode data by a property. order: 'ASCENDING' or 'DESCENDING'. await this.tm.getTN('list').applySortP('created_on', 'DESCENDING'); createEntityP() .createEntityP(json, successMsg, errorMsg) Promise<KloEntity> Create a new entity and add to the TransNode. Triggers onAfterCreate hook server-side. await this.tm.getTN('list').createEntityP({complaint_desc: 'test'}, 'Created', 'Failed'); C.3 — Controller Navigation & UI APIs​ API Signature Description navTo() await this.navTo(params, oEvent?) Navigate to section or page. See Part D of Session 6 for full parameter reference. setMode() this.setMode('EDIT' 'DISPLAY' saveTransaction() this.saveTransaction(successMsg, errorMsg, validate, resetMode) Commit dirty data, optionally trigger OnValidate, and optionally reset to DISPLAY. Standard Save button handler. refreshTransnode() this.refreshTransnode(nodeId, mode, discard) Refresh a named TransNode, set its mode, and optionally discard unsaved changes. Standard Cancel button handler. showBusy() this.showBusy(msg?, id?) Show the platform busy/loading indicator. Use during async operations. this.showBusy('Loading...'); hideBusy() this.hideBusy(id?) Hide the busy indicator. Always call in a finally block to ensure it's dismissed even on error. getAppData() this.getAppData() Retrieve AppData passed from the source page's navTo call. Returns the object passed as AppData: {...}. getPathFromEvent() this.getPathFromEvent(oEvent) Get the model path string from a press event. Use with getTN().getProperty(path.split('/')[2] + '/propertyId') to get a specific row value.

documents.t: Client-side validation in Klobase operates at two levels: (1) field-level required constraints using the 'required' property, and (2) full-form OnValidate triggered by commitP or saveTransaction. Both are enforced in the browser before any network call is made. D.1 — Required Field Validation​ Mark a control as required by adding the 'required' property and setting it to true. The platform renders a red asterisk and prevents submission if the field is empty. # Action Detail 1 Select the input control Page Builder → select the mandatory field control, e.g. complaint_desc m.Input. 2 Add 'required' property Properties tab → Add → required → set Value to true. 3 Test in Full Preview (CREATE mode) Click New → leave complaint_desc empty → click Save. Platform shows required validation error and blocks save. D.2 — OnValidate (Server-Side Validation Triggered from Client)​ OnValidate runs in the entity file (.ts) on the Private Node when saveTransaction is called with validate=true. The client sends the dirty object to the server; the server validates and returns errors if any rule fails. The client then displays these errors as message dialogs. // In d_complaints.ts entity file — OnValidate hook public async OnValidate(oEvent: IKloEvent): Promise<void> { const entity = oEvent.getEntity(); const errors: string[] = []; // V001: Description must be at least 20 characters if (!entity.complaint_desc || entity.complaint_desc.length < 20) { errors.push('V001: Complaint description must be at least 20 characters.'); } // V002: Priority is mandatory if (!entity.priority) { errors.push('V002: Priority is mandatory.'); } // V003: Cannot close without a remark if (entity.s_status === 'CLOSED' && !entity.remark) { errors.push('V003: Remark is required when closing a complaint.'); } if (errors.length > 0) { oEvent.setError(errors.join('\\n')); } } For OnValidate to fire from the UI, the detail TransNode's setActiveIf must be set to 'Valid' in the Page Data Model. Without this, saveTransaction with validate=true does nothing. # Action Detail 1 Set setActiveIf on detail TransNode Page Data Model → click detail TransNode → setActiveIf dropdown → select Valid. 2 Call saveTransaction with validate=true Edit button press: this.setMode('EDIT'). Save button press: this.saveTransaction('Saved.', 'Save failed.', true, true). 3 Test validation Leave complaint_desc with fewer than 20 characters → Save → OnValidate fires → error message dialog shows V001 text. 4 Fix and retry Enter a valid description → Save → passes validation → data persists → mode resets to DISPLAY.

These standards are non-negotiable on all Procify projects. Violations result in code review rejection and technical debt. The principles come from kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide §7.4 and §7.5. E.1 — Controller File Standards​ Rule Do Don't Reason Scope Write ONLY UI logic in the controller: formatters, navigation, show/hide, model reads for display. Write business logic (status transitions, validations, default-setting) in the controller. Business logic in the controller bypasses server validation and breaks when the screen is accessed via API. TypeScript typing Declare every variable with its type: const count: number = 0; const msg: string = ''; Use implicit any: let x = someValue; or omit types on function parameters. Untyped code hides bugs at compile time that surface as runtime errors in production. Variable declaration Declare variables only when necessary. Prefer const over let. Declare variables at file scope (class properties) when a local variable suffices. File-scope variables persist across page navigations and cause state leakage between sessions. Nested functions Keep functions flat. Extract complex logic to named private methods. Nest arrow functions inside controller methods: onClick(() => { const x = () => {...}; }) Nested functions are not testable, not readable, and difficult to debug. Async/await Use async/await for all TransNode API calls. Mark the function async. Use .then().catch() promise chains. Consistent await pattern is required by the framework for proper error propagation. Deprecated APIs Always use navTo(), tm.commitP(), this.setMode(). Use navToS(), navToByEvent(), getTN('x').commitP() Deprecated APIs are removed in future versions. Using them creates upgrade risk. Model mutation Only modify model properties via setProperty() for transient display values. Directly mutate entity properties from the controller (entity.some_prop = value). Direct mutations bypass the dirty-tracking mechanism and do not persist on save. E.2 — Entity File Standards​ Rule Do Don't Scope Write ONLY business logic in entity files: onCreate defaults, onUpdate role checks, onDelete restrictions, beforeQ filtering, OnValidate. Write navigation or UI state changes in entity files. Setter functions Use setter override pattern to automatically derive related values when a property changes. Compute derived values in the controller on button press — this is bypassed when data changes via API. Validation location All mandatory field checks and business rule violations go in OnValidate. Throw errors in onAfterCreate — onAfterCreate is called AFTER the record is saved; errors there cause data inconsistency. Error handling Always wrap async BOL API calls (createEntityP, LoadEntityByKeyP) in try/catch and log errors. Let unhandled promise rejections propagate silently. Role checks in rules Use oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID to get the runtime role and enforce role-specific logic. Hardcode user IDs or email addresses for role checks. E.3 — Naming Conventions​ Item Convention Example Pages p_ prefix + snake_case description p_complaints, p_complaint_dashboard Page Areas pa_ prefix pa_complaint_details, pa_complaints Sections s_ prefix s_complaints, s_detail_header Entities d_ prefix d_complaints, d_complaint_item Queries q_ prefix q_complaints, q_customers Transient properties t_ prefix t_open_count, t_selected_count Controller functions (formatters) format + PascalCase formatPriority, formatTAT, formatStatusLabel Controller functions (event handlers) on + PascalCase + action onEditPress, onSavePress, onDeleteConfirm Variables in TypeScript camelCase + explicit type const openCount: number = 0; Boolean variables is/has prefix isEscalated, hasAttachment, isLoading ⚠ Private Node must be running whenever you test controller functions, formatter functions, or OnValidate. Without the Private Node, server-side hooks are bypassed and the client shows incorrect results. Always verify Private Node status in the Dev Tools toolbar before testing.

Concept What It Does Where Controller TypeScript UI orchestration only: formatters, model reads/writes for display, dashboard counts. workspace/apps/<app>/p_complaints.controller.ts TransNode setProperty() Updates a model property — triggers UI re-render immediately. Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: # Objective 1 Create the application menu using the Menu Editor — matching the BRD menu structure exactly. 2 Configure the HomePage Editor to add screen tiles for all three personas. 3 Understand the App Status Lifecycle: ACTIVE → RELEASED → DEPRECATED, and when to transition. 4 Create an App Branch from an RELEASED version and understand the branch-to-version merge workflow. 5 Run Validate & Publish — identify and fix blockers before triggering a Full Build. 6 Transport the published application from DEV to QA using the Transport tool. 7 Perform an end-to-end smoke test covering all three personas (Employee, Manager, IT Team). ⚠ Important Pre-requisite Check — Trainer will verify ALL of these before Session 8 begins. ✔ p_complaints page is fully built: search, list, detail with all tabs populated. ✔ Status badges (OPEN/INPROCESS/etc.) are rendered with correct colours. ✔ Vienable is configured: Edit/Save/Cancel button visibility by Role, Mode, and Status Group. ✔ Dashboard (p_complaint_dashboard) is set as Landing Page for all three roles. ✔ formatPriority formatter renders priority with emoji labels. ✔ OnValidate blocks V001–V005 violations correctly. ✔ All three test users (emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, it_<prid>) can log in and see the application. If any item above is incomplete, resolve it BEFORE starting Session 8. 📘 Reference / Tip BRD Quick Reference for Session 8 (from Session 1 Part A) Menu structure: ONE item — 'Complaints' → p_complaints Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Roles: ALL Pages defined in BRD: p_home_page (home screen tiles) and p_complaints (main screen). p_complaint_dashboard = Landing Page (Session 5) — auto-loads on login. Does NOT need a menu entry. App ID format: customer_complaints_<your_prid> e.g. customer_complaints_pr0045
documents.s: Session 8 — Menu Configuration & App Management, Versioning & Publishing

documents.t: A.1 — What Is the Menu Editor?​ The Menu Editor (also called Menu Builder per PROC-26419) is the tool you use to define the navigation structure visible to users in the hamburger menu of the application at runtime. Without a menu entry, users cannot navigate between screens — they would need to know URLs manually. Access path: Running app → Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Menu Editor. A.2 — Menu Fields Reference​ Field Description Rules / Notes Menu ID Unique identifier for this menu item. ONLY alphanumeric + underscores. NO hyphens ( - ). NO spaces. Case-sensitive. Wrong: mn-complaints. Correct: mn_complaints. Target Page Page ID the menu item navigates to. Use the Value Help (VH) icon to pick from existing pages. Do NOT type the page ID manually. Menu Text Label shown to the user in the hamburger menu. Keep it short. Title case. Localisation supported. Page Parameters Optional JSON for navTo params (SS, QP, D, Mode). Leave blank for simple page nav. Not needed for the Complaints entry. Menu Icon SAP icon URI displayed alongside the text. Format: sap-icon://<icon-name>. Must be a valid SAP UI5 icon name. Example: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts. Sequence Sort order in the menu. Lower number = appears first. Use multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30) to leave room for future items. Roles Restrict visibility to specific application roles. Leave BLANK = visible to ALL roles. Fill role IDs (comma-separated) to restrict. Test Navigation Validates the menu item navigates correctly. Always click Test Navigation before saving — catches target page errors early. A.3 — BRD Menu Structure to Implement​ Menu Field Value Menu ID mn_complaints Target Page p_complaints (select from VH) Menu Text Complaints Menu Icon sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence 10 Roles Leave blank — visible to ALL roles (Employee, Manager, IT Team) Page Parameters Not required — leave blank A.4 — Step-by-Step: Creating the Application Menu​ 1 Open Menu Editor In the running application, open the hamburger menu (☰ top-left). Go to Dev Tools → Menu Editor. 2 Select the Application In the App dropdown at the top of the Menu Editor, select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏). The menu table becomes editable. 3 Add a Header Group Click Add (+) → Add Header. Fill in: Menu ID: hdr_main Menu Text: Main Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. (A Header groups child items visually in the menu.) 4 Add the Complaints Child Menu Item Select the hdr_main row in the table. Click Add (+) → Add Child. Fill in: Menu ID: mn_complaints Target Page: p_complaints (use VH picker) Menu Text: Complaints Menu Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. 5 Test the Navigation Click Test Navigation on the mn_complaints row. p_complaints should open correctly. If a 'Page not found' error appears — check that the Target Page is exactly p_complaints (no typos). 6 Save Click the Save button (disk icon 💾). Wait for the busy dialog to close. A success toast confirms the menu is saved. 7 Verify with All Personas Log out and log in separately as emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, and it_<prid>. In each session, open the hamburger menu. The 'Complaints' item must be visible and navigate to p_complaints for ALL three test users. ⚠ Important Common Menu Editor Mistakes Hyphen in Menu ID: mn-complaints causes the item to save but NEVER appear in the app. Always use underscore: mn_complaints. Typing Target Page manually: Always use the VH picker. Manual typos cause silent navigation failures. Saving without testing: Always click 'Test Navigation' before saving. It catches missing pages early. Role restriction accident: If the menu item is set to a specific role, other personas cannot see it. Leave Roles blank for all-role visibility.

B.1 — What Is the HomePage Editor?​ The HomePage Editor configures which screen tiles appear on the application's built-in Home grid — accessible via the Home (🏠) icon. This is separate from the Landing Page (p_complaint_dashboard configured in Session 5). The Landing Page loads automatically on login. The Home grid gives users tile-based navigation to frequently used screens. 📘 Reference / Tip Three 'home' concepts — don't confuse them Landing Page (Session 5): Configured via Landing Page Settings. Auto-loads after login. Shows p_complaint_dashboard. HomePage Editor: Tile grid shown when user clicks the Home (🏠) icon. Configure p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard tiles here. p_home_page (BRD): A screen defined in the BRD. Can be built as an additional home screen — not required for this session's delivery. B.2 — HomePage Editor Fields Reference​ Field Description HomePageID Unique ID for this tile. Convention: hp_<screen_short_name>. Screen The Page ID this tile navigates to. Use VH to select. Position Where the tile appears on the home grid. Use 'Body' for standard tiles. Sequence Order of the tile. Lower = appears first. Role Restrict tile visibility to specific roles. Leave blank = all roles. B.3 — Step-by-Step: Adding Tiles to HomePage Editor​ 1 Open HomePage Editor Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → HomePage Editor. Select customer_complaints_<prid> from the App dropdown. Click the Edit icon (✏). 2 Add the Dashboard Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_dashboard Screen: p_complaint_dashboard (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 5 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save (do NOT navigate away yet). 3 Add the Complaints Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_all_complaints Screen: p_complaints (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 10 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save. 4 Save All Click the Save icon (💾) in the toolbar. Wait for busy dialog to close. Success toast confirms. 5 Verify Log out. Log in as emp_<prid>. Click the Home (🏠) icon. Two tiles must appear: 'Dashboard' and 'Complaints'. Click each tile — verify it navigates to the correct screen. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>.

C.1 — App Status Values​ Every version of an application on the Procify platform has a Status that controls what operations are allowed on it. Understanding these statuses is essential before releasing or transporting. Status Meaning Can Develop? Can Transport? Can Create New Version? ACTIVE Current working version. All development happens here. ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No RELEASED Development complete and locked. Ready for transport. ❌ No ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (create from RELEASED) DEPRECATED Retired. Superseded by a newer version. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No DISCARDED Abandoned branch/version. Excluded from main path. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No ⚠ Important Critical Versioning Rules — memorise these before proceeding A NEW VERSION can only be created from a RELEASED version. A BRANCH can only be created from an ACTIVE version. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Merge the branch into a new version first, then transport. Once status is changed to RELEASED, no further development is possible on that version. Always build (Validate & Publish) BEFORE changing status to RELEASED. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Releasing the Application​ 1 Navigate to Account Console (also called Workspace Hub) Open the hamburger menu → Sys Admin → Account Console (or Workspace Hub). Alternatively: Hamburger menu → My Apps (if visible in your role). 2 Find Your Application In the Apps list, search for customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the App ID to open the application detail screen. 3 Open Edit Mode Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏) in the toolbar. The Status field becomes editable. 4 Change Status to RELEASED In the Status dropdown, select RELEASED. Read the confirmation message carefully — this action locks all development on this version. Click Save. The app status changes to RELEASED. The Edit icon in Data Studio and Page Builder will now be disabled for this version. 5 Verify In the App detail, the Status badge shows RELEASED. Open Data Studio → select customer_complaints_<prid> → click the Edit icon. You should see a message that the app is locked for editing.
documents.s: Part C — App Status Lifecycle & Versioning

documents.t: D.1 — Why Branch?​ A Branch creates a parallel ACTIVE copy of your application. Use it when you need to work on next-phase enhancements while the current version is being tested in QA. The branch is fully isolated — changes in the branch don't affect the main RELEASED version until you explicitly merge them. Scenario Use Branch? Bug fix on the current version in QA ❌ No — fix directly in main, create new minor version New feature development while current is in QA ✅ Yes — branch from current ACTIVE version Experimental UI changes for client review ✅ Yes — branch lets you show without committing to main D.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Branch​ 1 Go to Account Console → My Apps Locate customer_complaints_<prid>. The app must be in ACTIVE status to create a branch. 2 Click Branch In the app detail view, click the Branch button (visible only when status = ACTIVE). The platform creates a new Branch Flavor automatically. The branch version appears in the My Apps list with a branch indicator. 3 Assign Users to the Branch Click the branch version to open its detail. Go to the Roles & Users tab → click Edit. Assign ALL three test users and your developer account to their respective roles. ⚠ Users are NOT copied automatically from the parent — you must assign them manually in the branch. 4 Develop in the Branch Open Data Studio or Page Builder. In the App dropdown, select the BRANCH version (not the main version). Make your changes. Save and test independently. D.3 — Branch Merge Workflow (Summary)​ When the branch is ready to be merged back into the main release cycle: 1 Export Both ZIPs Account Console → Export section. Download ZIP of the main RELEASED version (Set 1) and the branch version (Set 2). 2 Open App Compare & Merge Account Console → App Compare & Merge. Upload Set 1 (main) as Left and Set 2 (branch) as Right. Click Compare. 3 Review the Differences The tool lists differences per component: entities, pages, queries, VH, menus, etc. For each difference, select which version to keep: Set 1 (main), Set 2 (branch), or a Custom combination. 4 Download Merged ZIP Once all decisions are made, click Download to export the merged ZIP. 5 Create New Version and Import In Account Console, create a new Major or Minor version from the current RELEASED main version. Import the merged ZIP into the new version. Run Update Schema, Full Build, and test before releasing. 📘 Reference / Tip Reference: App Branching & Merging User Guide — App_Branching___Merging-User_Guide.docx PROC-26419 note: 'Account Console' may be renamed 'Workspace Hub' in platform help content. Both names refer to the same tool.
documents.s: Part D — App Branching and Merging

documents.t: E.1 — Validate vs. Publish — What's the Difference?​ Action What It Does When to Use Validate Scans the application for errors WITHOUT building. Safe — nothing changes in the running app. Run first, every time. Fix all errors before triggering Publish. Publish Validates first, then builds the app if no blocking errors exist. Updates the running app. After Validate passes with 0 errors. Use Full Build for first publish or after VH Config changes. E.2 — Common Publish Blockers​ Blocker Cause Fix VH Config not visible in UI after Publish VH Config changes require a Full Build. Always select 'Full Build' for the first publish or after adding/editing VH Configs. TypeScript compilation error Syntax error in entity .ts or controller .ts file. Open VS Code → check terminal for tsc errors → fix, save, re-validate. Update Schema not run Entity properties added but schema not updated in DB. Data Studio → select entity → Update Schema → confirm success toast. Another build IN-QUEUE A previous build is already running. Click 'Proceed' to queue behind the current build. Do NOT cancel it. Missing app_util flavor Validate and Publish menu not visible. Ask trainer — app_util must be assigned to your developer account. E.3 — Step-by-Step: Validate and Publish​ 1 Open Validate and Publish Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Validate and Publish. (If this menu item is missing, app_util flavor is not assigned to your account. Ask the trainer.) 2 Enter the Application In the App field, type customer_complaints_<prid> and press Enter. The application version details load. 3 Run Validate First Select Action: Validate. Click Submit. Wait for the validation report to generate. Download the XLSX report if errors are listed. Fix every ERROR before proceeding. Warnings can be reviewed but do not block the build. 4 Fix All Errors For each error in the report: - Missing Update Schema → Data Studio → Update Schema on the entity. - TypeScript error → VS Code → fix tsc error → save → re-validate. - Missing VH Build → select Full Build in the next step. Re-run Validate until the report shows 0 errors. 5 Run Publish Select Action: Publish. Build Type: Full Build (required for first publish and after any VH Config changes). Click Submit. The Publish Log shows the progression: IN-QUEUE → IN-PROCESS → PUBLISHED Do NOT navigate away while the build is running. 6 Verify the Published App Log out completely. Log back in. Open the hamburger menu → confirm 'Complaints' item is visible. Navigate to p_complaints → confirm live data loads. Verify: status badges render, VH dropdowns populate, all tabs in detail section work. 📘 Reference / Tip Publish Logs reference: Publish_Logs_Screen.docx — explains each status stage and error codes. Validate & Publish reference: Publish_or_Validate_Screen-7_0_App_utility__.docx

F.1 — How Transport Works​ Transport is a PULL mechanism: the TARGET system (QA) asks the SOURCE system (DEV) for the latest published version. You perform ALL transport steps while logged into the QA environment, not DEV. Stage What Happens Setup Transport creates entries in QA metadata tables for the application, groups, and flavors. Download Application ZIPs are pulled from DEV and extracted in the QA server's file system. Update Schema Database tables for all entities are created or altered in the QA database. Finalising Application is set to ACTIVE in QA so users can log in and access it. ⚠ Important Transport Pre-requisites — verify ALL before starting 1. The application must be in RELEASED status on the DEV system. 2. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Create a new version, merge, then transport. 3. The QA server's config.json must have mm_klo_online_server pointing to the DEV landscape URL. 4. A host file entry for the DEV system must exist on the QA server. 5. The transport_1 app must be assigned to the developer account on the QA system. If any pre-requisite is missing, the transport will fail at Setup or Download stage. Ask the trainer to verify the QA environment config before proceeding. F.2 — Step-by-Step: Transporting to QA​ 1 Log in to the QA System Open the QA environment URL in a browser (trainer provides the URL). Log in with your developer credentials. ⚠ ALL remaining steps are done on QA, not on DEV. 2 Navigate to App Transport Hamburger menu (☰) → Sys Admin → App Transport. The App Transport screen lists all available applications from the connected DEV system. 3 Find Your Application In the list, locate customer_complaints_<prid>. If not visible, toggle the 'Show All' button to see all available apps (not just those with pending updates). 4 Click the App Row Click on customer_complaints_<prid>. A detail panel opens showing available versions from DEV and any already-installed versions in QA. 5 Install As Writable Click the available version update. A dialog appears with two options: As Readable — locked, cannot edit in QA. As Writable — editable, allows continued development in QA. Click 'As Writable' (recommended for training so you can fix issues in QA if needed). 6 Accept Conditions and Proceed A mandatory conditions dialog appears. For each mandatory item (⚠ icon), tick the acceptance checkbox. If prompted about shared flavor movement (on QA/PROD systems), click Proceed. Click Proceed to start the transport. 7 Monitor Transport Stages The screen shows progress through: Setup → Download → Update Schema → Finalising. Wait for each stage to complete. The overall status changes to ACTIVE when done. 8 Assign Users in QA After transport, the app is ACTIVE in QA but has NO users assigned. Go to Account Console → My Apps → customer_complaints_<prid>. Go to Roles & Users tab → assign: emp_<prid> → Employee role mgr_<prid> → Manager role it_<prid> → ResponsibleTeam role Your developer account → Manager role 9 Verify in QA Log out of the QA developer session. Log in as emp_<prid> in QA. Verify: hamburger menu shows 'Complaints', p_complaints loads, all VH dropdowns work. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>. 📘 Reference / Tip Transport User Guide: Transport-_User_Guide.docx The Transport tool supports DEV → QA, QA → PROD, and DEV → DEV movement. Script Master (second tab in Transport screen) shows automated scripts maintained for the system — ask trainer if any scripts need to be run after transport.
documents.s: Part F — Transport: DEV to QA

documents.t: This smoke test must be completed AFTER publish. It verifies every major feature built across all 8 sessions works correctly in the published application. Run it on DEV first, then repeat on QA after transport. # Persona Action Expected Result 1 EMPLOYEE (emp_<prid>) Login → Menu → Complaints. Click Add (with Object Type = PROCIFY). Fill complaint_desc (10+ chars), priority = HIGH, select customer from picker. Click Save. complaint_id = P-000XX auto-generated. s_status = OPEN. assigned_to = emp_<prid>. Record appears in list. 2 EMPLOYEE Open the new complaint → Edit → Clear complaint_desc → Save. V001 error blocks save: 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters'. 3 EMPLOYEE Edit → priority dropdown. ComboBox shows Low / Medium / High / Critical (from vhc_priority). 4 EMPLOYEE Edit → customer_id field. F4 picker opens showing d_customers records. 5 MANAGER (mgr_<prid>) Login → open the OPEN complaint → Edit → set responsible_team from picker → Save. responsible_team field is editable for Manager. Record saves. Status remains OPEN. 6 IT TEAM (it_<prid>) Login → open assigned complaint → Edit → s_status = INPROCESS → Save. Status badge changes to INPROCESS (orange colour). Edit button remains visible. 7 EMPLOYEE Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → try s_status = CLOSED → Save. V005 error: 'Employees cannot close a complaint'. 8 MANAGER Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → s_status = CLOSED → closed_on = today → Save. Status badge changes to CLOSED (grey). Edit button disappears (COMPLETED Vienable). actual_tat computed in Data Browser. 9 ALL ROLES Navigate to Home (🏠). Two tiles visible: Dashboard and Complaints. Each tile navigates correctly. 10 ALL ROLES Preview In → Phone (Page Builder). Grid in s_complaints shows only 3 columns (ticket_id, priority, s_status) on phone view.

Concept What It Does Where to Configure Menu Editor (Menu Builder) Defines hamburger menu structure. Roles blank = all users. NO hyphens in Menu ID. Dev Tools → Menu Editor → select app → Edit Header + Child Item Header groups child menu items visually. Children point to actual screens. Menu Editor → Add → Add Header, then Add → Add Child sap-icon:// SAP UI5 icon URI format used in menu and controls. Menu Editor → Menu Icon field HomePage Editor Adds tiles to the Home (🏠) grid. Separate from Landing Page. Dev Tools → HomePage Editor Landing Page Settings Sets auto-load screen after login. Configured in Session 5. Dev Tools → Landing Page Settings App Status: RELEASED Locks development. Enables transport. New version must be created from RELEASED. Account Console → My Apps → Status field Branch Parallel ACTIVE copy for next-phase development. Not transportable directly. Account Console → My Apps → Branch button (ACTIVE only) App Compare & Merge Compares two ZIP exports; per-component merge decisions; produces merged ZIP. Account Console → App Compare & Merge Validate Checks for errors. Safe — nothing deployed. Download XLSX report. Dev Tools → Validate and Publish → Action: Validate Publish (Full Build) Validates then builds. VH Config changes REQUIRE Full Build. Dev Tools → Validate and Publish → Action: Publish → Full Build Transport (Pull) QA pulls RELEASED app from DEV. Requires config, host, transport_1 app. QA system → Sys Admin → App Transport

🎓 This Is the Final Session of the Beginner Training Track The Customer Complaints Application is now a fully published, transportable product. All three personas (Employee, Manager, IT Team) have correct access, menu, and data visibility. After this assignment you will have built and shipped a complete enterprise application from scratch. Mandatory Tasks​ # Task Verify By 1 Configure the Menu Editor with hdr_main header and mn_complaints child item pointing to p_complaints with icon sap-icon://customer-and-contacts. All 3 test users see 'Complaints' in hamburger menu after login. 2 Add HomePage tiles: hp_dashboard (Sequence 5) and hp_all_complaints (Sequence 10) for all roles. Home (🏠) icon shows both tiles and each navigates correctly. 3 Run Validate → fix ALL errors → re-run until 0 errors. Validation report shows 0 errors. 4 Publish (Full Build) → wait for PUBLISHED status. Logout and login — app loads correctly with all features working. 5 Change app status to RELEASED in Account Console. Status badge shows RELEASED. Edit icon is disabled. 6 Create a Branch from the ACTIVE version (if instructed). Assign all 3 test users to the branch. Branch appears in My Apps list. Users can login to branch version. 7 Transport to QA (trainer-guided). Assign users in QA. App is ACTIVE in QA. All test users can login. p_complaints loads end-to-end. 8 Run the full 10-step smoke test above on DEV and on QA. All 10 smoke test checks pass on both environments. documents.t: "Initial sync" refers to the process of syncing data from the server to the client. When a user registers, all their relevant data is transferred from the server and stored in the client’s local database, enabling the application to function offline. The term "DeviceRegisterCall" refers to the registration process of a user in a system and after this assigned flavors can be fetched for the user. ST here, stands for Start Time, which indicates the starting timestamp of an activity/process. ET here stands for End Time, which indicates the ending timestamp of an activity/process. Here, ST and ET is stored to track how much time an activity is taking to complete. noofqueries: The total number of SQL queries that has been executed during the initialSync process of a particular flavor. noofsqlrecords: The total number of data/ records that have already been fetched after executing the queries. Eg:In this case;(shown in above screenshot) 55 SQL queries were executed. A total of 1324 records data were retrieved. "queryids" typically refers to unique identifiers associated with individual SQL queries or database queries that are executed by a system. Each queryid helps track, identify, or differentiate between specific queries that are run, making it easier to debug, analyze performance, or monitor system behavior. This contains the ids of all the initial sync queries in that particular application. “ROTdownload” stands for root download. It contains the list of applications’ zips that have been downloaded. “table generator” for storing above data in the client side tables corresponding table are required. In clientGlobalObj._log is generating table logs on the client side in opfs/ sqlite db/ etc. “Before Login”, track user input, validation, and any checks made before the user is authenticated. “After Login”, track session creation, successful login, and post-login actions. “TT” often refers to Total Time. This is the amount of time it takes to complete a particular activity or query in a system. Note:Similar for every flavor as shown in the below screenshots there are activity log details of ET,noofqueries,noofsqlrecords,STATUS,Queryids,ST,and TT.

documents.t: For the app setup, any failures during the setup process (including config updates) will be displayed in the about page. Icons are used to indicate the setup status: a green icon represents success, while a red icon indicates failure.This approach provides a user-friendly and informative method for handling only the InitialSync setup issues. Clicking on the red icon opens a popup that shows any associated error messages. From the popup, users can download the logs in a .txt file format by clicking the Download Log button, or they can reinstall the app by selecting the Reinstall button. The "Download Log" option typically refers to the ability to download a record or history of events or actions taken within a specific application or system. This log file might contain useful information such as: System actions or operations performed Errors or warnings encountered timestamps The purpose of downloading the log is usually for record-keeping for understanding the system's performance. The format of the log file can be downloaded in txt format using the download log button present in the popup.

documents.t: Date of Issue: January 2023 Target Audience: Application Developers.

The below methods are for developers. All methods take two parameters, the first parameter is the definition of the callback method and the second parameter is the context of the class where that callback method is defined. Eg: clientGlobalObj.attachShowError(this._fnShowErrorPage,this); Here fnShowErrorPage is the method definition you want to attach to an attachShowError method and this is class context or class ‘this’ where fnShowErrorPage is defined attachShowError( errFn , context ) Attach your error page to what you want to display in the UI when any error comes. Framework will internally call this method when any error comes. attachLoadComponent(loadComponentFn,context) Attach your component method using this function. Components can be seam4 components or any other SAP component. By default, the framework uses the kloTouch component to load after registration. attachOfflinePageLockMethod(offlinePageLockFn,context) Attach your offline lock method which will be called during offline login by the framework. attachForgetPasswordOffline(offlineForgetPasswordFn,context) Attach your offline forget password UI method by calling the upper method which will be internally called by the framework to display the offline forget password page. clientGlobalObj.htmlBanner.showHTMLUpgradeBanner(actionButtonEventHandler,targetContainerId,message?:string,actionButtonText?,timeLimitInMinutes?:number, timerLimitInTimestamp?) Attach your html banner on the top level of the page by calling the upper method. 5.1. Parameters - actionButtonEventHandler (mandatory) - A reference to the function that will be called when the user clicks on the action button present in the banner or after the specified time passes. targetContainerId (mandatory) - This will take the html container id. To use the banner similar to the upgrade banner, provide “html_banner_container” as the value. Message (optional)- This will take the message to be displayed in the banner. By default it takes the hardcoded Upgrade message. actionButtonText (optional)- This will take the text to be displayed in the action button. By default it takes hardcoded text ”Upgrade Now”. timeLimitInMinutes (optional)- This will take the time for which the banner will be displayed. Value must be in minutes, once the time limit is expired/once the user is clicking on the action button, the actionButtonEventHandler will be called automatically. By default, it is set to 3 minutes. timerLimitInTimestamp (optional)- This is the same as the above time limit, it can be passed in timestamp. 6.clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() - It removes data from Local Storage, Session Storage, and any cached data. After the data is cleared, the page will reload, and the user will be redirected to the registration page. For devices with QR functionality enabled, the user will be directed to the QR scanner page. Note: It is recommended to use this API only when necessary, as it may result in data loss.

ClientGlobalObj of the ClientGlobal class of ADM clients is available globally to be used by application developers. It provides the following variables and methods which help application developers to configure different aspects of client features. ADM client registration log details are also explained in this document.

Variables are recommended for changes in the index.html page after rendering of ClientGlobal class. For example, suppose the variable name is a system so in index.html it is changed as clientGlobalObj.system = “KLARION” clientGlobalObj.system = "KLARION"; system - Used to specify the system in which an application is running. Currently, there are only two values that can be used i.e. KLARION or SAP. By default the system value is Klarion. public system: "KLARION" | "SAP" = 'KLARION'; deviceType - Used to specify the device in which the application is running. Values are browser or cordova. Currently, its value is maintained automatically depending on the device type i,e if the device is a browser then the value is a browser and if it is cordova (Mobile) then its value is cordova. public deviceType: "Cordova" | "Browser"; sapUITheme - Used to set sap UI library themes. The default value is sap_belize_plus public sapUITheme: string = "sap_belize_plus"; sapUIVersion - Used to set the sap UI library version. The default value is 1.102.7 public sapUIVersion:string = "1.102.7" appName - Used to specify the name of the application. It is used to construct url SAP related URLs for seam4 type of application Eg: moast4, seam4 etc. baseRot - List of rot/app/flavor which can be mentioned at the beginning in index.html, which will be downloaded and extracted before the registration page is visible. Note: - Until the baseRot is downloaded, the user cannot perform any kind of operation. Treat it as a mandatory rot/app/flavor which is required before the user can perform any operation Structure of list: [{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildNo:number}] public baseRot:Array<{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildno:number}> = []; extendedRot - List of rot/app / flavortotally similar to baseRot with only one difference: it will get downloaded and extracted in the background. I.e User will not have to wait to begin any operation. Structure of list: [{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildNo:number}] public extendedRot:Array<{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildno:number}> = []; documentTitle - Used to specify title value in the title tag of html page. For more information refer to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/title isLog - Boolean value to enable or disable clientGlobalObject log. The log can be accessed using clientGlobalObject._log preloadScript - List of script files with the proper path which can be mentioned in the index.html file which will get loaded in the client before the user can perform any operation. Eg: clientGlobalObj.preloadScript=["closedmodules/kloExternal/core.js"] postLoadScript - List of script files with a proper path similar to preloadScript with only one difference. Users do not have to wait for the script to load to perform any operation. enableBioMetric - its value is either true or false based on that you will view a biometric login at the offline login page. By default true is maintained is_browser_sync - value is either true or false. If true then the middleware works through the index DB of the client and if the value is false or not maintained then the middleware works through the sync adapter. oUIConfig - It is an object containing a key-value pair which is used to hide or show a particular view/div in the index.html page. Note: Developers can add more key value in this object for their usage. Key value pair listed below:

documents.t: Application URLs support version-based access using the following format: https://<domain>/appservice/<landscape>/<flavor>_<version>/<api_id> where <version> follows the format: <major>-<minor>-<patch> When resolving an application version: The specified major and minor versions are honored. The system automatically resolves the request to the latest available patch version within the specified major.minor version. Example​ Available versions: 7-0-1 7-0-5 7-0-20 Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_7-0-1/api123 Resolved Version: 7-0-20 Similarly, if versions 8-1-3, 8-1-10, and 8-2-5 are available: Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_8-1-3/api123 Resolved Version: 8-1-10 This behavior ensures that consumers automatically receive the latest available patch fixes and improvements within the requested major.minor release stream without requiring URL updates.

documents.t: Add your new automation folder inside allAutomation folder. Here You’ll need to incorporate the automation files and folders you’ve created, following a standard project structure. Changes in conf.Data.js If you're running automations locally, your conf.data.js file may contain hardcoded values, as shown in the example below. However, in AWS, all configurations in conf.data.js are dynamic and sourced from master.conf.json. Add the following import statement at the top of your conf.data.js: import masterConf from '../master.conf.json' with {type: "json"}; Open master.conf.json and check whether the variables you need are already declared.If they are missing, add them manually. Replace hardcoded values in conf.data.js with references to the corresponding variables from masterConf. Refer to the example shown in the image below for guidance. Changes in KloAuWdio.js file inside kloAU folder in a automation If you're running automations locally, your kloAuWdio.js file may contain hardcoded values in the args section of config, as shown in the example below. However, in AWS, all configurations in conf.data.js are dynamic and sourced from master.conf.json. Add the following import statement at the top of your kloAuWdio.js: import masterConf from '../master.conf.json' with {type: "json"}; Then, replace all hardcoded values in conf.data.js with references to the corresponding variables from masterConf. These changes ensure that your automation setup is flexible and optimized for dynamic execution in AWS environments. Refer to the example shown in the image below for guidance. Changes in master.bat In master.bat, add the path to the newly added automation. Refer to the following code snippet for guidance: The first line navigates to the folder created with the current date. The second line navigates to the target repository inside that folder (i.e., the newly added automation). Inside that folder, a new command prompt is opened and npx wdio is executed to start the automation. The output of the automation running in the command prompt is saved to Regression.txt(change the name according to the automation created). Once the automation completes, the message "npx wdio is completed" is appended to log.txt. Changes in checkforcompletion.bat Update the count based on the number of new automations added. For example, if you’ve added 2 new automations, increase the count by 2.So, if the original count was 24, update it to 26. Changes in copyandgeneratereport.bat The copyandgeneratereport.bat script is primarily used to copy report and log files between systems and to an S3 bucket. In addition to file transfers, it also generates reports that are intended to be attached in emails. ::------ Copy of Automations report files one directory back ------- copy "Flavor_Build\reports\Flavor_Build.html" ".\ copy "Unique_Key_1\reports\Unique_Key_1.html" ".\ copy "Unique_Key_2\reports\Unique_Key_2.html" ".\ copy "Vh_Testing\reports\Vh_Testing.html" ".\ The code snippet shown above copies HTML report files from their respective automation subdirectories—such as Flavor_Build, Unique_Key_1, Unique_Key_2, and Vh_Testing—into the parent directory, which corresponds to the automation folder within the date-specific folder. This intermediate step organizes the reports in a central location, preparing them for a subsequent move to the final reports folder in later stages of the script. So if you are adding any new automation add a new line here by changing you automation folder name and report name. If you're adding a new automation, make sure to include a new line in this section by specifying the appropriate automation folder name and the corresponding report file name. ::-----------------GENERATE REPORT-------------------------------- call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A1 call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A2 call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A3 call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A4 This part of the script runs finalreportgenerater.bat for each automation module to generate a summary of its test results. The batch file reads the current date, locates the module’s HTML report, extracts key metrics like pass/fail counts and execution time, and formats them into HTML summary lines. These lines are then added to categorized report files—report_pass.txt, report_fail.txt, or report_notRun.txt—based on the outcome. Each summary includes links to the full reports stored in an S3 bucket, making it easy to access detailed results. If you're adding a new automation, be sure to add a new line in this section using the correct automation folder name—assuming the folder name matches the report file name. This part of the script copies all the log files from the date-specific folder inside the automation directory to the reports folder. From there, the files are uploaded to an S3 bucket, making them publicly accessible from anywhere. If you're adding a new automation, make sure to include a new line in this section by specifying the appropriate automation log file name. This part of the script copies all the report files from the date-specific folder inside the automation directory to the reports folder. From there, the files are uploaded to an S3 bucket, making them publicly accessible from anywhere. If you're adding a new automation, make sure to include a new line in this section by specifying the appropriate automation folder name and the corresponding report file name.

documents.t: After registration in AWS, the menu wasn’t always clickable—automation was jumping ahead before it had finished loading. To further stabilize post-registration behavior—especially in AWS environments where UI components may load asynchronously—a new safeguard was introduced to ensure the ham menu expansion completes before proceeding. This was necessary because menu navigation was intermittently failing when the automation advanced before the menu system had fully initialized. Waits up to 5 times with 2-second intervals to check if the ham menu grid (__cssgrid0)(id for the whole menu ) is expanded. Uses data-menu2hbox attribute to determine expansion state (expanded-true). This checks whether the menu is expanded or not. Logs each attempt with detailed status messages for visibility and debugging. If not expanded, triggers the SAPUI5 firePress() event on the ham button (ham) to manually initiate expansion. Handles errors gracefully during both state checks and press events. Waits between retries to allow UI components time to load and respond. Provides a final summary indicating whether the menu successfully expanded or failed after all attempts. Note: To use the checkHamMenuExpansion function effectively, you must first trigger a click on the ham menu first in the data file and then using a separate function called menuSelectionLogin. This is necessary because, in the earlier approach, we used a function named menuSelection, which handled both the expansion of the hamburger menu and the selection of the menu header and its child items. However, since checkHamMenuExpansion now explicitly checks whether the hamburger menu is expanded—and expands it only if needed—we need to ensure the menu is clicked once beforehand. That initial click is handled in the data file before invoking checkHamMenuExpansion. If the menu is already expanded, the function does nothing; otherwise, it triggers the expansion. After confirming the menu state, we then call menuSelectionLogin to proceed with selecting the appropriate menu header and child. We avoid using menuSelection here because it includes its own ham menu click logic, which could interfere with the flow—causing the menu to open and then immediately close if called after checkHamMenuExpansion. At the same time, we can't remove the hamburger click from menuSelection entirely, as it's still needed in scenarios where the page is refreshed and the menu state resets. documents.t: In Bitbucket Pipelines, you can schedule a pipeline so it runs automatically at specific times without manually triggering it. 1. Open the Repository Go to Bitbucket → Repositories → Select your repository (e.g., klo_automation). 2. Go to Pipeline Settings Navigate to Pipelines → Click on Schedules in the left-hand menu. 3. Create a New Schedule Click Add schedule (or Create schedule, depending on your Bitbucket version). 4. Configure the Schedule Branch → Choose the branch you want the pipeline to run on. Pipeline → Select which pipeline definition to run (e.g., custom: run-public-master1 or custom: run-public-master2 or custom: run-private-master1 or run-private-master2). Frequency → Choose how often it should run: Daily Weekly Custom CRON (for advanced scheduling, like every 15 mins, every Monday at 9 AM, etc.). Example CRON expressions in Bitbucket: 0 9 * * * → Every day at 9:00 AM. 0 */6 * * * → Every 6 hours. 30 2 * * 1 → Every Monday at 2:30 AM. Note :- when you schedule a pipeline in Bitbucket, all times are interpreted in UTC, not your local time. 5. Save the Schedule Click Save. Bitbucket will now automatically trigger the pipeline according to the schedule you set.

documents.t: Date of Issue: July 2025 Target Audience: Testing Team, Automation Developers Prepared by: Ankit Sen Platform Version: 7.0 A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.

The original registration script was built with a linear, pause-heavy structure. It relied on fixed browser.pause() intervals between navigation steps and form interactions, assuming that the UI and backend would be ready within those timeframes. It performed the following steps: Navigated to multiple URLs in sequence. Executed clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() to reset client-side state. Waited for login input fields using waitForDisplayed() and filled them with credentials. Click the login and accept buttons. Entered a polling loop to check if registration was completed via localStorage. However, this approach had critical limitations: It did not verify if the page was fully ready before interacting with elements. It lacked error handling and diagnostics (e.g., no screenshots or logs for debugging). It assumed that all required data (like endPointId or downloaded files) would be available immediately after navigation. In AWS environments, this led to blank screens during registration because some asynchronous calls were still in progress, and the automation moved ahead too quickly. The structure of the previous registration code are illustrated below ➖ To address the shortcomings of the earlier implementation—especially the blank screen issue observed in AWS environments—the registration script was redesigned with a more resilient, diagnostic-driven approach. The updated code introduces structured polling, conditional logic, and robust error handling to ensure the automation waits for all necessary conditions before proceeding. It now performs the following steps: Waits for endPointId to appear in sessionStorage, retrying for up to 2 minutes and logging progress with screenshots. Polls localStorage for <landscape>_FILES_DOWNLOADED status, ensuring all relevant flavors (excluding openUI5 and openUI6) report "DONE" before continuing. Navigates through multiple URLs with retry logic, waiting for the #loginHeader element to confirm page readiness. Executes clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() only when required, improving efficiency and reducing unnecessary resets. Overrides window.confirm() to auto-accept prompts, preventing modal interruptions during automation. Waits for login input fields to become visible before entering credentials, using retry loops to handle delayed rendering. Ensures the #btn_accept button is visible, enabled, and scrolled into view before clicking, improving interaction reliability. Polls for registration completion for up to 9 minutes, checking for the _IS_APP_INSTALLTION_COMPLETED flag in localStorage. Injects UI5 and captures the client version once registration is confirmed, completing the flow with contextual awareness. These changes were introduced specifically to resolve issues in AWS environments, where backend or client-side calls were taking longer to complete after navigation. The earlier code did not wait for these asynchronous operations, causing the automation to proceed prematurely and resulting in blank screens. The new implementation ensures readiness at every step, making the registration flow stable, reliable, and cloud-friendly. The structure of the new registration code are illustrated below ➖ Note: Automation running on private nodes uses a different registration flow. Please review and update your code accordingly.

Modify the privateBaseUrl, publicUi5Url, and publicBaseUrl fields in the master.conf.json file to match your server's URL settings.Ensure that all user accounts referenced in the image below are accurately set up and maintained on your server. In both startingAutomation.ps1 and endAutomation.ps1, update the email subject lines to include accurate server details.This ensures that the emails received clearly reflect the correct server environment, making them easier to identify and track. Change the Flavor names and versions in every automation conf.data.js file.

All modifications applied to public automations are equally applicable to private Node automations. However, setting up a private node is your responsibility. To do this: Place the openUI5_1_120_27 package inside the closedmodules directory, as it's required for running the automation. Update the private node URL in the master.conf.json file accordingly. Once these steps are completed, the remaining process mirrors that of public automations, and your private automation setup will be ready to run.

documents.t: Previously, in the automation flows, whenever a busy indicator appeared, the scripts would automatically pause and wait for it to disappear before continuing. However, in recent runs—even in local environments also—the automations have stopped waiting for the busy indicator or busy dialog to fully disappear, causing them to proceed prematurely to the next steps. To address this issue, we've introduced the waitForBusyIndicator function. This asynchronous method ensures that the automation process pauses until the busy dialog has completely disappeared before continuing. Note: Our application uses two types of busy elements: sapMBusyDialog and sapMBusyIndicator. Please inspect your screen or application via the browser console to determine which one is currently in use. It repeatedly checks for the presence of the busy dialog every 2 seconds (CHECK_INTERVAL). If the dialog is visible, it continues to wait. Once the dialog is no longer detected, it waits an additional 10 seconds (WAIT_AFTER_CLOSE) to confirm it doesn't reappear. If the dialog remains gone, the loop exits and automation continues. Any errors during the check will also break the loop and log the issue. The structure of the new Wait for Busy Indicator code are illustrated below ➖

documents.t: In previous automation runs, registration occasionally failed silently—resulting in an "Oops" page without any visible error. Interestingly, re-registering often resolved the issue. To address this inconsistency, we’ve introduced a new checkRegistration() function. This function verifies whether the registration process has completed successfully. If not, it automatically re-invokes the appropriate registration function to retry the process. Important Implementation Notes: Replace the placeholder function name shown in the image with your actual registration function name. Depending on your setup, the registration function may be named register, login, or something else—ensure consistency when integrating checkRegistration().

Previously, automation processes occasionally failed due to the unexpected appearance of an upgrade popup during execution. To address this issue, we introduced the noUpgradeFunction(), which effectively suppresses the upgrade popup and ensures smoother automation flow. Important Usage Notes: The upgrade popup suppression must be re-applied after each registration and after every page refresh. This is necessary because the overridden function responsible for suppressing the popup is reset to its original state upon page reload.

documents.t: App Branching is done to create a branch of the actual app. This branch will be helpful in cases where the team wants to work on next-phase developments and at the same time provide fixes for the released application. Developers can create a new branch for the next phase of development and use this for the developments. When the developments are complete, the branch can be merged with the latest version of the app. To simplify this let's take a look at the below explanation: In the above diagram, we have an app named eam_6.0.1. Now there is a major enhancement that needs to be done for this app. This enhancement might take a long period to develop. This will automatically pause the further development progress of the app. Therefore, we will create a branch for this app. All the major developments will be done in this branch app. In the meantime, minor fixes and other changes are made to the main app and the versions are updated. Once the enhancement is complete the branch app will be exported along with the latest version and both will be merged into one major app version as the final product.

Step 1: From the menu navigate to the App Management page of the Workspace Hub. Step 2: Navigate to the App by clicking on the app link from the app list for which the branch needs to be created from the apps list section. Step 3: Create a branch for the app by clicking on the Branch action button. It will create a new branch version for the selected app. Note: Branches button will be enabled only on the released app version Note: If the app version is of type branch then the branch checkbox will be enabled. Step 4: Change the version if needed and click on the save button to save the changes. Now, our Branch app has been created. Step 5: Assign the users for this new branch in the roles & users tab(need to be manually added, will not be copied from the branched version) NOTE : Branch flavors cannot be transported or moved to any system. For doing so, create a new version, merge that branch to the new version and then move the new version to any system.

documents.t: It allows developers to compare two apps and prepare a newly exported (zip) file that can be imported to another app.

Step 1: Go to the export section, fill in the required fields and click on download. App ID: Flavor ID name. Version: Version of the flavor. Export: Export the flavor directly. This will create a zip in the server. Download: The download button will download the zip of the given flavor. NOTE: Export both the apps' zip for merging purposes. Step 2: Go to the compare section and upload both the zip files to Set 1 and Set 2. Set 1: App 1 zip which will compare with Set 2. Set 2: App 2 zip which will compare to Set 1. Step 3: After uploading the Zips, click on the compare action button. Compare button will list down all the differences between your apps. Child - It shows whether the relations of the root object are different. SET1 Vs SET2 - compares whether the root object( like m_entities, mu_screen, etc.) is same, different, or present only in one of the sets. Merge(O)- It will merge the whole object (like m_entities, mu_screen, etc..) Merge(O) field has a drop-down which has Vh items and a description of Vh items are mentioned below: Delete: It will delete the particular object from Merging. Set 1: After selecting SET 1, the object of set 1 will be added for Merging. Or we can say, it will pick the object from set 1 for Merging. Set 2: After selecting SET 2, the object of set 2 will be added for Merging. Or it will pick the object from set 1 for Merging. Merge(A)- It will merge the particular attribute(e.g. properties) of the object. We can also provide custom values via using Merge(A)- CUSTOM. Merge(A) field has a drop-down which has Vh items and the description of Vh items is mentioned below: Default: Contributes to the default way of merging. Custom: Custom is used to add custom values for attributes of the object. NOTE: Special care needs to be taken while merging, If you are adding property then property type also needs to be added. After clicking on any row, the difference between the two flavors for that row will be listed in another table. Properties: Properties of the object or attributes Set 1: Shows the values of properties Set 2: Shows the values of properties Custom: Used to add custom values for object attributes (e.g properties) Red dots (⬤): It specifies that the particular object or attributes have differences between the flavors Yellow Highlight will specify the exact difference of the selected object or attribute. Step 4: Click on the merge action button, A zip will be downloaded. Step 5: Create a new version of the app and import the downloaded ZIP to it. For importing, go to the import section and upload a Zip file using the Upload zip file button. Importing- app: The app id which you want to import. Importing- Version: The app ID which you want to import. Build: to build the app which you want to import. Update Schema: do updateSchema for the app which you want to import. Copy config data: copy the config data for the app which you want to import. Fill in the mandatory fields and click on the Submit button. Step 6: see the dialogue Import Status to check the status of the import. Step 7: After importing the app, the app needs to be published. This can be done via the Workspace Hub’s App Management page.

documents.t: The Status Change Process is used for segregating the version and branch hierarchy process to identify each dependent app and sequence. From Active, status can be changed to Released, Discarded. From Released, status can be changed to Deprecated. Deprecated: No users should be assigned to the App. Discarded: All the changes in the app will be discarded and not be considered in the main branch. Only from the Released version, a new version can be created. Only from Active Version, a new Branch can be created. Development can be only done in the App with Active Status. A branch can be ACTIVE, DEPRECATED, or DISCARDED.
