documents.t: App Cache Settings, as the name suggests, is for developers as a helping tool while developing applications. Previously, if any offline entity was created, any metadata was updated, or any entry was made in the server-side database, it required developers to clear their cache and do registration again to get it reflected in the browser. To resolve that issue, a App Cache Settings is introduced. Now, developers can update zip, drop and create web SQL tables, update configs (eg: vh configs), and do initial sync to get server data without any middleware sync (sync of data in the background whenever the device/browser is online). Note: The App Cache Settings should be handled by developers only to avoid any inconsistency or failure in the application.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/App Cache Settings/About App Cache Settings

documents.t: The App Cache Settings looks like a table with various features. Following are the details of those features: Features Description Zip Update Update the zip of any application in the browser. It will update offline files (files which are coming from browser cache) Table Generation (web SQL) Table generation provides two options: • Drop tables and create new ones. This means the old table will be dropped and a new table will be created instead. • Delete the data from the existing table. Initial Sync Here you will be able to get data from the server database into browser web SQL tables. A Web SQL is a database at the client side (browser or device). Update Config Update application-related configs. (eg- vh config)

documents.t: App merging is the process of merging one application branch with the current main branch (or vice versa) or merging one active branch into another active branch. It is important to note that this process merges metadata only.

Need to assign cockpit and account flavors Developer access is required to work on the targeted flavor. Deployment of the app/flavor should occur within a development environment. If you're merging into the main version, the main version must be active; if merging into a branch version, then the branch must be active. For Example: From version 1.0.2 of our app, we created a new branch, 1.0B.2, for developing a new feature. While the feature is being developed, changes may still occur in the main branch. Once the new feature is completed, we need to merge it back into the main branch. Version Type Description Example Base Version The starting version from which the branch was created. 1.0.2 Latest Main Version The most recent, stable version of the main branch. 1.0.5 Branch Version The version where the new feature has been developed. 1.0B.2
For the application merge, we need to consider three versions of the application: Target Version Source Version Base Version

The Target Version is where the changes will be applied after the merge. It is pre-filled by default based on where the user initiated the merge from. If the user navigates from a Branch, then that branch is the Target. If the user navigates from a Latest Main Version, then that main version is the Target. User Navigated From Target Version A Branch That Branch A Main Version That Main Version

The Source Version is selected by the user from a dropdown. The dropdown options depend on the type of Target: Target Type Source Options Branch Main Released Versions, Active Branches Main Version Only Branches of the App

The Base Version is automatically determined based on the selected Source and Target. It represents the common ancestor between the two — the point from which both versions diverged. You want to compare how both the Source and Target have changed since they split from the same origin — that's the Base. Usually, the Base Version is the version from which: The Branch was created, or The Main Version was forked for changes. Scenario Base Version Logic Branch → Main 🔄 Main → Branch The version from which the Branch was created The version from which the Branch was created Branch → Branch The most recent common version in both branch sequences

If there is any altered content in both the Latest Main Version and the Branch Version, it will be considered a conflict and must be resolved by the developer (user). The user will be presented with a selection option to choose either the Main Version or the Branch Version for the merge. Any further modifications can be made after the merge is imported into the version if needed. The conflicts should be resolved by the user based on their selection and any required adjustments as shown below; **Example: ** To illustrate the merge concepts discussed above, let's consider a simple scenario. **Case 1: Auto-Merge ** The title on our screen is "App Console". In the Branch Version, we are updating the title to "Workspace Hub". **Case 2: Auto-Merge **The title on our screen is "App Console". In the Main Branch Version, we are changing the title to "Workspace Hub". During the merge, the changes will be compared with the three sets, and it will be determined that the update is only in the Main Branch Version. Since this is an update exclusive to the Main Branch, it will be auto-merged into the branch without any conflicts. **Case 3: Conflict ** The title on our screen is "App Console". In the Branch Version, we are changing the title to "Workspace Hub". In the Main Version, we are changing the title to "Account Cockpit". During the merge, the changes will be compared across the three sets. It will be determined that there are changes in both the Branch Version and the Main Version when compared to the Base Version. This results in a conflict, as both versions have different updates to the title. The user will need to manually resolve this conflict by selecting the appropriate title or making adjustments as needed. Aspect Details Merge Target Only the active version (Main or Branch) can receive merged changes. Merge Concurrency Only one branch merge at a time is allowed. No support for simultaneous merges. Automatic Merge Scope Only metadata merges are handled automatically. Manual Merge Required Files like controllers, entities, queries, utils, resources require manual intervention. Unchanged Items No changes are applied if items are identical across all three versions (Base, Branch, Main). Auto-Merge Conditions Change exists only in Branch Version → Auto-merge Change exists only in Latest Main Version → Auto-merge Conflict Handling - If conflicts exist, they must be resolved manually by the user. - Compare Branch vs Base and Main vs Base to identify differences. - Then compare the resulting changes for conflicts. Default Target The Target App Version is pre-filled based on the version/branch the user navigated from. Source Options Based on Target Type If Target is a Branch, Source dropdown lists Released Main versions and Active Branches. If Target is a Main version, Source dropdown lists only Branches. Base Version Selection Automatically determined based on Source and Target versions. Supported Merge Directions ✅ Branch → Main ✅ Main → Branch ✅ Branch → Branch

Step 1: Navigate to the App Management screen in the Workspace Hub. **Step 2:**Click the "Compare and Merge" button.This will navigate the user to the App Merger screen. Note: The "Compare and Merge" button will only be visible in the Active version or branch of the app. Step 3: Compare and Merge dialogue box will appear as shown below. The Target App will be automatically set to the app version from which the user navigated. (Refer Target version to know more). Select the source from the dropdown list you wanted to compare and merge.
An App Selection popup will be displayed to the user as shown below;

The process may take some time depending on the size of the flavor and the scope of development changes. By default, an Auto-Merge will be performed. Only the conflicting items will be presented to the user for review and manual resolution. The red dot Icon shows the conflict in the child as shown below; Use the filter option to Show all items. The screen is split into three sections, displaying categories, their corresponding elements and its status, and detailed information for each item. (Section 1.4) In the Categories section, select the category with a number in brackets as shown in the screenshot above—this indicates a conflict that can be reviewed after the compare and merge process.

documents.t: On click of the link, the attributes will be shown on the right side. The user can choose to resolve conflicts by selecting either from the Source Value or the Target Value. This allows the user to focus on resolving conflicts while also providing flexibility in their choice of version for resolution. The Administrative Data screen displays creation (Created By, Created On) and modification (Modified By, Modified On) details for both the Source and Target. If a user tries to proceed with the merge without resolving all identified conflicts, the system will prevent the merge from continuing and display a warning. For example, as shown in the screenshot below, if conflicts are still present and the user clicks the Save button, a warning notification will appear indicating that conflicts need to be resolved before proceeding. This ensures that no changes are accidentally overwritten or merged incorrectly due to unresolved discrepancies between versions.

Click 'Save' to initiate actions such as publish, update schema, and config data in the background. When you click 'Save', a confirmation message will appear, as shown below, prompting you to proceed. Once the merge process begins, it may take some time to complete these steps: -Merging application versions -Publishing the merged application -Update schema -Copying configuration data The merge is considered complete when all steps in the process display a checkmark, indicating successful execution. If an error occurs during the merge process, the "Show Logs" option will display the error log as shown below; If everything is successful, it will navigate back to the App Management screen. If source is branch then after merge before navigation user can opt to change the status of app to MERGED by clicking YES. When there are unsaved (dirty) changes, navigation away from the current screen is prevented. A warning message is displayed with the following prompt: "You have some changes that are not saved." If the user selects "Discard", navigation is allowed, and any unsaved changes are discarded. If the user selects "Cancel", the warning message is closed, and navigation is halted, allowing the user to stay on the current screen.

📌 Note: If a child flavor is selected, a warning message will be displayed to inform the user. Example:​ Current Versions: Parent App Version: 1.0.5 Child App Version: 1.0B.2 (with custom features) Scenario: Developer 1 makes updates to the Parent App (e.g., new bug fixes, feature enhancements). Developer 2 works on the Child App (e.g., new UI design). Merging Child App: Developer 2 attempts to merge the child app **Warning Displayed: ** Action Taken: Developer 2 merges Parent App (1.0.5) first. After the parent app is merged, Developer 2 proceeds with merging Child App (1.0B.2), ensuring that all changes are consistent.
The screen is split into three sections, displaying categories, their corresponding elements and its status, and detailed information for each item.

The Categories section ( on the left side of the screen) presents a list of all major areas where differences were detected during the comparison. These are grouped into logical classifications, such as:Notifications,Settingvalue,Queries, Menuheader,screen,Property type etc. Some of these categories may display a number in brackets (e.g., "Queries (2)"), which indicates the count of conflicts found in that category. This helps users quickly identify where attention is needed.

When you click on a category, the Elements section (middle pane) shows a list of individual items within that category that have been flagged with **conflicts.**Each element here represents a specific piece of the application—such as a particular UI component, a schema field, or a configuration file. Example: Clicking on "Screen (1) " reveals conflicting fields like p_bol_editor, s_query_sort_order, entity_property_name, s_relations,ret_ent.

Once an element is selected, the Details section (rightmost pane) displays properties in side-by-side or split view showing how that specific item differs between the Source version and the Target version . This area allows you to: Review both versions of the element Understand what changed in each version since the Base Manually resolve conflicts by choosing one version, merging changes, or customizing a final output Example: If both versions have updated the entity_property_name field differently, you can decide which version to keep or manually edit the final result.

Use these filters to quickly navigate merge items based on their status: Filter Description ✅ Resolved Shows only items that were auto-merged or manually resolved. ⚠️ Conflict Displays only items that have merge conflicts and require user action. 📄 All Shows all items — both resolved and conflicting.

Items that have either been: Automatically merged (no conflict) Manually resolved by the user Behavior: Hidden from default conflict view (unless this filter is selected). Marked with a "Resolved" icon in green color.

Conflicts exist between Source and Target versions and User intervention is required. Behavior: Automatically shown by default when entering conflict resolution screen Requires user to choose between: Source version Target version Or edit manually to merge the two

Shows every item involved in the merge process: Auto-merged Manually resolved Still unresolved Behavior: Provides a full audit of what’s happening in the merge Useful for developers or reviewers on the changes done

Merge History screen: This screen displays records of previously completed merges, allowing users to review the details of past merge activities. Navigation to the Screen: Select Design Studio and navigate to Merge History Below is the image of the Merge History Screen. Users can search the Merge History based on the data entered in the advanced search. The 'Target App' in Advanced Search will display only the manager access app. Error message:

A:If the build fails or the user refreshes the screen, the process will resume from the build stage, not from the merge stage. Similarly, if the first two stages (e.g., schema validation and merge) are completed during the merge process but the process is interrupted midway, the system will resume from the update schema stage, not from the beginning.
documents.s: ❓:What happens if the build fails or the page is refreshed during the process?

documents.t: **A:**If there is a conflict — such as an app merge issue or a failure in two processes — a conflict screen will appear. This screen allows the user to resolve the conflicts before continuing with the merge. Additionally, if config data is present in the flavor, and the buildconfig, or any other process fails, the conflict screen will also appear to let the user address the issue before proceeding.
documents.s: **❓:**What happens if there is a conflict during the process?

documents.t: **A:**If the process is canceled or the screen is refreshed or the browser is changed, or an error occurs, the conflict screen will not reappear if the app merge has already been completed. In this case, the process will resume from where it left off — except when copying config data. If the interruption happens during the config copy stage, the process will restart from getting the app details.
documents.s: ❓:What happens if the process is interrupted or canceled?

App overriding is a feature where the child apps inherit the features of the parent app and override their properties. This screen is used to display and highlight the overridden elements and their properties.
Date of Issue: September 2024 Version: 7.0 Prepared by: Nayan Adhikary Target Audience: Application Developers

Maintaining a proper hierarchy between app versions is crucial for accurate dependency management, for this a correct approach to establish a multi-level hierarchy is required, ensuring that dependencies are calculated correctly. To maintain the hierarchy effectively, it always starts from the top-most parent and works your way down to the bottom-most child. Example: Current Versions: A-1 (Top-most Parent) B-1 C-1 D-1 (Bottom-most Child) Correct Hierarchy: A-1 -> B-1 -> C-1 -> D-1 Note: To ensure accurate dependency management; Always maintain hierarchy from the top-most parent to the bottom-most child. This method prevents errors in dependency calculations and keeps the app structure coherent.

Step 1: Go to the menu options and select App Lifecycle**.** Step 2: Transport has two screens. App Migration and Script Repository. When you install an app in a DEV landscape, App transport asks whether to install it As Readable or As Writable. The choice decides what is copied to the target landscape and what you can change there afterward. As Readable (Read-Only) As Writable What is moved The built application package (zip) only The app’s full metadata from the source DEV landscape Can the app be developed in the target? No Yes Can App Dependencies be maintained? No (see below) Yes Typical use Consuming an app as-is, e.g., in QA/PROD or as a parent app Continuing development in another DEV landscape Why App Dependencies can’t be maintained for a Read-Only app A Read-Only app has no metadata in the target landscape. It only has its built package. Maintaining App Dependencies writes a generated sequence to the database, and the app must be built again afterward. A Read-Only app can’t be built in the target landscape, so its dependencies can’t be changed there. Example: VP depends on OHR (VP ← OHR). If the dependency configuration has to change on the OHR side, OHR must be installed As Writable. Alternatively, make the change in the source landscape and migrate it again. Note: If you might need to change an app’s dependencies in the target landscape, install it As Writable. [Confirm] Whether a Read-Only app can be switched to Writable later, or must be reinstalled.

Transport is a tool that deploys applications from one server to another. It is mainly aimed at deploying from a dev system to QA system and from QA to PROD system but can be used across any system. Transportation of an application can be from: DEV to QA QA to PROD DEV to DEV Steps involved: DEV to QA Setup - Doing entries in tables like madm_app, madm_app_grp etc. Download- Downloading and extracting application zips from the source. Update Schema - Creating tables on the server for entities of that app. Finalizing - Making the app ACTIVE so that everyone can use it.

Maintain this configuration in target’s config file. (present in <landscape>/kloconfig/config.json) "mm_klo_online_server": { "serverUrl": "https://dev.procify38.com", "Landscape": "tools_dev6", "username": "transport", "password": "1", "realm": "cloud_app" }, Where, serverUrl is the source system’s url, landscape - source System’s landscape, username - one specific user should be there with transport flavor assigned to it. password- password for that user realm - keycloak’s realm Maintain host file entry for the source system in the target system transport_1 app should be assigned to the user.

Transport takes care of the following: Maintaining entries of applications in tables like madm_app,mf_fl,mf_fv etc., if any. Moving application zips across the system (QA or PROD system) and extracting them. Getting the metadata of the application from the source DEV system and extracting it in the target DEV system. Running automated scripts if maintained. Track manual scripts and run when required. Publishing Application. Doing an updated schema on the application.

When creating a build URL, the current klobase version (known as bol_version) must be included for the core_fw component. The bol_version indicates the version of the build running on the system and should be included in the URL to generate the correct build.

Suppose the current bol_version running in the system is 7-2-27. Previous Build URL​ Before adopting the current_bol_version, the build URL would look like this: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/EAM/core_fw_6-0/generateBuild?fv=my_test_6-0-1&buildtype= Current Build URL (7-- onwards)​ After updating to the current bol_version (7-2-27), the build URL format will be updated as follows: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/\<landscape>/core_fw_<current_bol_version>/generateBuild?fv=<flavor_name>_<flavor_version>&buildtype=<typeofBuild> For the example provided with a current_bol_version of 7-2-27, the updated URL would look like this: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/EAM/core_fw_7-2-27/generateBuild?fv=my_test_6-0-1&buildtype=devbuild **Note: ** To generate a build URL for the core_fw version: Retrieve the current bol_version from the system using clientGlobalObj._bolVersion. Update the URL with the correct core_fw version and the appropriate build type. Use the following format: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/\<landscape>/core_fw_<current_bol_version>/generateBuild?fv=<flavor_name>_<flavor_version>&buildtype=<typeofBuild> This ensures the build URL points to the correct version and build type for the system.

The build process is not needed every time; it should only be used in specific scenarios. Below are the cases when you should use the build: Under prodBuild, whenever the developer needs to deploy apps to the QA server, a build is required. After entity creation, whenever we change the persists on of the entity,build is required. Whenever we maintain the Parent -child hierarchy, we need to build. Whenever we are creating vh-config, we need to build. Before doing import/export of apps, you need to build. Whenever you create new version of app, we need to build (this build is done automatically by the account console) For mobile apps, whenever you want to test app changes, you need to build. For both devBuild and prodBuild, if we are creating new env roles then we need to build. Note: When the fw_version of the application is changed, a new flavor_build must be created and re-registration will be required. The build process (both devBuild and prodBuild) should follow a parent → child order. You can trigger builds for both flavors at once. However, if the devBuild or prodBuild of a parent flavor has not been completed before building its child flavor, you will encounter an error like this:Error: Parent app(s) parent_app must be dev/prodbuilt before building child_app.

Note: If the developers want to make any changes to the Settings Definition Screen metadata then they will have to assign core_fw as a dependent app to the fw_settings1_1 app and then build the fw_settings1 flavor and reinitialize it. Only then any changes should be made. Also for save to work, assign is_external for fw_settings1 flavor as 1. To save any changes made on the Settings Definition user needs a shared, writable app.
Flavor: fw_settings1

Go to the menu App Settings. Click on the sub-menu named Settings Definition to open it. The Screen will be loaded initially with all the settings inside their respective Settings Group in a tree in ascending order based on their sequence value. Settings Group will also be in ascending order of their sequence values. Click on the Edit option in the upper right corner of the screen. On the toolbar of the screen, you will find the Create Group, Create Settings, Save, Delete and Cancel buttons. You can create the settings group by clicking the +Group button on the top right of the screen. It will ask the developer to provide the Settings Group ID in an input dialog. Click on the Create button in the input dialog. After creating a new Settings Group, users can see it updated in the Table Tree below. Users need to fill in the Sequence number, Title and Icon of that settings group and then click on the Save button to save the newly created settings group. All the settings groups will now be shown in ascending order of their sequence value. The developer then needs to create Settings inside the newly created settings group. To do that the user needs to select that settings group on the tree and then click on +Setting Button. It will ask for the Settings ID under Create Setting and the developer needs to provide the ID and click on the Create button. A new setting will be created inside the selected settings group. The developer needs to fill in the Title, Description, Sequence Number, Icon, Data Type, UI type, Vh ID, Default value, visible and modifiable_in and then click on Save to save all the changes. After successful save, all the settings in their respective groups will be in ascending order of their sequence value. Components Descriptions Title It's the name you want to put to identify the setting control. Description A short description of the setting element. Sequence Number This will put the setting elements according to the order of its sequence. Icon This implies an individual settings icon. Data Type It's the type of the setting, whether it's a number, an integer or a string etc. UI Type It is the type of Control that you want to render in the UI for those Settings such as Input, Slider, value Help, etc. Vh ID It is the value help ID created from bol editor on application flavor and it will be shown to the user as value help items in case the user has chosen UI type as VH. Default Value It's a pre-value that has been set for some particular setting. This is changeable according to your requirements. visible This implies who will be able to see the particular setting item. modifiable in This puts down conditions on who can see the setting items and so on. To update any details click on the edit button in the toolbar and after updating the details click on save to commit the changes. If you have updated any details and do not want it to commit then you can click on the reset button in the toolbar to set the details to the original state.

Our application is designed to operate with a specific Framework (FW) version. However, in certain situations, it may be necessary to downgrade the FW version to maintain compatibility, stability, or consistency across different environments. Below are the scenarios where a FW downgrade is required: **Latest FW Version Unavailable in QA and Production Environments ** Scenario: The latest FW version is deployed only in the development environment, but it has not been made available in the QA or production environments. **Reason for Downgrade: ** To ensure that the application team can move their developments to QA and production environments without facing compatibility issues. To align the development environment with the FW version currently in use in the QA and production environments. **Limited Testing of the Application with the Latest FW Version ** Scenario: The application has only been partially tested with the latest FW version, which introduces a risk that untested features or components may not perform as expected. **Reason for Downgrade: ** To provide more time for comprehensive testing and validation of the application on the latest FW version in a controlled environment before deploying it to QA or production. **Latest FW Version Exhibits Stability Concerns ** Scenario: The latest FW version has shown some performance issues or minor bugs that could affect application behavior. Reason for Downgrade: To ensure continued stability in the QA and production environments. To maintain a smooth user experience by avoiding potential disruptions in application performance.
documents.s: Framework Downgrade Scenarios in the Application
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Applications FW Version Update/Framework Downgrade Scenarios in the Application

documents.t: If the application was initially developed using the downgraded FW version and the latest FW version becomes available in the QA and production environments, the following steps should be followed: **Upgrade the FW Version in the Development Environment: ** Update the development environment to match the latest FW version used in QA and production. **Validate Application Compatibility: ** Test the existing application, which was developed with the previous FW version, to ensure it is compatible with the latest FW version. **Make Necessary Updates: ** Update the application code or configurations as needed to support the latest FW version. **Conduct Thorough Testing: ** Perform end-to-end testing in the development environment to ensure the application functions correctly with the upgraded FW version. **Transport the Updated Application: ** After successful testing, move the updated application to the QA and production environments.

Whenever there's a change in the major or minor versions of the FW platform, the apps that use the FW platform version need to be updated manually by the Application/Implementation team. For Example: We have an app named eam_6.0.1 that uses FW version 7_2_30. A major enhancement is required for this app due to the recent update to the FW version.Therefore, we will create a branch for this app and all the adoptions will be done in this branch, using the latest FW version 7_3_1. By reviewing the release notes for the FW update, the application team will learn about any adoptions or new features in the FW. Once the enhancement is complete, the branch app will be merged with the latest version into a single major app version, resulting in a final product, such as eam_6.0.3,FW version 7_3_1. Once all necessary fixes and updates are made to the app, it will be moved to the QA branch/environment for testing. If testing is successful, the updated app will be deployed to the production environment. Note: How to do the app branching and merging is mentioned in the UG. When the FW version is upgraded(major/minor) and is deployed,the applications that work on the FW version should be changed to the latest version.For that to achieve,create a branch and update the FW version as explained above. Once done with all the adoptions and changes, it is merged to the main branch and then the FW version is updated to transport it further to QA. Once the test is passed, the FW version will be updated in the application with the new FW version. As shown in the above diagram, if the test fails, then the app will not be taking the FW update and it will downgrade to the most recent functioning version of FW to ensure everything functions properly.

documents.t: Every Application / App version built on the Procify platform uses a FW/Platform version. The platform releases a new version every month with new features and bug fixes reported. It is recommended for users to stay updated with the latest version of the platform. This document serves as a guide for users on the understanding of Framework version updation(upgrade/downgrade) for applications. If an app running on the latest Framework version requires adjustments, users can use this guide to revert to an earlier version. This process involves either upgrading or downgrading the FW version. Note:Framework version can be changed only for ACTIVE Apps. App FW version cannot be changed by users when it's in QA/production.

During the patch upgrade in Framework platform, this upgrade will be automatically updated in all the applications which use the FW platform once they are released. So it's completely up to the FW team, when it comes to the patch update and there's nothing to do with the application team in the upgrading of FW version.

documents.t: Add a value to an input or textarea element found by the given selector.Send a sequence of keystrokes to an element after the input has been cleared before. Note: For the "sendKeys" action, an additional key-value pair, "keyVal", must be included in the object. This "keyVal" will hold the text you wish to input into the selected control. documents.t: The "replaceMap" action is utilized for incorporating additional variables that can be utilized across all files during runtime. This method proves beneficial for transmitting parameters within our functions, given that direct argument passing isn't feasible in array format. By employing this workaround, we simulate the behavior of passing arguments as done conventionally in regular functions. Note :- For the "replaceMap" action, an additional key-value pair, "data", must be included in the object. The "data" attribute is designed to store an array of objects, each representing a variable and its value that you wish to declare or store within the replaceMap. Upon repeated use of the same variables within replaceMap, it will overwrite the older values with the newly assigned ones. In the provided example, you'll notice the absence of "controlID" or "domElementId". This is because no actions were performed on any specific element; hence, the user needs to craft this function manually instead of generating it through a test recorder. Same will happen with many actions that are not performed on any elements.

documents.t: The "ifPresent" action serves as a mechanism for verifying certain operations executed during automation. Specifically, it checks if a selected control element is indeed displayed on the screen. By utilizing its domElementId, it searches for the presence of the DOM element on the screen. Note: For the "ifPresent" action, an extra key-value pair named "type" needs to be added to the object. The "type" parameter specifies the kind of control that the action targets. This "type" should match the "controlType" found within the controlID.

documents.t: The "ifNotPresent" action functions as a counterpart to "ifPresent," serving to verify specific actions carried out during automation but in reverse. It specifically verifies whether a chosen control element is absent from the screen. Utilizing its domElementId, it searches to confirm the absence of the DOM element on the screen.

documents.t: Within the closedmodules directory, establish a new folder titled klo_automation_1. Within this, create another folder dedicated to your automation, housing all requisite files needed to execute the automation. Note :- Adhering to this specific structure is crucial for the successful execution of the automation. The automation process attempts to access certain files, notably the klarion.json file located within the kloconfig folder, from your private node. Therefore, maintaining this structure ensures that the automation can correctly locate and utilize these files from their designated locations. Should you deviate from this structure, you will need to adjust the paths in conf.data.js accordingly to reflect the correct locations of your files. The files mentioned above are essential for running the automation. Let's examine each of these files individually.

Located within the kloAu directory, this file stands as the core component of the automation suite. It houses all necessary functions tasked with transforming array-formatted code into a conventional format. Since WDIO cannot interpret array formats directly, this conversion is imperative for compatibility.

This file will house all fundamental configurations necessary for the automation to operate, including user credentials, URLs, and the specific Chrome directory in which the execution should occur. baseUrl: Users must specify the URL to be accessed at the beginning of the automation process. userId: The User ID associated with the login or registration conducted on the previously mentioned URL. Password: The user's password, if applicable. desktopLoginID: For the desktop login ID, users need to supply the User ID used for logging in on their desktop. Profile_directory: Users must indicate the Chrome profile directory where they intend to run the automation. Specs: Within the Specs object, users must list the names of the specs they wish to execute, adhering to a sequential order. It's important to note that the names provided are case-sensitive. Ensure consistency in naming across all references to avoid discrepancies. NOTE :- The Spec and Data file names should be entered exactly as demonstrated in the preceding example. Additionally, the object name must remain consistent. Please remember that the names provided are case-sensitive. ReplaceMap :-This file includes all the application variables required for test cases. Variables must be declared within double dollar signs, like $variable_name$ How replaceMap Operates in Automation:​ In the array format data file, replaceMap searches for all variables declared either in conf.data.js or at runtime within the data file itself. Whenever it encounters a match, it substitutes the matched variable with the corresponding value from the object's key-value pair. Note: By default, two variables, $dateKey$ and $landscape$, are automatically created within replaceMap at runtime. These variables can also be utilized within your data file. $dateKey$: This variable holds the current date and time. It's particularly useful for generating unique names for entities and screens each time the automation runs. For instance, in the example provided, the $entityName$ variable is set to "d_autest_$dateKey$". During execution, %dateKey% is replaced with the current date and time, resulting in a unique identifier like d_autest_25_06_12_11. $landscape$: Contains the name of the landscape for which the private node was created. This value is derived from the klarion.json file, indicating the landscape's name.

This file encompasses all the scripts generated by the test recorder. Essentially, it stores the test script or code in array format that was produced. Observing the header section of the tsData variable, we find an object containing several key-value pairs. Let's explore these details further. Remark: This field allows you to summarize what the entire specs entails or outlines the actions performed by the specs. A point to remember is that this summary will also appear as the specs name in the HTML report. Reload and Login: These should always be set to true to ensure that the login process occurs every time the automation starts. Menu: Used to specify the navigation path to the desired menu. The structure follows the pattern of the menu group name, preceded by a forward slash, and then the menu name. For instance, to open the Procify Data Studio inside App Builder, the menu entry would be “App Builder/Procify Data Studio”. It's important to note that both the menu group and menu name are case-sensitive. Note: Test Spec/Data files generated from the Test Recorder will not include the menu key-value pair in the header object. Developers must manually add this information.

This file encompasses all the function declarations originally listed or created in the myUtil.js file. Additionally, it provides a designated space for declaring any function that is intended to be utilized exclusively within its corresponding data file. NOTE :- In the spec_name.spec.js file, towards the end, there's a highlighted segment shown in the accompanying image. Within the loadData function located at the bottom of this file, you must include your spec's name as a parameter. This name should precisely match the one listed under the specs section in the conf.data.js file. To ensure consistency across your files and facilitate the automation process, it's crucial to maintain identical naming conventions. Any discrepancy in naming, including variations in capitalization, will prevent the automation from initiating.

This file will contain all the functions that you want to use throughout your entire automation. We can create function in two formats here :- Normal Function​ Standard functions will adhere to the conventional coding practices of WDIO. We cannot incorporate any code snippets formatted as arrays in this context.These functions prove beneficial when dealing with non-UI5 pages, such as the registration or login pages of our servers. These functions are utilized in scenarios where there is no requirement for using replaceMap or variable replacement from a replaceMap.json file, as the standard functions do not support the replacement of variables denoted by $variable_name$ for ui5 pages. As demonstrated in the following example, neither replaceMap variables nor code formatted as arrays are employed, eliminating the need for runtime replacements. To grasp how we can manage non-UI5 pages or write code in a standard format, let's delve into the following: The $ command serves as a concise method to retrieve a single element from a webpage. addValue: This function allows adding a value to an input or textarea element identified by a specific selector. click: Executes a WebDriver click action on the chosen element. By default, this action involves scrolling to and clicking the targeted element unless otherwise specified. In the subsequent example, we demonstrate the process of selecting a password field element and verifying its presence on the screen using the isDisplayed() API. If the element is visible, we proceed to insert the user's password using addValue and subsequently click the login button. Array Format Function​ Array format functions in the context of writing code snippets in spec_name.data.js allow for the creation of reusable functions that can be called multiple times within the file. These functions are particularly useful for performing repetitive actions, especially when those actions need to be executed in a recursive manner. In such cases, defining a function within myUtil enables you to easily invoke it as many times as needed without duplicating code. Using new test recorder that generates actions in an array format, you would parse these actions and pass them to your function.By structuring your code in this way, you can efficiently manage complex sequences of actions, especially when dealing with arrays of elements or actions generated from automated tools like a test recorder. This approach promotes code reuse and simplifies the management of repetitive tasks within your tests. Understanding functions, we recognize that they can be invoked repeatedly, each time with varying parameters. Following this principle, we too employ a similar strategy. To explore how we pass parameters, we'll initially focus on utilizing these parameters within our array format code. Specifically, we leverage the replaceMap.json file, which stores the values of parameters passed to functions at runtime. Essentially, we're retrieving these parameter values stored in replaceMap.json through a function designed for our array format code. Our methodology involves declaring a variable and importing a utility function named getWordFromReplaceMap from the kloAuWdio file into our myUtil file. This function accepts a variable name (such as $entity$, which is declared in spec_name.data.js) as its parameter and returns the corresponding value from replaceMap.json at runtime.

For Node.js projects, the package.json file provides a simplified way to manage a project's metadata and dependencies. The file ensures a project always has current information about the libraries and tools it needs to work correctly.Every npm package and Node.js project has a package.json file with metadata for a project. The file resides in the root directory of every Node.js package .The package.json file contains descriptive and functional metadata about a project, such as a name, version, and dependencies. The file provides the npm package manager with various information to help identify the project and handle dependencies. To install the dependencies, transfer your most recent package.json file to your automation directory. Afterward, navigate to this directory using the command prompt and execute npm install.
The configuration file contains all necessary information to run your test suite. It’s a NodeJS module that exports a JSON. No changes should be made in that file by the developer.

WebdriverIO-plugin for wdi5. It provides the ui5-service to WebdriverIO, running tests in the browser.In case the very first called page is non-UI5 (think SAP CP CloudFoundry login), the config option skipInjectUI5OnStart can be set to true to postpone injecting wdi5 into the browser context. Consequently you have to do it later, as soon as the UI5 page to test is available. This can be done by calling injectUI5() on the wdio-ui5-service. So, the UI5 service will prove beneficial when encountering a stale element reference error during automation, preventing the automation from halting or performing unexpectedly. The stale element reference error is a WebDriver error that occurs because the referenced web element is no longer attached to the DOM.Every DOM element is represented in WebDriver by a unique identifying reference, known as a web element. The web element reference is a UUID used to execute commands targeting specific elements, such as getting an element's tag name and retrieving a property off an element. When an element is no longer attached to the DOM, i.e. it has been removed from the document or the document has changed, it is said to be stale. Staleness occurs for example when you have a web element reference and Upon navigation, all web element references to the previous document will be discarded along with the document. This will cause any subsequent interaction with the web element to fail with the stale element reference error. To overcome this ui5 service needs to be injected again in the page again. Refer to the screenshot above for more details.

To utilize the $dateKey$ variable from conf.data.js in myUtil.js or spec_name.spec.js, the conf.data.js file must be imported into the relevant file and used appropriately since replaceMap does not operate directly within normal functions; it works only in array format code snippets. Additionally, it's crucial to note that if the $dateKey$ variable is required in the first spec_name.spec.js file, it must be imported from conf.data.js. However, if it needs to be used starting from the second spec onwards, it should be imported from replaceMap.json.

documents.t: When using variable names in getText() and getValue() actions, they should not be reused. Although it operates similarly to replaceMap, where initializing the same variable with a different value results in replacement, this principle does not apply when storing values from the screen using getText() and getValue() actions. In these cases, repeating variable names is not allowed.

documents.t: Occasionally, due to failed automation execution or termination mid-execution, the replaceMap.json file may become empty. Consequently, attempting to run automation afterward will fail to start. To mitigate this problem, an empty object must be explicitly declared within the replaceMap.json file.

For checkboxes within a grid, the necessary wdio code is not automatically generated. To resolve this challenge, the browser.keys() APIs should be employed as a temporary fix. Leveraging keyboard actions can also help address this issue.

If users are conducting validations on a UI-created screen following a full preview, certain codes need to be made dynamic. Otherwise, the automation will not execute correctly if triggered again or under different conditions. As illustrated in the preceding image, there are several areas (e.g., 2-3 spots) where the code requires modification to ensure successful execution each time the automation runs. For instance, consider the scenario where the automation's flavor changes; without making the code dynamic, the automation would fail. Additionally, the page name appears in both the view ID and model ID sections of the code. If a new page is introduced with a different name, the automation will also fail unless the code is updated accordingly to reflect this change dynamically.
documents.s: Validation for screen created in UI

documents.t: Sometimes, as noticed, once the menu is opened during automation, the process halts in the browser and begins displaying errors in the console. The primary issue here is that the replaceMap, which is intended to substitute variables for viewID and modelID at runtime, fails to do so; instead, it retains the original values provided in the spec_name.data.js file. To update the page's viewID and modelID with the current ones, since these identifiers change with every screen navigation, the automation executes the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console. This function retrieves the current page's viewID and modelID, which are then stored in replaceMap. If a match is found, the existing viewID and modelID in the code, formatted as an array, are replaced with the current ones. After the menu is opened in automation, the code proceeds to the next segment. Occasionally, the screen remains partially open, still showing the loading state. At this point, even though the code execution has moved forward, the screen is not fully loaded. Consequently, when the automation runs the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console, it returns the modelID and viewID of the previously viewed page, not the current one, because the page is still in the process of rendering and is not yet fully visible. Because of this, replaceMap does not work in this case. To address this issue, after the menu is opened, we need to insert a code block that does not involve viewID or modelID. The only element on the screen that lacks either viewID or modelID in its code block is the Procify logo at the top.
documents.s: replaceMap does not work after menu opening sometimes

documents.t: There may be instances where a list of elements exists, and a specific item needs to be selected from it. For example, choosing the screen type of a section from a VH list. As depicted in the image below, we generate code for selecting the search screen type from the VH list. However, within the code block, no mention of 'search' is made; instead, it merely indicates the specific path or index where the search type screen resides. If the path or index of the search were to change, the automation would encounter issues at this stage. To address this issue , we've linked it with "search" such that it consistently selects the “search” screen type from the VH list, regardless of the index. Let’s see how we will do that. Upon generating the code in procify control list section , navigate to the properties tab of test recorder. There we will be able to see different properties from which we will be able to bind this element. Therefore, among the highlighted attributes, we choose the ones that can uniquely identify this element. Specifically, for this element, both the title and description can serve as distinguishing features. Lets see how we can do the binding in the code block :- In this scenario, the path within the binding path must be commented, and a new key-value pair should be introduced, specifically 'properties'. Within the value of 'properties', there should be another key-value pair, which includes the attributes derived from the properties section of the test recorder, which we are utilizing for binding. Here we are using title as attribute for search property and providing its value as “search” .

Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5_1_120_27 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5_1_120_27. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process WDIO can work with any web application but lacks the awareness of the web framework that the application uses. WDI5, which is a WDIO plugin, bridges this gap and provides two key benefits, namely control locators and synchronization with the web framework. WDIO supports many types of locators - css, xpath, even plain javascript code but it lacks understanding of the UI5 controls. WDI5 exposes a browser.byControl() method that accepts a control locator and returns a proxy for the real control. Then the test can assert on the control state or even interact with the control. The second benefit is transparent but equally important – on every element interaction, WDI5 waits for UI5 rendering to complete and for the application to be completely stable.
documents.s: Use WDIO and WDI5 for testing UI5 apps
