documents.t: Set of frequently used values, which remains constant, are provided as variables. These are framework provided and are extensible in shared flavor. But can not alter the framework provided fields. $USER login_id, employee_id, (userID) Owning_bp ExtendedBP + application extended fields. USER data is synced as a part of initial sync. All updates on user data are communicated to relevant endpoints of the user by FW vai kloBrokermessage using a user entity. Client side user entity should update the global $user variable. $BP has me, bp_type, Has_own_tenant + application extended fields $ROLE $role is a configuration data that needs to be modified only on dev and deployed on QA,PROD. It does not depend on flavor/version. And available for extension in Shared flavor. Application maintained data in the extended fields. Useful for controlling the UI Controls visibility/ editability per role within the flavor. My Role date is synced as a part of initial sync. All updates on the role date are communicated to relevant users by FW vai kloBroker message. On assignment of a new app to a user this is also pushed to the user. $SYSTEM (readOnly) - non extendable by application. flavor --transient field and calculated in runtime and set version --transient field and calculated in runtime and set role - not Available as kloBroker userID - not Available as kloBroker isMiddleWare isScheduler today --transient field and calculated in runtime and set (date ) now --transient field and calculated in runtime and set (timestamp value) $GLOBAL Application defined fields act as global variables. Gives the substitute feature. Usage All the above global variables are accessible on the event object, $Global is only available in client. When used as a string literal in a meta model in query, id series, authorization it is replaced with real value. E.g. $USER.login_id will be replaced with the currently logged in user id. Syntax: ${<Variable name>.<property id>} API EnvironmentalVariable.getEnvironmentMap(flavor,version) will return the env variable map, which will have all the ENV objects as key- value pairs, and use the ENV variable name to get the actual Variable Entity. BaseController has API to access ENV Variables in Controllers, Please refer KloTouch API Example: event[‘$USER’].login_id; will return you the current logged in user id; event.getEnv(“” getDefaultEntityQuery: returns instance of Entity Query with specified name getDefaultBOQuery:

An attachment is any file or document that you upload against any object. Attachment component is used for uploading and downloading the mime (images, videos, audio, pdf etc). This is an entity level flag and it indicates that attachment is allowed to store against the entity. If enabled, the attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. Users can only add/edit/delete attachments when the component is in edit mode. Framework adds primary relation with attachment link entity and the Entity where attachment is enabled. The name of the relation is ‘attachments’. Within one BO, Attachment Entity can have relations with multiple Entities like order_hdr and order_items both are attachment enabled. Uploads a file in a common folder(local) and also maintains a link with the object. Mime gets pushed to the server repository via middleware. If the parent object is deleted, it deletes the attachment also but not the mime. Mime might have a reference with another attachment. Attachment with new entity: as attachment is part of the same BO, commit and rollback works like other entities in a BO. Mime upload to the local folder is separate and it does not rollback if the transaction is cancelled or failed. To upload or display the attachment UI controls are part of kloTouch. Steps to enable the attachment for an entity: Import kloAttachment in Account flavor/s. Attachment config. Enable attachment in the entity definition. Define attachment type. Define attachment subtype. Call the APIs to upload and download the attachment. Attachment config: Account Landscape Attatchment_upload_class: Fully qualified name of the attachment class which implements AttachmentHandler interface which has two methods upload and download. This class is to be written by an application developer. These methods are available in controller or Rule. Sample code is provided below. Content repository: Location(base path) to store the mime on the server side is part of this upload class. thirdParty_application: Client application. min_battery: minimum battery required for upload and download. If the battery level goes down and the user tries to upload/download, it ends with an error/warraning. Sample code for upload class: public interface AttachmentHandler { public void upload(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,String landscape) throws IOException, JSONException, JCodecException ; public Response download(String file ,HttpServletRequest request,HttpServletResponse response,String landscape); } public class CustomAttachmentHandler implements AttachmentHandler { public void upload(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,String landscape) throws IOException, JSONException, JCodecException{ //TODO } public Response download(String file ,HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response1,String landscape) { //TODO } } Define Attachment Type: once “Has Attachment is marked TRUE, the attachment section in Data Studio will be enabled where you can define the attachment type. Below are the attributes: Attachment type: this is to categorise the attachment. Like Product, Equipment, Invoice, Profile pic, etc. Doctype: indicates that document type of attachment like user manual etc Max Files: max number of files allowed to upload. Download Type/Sync Type: WIFI, Battery Level, Always. Mime type: This specifies the accepted mime types of the mime. One mime type is mandatory. Multiple mime types are allowed with comma(,) as separator. Allowed mime types are .jpeg, .png, .mp3, .3gp, .wav, .mp4, .pdf, .xls, .xlsx, .doc, .docx, .zip, .RAR Application has to decide the mime types. There is no exclusion from the framework side. Size per file: Define the max allowed size (in KB) of a file to upload. If file size exceeds, it ends with an error. Size is defined per attachment type. Source: There are different sources from where media files are allowed to capture. Multiple sources are allowed with comma(,) as separator. If only one source is selected, it directly opens Camera or Gallery or Mice otherwise this gives the option to users to select a source for upload. Camera Take Photo Record Video Gallery/Folder Mice Need Location: Capture GPS location while adding the attachment. Upload endpoint/location: location where attachment has to be dumped on the server. ( folder path, mount etc.) Entity Name: name of the transaction entity for which attachment to be allowed. Attachment should be enabled in Entity definition. Define Attachment Subtype : subtype is just a categorization to store the Sub Type: it is a sub categorization(child) of attachment type and it is optional. For example, uploading images of type equipment with subtype as front side, back side, etc. Entityname: Attachment link: This stores the entity attachment info. This link table has a primary relation with the transaction entity that means it is part of every BO attachment that is enabled. Table name is ‘dcatt_attachment_link’. Attachment ID: GUID generated for attachment. This gets generated at the client side. Attachment ID is a unique id across all the endpoints. Attachment Type: passed from UI as parameter. SubType: passed from UI as parameter. File name: Input from application and this is displayed on the UI. Entity Key: This is a unique key with a combination of entity name and primary key set. Mime Type: mime type(file extension) of the attached mime. Only one value is allowed. GPS Location : If enabled in setting, it captures the GPS coordinates. Is default: This is input from UI at the time of upload. Default marked attachment is considered for preview or thumbnail in UI. Sequence: Sequence in which attachment is displayed in UI. Attachment APIs: Upload: call onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError) function. Command Description Example onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError) This uploads the mime and makes an entry in the link table. As the link table is part of the transaction BO it gets updated with the BO. some_function_in_controller : function(oEvent){var parameters = {"type":"type1","subtype":"subtype1","modelName":"entity_name","path":"/list/0/attachments","objectType":1,"entityname":"entity_name",};oController.onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError);} Download: Command Description Example forceDownloadAttachmnet(attachmentId) This is to force download the mime from the server. oController.forceDownloadAttachmnet(attachmentId); Update: update attachment info like file name, is_default, etc. Delete: Use the Entity delete API. This deletes only the attachment link and does not delete the mime. Common folder : Common folder is used to store the mimes locally. This is hardcoded in the framework. While uploading the file it first copies the file to a local folder which might be different for mobile and desktop. Attachment id gets generated after the source of the image is copied to the common folder. Message processing: note that attachment entity and the mime are separate messages. Attachment entity message flow is similar to other entities and part of the parent entity’s BO. Upload: Mime messages get stored in _attachments table at client side and processed separately. From the device it is a direct Ajax call to the server for all the messages in _attachments table. Once it is synced to the server it makes an entry in the d_attachment_log table. Download: First check if mime is available in local storage. If not, a request is made from the device and mime gets downloaded to the local storage. This request is through middleware. Object cloning: attachment link is also cloned with the BO. This points to the same mime. Convert Object Type: attachment and mime does not get copied to the target object even though it is part of BO. Initial sync: write initial sync queries for attachment link. Download all: for all attachments, it loads the mime immediately after initial sync is completed. Download on demand: mime is loaded only on user request from UI. Send attachment with email: separate notification API. This is part of the Notification component. Archive Settings - Download/Upload only if: Download/ upload only on wifi Download/ upload only on wifi and power always download

kloConfig is application data defined during application development and embedded together with code. kloConfig data is maintained using kloTuner. kloConfig behaves like a read only entity, columns/property/fields called config property is defined by the application developer. Developers can specify multiple rows/ value set/ entityset for the particular configuration. Klobase selects and returns the qualified row at runtime. kloConfig is used to customise the application flow by using the variable value in code for decision making , or in UI for enabling disable/ controlling visibility of UI controls. All kloconfig except $Role are customizable per flavor, although best practice does not advise to change values across flavor. Broadly config needs below three parts to be completed to work: kloConfig Definition: modelling kloconfig by defining config properties with its type and Value Help if required. It follows a similar approach as entity definition. Providing default value is must for each config entity property, Default value is used for returning the value until real object values are loaded, hence default value must be most restrictive. Maintaining ValueRow per unique key. It should be done using kloTuner. Each row should be self-sufficient, it does not borrow values from other rows. Using the value: filtered row is returned by API, these APIs are async. To ensure value is loaded use fetch() to resolve. Until fetch resolves, the config object returns the default config property value. Configuration controls or changes the behaviour of the application. Below are the different type of configuration supported: Entity Config $Role Config Entity Status Config App Global Config

Possible set of configuration for an entity by which the application process flow or behaviour is controlled. Works when an entity is marked with ‘Has Config’ TRUE and configuration entity properties are maintained. Entity Naming convention: Framework creates a Configuration Entity. It is calculated from the entityname by replacing the first character to ‘c’. For example the main Entity is ‘d_order’ then configuration Entity gets created with the name of ‘c_order’. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. Configuration is Object Type and Flavor based. In case of no object type applicable to an Entity, default Object Type is -1. Configuration can be defined on any entity in a BO but it is recommended to define at root entity level. In case a child entity does not have an object type but the root entity has the object type, it does not consider the root entity object type. Metadata definition(Entity properties) for configuration entities is to be filled using Data Studio. Each config has to be defined as Entity Property in Config Entity. Possible values for a Config have to be maintained through kloTuner. Configuration is accessible throughout the application including Rules and middleware. <entity instance>.configP will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for this entity with respect to the current object this holds. If no object type is found / has an object type that is false, the framework will try to find a default configuration with -1 as the default object type. If no configuration is found, return an empty object. Define the configuration structure in Entity owning flavor only. Not customizable in other flavors. Configuration values are customizable across flavors. Steps for configuration: Mark ‘Has Config’ for the entity (d_order) in Data Studio. Framework creates a Configuration Entity. Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create/update a database table. One Entity has only one Config table and one value per Object Type in a flavor. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in kloTunner. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change/maintain the configuration. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Application behaviour can be controlled on client side or APIs/Backend based on the configured value. For Example, Sales Order has few configurations like: Credit Limit Check Free Goods Order Approval Order Close ATP Check Expected Delivery Days Part Delivery Allowed Configuration Entity name: c_order Field Name Data Type Possible values s_object_type int(11) (pk) All object types s_role varchar(32) (pk) credit_limit_check boolean TRUE/FALSE free_goods boolean TRUE/FALSE order_approval boolean TRUE/FALSE order_close boolean TRUE/FALSE atp_check boolean TRUE/FALSE expected_del_days int(11) Only Numeric values >=0 part_del_allowed boolean TRUE/FALSE APIs: <entityinstance>.config Returns config values of an object.This returns only one record for a given object type. Example: orderinstance.config or**this.config

If application behaviour differs on user role based, use role based configuration. Define Role configuration in Account “shared” flavor only. Not allowed to customise in other flavors. Config values can not be customised across flavor. Role and Designation of a user are two separate things. Example: One user can have only one designation. One user can have multiple roles assigned combined with ROT (Role+ROT is unique). Use for UI binding and business logic in controllers. Not available to use in server side Rules, MW because the role is not known in case of MW message processing, upload, etc. oController.getEnveronmentMap($role) will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for logged in user’s role. Entity Naming convention: Entity name is ‘env_role’. Steps: Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Framework will take care of loading the config values. No need to write additional queries. Run Update schema to create/update a database table. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change/maintain the configuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Examples: Manual header discount in order. Manual Item discount in order. Configuration Entity Name: env_role Field Name Data Type Possible values role varchar(32) (pk) All roles manual_hdr_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE manual_item_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE APIs: Command Description Example oController.getEnveronmentMap($role) Returns config values of the user logged in. This returns only one record for a given role. oController.getEnveronmentMap($role)

In case application behaviour differs based on custom status and object type, use status config. Define the configurations in account owning flavor. Not recommended to customise in other flavors even though it is supported. Config values are bindable to UI elements and can be used in UI and backend both sides. For a selected object only one row(set of configuration) is qualified. If no configuration is defined it will return an empty object. If the status value is not known and trying to get the status config, it will return an empty object. <entityobject>.statusconfig will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for the selected record. Entity Naming convention: It is calculated from the entityname by replacing the first character to ‘u’. For example the main Entity is ‘u_order’ then configuration Entity gets created with the name of ‘u_order’. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. Steps: If an entity is marked ‘Has Status’ TRUE, Framework creates an status config entity where object type and status fields are part of the primary key. Entity type is ‘Configuration Entity’. Framework will take care of loading the config values. No need to write additional queries. Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create a database table. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change/maintain the configuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Configuration Entity Name: u_status_config Field Name Data Type Possible values s_object_type int(11) (pk) All object types s_status_custom varchar(32) (pk) Status of selected object type s_role varchar(32) (pk) flavor_version varchar(32) (pk) manual_hdr_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE manual_item_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE

App config is a complete custom config decided by the application team. Use Global config in case of common or across BO scenarios or the scenarios where Entity, $Role and Status config do not fulfil the requirement. Define global configuration entities in any flavor. Customisation is allowed only in entity owning flavor. Depending on business requirements, multiple config entities can be created. Entity Naming convention: Entity name starts with ‘cg_’. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. Steps: Create a configuration entity. This entity should be a type of ‘Configuration Entity’. This is a completely customised entity. Framework will take care of loading the config values on demand and filter the config at application side. No need to write additional queries. Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create a database table. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change the configuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Example: Need a configuration to sync the objects to SAP with the restriction of BP ID and object type. Configuration Entity Name: cg_sync_to_sap Field Name Data Type Possible values flavor_version char(32) (PK) s_object_type int(11) (pk) All object types bp_id char(32) (PK) BP ID or ALL enable_sync boolean TRUE/FALSE

A domain is a unique set of values permitted for an attribute in a table. KloBase Datastore supports a variety of data types for property values. A domain represents data type. The following domain types are supported : CDomainType JS Type DB type MsgType Remark I8 number Number(3,0) number number I16 number Number(5,0) number number I32 number Number(10,0) number number I64 number Number(13,0) number number DEC number Number(p,s) number number B boolean Number(1,0) number (0/1) Returns true/false CHR string VarChar(n) string string ANUM string VarChar(n) string Not supported cwns string VarChar(n) string Not supported BLOB string VarChar(n) string string D Date Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) number (milliseconds) T milliseconds Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) number (milliseconds) DT / TSTAMP Date Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) UTC enabled CLOB Not supported GUID Not supported JSON Not supported DURATION Not supported Here, Domain is defined as an enum in CDomainType. Applications must use the JS Type for all coding purposes. Note: DT / TS is UTC-based date time, hence, must not be compared with local time as hard-coded time.

A network mode is a state, or means of operating, that a wireless network can employ. In other words, they describe the various operational characteristics of the wireless signals. kloBase supports a rich set of network modes. The two most frequent network modes are online and offline. Online: Online network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) to communicate with the server for day-to-day needs. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. For example, if the screen needs to show Open Orders, kloBO will go to the server to get the data for Open Order and give it to the UI for display. All the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. Offline: Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. The application stores the relevant data locally and keeps the local cache and server data updated as and when it finds connectivity. Browsers and installed mobile apps (client) both are capable of offline operations. Cached Online: It refers to the client’s capability to connect with the server whenever required. Speeds up the interaction of the client with the server by suggesting data from the local cache. Offline Confirmed: It refers to the capability of the client to serve data offline. The save (message) always goes through online. It modifies the local cache. There is no message flow from offline to server during modification. SAP Online: This refers to the capability of all the transactions that go to SAP via the gateway server. SAP Cached Online: Refers to the configuration of the web browser or mobile application in such a way that the contents (static and dynamic) are stored in the cache, and the next request to the page concerned can be satisfied quickly from the cache. enum NetworkModes { OFFLINE = "OFFLINE", ONLINE = "ONLINE", PREFERRED_ONLINE = "PREFERRED_ONLINE", PREFERRED_OFFLINE = "PREFERRED", SAP_ONLINE = "SAP_ONLINE", SAP_PREFERRED_ONLINE = "SAP_PREFERRED_ONLINE" }

The medium through which the end users log into the application is known as the client. Web browsers are used to open an online application, here the browser is the client. Similarly, when an Android application is installed on mobile to run an application, the Android app becomes the client. Each client is identified by a unique identifier called the endpoint ID.

Tenant is an environment or space created for the users' data storage. Physical data on a server needs to be partitioned across multiple sets of users. Generally, in any multinational organisation, each department owns a tenant. Each tenant is assigned a unique endpoint ID. Individual tenants can host data for multiple organisations.

Endpoint helps klobroker in sending and receiving messages across various participants. Each endpoint is identified by a unique endpoint ID. Every user logging into an application sends a signal to the server through the installed app. Hence, each installation gets a unique endpoint ID. Each browser gets an endpoint ID. Every individual tenant and the external system linked to the server have an endpoint ID.
When one endpoint (source) sends the instruction (message) to another endpoint. The receiving endpoint (target) gets the message through the channel.

The app is an object-oriented programming system*.* Flavor encourages program modularity, eases the development of large, complex programs, and provides high run-time efficiency. Flavors are integrated into Lisp and Symbolic program development environments. Applications can use resources available in the current flavor plus the version only. API for: Shared flavor + version. Core flavor + version. Current flavor + version.
The Business Object Editor is the blueprint of the interface in KloBO administrator that allows you to manage (create, edit, and delete) the various aspects of a Business Object.

The loadAll feature retrieves all available rows from the database, including all configured properties for each record, in a single query execution. To enable this feature, set the loadAll flag on the queryInstance object before executing the query: queryInstance.setLoadAll(true); To revert to the default behavior, disable the feature and then execute the query: queryInstance.setLoadAll(false); Note: Enabling loadAll may increase memory consumption and query execution time when working with large datasets, as all records and properties are fetched at once.

documents.s: Business Rules: Business Rules provide a true abstraction level and separation from the user interface. The business rule is not actively selecting user interface elements to collect input values, which allows flexible modification of the presentation and the rule itself. The same business rule can service any number of data controller views regardless of the view types

Thus metamodeling or meta-modelling is the analysis, construction and development of the frames, rules, constraints, models and theories applicable and useful for modelling a predefined class of problems
