The server treats all client connections equally and saves no information from prior requests or sessions. A website that serves up a simple static web page is a good example of the stateless model

documents.t: BOL Reference Guide Date of Issue: January 2023 Target Audience: Application Developer, Consultants. A Reference Guide for application creation, knowledge and work reference.

Parent Key Mapping: This is to auto populate the parent keys while creating an entity. Pass entity or JSON format on new entity creation. Keys are auto populated before save and accessible in UI controllers and callbacks. Key gets populated upto N level in a BO. In case if the object type is not passed, it will return with error. ID series gets generated on entity creation if applicable and populates the IDs to UI/Model. In case any child entity exists and ID is part of the primary key, it populates with the child entity also. Mapping for already existing objects. Like two BPs are already created and map these as BP relations. Primary relation: If primary relation is maintained for two entities, keys get auto-populated from the parent. To understand this, take an example of order creation. While adding a line item in order, the order ID gets filled from the header automatically. Aggregation: This is to populate the key in the entity which is not part of the same BO. Separate metadata input required if key mapping to be supported in aggregation relation. Or API to be provided. Association: This is a structural relationship which connects one entity to another. An associate between two entities is able to navigate from one entity to another entity and vice versa. From UI: From Callback: From Middleware message: Entity conversion: At the time of entity conversion from one object type to another, the new BO created is treated similar to new Entity creation from UI. Secondary key mapping: This is to decide either to perform create or update operation on messages received from Middleware. For example, order ID is a primary key in order BO and map this with legacy ID as secondary key. While processing messages from SAP this, if legacy ID already exists it performs update operation otherwise create operation. Field Mapping: Message processing Entity conversion Source entity Source entity property Target entity Target entity property Object type Mapping: entity conversion from one object type to another is allowed if maintained here. Source entity Source object type Target entity Target Object type

EntitySet is a collection of Entity objects. KloEntitySet extends the Array prototype. KloEntitySet has three behaviours. Query result: direct result of query execution. Part of primary relation: by accessing primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet. Part of non-primary relation: by accessing non-primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet.

Business Object (BO) is a logical unit used in a business. It is made up of one or multiple entities. E.g. If we take an invoice (bill of purchase) it consists of a header and purchased items. Header and item entities (tables) are required to store this information. Either item or header alone does not make any sense. So invoice header and invoice item entity together make the invoice BO. BO is a hierarchical tree of entities. Each entity must belong to one and only one BO definition. BO has only one root entity (top-level). The rest of the entities (child entities) are aggregated into root or other entities to construct the entity tree. kloBroker always transmits the full BO in the Message. When any entity becomes dirty it also pulls the root entity instance in the writeset. Deletion of any entity instance deletes all the cascaded aggregate entity instances. In authorization, all the authorization upon parents up to root are also applied except the middleware message process. Example: d_order (root entity/BO) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity)

The data object in KloBase is known as Entity. An entity has one or more named properties, each of which can have one or more values. Each entity in the KloBase Datastore has a key that uniquely identifies it. In simple words, we can say Entity is a database table. In DBMS, we store data in the form of a table containing information about entity types like order, address etc. In an order database, a table containing information about all the orders. For example, orders have properties like customer, amount, products, etc these are attributes which combine to make a table. One entity must be part of only one BO. Types of Entity: Persistent: Entity which physically exists/ stored in a database as a table. Fields in Persistent Entities could be either Persistent or Transient. Persistent Entity by default Tenant Dependent can be made Tenant Independent <roadmap> Persistent Entity by default are User Dependent can be made User Independent Transient: It is an in-memory entity that doesn’t exist in a database. All fields in Transient Entity are Transient only. It can be constructed out of query results or by code to hold the value at runtime. Messages can’t be communicated through Middleware using a Transient entity. Config: The application can create a config entity that holds the fixed values provided at design time . It can be accessed with a key only. Query does not work on these entities. FW only- Types: Metadata <roadmap> Archive <roadmap> History Entity Naming convention and length​ Entity names should use only English lowercase alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and up to 31 chars max length. The first char must be d/t/c based on type. Transactional (‘d’), Transient (‘t’), Config (‘c’). The following are auto-generated Status config starts with ‘s’ Custom Status starts with ‘u’ Framework entity starts with ‘m’ <roadmap> Archive entity starts with ‘a’ <roadmap> Union or archive and transactional entity starts with ‘v’ <roadmap> History entity starts with ‘h’ Each entity has one or more properties. Each entity property has one property type. Each property type has a domain assigned. Entity Entity Property (1-n) Property Type (1) Domain (1) Provide a unique entity name and mark if it is a root entity. The root entity is considered a BO. To define an entity you need at least one entity property, It could be either transient or regular (persisted in DB). Entity attributes: Attribute Description Entity Name : string Unique ID across all flavors. See the naming convention Is Root : boolean This defines the Root entity of a BO. BO Name is the same as this Entity Name. Root entity also behaves as BO. Entity Type Persistent/Transient/Configuration. Network mode This is an optional parameter. Effective network mode is determined with the following precedence rule. First having the highest precedence. 1. Network specified at QueryInstance Level. 2. Network specified at Query Metadata Level. 3. Network specified at Entity Metadata Level. 4. Network mode of Parent Query if it is a relation query. 5. Network mode of App. BO Name Name of Root entity name. Can create/read / update / Delete The default value is TRUE, insert/read/update/delete is allowed on the entity. False value forces insert/read/update/delete operation to return an error in the specified flavor. Use it for master and other protected objects to be editable only in maintenance or OEM flavor. Applied only on the Server side for calls initiated from clients. Server-side rules and kloBroker still allow even if false Check Dirty: re-evaluate all entities for dirty before calling on an update. Has created fields To know when and by whom facts are created in the datastore. if TRUE, s_created_on and s_created_by fields will be added. Values in these two fields are maintained only by a system, Application code can not alter this. s_created_on is a timestamp data type and s_created_by is the logged-in empID as a string datatype. Values of these fields are captured on user events hence if the entity is getting created by klobroker it accepts the value from the source. If a new entity is created within kloBroker message processing or by scheduler then technical user and creation time is recorded. Created By is the user by which the Background job is scheduled. Has modified fields To know when and by whom facts are last modified in the datastore. This records the last changed time and employee ID. If true, s_modified_on and s_modified_by fields are added. The system updates these fields on every create/change of entity. The system also considers the root entity of the BO updated together with the modified entity. Tri-State : 1. None: fields do not exist 2. byUser: value is updated only by user action. kloBroker processing does not modify the value. 3. always Has Status If TRUE, s_status and s_status_custom fields will get added by kloBase at the time of update schema. See more details in the Status section. Has Attachment If enabled, Framework allows the attachment against this entity object and the attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. See the Attachment section for more details Has Brand The entity is brand dependent or independent. if TRUE, the s_brand field will get added by FW at the time of update schema. See the Configurability section for more details. Has Object Type Entity follows Object Type behaviour. if TRUE, s_object_type field of type int(11) gets added by FW at the time of update schema. See the Configurability section for more details. Has Config Framework will provide a config entity which can be further customised with configuration fields. If object type is not applicable this is an object type independent config. Config is accessible in application by using entityInstance.config See the Configurability section for more details. <roadmap> Has Doc Flow <roadmap> Owns Doc ID <roadmap> Has History This is to maintain the changing history of a BO. If TRUE, it creates a separate blob or transactional table to maintain the history of all changes. Every change on an entity gets captured in the history table and the main transactional table holds only the latest record. The table name starts with ‘h’. Only on the root entity or full BO? Maintain change history only for specific status? Object type-based configuration? is this supported offline <roadmap> Has Archive This is to facilitate data archiving. This can be enabled only on the root entity/ BO. Always complete BO gets archived. Table name starts with ‘a’. One more table was created as a view which starts with ‘v’ to fetch transactions and archive table data as a union. > Is the ID series exhausted? - Server Side: Push data from the transaction table to the Archive table. This means data will get deleted from the main table once moved to the archive table. - Maintain configuration based on which data to be archived. - Background job scheduler to push data from transactional table to Archive table. While archiving no dirty objects are allowed. - APIs: archive(). This API will work only on the server side. - clearArchive() : this deletes all records from the archive table. - Update to offline endpoints. This deletes the entity in the local DB - ON_ARCHIVE event. - Query: by default, the query fetches data from the transactional table(d table) but if archiving is enabled, users can explicitly mark to fetch archived data. This is a union of both transactional and archived tables. - The IsArchived flag is returned TRUE by the framework if data is from the archive table. This flag can be used by the application to highlight archived data or disable edit options. - Do not allow the archived records to be updated. The framework throws an error if any dirty object is found for archived records. - Value help/ Association relation for archived masters. Example: - Update transaction entity: this should adjust the archive and view. - Add/Delete new property - New relation/ Delete relation - Client Side: delete data in client DB(local) and do not send any updates to the server. - API: deleteLocal() - kloQuery has deleteLocal(); Dependency: Does not allow you to archive until the related(supplied by application. Do not follow entity relation) object gets archived. Dependency is decided based on aggregate relations. Helper function to be written by Application to check if any dependent object exists. <roadmap> Has Time Dependent At any given point in time, an entity has a value for each of its attributes. If the values of any attribute for an entity may change over time and you are interested to know the value of an attribute at a particular point in time, it is meaningful for entities to have properties exactly when they exist and mark the entity as time dependent. In case you are interested only in the current value of the attribute, do not mark it as time-dependent. > This is to maintain the periodic(time-dependent) data with valid time. If any entity is marked as time-dependent, the framework creates below three fields in the table. In a BO any entity can be time dependent. - s_valid_from(Timestamp) - Validity start date and time. Part of the primary key. The default is the current date. - s_valid_to(Timestamp) - Validity end date and time. The default value is 31-12-9999. - s_active(boolean) - the latest record will be marked as TRUE. At a time only one entry should be active and the validity period should not overlap for two records. By default Valid from is current date but can be changed. Past date: Config to be maintained for a past date is allowed or not. Message processing(from SAP, device or to device) follows the config for the past date. If allowed it accepts the date from the message or UI otherwise it changes the FROM date to current. If the first entry, except the values provided from UI or Message, marks the active flag TRUE. In case of an update, modify the current existing active record’s s_valid_to accordingly(based on s_valid_from the new record). Also, mark the current entry as active flag FALSE and the new entry as TRUE. Both update and create should be in the same transaction. Mainly this will be used for master data tables where periodic data is required. For example, pricing, user address, etc. MRP/Pricing of a product can be changed periodically. Can not be changed based on object type or flavor. This can be defined only in the owning flavor of an account. <roadmap> Approval In case approval is required for a BO, at the time of creation of the BO it should not change the current record. Once it is approved, then only it gets activated. To consider this scenario, a separate blob table is maintained for ‘To Be Approved’ objects. Once final approval is done it will get moved to the main transaction table and activated. If enabled, an approval flag will be provided from the framework. - This is applicable for time-dependent and time-independent entities. - Configurable on object type based. Workflow will be discussed separately later. Is Metadata Has Tenant Is Config AppVariant Is History Is Archive Tenant Dependent TRUE Tenant Independent Configuration TRUE TRUE TRUE Transient TRUE Example: Take an example of order BO. Order BO has three entities: d_order, d_order_item, d_order_item. Out of this one entity has to be marked as a root entity to define a BO. d_order (root entity) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity)

Entity Property is also known as an attribute or member variable in an Entity or field in the database table. It holds the value in runtime. It has a Property ID (name) and Property type. Property names are used for accessing the value of the entity. The Property Type defines the data type and behaviour of the property. The behaviour of the Entity Property is captured in the meta-model by defining the below attributes. Attribute Description Entity Property ID Unique within an entity across all flavors. Can’t be changed later. Property Type/Element ID Select the existing Property type or create a new one. This defines data type, field length, precision, etc. It can be changed only in the owning flavor of an Entity. Selection of a domain, size and property type:Choose to existExtend fromCopy and override: copy any existing property type and change the parameters. This makes a copy of all attributes except Property Type ID.Create New Type Regular / Primary Key / Transient Field / Calculated Field /System Fields. / Secondary Key Value Help Select already defined Value help ID. Wherever this property ID is bound in UI, VH is automatically applied. Can be overwritten in the screen field. Is restricted Value Restrict the input value within the associated VH. Tri value: None, Strict(UI and BOL), Suggestions(Only UI side). (Note: Moved this to Entity property from Property type). Is Mandatory Empty or Null values are not permitted during entity creation/update. Do not force the UI as mandatory. Non-Key mandatory fields are not necessary for selection. Default Value Default values will be populated immediately after creating a new Entity. $ Variables can also be used. ID Series Mention the ID series here if applicable for this field. Naming convention: Max length allowed for property ID is 31 char. Only English lowercase alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) are supported. Entity property ID starting with ‘s_’ is reserved for systems fields by framework. Types of Entity Property: Persisted: Property which physically exists/stored in the database as a table column. Persisted Property-owning Entity also has to be a Persistent Entity only. Transient: Transient property is a runtime attribute only. Use this to hold some value at runtime. Example: query result alias value, value-filled or determined in rule, from UI set and get attribute. Primary key: Primary key of a table. Values of the set of primary key fields must be unique. If the field is the primary key, the isNull/Nulable property will be marked as false automatically. System-Defined Properties: Based on the relevant flags in entity definition, the framework provides standard columns in a table. Field name, Data Type, Label, etc are already defined and no changes are allowed here. Developers can’t add a system field in the following: Object Type Status Brand Tenant ID Created On Modified On Created By Modified By Valid From Valid To Active Source Field name Field DataType Has Object Type s_object_type int(11) Has Status s_status,s_status_custom varchar(32),varchar(32) Has Brand s_brand int(11) Tenant ID s_tenant_id int(11)(pk) Created Fields s_created_on,s_created_by Timestamp,varchar(255) Modified Fields s_modified_on,s_modified_by Timestamp,varchar(255) Date dependent s_valid_from,s_valid_to,s_active Timestamp**(pk)**,Timestamp,boolean Calculated Property: When the property is read, an application-defined get<Property_id> is executed. When the property is written, the application-defined set<Property_id> is executed. Mostly used to return some aggregated value based on other conditions. Works when is calculated property is selected in the entity property definition. These fields do not persist and cannot hold any value at runtime. It can only return some value. The getter/setter function will be provided by the application developer. BOL will invoke this method when the property is accessed. This property is also bindable in UI. Property with Variable, Method and persisted combination? Providing getter/setter function for the calculated field: Mostly used for dynamic calculations. Define an entity property in metadata. For each entity, the framework provides a <entityname>.ts class which can be used to define the getter/setter function of any property. Through KloIDE, the app developer has to write a getter/setter function for the entity property. These functions are accessible using entity objects. <entityobject>.<propertyID>() and this.<propertyID>(). When the getter/setter is invoked, this will be the entity object and you are free to access any property/relation of the entity. Example: Getter: Syntax of property getter: get<space><property name with the first letter capitalised> public Qty1 : number; public get Qty():number{ return this.Qty1; } OR public get Qty():number{ return 20; } Setter: Syntax of property getter: set<space><property name with the first letter capitalised> public set Qty(newVal:number){ this.Qty1 = newVal; } Note: ‘this’ is an instance of the current entity here. More generated helper functions of property missing like <propertyID>_vh

Entity relation relates one entity with another entity. Relation has a unique name within the Entity. Relation name is used for accessing the result of the relation. Assessing getter of relation as property returns entitySet object which gets filled on ES.fetch() resolve and also triggers data change events. Relations are categorised as primary relation, aggregate relation and association. Association: An association is a structural relationship which connects one entity with another. Given an association between two entities, one can navigate from one entity to the other entity and vice versa. Association relations can be across BOs. By default, each relation is of type Association if it is not marked as Aggregated or Primary. Example1: d_order_item (source) d_material_master (Related) Create a relation to show the material description, LOB, or other properties of the material. Example2: d_order_item (source) d_order (Related) If you want to navigate from the order Item to the order header. Define a relation between the Item as Source and Header as Related entity. Aggregated Relation: Aggregation is a type of association where two entities(tables) are tightly bound. In some cases, we might come across “whole-part” relationships between two Entities, in which one entity is a part of another entity. Such a relationship is known as an aggregation. An aggregation relationship can be described in simple words as "an object of one class can own or access the objects of another class. Aggregate relations can be across BOs. Primary Relation: This is a special kind of aggregate relation within the BO boundary. All entities in a BO are navigable from the root entity once unidirectional and only once. Below are the use cases of a primary relation: Message processing Keymapping Find Parent Example: d_order ( root entity) d_order_item d_order_conditions Here d_order is the root entity and the other two are child entities in Order BO. Hence relation has to be defined between these entities. Create a relation on d_order entity with d_order_item of type “Primary” and query property is “order_id”. Create a relation on d_order_item entity with d_order_conditions of type “Primary” and query properties are “order_id” and “order_item”. Define Relationship: Let’s create a relation between two entities using the Data Studio. To create a relation go to the source entity where you want a relation with another entity. Provide a unique Relation name. JOIN is constructed based on the defined relation. Attribute Description Relation Name The unique name is given within an Entity. Relation names and Property names can’t be the same. “Parent” and “Attachments” are reserved keywords. Related Entity Name of Entity with relation to be defined. Type of relation Either it's Aggregate or Primary type. If not selected, by default it is association type. Relation Query Select the relation query ID from the list. Cardinality (0:n, 0:1, 1:1, 1:n). The user has to select the correct cardinality for the relation. In this case, 0:1 is included in Join and if 0:n provides a separate query in VH. No validation on 1:1 and 1:n cardinalities from the BOL side.Description: describe the relation here in short. Relation Property Relation Property ID: unique within Entity.Source Property ID: Variables supported- Entity property ID and constants(number, single/double quote) comma separated. Source Property ID can be used multiple times.Related Property ID: it is entity property ID if the query type is Runtime and query property ID if query type is Modelled. Entity Name +Property ID in case of Runtime query. Can’t repeat within one relation.Related Entity property ID: new read-only column. Fetch from the selected query. Relation can be defined between two entities: Both Persistent Both Transient One Persistent and one Transient Variables supported: Source Property ID Entity property ID Constant: multi-value $VARIABLE Target Property ID Entity/Query property ID Call fetch on relation for business logic in UI and Rules. Syntax: <relation_name>.fetch().

Property Type is to define the behaviour of Entity Property(Database Table field) and Screen field. It is a reusable unit. Property Type has below attributes: Attribute Description ID Unique ID of Property Type within Landscape. Domain select Domain ID from a predefined list to define the data type. Length and precision of the field. Precision is applicable only for decimal data type. Specify length for decimal and ‘chr’ types. Value Help Define value help and assign it to property type. Value help will be applied to all the places wherever this Property type is used in UI or Rules. You can define restrictions(allow values only from VH list or accept manual inputs) on Entity Property. Authorization Text ID maintain the Text ID here which points to the actual text(Translatable). This text is available in the screen field as tooltip/caption/placeholder/validation(error) text wherever this property type is used. It helps maintain the unified text across all screens. Create Text ID in the editor. Default UI Format: Date ( Example: DDMMYYYY or DDMMMYY, ...)Numeric(currency, etc)Decimal Min Max Value Define min and max values allowed for numeric and string(chr) fields. This ends with an error if the value is not in a given range. This validation is applied in the UI. In the case of string min/max value is the number of chars. Extends From Extend from other property types and modify one or more attributes. Usage: Entity property Query Property Screen Extends: extend the existing property type to access the parent attributes and overwrite if needed. You can only extend one propertytype in your child propertytype. In the extended property type fill only the attributes which you want to overwrite, all other attribute values are inherited from the parent. Domain type, length, precision can not be changed in extended property type. Extend property type if: Data type, length, precision are same as these are not allowed to change in extended property type. One or more properties are different from the list below: Authorization Value help Text ID UI Formatting Min/Max value How to remove an attribute value in extended property type? Set null or empty string For example, you have created one property type called ‘customer’ and Text is provided as ‘Customer Name’. But in some scenarios you want to show the text as ‘Sold To Party’, in this case extend the ‘customer’ property type and create a new property type as ‘sold_to_party’ and change the text. A extends B. B extends C. All attributes of C are extended to A if not overwritten in B. Reuse: To define the common behaviour of multiple Entity/Query Properties, Property type can be reused across entities. It should be reused if entity properties are logically the same. Ordered Qty and Del Qty - not to use the same property type. But Ordered qty in two diff tables should share the property type. Property type should be different for Vendor and Customer fields in the same or diff entity. Both should be extended from BP ID because the data type should be the same for all. It is recommended to use the same property type for a field which is used in multiple tables as foreign keys. To understand this better let’s take an example of the Material Code field which is part of Material master as a primary field but also part of other tables like Order and Logistics items. Authorization: Authorization restricts the access of data(rows) valid for current logged-in users. Authorization on any entity of a BO is applied on the whole BO. Authorization is defined on Property Type and applied for all queries to the Entities wherever that Property Type is used. Do not apply Authorization on Query Property. For example, logged in users should be able to see only the Orders that belong to them. Below is the Entity definition: Entity Entity Property Property Type d_order order_id order_id d_order order_date order_date d_order customer_id cust_id d_order net_amount amount Here apply the authorization on “cust_id” Property Type to filter the orders of particular customers. If the same Property Type is used at other places, authorization will be applied on those entities also. In case you do not want to apply the authorization at all entities or apply the authorization at only one place, then extend the base property type and create a new Property Type. Variables Supported: $Variable Constants Syntax: const1, const2 In case authorization is applied on more than one property or multiple values in one property. Below is the behaviour: AND Operator: If authorization is applied on multiple properties in the same BO with different property types, all parameters will be ANDed. Example1: There are two properties in d_order entity customer and sales_person both have different property types. If authorization is applied on both, this will be ANDed. OR Operator: Used a property type with multiple entity properties in the same entity, all parameters will be ORed. (Reuse property type within entity). At the same time it will be ANDed with other parameters. Example2: There are two properties in d_order entity: customer and vendor both have the same property type, in this case both parameters will be ORed. IN Operator: If Multi values qualify for one property, all values will be considered with the IN operator. Example3: Authorization is set on the state field in d_order entity and multiple values passed at runtime, in this case all values will be passed with IN operator. Translation: This is to facilitate multilingual options for label text. Length suggestion on translatable text. Formation: Multi language setting. This is a global setting and not part of Property Type. Available options: Second language Only a second language.
For Entity APIs kindly refer to BOL Entity API 5.7.

Actions are the reusable functions defined inside the TypeScript class where application developers write the business logic. Type of Actions: Regular Actions. Private Actions. Rule subscription action. Override Actions. Remote Actions. Member Variable. TypeScript Class: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JavaScript. TS is an object oriented programming language with classes, interfaces and statically typed like C# or Java. This supports Inheritance, Abstraction, Polymorphism and Encapsulation. Import: to access any other typescript class you need to import the class in the declaration section of the class. Maintain the import class in metadata. Framework will generate the import statement with a full class path. Only current flavor and shared flavor classes can be imported. EntityName (Current flavor or shared flavor) or BO Util Class Name: Full file path of Import class Syntax: Import {class name} from “<class path>” Example(generated import statement): import {OrderUtil} from "SalesUsha/Base/Order/OrderUtil" Inheritance: inherit a class or interface by using extends keyword. All actions, variables in parent class are available in child class and can be overridden. Parent class has to be imported in Child class. Framework will generate the extended statement in file. Developers can not define inheritance. Typescript supports Multilevel inheritance but not Multiple inheritance. Syntax: class child_class_name extends parent_class_name this keyword: this refers to the current instance of a class. super keyword: super refers to the current instance of the superclass in the child class. Regular Action: On creation of an entity, Framework provides a <entityname>_gen.ts file which contains pre delivered setters and getters of all Entity properties, Relations, VH, etc. Framework also provides a class <entityname>.ts which inherits the generated class(<entityname>_gen) and developers can write their own action inside this class. These are reusable actions and accessible with EntityInstance in any Controller or Rules or Middleware and returns the desired result. On update of Entity/ EntityProperty the generated file will get adjusted by Framework. Can add the Import in <entityname>.ts class in metadata. Can not add additional imports in <entityname>_gen.ts class Naming conventions: Generated Class: <entityname>_gen.ts Entity Class: <entityname>.ts Regular Action: public <actionName>(parameters) : <return type>{ } It is recommended to follow the camel casing in Action names. File Path: flavor_version >> BO >> Class.ts Syntax to call Function: <entityInstance>.<function name(parameters)> Define any number of Regular Actions in a class. Regular Actions are always public. <entityname>.ts class extends the generated class(<entityname>_gen). The Extends statement is generated by the framework. You can access the related entities object of BO’s using *‘this.<relation name>.fetch()’ *in the entity class . *‘this.<relation name>’ *returns the EntitySet of the related entity instance. For example, Order BO has the order_item as a child entity, accessing the item entity object using ‘this.rel_order_item.fetch()’. The result set of the relation has to be type casted in relevant class objects. It is recommended to use a variable and store the return value in a temporary variable. let order_items : Entityset<order_item> = await this.rel_order_item.fetch(); Regular Actions of Entity class are available as a help on Entity instances while writing code. For Example, you want to check the stock of a material. Define a function called ‘checkStock(materialId:String)’ and write your business logic. Now this Regular Action is accessible wherever Entity Object is available. Base Flavor: Generated Class: export class Order_gen extends entitybase{ public get OrderID():String{ return “10”; } public set OrderID(OrderID:String){ this.OrderID = OrderID; } } Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "SalesBase/Order/Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { public saveOrder(){ //TODO } public updateRelease(){ this.getCustomer() //TODO } public getCustomer() : String{ return “c1234”; } }; Customer Account Flavor: Generated Class: import { Order } from "SalesUsha/SalesBase/Order/Order" export class Order_gen extends Order { public get SalesPerson(){ return this.em……. } public set SalesPerson(SalesPerson:String) : String{ this.em….setProperty(SalesPerson); } } Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "SalesUsha/Order/Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { Private custLoc: String; Public getCustomerLocation(){ super.getCustomer(); //TODO get customer’s location and set to custLoc variable return custLoc; } }; Private Action: Use protected Keywords for Private Actions. Private actions are visible only within the class, rest all are the same as Regular action. Can be called in all types of actions(Regular, Rule, Remote, Private). Can not call outside the defined class and child class. Super class private actions are available in the child class. Can have Event Context as parameter if needed. Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "SalesUsha/Order/Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { public saveOrder(){ //TODO this.getCustomer() } public updateRelease(){ this.getCustomer() //TODO } //this action is only visible inside Order class in all actions protected getCustomer() : String{ return “c1234”; } }; Rule Subscription Actions: Rule subscription actions are defined in the Entity Class(Developer Defined) or Utility Class and receive EventContext as a parameter. The defined actions can be subscribed only against that Entity. It is recommended to define rule subscription functions in the Root entity class. Define Rule action in metadata. Multiple ‘Rule Actions’ can be defined in one Entity class. Rule action should be public. Can call Regular and Private actions inside Rule actions. Syntax: public [async] <rule action name>(event: EventContext) This should generally return Promise<Any>. Promises should be resolved with Success or Error. If resolved with Error, the error code returns to the caller and this error results in a rollback and the whole transaction will get rolled back. Inside an Action if Promise is not returned then it is assumed to be a synchronous action. At a time only one rule is getting executed and other Rule actions are in waiting state. Promise has to be resolved ‘Success’ before executing the next Rule. If it is a synchronous action and does not return the Promise, immediately after finishing one rule execution it moves to the next action for execution. Can not change Rule action signature. Otherwise it will be considered as ‘Regular Action’. Can not subscribe to other Entity Class’s Rule subscription Action. Call Regular Action in Rule- Regular actions defined in Entity class <entityname>.ts can be accessed in the Entity Rules actions. Syntax: this.<actionName>(parameters) Call regular action in BO Util class’s Rule action eventContext.getObject() will return the Entity instance on which the rule has been subscribed. Call the Regular action on the returned instance. Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "SalesBase/Order/Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { public async saveOrder(event: EventContext){ //TODO } public updateRelease(event: EventContext){ this.getCustomer() //TODO } public getCustomer() : String{ return “c1234”; } }; Override Actions: Calculated property: no getter/setter provided by Framework. It has to be written by a developer in Entity class. Getter/Setter actions: override the framework provided getter/setter actions. Override used flavor Entity class actions. Generated Class: export class Order_gen extends entitybase{ public get SalesPerson() : String{ return “First”; } public set SalesPerson(SalesPerson: String){ this.em…...; } } Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "./Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { //override the parent class Action public get SalesPerson() : String{ return “First”+”Second”; } }; Inherit Used flavor class: Entity class actions: Inherits the entity class from used flavor and can override or add new actions. All actions and variables of used flavor class are accessible using the child class instance. In case if any generated action is overridden in base flavor Entity class and you are using the same entity in customer account flavor, the actions overridden by application Developer will be available in the customer account Entity class. Framework will generate the getter/setter in customer account flavor for only modified/added/deleted properties. Deleted properties getter/setter actions also get generated and return an exception. Base flavor: Generated Class: export class Order_gen extends entitybase{ public get SalesPerson() : String{ return “First”; } public set SalesPerson(SalesPerson: String){ this.em…...; } } Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "./Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { //override the parent class Action public get SalesPerson() : String{ return “First”+”Second”; } Private calcPendingQuantity(){ //TODO } }; Customer Account flavor: Generated Class: import { Order as Base_Order } from "SalesUsha/Base/Order/Order" export class Order_gen extends Base_Order { public get SalesPerson() : String{ return “First”; } } Entity Class: import { Order_gen } from "./Order_gen" export class Order extends Order_gen { public printSalesPerson() : String{ print(this.SalesPerson()); //This will print “First Second” here. } Public printPendingQty(){ ...print(this.pendinQuantity()); } }; Entity Remote Action: This is to execute an action on the server side from Client. If there is a requirement where you want to execute an action on the server side irrespective of whether the application is running ONLINE or OFFLINE. In case if the server is not reachable due to any reason, it will end with an error. Syntax: <entityInstance>.remoteActionP(<action name>, …..args, commitClient, commitServer). Define Remote action in metadata. Do not use Remote action as Regular action and vice versa. Can not call Private remotely. In case if remote action is called from the server side, the behaviour is the same as Regular action. Whatever modified on the client side is available on the server also(only the BO remote action called). Anything modified inside the Remote action, the modified state of the BO will reflect back on the client side. Dirty BO Commit on server and client side(save data in client DB) is based on the parameters ‘commitClient’, ‘commitServer’ passed. TRUE means commit and FALSE means do not commit. Default value: commitClient: FALSE, commitServer: FALSE All subscribed Rules get executed in case of commit. Middleware message: remote action save on client side should not generate the middleware message to sync to server because it is already saved on server. This can be controlled by the application developer. Exception handling: In case any error occurred on server side commit, remoteActionP(..) will return the reject. If the server side commit is successful and the client side is failed, the application has to handle this. Network error: Server side commit is successful but due to network error client did not get the success in response. In this case, remoteActionP(..) will return an error. Assume that remote actions can be executed multiple times so do not write any code which may create problems in case of multiple commits. Write this type of calculation logic on the client side. This returns what actual action returns with promise and Promise has to be resolved. This also modifies the BOs participating in the transaction and modified BO is available at client side. Example: check stock at the time of dispatch the delivery from the offline App. Call from UI: logisticsInstance.remoteActionP(checkStock, [event, materialID, location],FALSE, FALSE); Entity Class: import { Logistics_gen } from "SalesBase/Logistics/Logistics_gen" export class Logistics extends Logistics_gen { public checkStock(event: EventContext, materialID: String, location: String){ //TODO query to DB and check stock return availableStock; } }; Member Variable: you can define the member variables inside Entity or Util class to store values. Values stored in the variable/s are shared across Actions of a particular Entity Instance but should be defined carefully( if really needed) as this has the memory implications. Instance of the Entity class is available throughout the Transaction, the complete rule chain for an Entity is executed on the same instance. Member variables are defined inside class and outside actions. Static member/local variables must not be used. The static variables are shared across all users and all Transactions. Get approval from Project lead before use. Variables defined inside an action are only accessible locally. Variables should be defined carefully( if really needed) as this has the memory implications. Naming Convention: Variable names can contain alphabets and numeric digits. Can not contain spaces and special characters, except the underscore (_). Variable names cannot begin with a digit. Syntax: var <variable name> : <type>; var <variable name> : <type> = <value>; export class Order extends Order_gen{ var dislimit : number = 10; public headerDiscount():number{ //calculate discount } public itemDiscount():number{ //calculate discount } } Transaction Variable: To store the values temporarily you can also use a ValueBag object. This is available throughout the transaction. While using ValueBag it is recommended to define Variable name that has an embedded object ID because this is a shared property bag and has chances of mixing with other variables. BO Util Class: Application Developer can create his own BO Utility class to define the common actions which can be used at multiple places in the application. Class names can be decided by the developer and should follow Entity naming conventions and it has to be unique across Entity, Query and Util. Start the Util class name with ‘....’ Can define multiple actions and member variables in Util class. Can define public, private and Rule actions in Util class. Can call any member action inside other actions. Until class public actions can be called inside other classes like Entity Class, Query Class, Controller, View etc. This extends the Base flavor’s Util class. Can use EventContext to access the Entity object. Any modification using setter actions of the entity modifies the entity instance. In case any common action or validation is required across BOs, define a dummy BO and create Util class and define the action/s. You can define multiple dummy BOs if required. File Path: flavor_version >> BO >> <UtilClassName>.ts Syntax to call Util class Actions: <utilClassInstance>.<action name(parameters)> Define a Class: Create a class in the BO folder. Metadata entry is maintained by framework. Maintain metadata for import Class. EntityName (Current flavor or shared flavor) or BO Util Class Name: Full file path of Import class Application can’t extend the other class. Actions and Variables to be defined directly in Class file only. No metadata required. Syntax: Import { class name } from “<class path>” //metadata to be maintained class <class_name> extends Base_<ClassName>{ // Extends is generated by Framework //Define variables, actions here } Action Syntax: public/protected <actionName>(parameters) : <return type> { } Util class in base product: export class OrderUtil{ public headerDiscount():number{ //calculate discount } public itemDiscount():number{ //calculate discount } } Util class in customer project: import {OrderUtil} from "SalesUsha/Base/Order/OrderUtil" export class OrderUtil extends OrderUtil{ //Override the header discount calculation in customer project public headerDiscount():number{ //Calculation logic as per customer requirement } public itemDiscount():number{ super.itemDiscount() // call super class method //additional logic to calculate item discount } } Create new instance of a TS class: var orderInst = new OrderUtil() orderInst.headerDiscount(); Rule action in Util Class: export class OrderUtil{ public headerDiscount():number{ //calculate discount } public itemDiscount():number{ //calculate discount } public updateRelease(event: EventContext){ this.getCustomer() //TODO } private getCustomer() : String{ return “c1234”; } } Mime: CSS Class, JS, JSON, Audio, Video, etc.

A Rule is a program containing business logic written by a Developer as per the application's needs. It works with the event bus, any change in entity triggers the event, all the rules hooked to the event bus are executed sequentially. Rules are reusable objects across client, server and middleware. Based on subscription it is executed in the given environment. Define the Rule: Define ‘Rule Subscription Action’ in Entity/Query/Util class as a rule Define a rule with below inputs Rule ID - unique ID across all entities and queries. Class name: provide a class name it creates a new instance of a given class. Class could be Entity, Query, Util. Method: enter Rule subscription action name without signature. Mime Type: TS / JS Description Subscribe Rule: You can subscribe to a Rule for any Entity which can be executed based on the Event type assigned. Rule subscription is part of kloIDE. To subscribe to a Rule you need to provide below details. Recommended to subscribe to the rules on the root entity of BO. Rule should generally return the Promise<Any>. Promises should be resolved with Success or Error. Rule ID(PK): select existing rule on BO. BO Event Subscription ID: this is auto generated id. Event Type: ON_CREATE : execute on creation of Entity. CREATE_NEW_FROM_TEMPLATE : execute only if executeCreateFromTemplate() method called from application. ( deprecated) ON_UPDATE : execute only on update entity. ON_DELETE : execute only on delete entity. <roadmap>BEFORE_MAPPING <roadmap>AFTER_MAPPING Some additional Event types on Root Entity(BO) ON_SUCCESS : execute only after the successful transaction of a BO. ON_ERROR : execute only if the transaction failed for a BO. ENDPOINT_RESOLVER : this is to get all the endpoints to push the kloBroker message. This gets called on every create/update/delete of a BO. Object Group: This is optional and If Object Group is not specified, it will get called for all objects of that entity. Channel Type: there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule. All Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON CLIENT Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON SERVER Endpoint/Device to Server/Client---NETWORK CONTEXT SWITCH Klarion Server to Klarion Offline Server Klarion Server to Klarion Server Legacy to Klarion Server Sequence No(Mandatory): Decides in what sequence Rule to be executed. In case multiple Rules subscribed, sequence of rule execution is followed. All positive numbers(1-n) excepted. It is recommended to maintain the sequence like 10, 20, 30 and so on. So that any new Rule can be maintained in between without disturbing the other rule’s sequence. Rules are reusable hence can be subscribed multiple times with different Channel types or other combinations. Qualification of rules for execution:

Offline Mobile Application. On offline Network mode dirty entity is saved rules are filtered based on All Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON CLIENT Endpoint/Device to Server/Client---NETWORK CONTEXT SWITCH When message received on server from mobile following rules qualifies All Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON SERVER When Message is received from Server to mobile client Klarion Server to Klarion Offline Server Online Application On online Network mode dirty entity is saved rules are filtered based on following on client All Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON CLIENT On online Network mode dirty entity is saved rules are filtered based on following on server All Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON SERVER Endpoint/Device to Server/Client---NETWORK CONTEXT SWITCH Tenant to tenant On receive on server All Klarion Server to Klarion Server From Legacy to Tenant On receive on serve All Legacy to Klarion Server How to choose channelType: For Tenant to Tenant (K2K) there is nothing much to choose. Same for Legacy to Tenant (L2K) When it comes to core processing, we are talking about interoperability of network mode. Selecting event types for part of code becomes critical.

If any change in the DataSet of an Entity at any level of BO. Root entity is also set to WriteSet. Rules will be executed for all dirty objects one by one. Each record in an entity invokes the Rule. Execution is from Leaf Entity(of BO) Rule till Root Entity Rule for all WriteSet . First call all rules of the lowest level( Leaf Entity in a BO) Entity. If multiple BO changes are there in one WriteSet, first execute the rules of the lowest level entity in all BOs then next up… then next up. Within one BO if multiple entities are dirty but Root entity rules will get called only once for one BO. At the same level rule execution is as per sequence number( smallest is the top priority). Execute rule is based on Channel Type. Again jump to Child entity Rule if any modification by parent entity Rule. Example: For a BO all child entity rules are executed and now executing the Root entity rules, in that one child entity object is updated by root. Now only the updated child entity rules will get executed and root entity rules will not get called again.

Rollback Transaction: This cancels the full transaction and refreshes the Changeset/Writeset. Stop Rulechain only for the current entity Instance. Stop Rule chain only for the current BO instance. Eliminate the object from the writeset (refresh entity/BO using ‘refresh(deepRefresh)’) : Flush Changeset (commit) : Flush current transaction with intermediate commit. - Deprecated. Use the parallel transaction getTransactionParticipatingObjectsAtLevel(); Note: Developers should not use commitP() by using the same transaction at the rules callbacks. e.g., get the transaction from oEvent (function parameter) and use that for commitP() later on in the rules callback. Validation added in case the same transaction is being used for commitP() from callbacks throwing an error as “Transaction commit is already in progress. Please wait for the current commit to finish before calling commit again.“. Rule callbacks are now triggered on every transaction commit, even after a previous commit failure. This ensures consistent callback execution on the client side and also on the server side. How to write a Rule: Rule actions can be defined in Entity/Query or Util class as explained in the corresponding sections.

Middleware allows a set of configuration on its functionalities.

This method allows to attach a new message processor, a message processor is a class which intakes a downloaded message and builds the BO structure out of it and persists these BO/Entity. When middleware starts processing the downloaded message from the server, based on the download process count, messages are read and the message processor callback is invoked with the messages. Now, the MessageProcessor class is responsible to deal with the message and resolve when the message is processed or rejected in case of error so that middleware can continue processing the next message and handle errors on the current message. By default, Klarion BOL will attach a MessageProcessor class to handle the V4 middleware messages, in case the message processing has to be changed, attach a new MessageProcessor and encapsulate the logic to it only the expected return is a Promise and resolve or reject. Example: kloBroker.attachMessageProcessor(function(messages){ return new MessageProcessor().process(messages);})

Allows to attach convertor callbacks, which has to be called before BEFORE_ADD_TO_UPLOAD_Q BEFORE_PUSH_TO_SERVER_Q AFTER_PULL_FROM_SERVER_Q AFTER_LOAD_FROM_DOWNLOAD_Q These callbacks are called with the message object which can be morphed according to the application logic and the resultant message is considered by the framework. Each callback is expected to return the morphed message, or a Promise and resolve with a morphed message. Each call back can get an array of messages, and the call back should be able to handle this. Example: kloBroker.attachConverter(AFTER_PULL_FROM_SERVER_Q,function(messages){ //manipulate and resolve or return data here }) Dependent Entity: Maintain a dependent entity while subscribing to the endpoint resolver. This will be sent with a WM message under the Dependent[ ] section. Any entity is allowed. Relation is not mandatory.

Notification is an alert message like sms, email and notification in an app(fcm). Notification can be sent whenever it is required. This will work similarly like an endpoint resolver, it can send notification for multiple receivers. Types of notifications: Email notification SMS notification Application Notifications (fcm) API in javascript - var notificationEP = event.addNotificationEndpoint (Template_id, Channel,Object); Possible receiver ID can be for email TO and CC To persons can be set using setTO notificationEP.setTO([“userid1”,“userid2”]); To keep CC for emails use To setCC notificationEP.setCC([“userid3”,“userid4”]); These API are available in all type of exits(i.e ON_CREATE, ON_UPDATE, ENDPOINT_RESOLVER) Template Maintenance: Notification information should be maintained in the m_notification table entity so that notification mapping can be maintained in this table. This has a column for enabling different types of notification (i.e enable_email,enable_sms,enable_app) Template that has to be maintained in m_notification_template table and template can maintain channel type combination (i.e template id same but content is different for channel type). In this table we can maintain content. Exits while sending Notification: Notification exit can register, this exit is similar to normal exits but in this exit event.getObject() will return json object, not entity instance. Here, the json object can be modified at the end this json will take to manipulate the template. In this exit, all features are available like getEntityQuery, getQuery, getBOQuery, loadEntity can create a new entity at the end it will commit. Template writing: Sample template Dear <%=customer_id%>,

Your order is received with ID <%=ref_id%>. To track use the ID logistic id <%=logistics_id%>
Your invoice status is <%=inv_status%>.
Your Vendor id is <%=vendor_id%>.
<% logistics_item.forEach(function(item){ %> item id <%=item.logistics_item%>, material description <%=item.material_desc%>. <% }); %> JSON used to manipulate the above template {"ref_id":"PO076699","s_object_type":"403","ref_date":"2019-03-15 05:30:00.0","s_tenant_id":"2","inv_status":"INV_PENDING", "logistics_id":"030cc14a35ef32e4bb8c13d3bd4ada32","s_created_by":"21764", "currency":"INR","s_status":"DL_CREATED","logistics_date":"2019-06-19 16:57:14.0","s_created_on":"2019-06-19 16:58:20.0","s_modified_on":"2019-06-19 16:58:20.0","vendor_id":"21764","customer_id":"UNDB", "S_modified_by":"21764", "remarks":"Delivery to warehouse", "Logistics_transport":[{"s_tenant_id":"2", "logistics_id":"030cc14a35ef32e4bb8c13d3bd4ada32", After manipulation Dear UNDB, Your order is received with ID PO076699. To track use the ID logistic id 030cc14a35ef32e4bb8c13d3bd4ada32. Your invoice status is INV_PENDING. Your Vendor id is 21764. item id c48f97d11d673eb1a41a8290639a5f47, material description 600MM WIND W/O REG IVR CF. More details regarding template writing:- http://akdubya.github.io/dustjs/ Notification working flow:- This is similar to an endpoint resolver, it will collect entity, sender details, channel and template id at the end of the transaction it will put to queue. After that scheduler will take this data from the queue and it will send notification to the respective receiver. SUCCESS log goes to the dmqp_tenant_log_q table and FAILURE log goes to the dmqp_tenant_error_q. Sender Details:- Multiple sender details can be maintained, it will take sender details in a round robin algorithm. Sender details have to be maintained in the config.json. Template Details:- Template details has to maintain m_notification_template table: Template Details Functionality template_id It is the ID set by the caller. body It is the actual detailed content of the notification that is required to be shared. channel The channel or mode through which the notification is to be sent. This can be SMS, Email or Applications. setURL For Notification type APP config value URL can be specified using the following method:notificationObect.setURL(“index.html#work_order/detail”);

Object Type defines the possible behaviour of an BO/Entity. Object type has a unique key and description. Object type key is unique across all entities and can not be reused across entities. One entity can store multiple objects data if behaviour of the objects are different then define multiple object types. On the Entity Config, role based filters can also be enabled. Once the role is enabled, config picks the row from klotuner where object type and role both match. Works when has_object_type is marked TRUE for an entity. Do not add any Entity property to add object type field, this will be taken care of by kloBase based on the Object type flag on Entity level. Possible object types for an entity have to be defined at design time and maintained via kloIDE. Data type is int(11). Max value is 2147483648. Supports merging based on user relations. s_object_type holds the object type key. Descriptions are part of value help definition. Constants for Object Type. If the object type is false for an entity then -1 is a reserved value. Abbreviation : define object type abbreviation like ‘i’ for invoice and ‘o’ for order. This abbreviation can be used in ID series as a prefix. Syntax: $objecttype.abr Variable to be used: Constants $VARIABLE Object Group to Object Type Object Type to abbreviation Object Type to Object Type text Display Messages: Object type description supports translatable description use as substitute in title, message, etc with $objecttype.dec. Define language dependent text to support multilocal. Create Entity: while creating an Entity, Object Type has an important role to load the configuration, assign ID from ID series, Rule to be executed, VH to be loaded. Tuner: configurations are maintained on object type to control the behaviour of the application. For more details please visit the Config section. Rule subscription: rules are subscribed on Entity and Object Type. ID Series: ID series can be defined on object type or common for all object types. Middleware Message processing can be controlled in an endpoint resolver. Create operation (in UI-action or Rule) decide which object type to be used. From UI you can pass only the Object types which are part of the Object Group of that screen. UI elements behaviour can be defined like editable, visibility, mandatory, etc. Not supported: Authorization is not applied on object type. For example there are different types of orders. Object types in Order can be defined like: Normal Order Emergency/Fast Track Order

Collection of Object Types is Object Group. Screen usage Object Group which defines the behaviour of a particular screen/object. Object types of similar kind of behaviour and going to be used in one screen has to be bundled in one Object Group. Object Group to Object Type mapping(m:n): One object type can be part of multiple Object Groups. One screen can have only one Object group. Abbreviation : define object group abbreviation like ‘i’ for invoice and ‘o’ for order. This abbreviation can be used in ID series as a prefix or some other cases where you want to differentiate the object. Usage: Screen Rule execution Example: Object groups in Order: Sales Order Purchase Order Stock Transport Order

The Status of an object represents the current state of a particular object. Possible status of transactional objects is maintained in a meta model using kloIDE which has Key and Description. Based on the current status of the object, screen behaviour can be controlled like Visibility, Read-only, Actions, other behavioural decisions, etc. Work when has_status is marked true for an Entity. s_status column is created in all the entities where Has Status is marked as True which holds the status key. Supports merging based on user relation. To understand Status usage let's take an example. There is an Order placed on any online web portal. Order has the status like Order Placed Dispatched Delivered Cancelled Returned Here the first three status are sequential but order can be cancelled only with the status “Order Placed”, “Dispatched”. Also “Dispatched” and “Delivered” status can be changed by Delivery Boy or Backend team but “Cancelled” status can be set by Customer, Supplier Backend team and Customer Care Executive. Status Types: None Single Multi valued Custom status Customization of status as per account/rollout. Works when status is marked true for an entity. Possible mapping between status as per implementation is maintained in m_status_custom table as metadata. Supports merging based on user relation. Used in the implementation phase. s_status_custom holds the value of the custom status key. Description, icon or additional properties will be part of value help definition. Object type will have -1 if the entity does not have object types.

KloBase(kloudBase) is an extremely comprehensive, enterprise-class low-code (or no-code) platform. kloBO (kloud Business Object) is one of the most important pillars of kloBase. It is a mid-tier in the KloBase architecture that is based on a meta-model. Features of kloBO: kloBO immensely simplifies the process of application development. It ensures the application's best performance by applying many standard tricks by itself and also provides a low-coding option for modelling and gives independence for choosing database vendors. It accelerates the application development by providing reconfigurability, compatibility (browser, android app, IOS app, windows mobile app) and full abstraction for the multi-tenant cloud. Developers can write the business rules in JavaScript and based on the deployment model, kloBO runs it. KloBase promotes microservice with stateless models that give immense portability and infinite scalability to meet business requirements. Data exchange with multiple users within the network becomes easy with the help of in-built klobroker. KloBO can be visualised as Object Relational Mapping. Each entity(table) represents a class that is capable of saving its data; entity properties acting as class members and rules acting as methods. The behaviour of kloBO varies as per the environment. Given the same model (meta-model for application), the behaviour of the query, when it is executed on a UI (device or browser), is different compared to when it is executed by kloRule as Business Logic. Let’s see the working example for Order Object: A simple example of reading and writing Data let q = kloQuery.getQuery(“d_order”);q.orderid = “1234”;;let es = await q.executeP();If (es.count >0){let ord = es[0];ord.qty = Ord.qty +1;await Tr. commit();

Query statistics helps the developer boost the application performance by providing useful information of queries to be executed on the server. Query statistics contains a list of queries and the number of times they are executed on the server within a given period. It also provides the information like max/min time taken by the queries. Application developers can find the query statistics data in the “query_stats” table in the transaction DB.

KloScheduler is a program that schedules any operations that are required to be executed at any particular time period. Schedulers are of two types namely, server side scheduler and client side scheduler. Server side scheduler handles all events or tasks that are scheduled on the server side. This is generally used for monitoring tasks, notifying task completion, scheduling reports, and monitoring performance etc. This is also used to notify any open notifications or work orders to responsible users through app, email or sms. Client side scheduler runs on applications and browsers. When an application is loaded after registration or after refresh in the browser, the scheduler automatically gets triggered and continuously runs from there until it faces any error or the application gets closed. Client side scheduler works both in online and offline mode. When the device is in offline mode it receives data or task reminders through push notification. The scheduler also clears unwanted data from devices (Eg: closed or completed notifications or work orders from client side databases). Metadata for Scheduler: Field Mandatory Default Value Remarks schedulerid X Unique ID that is to be used for scheduling any task or event.**Each application(flavor) has a different scheduler ID. In case two or more applications have the same scheduler ID, any one task is picked automatically by the scheduler. Mandatory*(Applicable only for Client side)* False Mandatory helps in getting any particular task done that was otherwise skipped in the scheduled time period due to some unforeseen reason.For eg:-If a task is scheduled for 8:00 am every day and the application is not running that time then that particular task gets skipped . If mandatory is marked as true then that skipped task can be run any other time when the application is running. Cron Expression It is used to specify a certain date and time interval in which a scheduled task needs to be executed.For more information (Read this) exit_id Whenever a framework runs the scheduler, it calls for an application file. The application file (also known as the js file) contains the business logic in it.**[**File Path - **flavourName/util/filename]**Here,flavourName -> app nameutil-> the file where business logic is saved.Filename -> Name of the file that is being executed. Params Params implies application (flavor) and version name that determines which flavor and version mentioned as exit_id need to be executed.Eg:-{"flavor":"usha_order_ui", "flavorversion":"1"}Here,Flavor-> the application usha_order_uiFlavor version-> version 1. Network*(Applicable only for Client side)* Network is online and offline. We have two types of applications: online and offline. When a scheduler runs in an online app, if the network is interrupted then the scheduled task will also stop. On the contrary, in an offline app the scheduler doesn't face network interruption as it does not require any network. isdevice False This is a boolean field which states how many devices are connected. This has two values, true or false. When set to true it runs on the client side, when set to false it runs on the server side. s_tenant_id This implies the tenant identification used for entering the scheduler. Invocation_methoddeprecated This specifies the name of the action that is to be executed. This is a part of the Rule ID.

A stack trace (also known as a stack backtrace or stack traceback) is an incredibly useful tool when it comes to debugging code. A stack trace shows the call stack and provides information on the query/transaction save that your code called. The stack trace contains the information,status and list of all the queries and exits called during execution of a query or on transaction save. Information provided for Query in stack trace : queryID queryParameters querySQL queryResult totalTime taken Information provided for Exits in stack trace: entitykey eventType exitID, channelType exitClass resolved status Stack trace information will be available in the transaction. Application developers can enable or disable the stack trace for an application. Stack trace can be enabled by specifying the following url parameter “enableStackTrace” as true. <URL>/index.html?enableStackTrace=true# Example: transaction = new Transaction().getTransaction(“txn”)); tansaction.stackTrace will return a stack trace of the queries and exits called in that transaction. clearStacktrace: clearStacktrace method can be used for clearing the stack trace in the transaction. Example: transaction.clearStackTrace();

Once an entity is defined in the meta model, run the Update schema to convert an entity to a physical database table. All the entity properties and the system fields as per entity definition are part of the Database table. Create a new table. Add new fields in a table. Add/Remove any field (existing) from the primary key set. Unused table: show unused (not defined in meta model) table list. Show unused (not defined in meta model) fields in a table. Datatype change of any field. Create and drop DB indices. Run update schema on: All Entities (Landscape). One Entity. Update Schema can be run in two ways: Direct Run: update the schema without preview. Preview & Run: see the changes list before updating the schema. Not supported: Unused tables and fields are listed in the output. Deletion of table/fields to be done manually after verification. Drop table Delete field Updated schema UI is part of Admin.

In Application, ID/key is frequently used to store the related data and at the same time in the user interface descriptive explanation is required. To achieve it, the ID/key is represented by other single/ multiple data from the related table. Value help is also used to supply the choices available to fill (combo, dropdown, auto complete) as selection data. Value help can impose the restriction for accepting the input value only from valid sets. Value Help (VH) is an independent reusable object hence as a best practice always check the existing VHs for reuse before creating the new one. While creating a new one always categorises with entity names so later others can find it easily for reuse. VH definition can be overridden in any used flavor. Except VHID and Entity Name(Group By), all parameters can be changed while overridden. Caching: VH values which are used by the user will get automatically cached on the browser. If the required value is not available in cache, the query gets fired to DB. Usage: Provide users with a set of possible values or suggestion items in the UI. Get the suggestion list in callbacks. Show descriptive explanation in user interface. Steps for Value Help definition and usage: Define the Value Help. Assign the Value Help. Maintain Suggestion List (If applicable).

Attribute Description Value Help Name Unique ID across all flavors.Naming convention:Length: 32 charStarts with **‘vh_’**Char and numeric are allowedSpace is not allowedNo special character other than underscore ‘_’ Entity Name/Group By Used as grouping ID with provider entity name. Value help is provided either by an entity or generic, hence it is grouped by an entity.Example: material master can provide a value help that gives material_id and material_description and can be used at multiple places like sales order or in procurement or delivery. VH Type Select any of the below types.QuerySaved QueryVH TransactionVH Language DependentConfigConfig Language DependentSystem Fields Parameter Depending on the VH type selected, select the ID here. Like:Query : Query ID or Entity Name(incase of Runtime query). In case if a query is not available, define the query first then you will see in the list.Saved Query : Select the available Saved Query ID.VH Transaction & VH Transaction Lang : defaulted with VHID. Can be changed if needed.VH Config & VH Config Lang: defaulted with VHID. Can be changed if needed.VH System Fields : N/A Help Text Fill about VH so that other consultants can easily understand the purpose of this. Length: 255 char. Key Name of entity property of returned entity. The returned value is mapped with Key.Valid for Query, SavedQuery types only. Select the entity property from the suggested values. Value Name of result entity property from which value came and exposed as l_fieldName. Select from the suggested values.Valid for Query, SavedQuery types only. Icon Name of result entity property where icon is maintained.Valid for Query, SavedQuery types only.URLImage PathFont Path Dependent Name of the QueryProperty where the dependent-on field value is passed as input. For example, state VH is dependent on Country value. In this case define Country as QueryProperty and maintain the same as Dependent.Multi attribute is not supported.Three or more level dependency is not supported (Only two levels supported).Not applicable for System Fields VH type. Life Cycle This is about when to load the VH values.On Session: Loading VH on first time request and cache till the session is alive.On View: Loading VH on first time request and cache till view destroy.Dependent: Reload on change of parent value and cache.Live Change: Load values every time based on the time interval defined in UI control. Preview: Provide VH preview in Data Studio. It should ask for the input in case of dependent or query parameters. Suggest existing value helps based on the parameters input by the consultant at the time of creating any new VH. Can select existing VH if fulfils the requirement. Example: VH Name Entity Name/ Group By VH Type Parameter Help Text Key Value Dependent vh_mat d_material_master Query d_material_master …... material_id material_desc vh_state d_state Query q_statelist …… state_id state_desc country vh_city d_city Query q_citylist city_id city_desc state vh_priority VH Transaction vh_priority N/A N/A vh_priority VH Config vh_priority N/A N/A vh_status System Fields ? ?
