documents.t: Developer AI is an enhancement to the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform that enables users to build enterprise applications by describing their requirements in natural language. Instead of manually configuring application components, users can generate applications through a single prompt, significantly accelerating the application development process.

We can access Developer AI from chatbot, the chatbot Icon is preset beside notification icon, in Homepage header Note: The chatbot icon is displayed only when Developer AI is enabled for the current landscape. If Developer AI is not enabled, the chatbot icon will not be visible. After click on this chatbot Icon, it will open the chatbot, from there to use the Developer AI, click on “Advanced Mode “ option, which will open the screen for using Developer AI

The Upload Business Requirement Document screen is the first step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this step, users select the target application, review the available AI token quota, and upload the Business Requirement Document (BRD) or Business Blueprint (BBP) that Developer AI will analyze to generate the application. Select Application​ The Select Application dropdown displays all applications, select application with Developer AI enabled the selected application acts as the target application where Developer AI will generate all the required components. All AI-generated artifacts, such as entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, and configurations, are created within the selected application. Ensure the correct application is selected before proceeding with document upload. Note :- 1. Developer AI not Enabled for Application If Developer AI is not enabled for the selected Application, It will show warning that Developer AI is not enabled for that application 2. Developer AI server is not available If the Developer AI Server is not running, a dialog will be displayed with the message: “Developer AI server is currently unavailable. Kindly contact the Administration team.” 3. BBP Build is triggered when other BBP build is in-progress in the same application If Build is triggered in the same application when other BBP Build is in-progress in the same application, then also the warning will come showing the BBP Build is already in progress Token Quota​ The Token Quota section displays the AI token consumption details for the selected user. A token represents a unit of text processed by the AI model. Every analysis performed on a BRD or BBP consumes tokens. The Token Quota panel provides the following information: Tokens Used – Total number of tokens consumed by Developer AI. Total Token Allocation – Maximum tokens allocated to the application. Remaining Tokens – Tokens still available for future AI operations. Usage Percentage – Visual progress bar showing the percentage of the allocated quota that has been consumed. Token Units​ Developer AI displays large token counts using abbreviated units: Unit Meaning Example K Thousand (1,000) 250K = 250,000 tokens M Million (1,000,000) 2.0M = 2,000,000 tokens Example If the Token Quota displays: 2.0M / 26.5M tokens 7% Used 24.5M Remaining It means: A total of 26.5 million tokens have been allocated. 2.0 million tokens have already been consumed. 24.5 million tokens are still available. Approximately 7% of the total token allocation has been utilized. Generate BBP​ The Generate BBP feature enables users to generate a Business Blueprint (BBP) by simply describing their application requirements in natural language. Instead of manually preparing a detailed BBP document, users can provide a high-level business description, and Developer AI automatically transforms it into a structured Business Blueprint. Upload BRD / BBP Document​ Once the application has been selected, upload the project documentation for analysis. Developer AI supports the following documents: Business Requirement Document (BRD) Business Blueprint (BBP) The document can be uploaded by: Dragging and dropping the file into the upload area. Selecting the file from the local system. Once the document is uploaded, Developer AI begins analyzing its contents to understand the business requirements and extract key information required to build the application. During this process, Developer AI identifies and generates: Business entities Functional requirements User roles Application screens Menu structure Business workflows Notifications Schedulers Dashboard requirements Homepage configuration Relationships between business objects The extracted information is then used to automatically generate the initial application structure within the selected Procify application. Preparing a BBP for Developer AI​ Developer AI expects the Business Blueprint (BBP) to follow a predefined structure for accurate analysis and application generation. If your existing BBP is not already in this format, it must be converted before uploading. To prepare a Developer AI-compatible BBP: Ensure you have the existing Business Blueprint (BBP) for your project. Refer to the Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt document (Prompt). Upload both: Your existing BBP. The Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt. Submit both documents to Claude for processing. The conversion prompt has been specifically designed and validated for Claude, and it is recommended not to use other AI models for this conversion. Claude will generate a new BBP that conforms to the standardized format required by Developer AI. Review the generated BBP to verify that the business requirements have been accurately converted. Upload the converted BBP using the Upload Business Requirement Document section to continue the application generation process. Once uploaded, Developer AI will analyze the standardized BBP and generate the application's foundational components, including entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, configurations, and other required artifacts.

The Analyze & Review tab is the second step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this stage, Developer AI processes the uploaded BRD or BBP and extracts all the business information required to build the application. The purpose of this step is to validate that the uploaded document has been successfully analyzed before proceeding with application generation. Once the document analysis is completed successfully and the extracted summary has been reviewed, click Open Dashboard to proceed to the detailed review screen. The Open Dashboard button opens the Review Extracted Information dashboard, where users can: Review all extracted business components in detail. Verify entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, schedulers, menu access, and homepage configuration. Modify, add, or remove extracted items as required. Validate the extracted information before proceeding to the Execution Plan stage. Review Extracted Information​ This section provides categorized access to all the information extracted from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Each category displays the number of items identified during the analysis, allowing users to review every component before proceeding with application generation. The available categories include: Entities – Displays the entities extracted from the document. Screens – Lists the application screens identified during analysis. Schedulers – Displays scheduled jobs or background processes. Functional Requirements – Shows the extracted business requirements. Notifications – Lists notification and alert configurations. User Roles – Displays user roles identified for role-based access control. Menu Access – Shows the application's navigation menu structure. Homepage – Displays the extracted homepage configuration. Out of Scope – Lists requirements identified as outside the application's scope. AI Visualize – Provides AI-generated visual representations of the extracted business information. Ask BBP – An AI-powered assistant that answers questions related to the uploaded BBP. Selecting a category displays its corresponding details in the main content area for review. Note: At present, manual addition, modification, or deletion of extracted components is not supported. The entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, and other components displayed on this screen are generated by Developer AI based on the uploaded BRD or BBP and are used as the foundation for application generation. Users can review the extracted information before proceeding to the next step.

Developer AI provides an option to export the extracted entity information for offline review or integration. Export to JSON​ The Export to JSON button downloads the extracted entity metadata in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format. The exported file contains structured information such as: Entity details Attributes Relationships Entity types Associated metadata The JSON format can be used for documentation, integration with external systems, or further processing. Export to TXT​ The Export to TXT option is currently not supported. Although the option is visible in the interface, exporting the extracted information in TXT format is not available in the current release and will be supported in a future version.

The Re-Analyze button allows users to run the document analysis again if changes have been made to the uploaded BRD or BBP, or if the extracted results need to be refreshed. When clicked, Developer AI: Reprocesses the uploaded document. Extracts the latest business requirements and application components. Updates the extracted entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, menu access, and other information.

The Mark All Review Completed button confirms that the extracted information has been reviewed and approved. Selecting this option indicates that: The extracted entities have been verified. Screens and functional requirements have been reviewed. User roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other extracted components have been validated. The application is ready to proceed to the next stage. Note: Marking the review as complete is mandatory before proceeding. If this step is not completed, an alert message will appear when you attempt to continue, prompting you to mark all reviews as completed before moving to the next stage.

The Execution Plan button navigates to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. After the review is completed, clicking Execution Plan opens the Execution Plan screen, where Developer AI displays the sequence of activities required to generate the application. The Execution Plan provides an overview of: Components to be generated. Order of execution. This serves as the final review before Developer AI begins generating the application.

The Refine BBP with AI feature is designed to allow users to improve or modify the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) using natural language instructions before proceeding with application generation. This option can be accessed by clicking the ✨ (AI Refine) button available on the Review Extracted Information screen.

Click the ✨ (AI Refine) button. The Refine BBP with AI dialog is displayed. What should AI change? text box, enter the required modifications or enhancements in natural language. Examples: Tighten the module scope. Add missing approval rules. Correct notification triggers. Add a new business entity. Update the workflow for order approval. Click Apply AI Changes. Developer AI is designed to analyze the provided instructions and update the extracted BBP accordingly. The refined information would then be reflected in the extracted components for further review before proceeding with application generation. Note: The Refine BBP with AI feature is currently not supported in the current release. Although the option is available in the interface, AI-based refinement of the extracted BBP is not yet functional and will be supported in a future release.

After clicking Execution Plan, the Review BBP Changes Before Build dialog is displayed. This screen provides a final summary of the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) before the application build process begins. The summary displays the number of: Existing in BBP – Components that were identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Added – New components that have been added during the review process. Updated – Components that have been modified before execution. The dialog also lists all the extracted application components, such as: Entities Screens Functional Requirements Notifications User Roles Other extracted artifacts This allows users to perform a final verification of the application metadata before proceeding with the build. Available Options Compare AI Changes – Displays a comparison between the original extracted information and any AI-generated changes (if applicable). Back to Review – Returns to the Review Extracted Information screen to make further changes or validations. Proceed to Execution Plan – Confirms the review and navigates to the Execution Plan screen, where the application generation workflow is initiated.

After clicking Proceed to Execution Plan, the Execution Selection screen is displayed. This screen allows users to review all extracted components and select the items that should be included in the application generation process. A summary at the top of the screen displays the total number of extracted components, including: Entities UI Screens Schedulers Workflows Notifications User Roles Menu Access Homepage Each category shows the number of items identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP.

The lower section displays the extracted components grouped by category. Each item is accompanied by a checkbox, allowing users to choose whether it should be included in the application build. Users can: Review the extracted entities and screens. Select or deselect individual components. Use the Select All option to include all available components for generation. Only the selected components will be considered during the application generation process.

After reviewing and selecting the required components, click Execute to start the application generation process. Developer AI begins generating the selected application components within the chosen Procify application. This includes creating the selected entities, screens, workflows, notifications, user roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other supported artifacts. Note: Ensure that all required components are selected before clicking Execute, as only the selected items will be included in the application generation process.

After clicking Execute, the Execution Progress screen is displayed. This screen tracks the progress of the application generation process and shows the status of each component being created. To begin generating the application, click Build Application.

The Build Application button initiates the application generation process based on the components selected in the Execution Plan. During the build process, Developer AI automatically creates and configures the selected application components, including: Business entities UI screens Value Helps Sample data Application roles Notifications Business rules Menus Homepage configuration Permissions Other supported application artifacts

As the build progresses, the Execution Progress section displays the status of each component. Each component is marked with one of the following statuses: In Progress – The component is currently being generated. Completed – The component has been successfully created. The progress cards provide a quick overview of the build status for each application component.

The Execution Log records every step performed during the application generation process. The log includes information such as: Analysis completion Entity creation Screen generation Business rule creation Sample data insertion Role creation Menu generation Homepage configuration Permission assignment Any warnings or errors encountered during the build The execution log helps users monitor the build process and troubleshoot issues if required.

When all selected components have been generated successfully, the status changes to Build Completed. A confirmation message indicates that the application has been successfully created within the selected Procify application. Users can then click Continue to proceed to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. Note :- Build Queue Notification When a BBP build is triggered for an application while another BBP build is already in progress for a different application, the new build request is not started immediately. Instead, it is automatically placed in a system-wide queue and will begin execution once the currently running build is completed. Build Already in Progress If a BBP build is triggered for an application that already has an active build in progress, Developer AI does not start a new build for the same application. Instead, it notifies the user that a build is already running and provides an option to view the current build progress. Click Yes, Show Progress to open the ongoing build progress screen, or click Cancel to close the notification

This step will allow users to configure application settings, assign users and roles, manage permissions, customize branding, and define deployment-related configurations before publishing the application.
This step will allow users to validate the generated application, perform publish readiness checks, and publish the application to the target environment.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered test cases and execute automated Playwright tests to validate the generated application.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered technical documentation, user guides, configuration guides, and downloadable project documentation for the generated application.
This step will allow users to review the final application generation summary, verify the completed workflow, and conclude the Developer AI application generation process.

Developer AI is an AI-powered application development capability built on top of the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform. It transforms business requirements, provided in natural language, into a structured application design and automatically generates the foundational components required to build an enterprise application. Rather than requiring users to manually analyze requirements, design data models, create user interfaces, and configure application components, Developer AI automates these activities using artificial intelligence. This significantly reduces the time and effort involved in the initial stages of application development while ensuring consistency and alignment with business requirements.

Developer AI is designed to simplify and accelerate enterprise application development by leveraging Artificial Intelligence. It minimizes manual effort in the initial stages of development and enables organizations to transform business ideas into functional applications more efficiently.

This document explains about the various types of events associated with the page area of type ‘Dialog’ and their implementation.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function after the dialog box has closed. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 After Close Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the afterClose event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function after the dialog box has opened. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 After Open Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the afterOpen event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function before the dialog box has closed. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 Before Close Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the beforeClose event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function before the dialog box has opened. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 Before Open Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the beforeOpen event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to override the default escape handler function on the press of escape button on the keyboard provided by sap by providing a user defined function.

In the events tab of Dialog config, select the escapeHandler event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file. When the event is triggered, the dialog’s promise object is passed as a functional parameter. It contains two properties: resolve(): This is the dialog promise’s resolve function that can be used to resolve the dialog’s promise on close by pressing the escape button on the keyboard. reject(): This is the dialog promise’s reject function that can be used to reject the dialog’s promise on close by pressing the escape button on the keyboard. Note: Application developers can manually close the dialog by either getting the dialog instance using the getActiveControlById()function or by resolving the dialogs promise.

documents.t: Click on the app for which you want to change the version. Go to the details section. In the details section, when you make the screen editable, you will find the Version Action Button of a “Released” App. Click on that to create a new app version. When a new version is created it will inherit all the adoptions that were made in the previous version. Also, when we add new features and make changes in the new version, those changes will reflect in the new version only, making the older version obsolete or deprecated. This can be shown with a specimen below: We have created an app named tech_services_app, and we have created a new version for this app. We have added all the basic details required. Next, we will go to the Language section. Languages will be adapted from the previous version only. If we need to add or remove any language in this section that can be done here. Similarly, the FAQ keys will be inherited from the previous version; we can add or remove any keys as per our need. Furthermore, we will see that once we adapt to a new version (steps mentioned above), it will inherit all the features such as the created page, entity query, etc. from the previous version. We can check this inheritance under Artifacts. Note: The image above shows the Page from UI Objects that have been inherited. This is because only one page has been created in the previous version.

Applications developed need to be changed frequently to adapt to changing requirements as well as to add new functionalities. This document will teach you how to enhance your existing applications in these scenarios.
One must be assigned a Cockpit app to get full access to the Workspace Hub. The Private Node setup should be done in the user's system. VS code should be available in your system.

To enhance your application, you need to go through the following steps: Create a new version of the application Assign version to users (Automatic) VS Code initialisation Rollout of new application Publish the new version

When a new version of the app is created, it only inherits data from the previous versions. The other changes or new features need to be added by the users. Once that is done the app needs to be published. Doing so, the change will reflect on the relevant devices.
documents.s: When do we Publish the new version?
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Enhance and Upgrade Your Application/Publish the New Version

documents.t: Publishing an app is the final step after all the changes and upgrades have been made in the new app version. Once all the page creation, entity creation, user, and role assignments are in place we can move ahead and publish the app. For this: Go to App Management, then select the app with its new version and click on the Publish button.
documents.s: How do we Publish a new version?
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Enhance and Upgrade Your Application/Publish the New Version

documents.t: When a new app version is created, that version will not immediately be made available to all the users. It will be made available to a certain group of users so that they can test and check whether the application is working properly. Once it gets verified and approved by those users, the app will be made available to the rest of the users.
documents.s: Rolling the app to Assigned Users
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Enhance and Upgrade Your Application/Rolling the app to Assigned Users

documents.t: To assign the app to a group of users, we will use User Collections in the Workspace Hub. Step 1: Create a user group by adding the basic details. Step 2: Go to users and add the number of users required for this trial. Step 3: We will add the App Groups under this particular user group and save the entire process. Note: Under the App Groups, individual groups related to a single app get created automatically. These groups can be seen in case we click on Show All as shown in the image below: If you see the image, you will find tech_services_app has individual groups, one for the Manager, one for the Developer, and one tester. You can assign the required group to your user group or you can create an App group separately for your app and assign the user group respectively.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Enhance and Upgrade Your Application/Rolling the app to Assigned Users

documents.t: In case we want to create a separate App group follow the steps below: Step 1: Go to App Collections and click on Create Group. Step 2: Add the Basic Details and move to Apps. Step 3: Click on the Add button. A popup will appear. Select the app or apps needed to add to the group and press the Add Button. Step 4: Now we must select the Installation type and the Roles for the particular apps. Update Type: It specifies how the app will be installed. Regular: It installs the registered app normally for the user and creates initial sync, table generation, etc On-Demand: It helps to assign the app to the user but the user has to install the app through the Developer Page. Default: It is the same as regular installation type which helps the user to assign the app directly with table creation. Upgrade Type: It specifies how the app will be upgraded. Immediate: It upgrades the app with an immediate notification where the user will have the option of the OK button and it upgrades the app. Postpondable: It upgrades the app with an optional notification where the user will have the option of the OK and Cancel buttons and it will install the app later on. Role: specifies via which role the application will be assigned to the users of that group. Once these are selected, we will move to User Groups and add our user group. The App Group is created and the User Group has also been added to the App group.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Enhance and Upgrade Your Application/Rolling the app to Assigned Users

This is a screen in the KloTouch application that helps the users search for the queries that they face while using the application with detailed answers. This is used to edit and create question-answers and groups in an optimised way which will benefit the ultimate consumers while using the application.
faqs_editor_1 flavor should be assigned to the User.

1. Go to the FAQs Editor menu and click on the sub-menu named FAQs Editor to open it. A screen will initially load with the FAQ Groups based on their sequence in ascending order. Note: Now the button is visible at the screen title toolbar. On click of the Procify logo, the screen title toolbar will collapse resulting in the buttons not being visible. 2. Users can search for the FAQs based on their Group Title, Question, Key ID and Key Description. Users need to enter the relevant texts and click on the OK button to perform the search. Group Title: This denotes the title under which one will find their relevant queries. Eg: If a user has a query related to Work Order, they can search for it under that very group. Questions: This denotes any search by directly writing the question on the search bar. Key ID: Key ID helps us get the element which we want. Each Flavor will be associated with one or more keys and based upon those keys, groups will be loaded for that flavor. Each key can be used in multiple flavors. Key Description: It is a relevant and memorable description that we put for the key ID. 3. Users can clear the search criteria by clicking on the cross button in the search bar. 4. Users can expand any group to see the list of questions associated with that group by clicking on the dropdown. 5. Users can click on the add button beside the search bar to create a new group. After clicking on the button, a popup will appear and the user needs to select a key to which this group will be associated. Note: These Keys are created and maintained in the Account Console. In case you do not find the key you are looking for, kindly go to the Account Console and create the relevant key. 6. Users then need to select a key and then click on the Create button. Users will be navigated to the detail section where they have to fill in the group title (mandatory), sequence, and icon and then click on the Save button. 7. Users can also edit the group details by clicking on the Edit button on the right side of that particular Group Title. 8. Users can then update the group details and then click on the Save button again. 9. Users can delete a group by clicking on the delete button on the right side of that particular group title. Upon clicking it will ask the user for confirmation. On giving the delete confirmation it will delete the group along with its entire associated question. 10. Users can create a new question inside a group by clicking on the add button at the right side of that particular group title. 11. Users then need to fill in the device type (mandatory), sequence, Question Title (mandatory) and answer and then click on the Save button. By default, the language will be set to English. 12. Users can edit a question by clicking on that particular question link. Users then need to make the changes and click on the Save button. 13. Users can also delete a question by clicking on the delete button on the right side of that particular Question Title. It will ask the user for the confirmation. Upon user confirmation, it will delete the question. 14. Users can also create the language variants of a particular question by clicking on that particular question title and then clicking on the language button in the Question Detail section. On clicking on the language button the user will get a language selection popup where they have to select the language in which they want their translation. 15. After the selection of language a popup will appear where on the left-hand side the English variant of the question will be visible and on the right-hand side, the selected language variant will be visible. Note: If the question in the selected language variant is already created then it will open in edit mode otherwise it will open in create mode. After filling in all the details, the user can click on the save language button to save all the changes. Users can click on the close button in the top right-hand side of the popup to close the language popup.

This document provides a complete guide for enabling and using Git integration within the Procify platform. It explains how to configure GitHub or Bitbucket repositories, set up SSH access, connect them to your Procify flavor, and work with Git-based version control during development. It covers the end-to-end process—including repository setup, user access, configuring Git details in the Workspace Hub, checking out flavors, and using Git-linked workflows within the Procify environment.
Basics of version control
Go to GitHub. Click “New repository” → create it under your organization account (not personal). Example organization: procify-vsix-integration(only one time setup required by respective app manager)

documents.t: Note: by default it will checkout from branch which is configured, but there might be case that you don’t have valid access of that branch, so before doing any change checkout that branch. For gitconfigured flavors any change made will not show in existing button(commit All) so you can’t save your changes to public via that button, for committing your change to public commit to corresponding git branch ⚠️ Note — newly created files: The above applies to changes to existing files. When you create a new file (controller / entity / query / rules / view), the Private Node save still records it in the app so it appears in your file explorer — but Build & Deploy reads these file types only from your Git repository, never from the app database. You must commit and push the new file to Git — even if it still holds just the initial template it was scaffolded with — before running Build & Deploy. Skipping this step causes the build to succeed with no warning, but the file will be missing from the deployed app, and the screen using it will fail to load at runtime.

Create a folder named: ‘scheduler’ inside the App. Inside the scheduler flavor, scheduler files can be created with the same name as ‘scheduler_id’. Inside the files, the class name should be ‘scheduler_id’ and should extend the kloBo/kloScheduler/KloScheduler class. Developers must override the onExecute method of the parent class, which gets executed on a defined time. eventContext and params can be accessed through ‘this’ keyword. E.g: this.eventContext, this.params . The flavor build needs to be triggered after the creation/modification of the file. If the onExecute() function is not found on the scheduler file,it will execute the function from the parent class and the Jobs will be returned with COMPLETED status. If we want the Jobs status to be failed,we can call the throw(“string”) function in the onExecute() Function of the scheduler file.The String passed to the function will be displayed in the log.

Background jobs are classified into four categories: - Class S (System): A class system for fw jobs. System jobs are not part of the quota Class A (Critical Priority): - Some tasks are urgent or critical and must be scheduled with class A priority jobs. Class A priority reserves one or more background work processes. Users must decide how many background work processes should be assigned to Class A priority jobs. Class B(Normal Priority): - Once Class A jobs are completed, Class B jobs will start executing in the background before Class C jobs. Class C(Low Priority): -It runs after class A and class B jobs are completed.

Scheduled Tasks, Jobs, and Job Execution Log together form the core components of a Job Scheduler, which automates, monitors, and logs job executions, ensuring that tasks are completed on time and according to predefined rules.
A Job definition is a screen where the job’s templates are created, set/scheduled and kept systematically.

A Job refers to a specific execution of a job. Each time a job is run, a new instance is created. It represents the occurrence of that job with its unique execution parameters, timestamps, status, and related metadata. A Job allows you to track the job's progress, its start and end time, and its outcome (whether successful or failed). Each Job is distinct and can be tracked individually.

A Job Execution Log contains detailed records or entries related to the execution of a Job. It provides a step-by-step log of events, actions, and messages generated during the execution of the job. Job Execution Logs are useful for debugging, auditing, and understanding the behavior of a job during its execution. They typically include information like warnings, errors, and system outputs that occurred while the Jobs was running.
To CRUD and maintain background jobs.

Jobs can also be duplicated. Select a Job and press on Duplicate(Only one Job can be duplicated at a time; By default, the lowest selected Indexed Job is duplicated). Note: A job can not be deleted. It can only be disabled.Any new job created from the Jobs screen will be in a disabled state by default. To run the job, you must manually enable it by clicking the Enable button. Whenever a new Version of the app is created, and if any jobs are newly added or existing jobs are modified(either in code or metadata), the jobs must be imported from the latest version of the app. During job transport, using the [Import Job] option, this will retain the job's original status. documents.t: A Job can be edited while it is Disabled and Next Scheduled is more than 2 minutes. It can’t be edited while enabled.Edit permissions are restricted to managers of the associated scheduled task. Cron Expression needs to be present in order to save the job. Needs to provide a cron expression before saving. The cron expression is a required property; if it is not included in the job definition, the import of the jobs will fail. Additionally, attempting to start the job without it will also result in failure. If you don't wish to schedule a job, you can just disable the job. Please provide a Valid cron expression, currently valid cron expression can be checked using this site. The provided site may not work in the future. Note:-There is currently no minimum limit set for the scheduler task execution interval. Note: We follow the FreeFormatter Cron Expression Generator, which uses Quartz-style 6/7-field cron syntax. For example, the expression shown there for running a task every second is: * * * ? * * However, this expression does not trigger even once in our implementation. This is because we use the later.js library with useSeconds = true, which expects 7 fields in the cron expression. Missing the seconds field causes the expression to be parsed incorrectly, resulting in no execution. There is no need to restart the master after enabling a job for it to be scheduled. However, if the master has been manually stopped, the newly enabled job will not be scheduled until the master is started again.

documents.t: Elements Description Create Creates a new Job Duplicate Duplicates a Selected Job Restart Master Reschedules the Jobs with the changes. Stop Master Stops all the jobs for the next schedule. Start Master Schedules all the jobs according to cron expression. Start Jobs Initiates all the jobs that have been selected. Note: Jobs that have already been executed will not be run again, but jobs that have not started yet will begin. Stop Jobs Stops all the selected(running) jobs. Enabled(in the list) Enables/Disables a particular scheduled job. Refer to Code to create the file.

documents.t: Enable button is used to enable the scheduled jobs. Disable button is used to disable the scheduled jobs. Start:The "Start" button initiates the job immediately. If the job is already running, a warning message will appear: "The job is already running. Do you want to trigger a new instance?" Selecting "Yes" will start the job immediately, while "Cancel" will take no action. Stop: Stops the running job immediately. Refresh: Refresh the detail section to show current Data and logs related to the job. "Job logs" button will navigate to the Job Execution Log screen. In the Job Execution Log screen you can see the Job Execution Logs for specific Jobs. Edit: Refer to Editing a Job.

documents.t: Navigating to a different job without saving, doesn’t save the changes done. Filters Job Execution Log data for the particular job. (After opening a log in the Job Execution Log section it loads all the logs. Press the refresh button to reload jobs for that particular Job). NOTE: Restart master is required after any changes in order to reschedule the jobs with new changes. Enabling a job also requires a Restart master in order to reschedule it. The scheduler can run max 2 jobs at a time in a particular landscape, other jobs will be stacked depending upon priority and cron expression. The scheduler will pick a third job after completion of any of the two jobs. If two jobs are having the same cron expression and same priority then the scheduler can run both of them parallelly and if any other job is already in running status then the scheduler can pick any one of them to execute. If one job is running and the server has stopped in between,it will not create an entry on the Job Execution Log and after restarting the server, it will check for the Mandatory field, if it is marked true, then the scheduler will start that particular job immediately else it will be skipped. If the onExecute() function is not found on the scheduler file,it will execute the function from the parent class and the Jobs will be returned with COMPLETED status. To ensure transactions are available 2 minutes after the job starts, enable the long-running option. If we want the Jobs status to be failed,we can call the throw(“string”) function in the onExecute() Function of the scheduler file.The String passed to the function will be displayed in the log. Difference between Restart Master**,** Start Master, Start Selected and Start in detail: Restart Master: Used to apply changes to the scheduler. It restarts the scheduler to reflect new configurations, ensuring jobs run with the updated version. Start Master: Starts the entire scheduler and executes scheduled jobs. Stop Master: Stops the scheduler, pausing all jobs and attempting to stop running jobs. Start Jobs: The "Start jobs" button triggers the start of all selected jobs. If any job is running, a warning will prompt, "Do you want to trigger new instances?" Selecting "Yes" will restart all jobs, and "Cancel" will prevent any restart. Stop Jobs: Stops only the selected jobs. Start/Stop (in detail): Used for immediate job execution or termination, typically for testing or debugging purposes, bypassing regular schedules.. Note:

documents.t: An attachment is any file or document that you upload against any object. Attachment component is used for uploading and downloading the mime(images, videos, audio, pdf etc). This is an entity level flag and it indicates that attachment is allowed to store against the entity. If enabled, the attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. Users can only add/Edit/delete attachments when the component is in edit mode. Framework adds primary relation with attachment link entity and the Entity where attachment is enabled. Relation name is ‘attachments’. Within one BO, Attachment Entity can have relations with multiple Entities like order_hdr and order_items both are attachment enabled. Uploads a file in a common folder(local) and also maintains a link with the object. Mime gets pushed to the server repository via middleware. If the parent object is deleted, it deletes the attachment also but not the mime. Mime might have reference with another attachment. Attachment with new entity: as attachment is part of the same BO, commit and rollback works like other entities in a BO. Mime upload to the local folder is separate and it does not rollback if the transaction is canceled or failed. To upload or display the attachment UI controls are part of kloTouch. Steps to enable the attachment for an entity: Import kloAttachment in Account flavor/s. Attachment config Enable attachment in the entity definition. Define attachment type. Define attachment subtype. Call the APIs to upload and download the attachment. Attachment config: Account : Landscape: Attatchment_upload_class: Fully qualified name of the attachment class which implements AttachmentHandler interface which have two methods upload and download. This class is to be written by an application developer. These methods are available in controller or Rule. Sample code is provided below. Content repository: Location(base path) to store the mime on the server side is part of this upload class. thirdParty_application: min_battery: minimum battery required for upload and download. If the battery level goes down and the user tries to upload/download, it ends with an error/warraning. Can modify in device settings? Sample code for upload class: public interface AttachmentHandler { public void upload(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,String landscape) throws IOException, JSONException, JCodecException ; public Response download(String file ,HttpServletRequest request,HttpServletResponse response,String landscape); } public class CustomAttachmentHandler implements AttachmentHandler { public void upload(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,String landscape) throws IOException, JSONException, JCodecException{ //TODO } public Response download(String file ,HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response1,String landscape) { //TODO } } Define Attachment Type: once “Has Attachment is marked TRUE, attachment section in BOL editor will get enabled where you can define the attachment type. Below are the attributes: Attachment type: this is to categorize the attachment. Like Product, Equipment, Invoice, Profile pic, etc. Doctype: indicates that document type of attachment like user manual etc Max Files: max number of files allowed to upload. Download Type/Sync Type: WIFI, Battery Level, Always. Option to view only in App but can’t download to gallery?- phone setting Mime type: this specifies the accepted mime types of the mime. One mime type is mandatory. Multiple mime types are allowed with comma(,) as separator. Allowed mime types are .jpeg, .png, .mp3, .3gp, .wav, .mp4, .pdf, .xls, .xlsx, .doc, .docx, .zip, .RAR Application has to decide the mime types. There is no exclusion from the framework side. OR Audio, Video, Image, Document Size per file: Define the max allowed size( in KB) of a file to upload. If file size exceeds, it ends with an error. Size is defined per attachment type. What if a live camera used to upload and size is more? Cardinality: Extends from: Request sequence no: Source: There are different sources from where media files are allowed to capture. Multiple sources are allowed with comma(,) as separator. If only one source is selected, it directly opens Camera or Gallery or Mice otherwise this gives option to users to select a source for upload. Camera Take Photo Record Video Gallery/Folder Mice Need Location: Capture GPS location while adding the attachment. Upload endpoint/location: location where attachment has to be dumped on receive on server. ( folder path, mount etc..) Entity Name: name of the transaction entity for which attachment to be allowed. Attachment should be enabled in Entity definition. Define Attachment Subtype : subtype is just a categorization to store the Attachment type: Sub Type: it is sub categorization(child) of attachment type and it is optional. For example : uploading images of type equipment with subtype as front side, back side, etc. Entityname: Attachment link: This store the entity attachment info. This link table has a primary relation with the transaction entity that means it is part of every BO attachment is enabled. Table name is ‘dcatt_attachment_link’. Attachment ID: GUID generated for attachment. This gets generated at the client side. Attachment id is a unique id across all the endpoints. Attachment Type: passed from UI as parameter. SubType: passed from UI as parameter. File name: input from application and this is displayed on the UI. Entity Key: this is a unique key with a combination of entity name and primary key set. Mime Type: mime type(file extension) of the attached mime. Only one value is allowed. Name: Additional description about attachment? GPS Location : If enabled in setting, it captures the GPS coordinates. Is default: this is input from UI at the time of upload. Default marked attachment is considered for preview or thumbnail in UI. Sequence: sequence in which attachment is displayed in UI. Attachment APIs: Upload: call onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError) function onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError) This uploads the mime and makes an entry in the link table. As the link table is part of the transaction BO it gets updated with the BO. From Device: From portal: Example: some_function_in_controller : function(oEvent){ var parameters = { "type":"type1", "subtype":"subtype1", "modelName":"entity_name", "path":"/list/0/attachments", "objectType":1, "entityname":"entity_name", }; oController.onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError); } Download: forceDownloadAttachmnet(attahchmentId) This is to force download the mime from the server. Download user manual or FAQ kind of doc which are not part of any object? Example: oController.forceDownloadAttachmnet(attahchmentId); Update: update attachment info like file name, is_default, etc. Delete: Use the Entity delete API. This deletes only the attachment link and does not delete the mime. Common folder : Common folder is used to store the mimes locally. This is hardcoded in framework. While uploading the file it first copies the file to a local folder which might be different for mobile and desktop. Attachment id gets generated after the source of the image is copied to the common folder. Message processing: note that attachment entity and the mime are separate messages. Attachment entity message flow is similar to other entities and part of the parent entity’s BO. Upload: Mime messages get stored in _attachments table at client side and processed separately. From the device it is a direct Ajax call to the server for all the messages in _attachments table. Once it is synced to the server it makes an entry in the d_attachment_log table. Download: First check if mime is available in local storage. If not, request is made from device and mime gets downloaded to the local storage. This request is through middleware. Object cloning: attachment link is also cloned with the BO. This points to the same mime. Convert Object Type: attachment and mime does not get copied to the target object even though it is part of BO. If needed, how do application developers copy? Initial sync: write initial sync queries for attachment link. This Download all: for all attachments, it loads the mime immediately after initial sync is completed. Download on demand: mime is loaded only on user request from UI. Send attachment with email: separate notification API. This is part of the Notification component. Archive: How to mark attachment mandatory? In screen fields? Authorization to add, edit, delete attachment? Delete mimes which do not have any reference. Online upload and download from portal? Virus scan? Settings - Download/Upload only if: Download/ upload only on wifi Download/ upload only on wifi and power always download

Business Object (BO) is a logical unit used in a business. It is made up of one or multiple entities. E.g. If we take an invoice (bill of purchase) it consists of header and purchased items. Header and item entities ( tables) are required to store this information. Either item or header alone does not make any sense. So invoice header and invoice item entity together makes the invoice BO. BO is a hierarchical tree of entities. Each entity must belong to one and only one BO definition. BO has only one root entity (top level). Rest of the entity (child entity) are aggregated into root or other entities to construct the entity tree. Root entity represents the BO, root entity name becomes the BO name. Root entity also takes the full responsibility as BO apart from it’s entity responsibility.There are BO rules which are executed on root entities only like EndPointResolver, Success/ Fail / message mapper etc. kloBroker always transmits the full BO in the Message. When any entity becomes dirty it pulls parents till root within BO in writeset. Deletion of any entity instance deletes all the cascaded agrragaed entities instances. Primary relations are used between entities to bundle to construct entities tree in BO. All participating instances are traversable by primary relation with in BO. and each object can be visited only once. Primary relation represents aggregation with 0..n cardinality. BO tree is made of entity as node and primary relation as connector. In authorization all the authorization upon parents up to root are also applied except the middleware message process. Example: d_order (root entity/BO) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity)

Users may install the android app on mobile and login to use offline application, hance android app is client here. Each client is identified by a unique id called endpoint ID.
