KloBase Datastore supports a variety of data types for property values. Domain represents data type following domain types are supported Domain ID JS Type DB type MsgType Remark I8 number Number(3,0) number number I16 number Number(5,0) number number I32 number Number(10,0) number number L / I64 number Number(13,0) number number DEC number Number(p,s) number number B boolean Number(1,0) number (0/1) Returns true / false C / chr string VarChar(n) string string anum string VarChar(n) string string cwns string VarChar(n) string string BLOB string VarChar(n) string string D Date Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) number (milliseconds) T milliseconds Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) number (milliseconds) DT / TS Date Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) UTC enabled clob Not supported GUID Not supported JSON Not supported duration ?DU Not supported Application must use the JS Type for all the coding purpose. Please note DT / TS is UTC based date time hence must not be compared with local time as hard coded time.

End point enables the klobroker to send and receive the message across various participants. Endpoints are identified by end point ID. When a user logins into an application, installed app, needs to communicate with the server hence each installation (apk) gets a unique endpoint ID. Similarly each browser also gets endpoint id. Individual tenants on the server also get endpoint ID. and external system also have endpointID.

Data object in KloBase Datastore is known as entity. An entity has one or more named properties, each of which can have one or more values. Each entity in KloBase Datastore has a key that uniquely identifies it. In simple words we can say Entity is a database table. In dbms we store data in the form of a table containing information about entity type like order, address etc. In an order database, a table containing information about all the orders. For example, orders have properties like customer, Amount, products, etc they are attributes which combined make table. One entity must be part of one and only one BO. Types of Entity: Persistent Entity: Entity which physically exists/stored in database as a table. Fields in Persistent Entity could be either Persistent or Transient. Persistent Entity by default Tenant Dependent can be made Tenant Independent Persistent Entity by default or User Dependent can be made User Independent Transient Entity: It is an in memory entity that doesn’t exist in a database. All fields in Transient Entity are Transient only. It can be constructed out of query result or by code to hold the value at runtime. Messages can’t be communicated through Middleware using Transient entity. Config FW only Types Metadata Archive History Entity Naming convention and length. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. First char must be d/t/c based on type. Transactional (‘d’) , Transient (‘t’), Config (‘c’) Following are auto generated Archive entity starts with ‘a’ Union or archive and transactional entity starts with ‘v’ Status config starts with ‘s’ Custom Status starts with ‘u’ History entity starts with ‘h’ Framework entity starts with ‘m’ Each entity has one or more properties. Each entity property has one property type. Each property type has a domain assigned. Entity Entity Property (1-n) Property Type (1) Domain (1) Provide a unique entity name and mark if it is a Root entity. Root entity is considered as a BO. To define an entity you need at least one entity property, It could be either transient or regular(persisted in DB). Entity attributes: Entity Name : Unique ID across all flavors. Is Root : This defines the Root entity of a BO. BO Name is the same as Entity Name if this is marked TRUE. Entity Type: Persistent/Transient. Network mode : This is optional here and inherited from flavor this entity belongs to. You can overwrite if required. BO Name : Root entity name. Entities in the same BO should have a primary relation. Is metadata : This decides whether it is a meta model entity or transactional. If marked TRUE, framework creates table in metadata DB. Otherwise in transactional DB. Has appvariant : Starts following the flavor behaviour. If is_metadata FALSE, by default has_appvariant is FALSE and not allowed to change. Has Tenant : Entity starts following the Tenant behaviour. if TRUE, s_tenant_id field will be added in DB table at the time of the update schema. Is Config : if TRUE, this is considered as config entity. Has Config : Framework will provide a config entity which can further customized with configuration fields. If object type is not applicable this is an object type independent config. Config is accessible in application by using *entityInstance.config * Has created fields : To know what time facts are recorded to database and by whom. if TRUE, s_created_on and s_created_by fields will be added by FW at the time of update schema. These two fields are filled by a system of entity creation. UI: s_created_on is server time in UTC format when record created and s_created_by is the logged in user. Message processing: Created On gets updated with server time(UTC format) if blank otherwise accept from message and Created By will be taken from message. Background Job/Upload: Created On gets updated with server time( UTC format) when record got created. Created By is the user by which Background job scheduled. Archive Data: accept created on/By field’s values from transaction entity as is. Has modified fields : This is to record the last changed time and user. if TRUE, Modified On and Modified By fields will be added by FW at the time of update schema. System updates these fields on every create/change of entity. Change in a BO: In case if any change on root/header level only, this updates only header table modified fields. In case any change is made to the child entity, this updates the parent entity also upto root. UI: same as created fields. Message processing: Background Job: same as created fields. Archive Data: accept all values from transaction entity. If an object is modified during the archiving process, then modify fields get changed accordingly. Check Dirty: re-evaluate all entities for dirty before calling on update. Default value: ? Has Brand : Entity is brand dependent or independent. if TRUE, s_brand field will get added by FW at the time of update schema. Has Object Type : Entity follows Object Type behaviour. if TRUE, s_object_type field of type int(11) gets added by FW at the time of update schema. Has Status : if TRUE, s_status and s_status_custom fields will get added by kloBase at the time of update schema. See more details in the Status section. Can create/read/update/Delete: if TRUE, insert/read/update/delete is allowed in the table otherwise not allowed. Applied only on Server side. Server side Exit and MW still allows even if false. Can read all : if TRUE, read all values allowed from the table otherwise not allowed. Applied only Server side. Exit and MW still allows even if false. Runtime query will not work if it is FALSE. Has History: This is to maintain the changing history of an BO. If TRUE, it creates a separate blob or transactional table to maintain the history of all changes. Every change on an entity gets captured in the history table and the main transactional table holds only the latest record. Table name starts with ‘h’. Only on root entity or full BO? Maintain change history only for specific status? Object type based configuration? Is this supported offline? Has Archive: This is to facilitate the data archiving. This can be enabled only on the root entity/ BO. Always complete BO gets archived. Table name starts with ‘a’. One more table created as a view which starts with ‘v’ to fetch transaction and archive table data as union. If the ID series is exhausted? Server Side: Push data from transaction table to Archive table. Which means data will get deleted from the main table once moved to the archive table. Maintain configuration based on which data to be archived. Background job scheduler to push data from transactional table to Archive table. While archiving no dirty objects are allowed. APIs: archive(). This API will work only on server side. clearArchive() : this deletes all records from the archive table. Update to offline endpoints. This deletes the entity in local DB. ON_ARCHIVE event. Query: by default query fetch data from transactional table(d table) but if archiving is enabled, users can explicitly mark to fetch archived data. This is a union of both transactional and archived tables. IsArchived flag is returned TRUE by framework if data is from the archive table. This flag can be used by application to highlight archived data or disable edit option. Do not allow the archived records to be updated. Framework throws an error if any dirty object found for archived records. Value help/ Association relation for archived masters. Example: Update transaction entity: this should adjust the archive and view. Add/Delete new property New relation/ Delete relation Client Side: delete data in client DB(local) and do not send any updates to the server. API: deleteLocal() kloQuery has deleteLocal(); Dependency: Does not allow you to archive until the related(supplied by application. Do not follow entity relation) object gets archived. Dependency is decided based on aggregate relations. Helper function to be written by Application to check if any dependent object exists. Has Time Dependent : At any given point in time, an entity has a value for each of its attributes. If the values of any attribute for an entity may change over time and you are interested to know the value of an attribute at a particular point in time, it is meaningful for entities to have properties exactly when they exist and mark the entity as time dependent. In case if you are interested only in the current value of the attribute, do not mark as time dependent. This is to maintain the periodic(time dependent) data with valid time. If any entity is marked as time dependent, framework creates below three fields in the table. In a BO any entity can be time dependent. s_valid_from(Timestamp) - Validity start date and time. Part of the primary key. Default is the current date. s_valid_to(Timestamp) - Validity end date and time. Default value is 31-12-9999. s_active(boolean) - the latest record will be marked as TRUE. At a time only one entry should be active and the validity period should not overlap for two records. By default Valid from is current date but can be changed. Past date: Config to be maintained for past date is allowed or not. Message processing(from SAP, device or to device) follows the config for the past date. If allowed it accepts the date from message or UI otherwise it changes the FROM date to current. If first entry, except the values provided from UI or Message and mark active flag TRUE. In case of update, modify the current existing active record’s s_valid_to accordingly(based on s_valid_from the new record). Also mark current entry active flag FALSE and new entry as TRUE. Both update and create should be in the same transaction. Mainly this will be used for master data tables where periodic data is required. For example, pricing, user address, etc. MRP/Pricing of a product can be changed periodically. Can not be changed based on object type or flavor. This can be defined only in owning flavor of an account. Approval : In case if approval is required for a BO, at the time of creation of the BO it should not change the current record. Once it is approved, then only it gets activated. To consider this scenario, a separate blob table is maintained for ‘To Be Approved’ objects. Once final approval is done it will get moved to the main transaction table and activate. If enabled, approval flag will be provided from the framework. This is applicable for time dependent and time independent both entities. Configurable on object type based. Workflow will be discussed separately later. Has Attachment : If enabled, Framework allows to store the attachment against this entity object and attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. Has Doc Flow : Owens Doc ID: Is Metadata Has Tenant Is Config AppVariant Is History Is Archive Tenant Dependent TRUE Tenant Independent Configuration TRUE TRUE TRUE App Metadata TRUE TRUE Transient TRUE Archive TRUE History TRUE Metadata table but app_variant is false? m_bo_entity_map Example: Take an example of order BO. Order BO has three entities: d_order, d_order_item, d_order_item. Out of this one entity has to be marked as root entity to define a BO. d_order (root entity) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity)

Entity Property describes the attribute/member variable in an Entity(field in the database table) and holds the value in runtime. It has a Property ID(name) and Property type. The Property Type defines the data type and behaviour of the property. Entity Property’s attributes define the behaviour of the property. Entity properties can be added or archived only in the owning flavor of an account. Below are the parameters: Entity Property ID: unique within an entity across all flavors. Can’t be changed later. Property Type/Element ID: select the existing Property type or create new. This defines data type, field length, precision, etc. It can be changed only in the owning flavor of an Entity. Selection of a domain, size and property type: Choose existing Extend from Copy and override: copy any existing property type and change the parameters. This makes a copy of all attributes except Property Type ID. Create New Type: Regular / Primary Key / Transient Field / Calculated Field /System Fields. / Secondory Key Value Help: select already defined Value help ID. Wherever this property ID is binded in UI, VH is automatically applied. Can be overwritten in the screen field. Is restricted Value: Restrict the input value within the associated VH. Tri value: None, Strict(UI and BOL), Suggestions(Only UI side). (Note: Moved this to Entity property from Property type). Is Mandatory: Empty or Null values are not permitted during entity creation/update. Does not force in UI as mandatory. Non Key mandatory fields are not necessary for select. Default Value: Default value will be populated immediately after creating new Entity. $ Variables can also be used. ID Series: mention the ID series here if applicable for this field. Naming convention: Max length allowed for property ID is 31 char. Only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) are supported. Entity property ID starting with ‘s_’ is reserved for systems fields by framework. Types of Entity Property: Persisted : Property which physically exists/stored in the database as a table column. Persisted Property owning Entity also has to be Persistent Entity only. Transient: transient property is a runtime attribute only. Use this to hold some value at runtime. Example: query result alias value, value filled or determined in rule, from UI set and get attribute. Primary key: primary key of a table. Values of set of primary key fields must be unique. If field is primary key, isNull/Nulable property will be marked as false automatically. System Defined Properties: based on the relevant flags in entity definition, framework provides standard columns in a table. Field name, Data Type, Label, etc are already defined and no changes allowed here. Developers can’t add a system field. Object Type Status Brand Tenant ID Created On Modified On Created By $46 Modified By Valid From Valid To Active Source Field name Field DataType Has Object Type s_object_type int(11) Has Status s_status, s_status_custom varchar(32), varchar(32) Has Brand s_brand int(11) Tenant ID s_tenant_id int(11)(pk) Created Fields s_created_on, s_created_by Timestamp, varchar(255) Modified Fields s_modified_on, s_modified_by Timestamp, varchar(255) Date dependent s_valid_from, s_valid_to, s_active Timestamp**(pk)**, Timestamp, boolean Calculated Property: When the property is read, application defined get<Property_id> is executed . When the property is written, the application defined set<Property_id> is executed . Mostly used to return some aggregated value based on other conditions. Works when iscalculatedproperty is selected in the entity property definition. These fields are not persisted and cannot hold any value at runtime. It can only return some value. The getter/setter function will be provided by the application developer. BOL will invoke this method when the property is accessed. This property is also bindable in UI. Property with Variable, Method and persisted combination? Providing getter/setter function for the calculated field: Through KloIDE, the app developer should write <entityname>.js file in js folder of the required folder. Provide a getter function for the entity property. Use a modularised way of writing js files and use require on the file before it is used. Example: File: asn_hdr.js define(["require","exports"], function(require,exports) { getR_invoice_id = function(parent) { return ‘calculated value’; }; exports.getR_invoice_id = getR_invoice_id }); Syntax of property getter : get<property name with first letter capitalized> Example: r_invoice_id → getR_invoice_id. When the getter is invoked, this will be the entity object and you are free to access any property/relation of entity. Mostly used for dynamic calculations (example: state management);

Property Type is to define the behaviour of Entity Property(Database Table field) and Screen field. It is a reusable unit. Property Type has below attributes: ID : Unique ID of Property Type within Landscape. Domain: select Domain ID from predefined list to define the data type. Length and precision of the field. Precision is applicable only for decimal data type. Specify length for decimal and ‘chr’ types. Value Help: Define value help and assign it to property type. Value help will be applied to all the places wherever this Property type is used in UI or Rules. You can define restrictions(allow values only from VH list or accept manual inputs) on Entity Property. Authorization Text ID: maintain the Text ID here which points to the actual text(Translatable). This text is available in the screen field as tooltip/caption/placeholder/validation(error) text wherever this property type is used. It helps in maintaining the unified text across all screens. Create Text ID in editor. Default UI Format: Date ( Example: DDMMYYYY or DDMMMYY, ...) Numeric(currency, etc) Decimal Min Max Value: define min and max values allowed for a numeric and string(chr) fields. This ends with an error if value is not in given range. This validation is applied in UI. In case of string min/max value is the number of chars. Extends From: extend from other property types and modify one or more attribute/s. Usage: Entity property Query Property Screen Extends: extend the existing property type to access the parent attributes and overwrite if needed. You can only extend one propertytype in your child propertytype. In the extended property type fill only the attributes which you want to overwrite, all other attribute values are inherited from the parent. Domain type, length, precision can not be changed in extended property type. Extend property type if: Data type, length, precision are same as these are not allowed to change in extended property type. One or more properties are different from the list below: Authorization Value help Text ID UI Formatting Min/Max value How to remove an attribute value in extended property type? Set null or empty string For example, you have created one property type called ‘customer’ and Text is provided ‘Customer Name’. But in some scenarios you want to show the text as ‘Sold To Party’, in this case extend the ‘customer’ property type and create new property type as ‘sold_to_party’ and change the text. A extends B. B extends C. All attributes of C are extended to A if not overwritten in B. Reuse: To define the common behaviour of multiple Entity/Query Properties, Property type can be reused across entities. It should be reused if entity properties are logically the same. Ordered Qty and Del Qty - not to use the same property type. But Ordered qty in two diff tables should share the property type. Property type should be different for Vendor and Customer fields in the same or diff entity. Both should be extended from BP ID because data type should be same for all. It is recommended to use the same property type for a field which is used in multiple tables as foreign key. To understand this better let’s take an example of the Material Code field which is part of Material master as a primary field but also part of other tables like Order and Logistics items. Authorization: Authorization is to restrict the access of data, for logged in user. Authorization on any entity of a BO is applied on the whole BO. Authorization is defined on Property Type and applied for all queries the Entities wherever that Property Type is used. Do not apply Authorization on Query Property. For example, logged in users should be able to see only the Orders that belong to them. Below is the Entity definition: Entity Entity Property Property Type d_order order_id order_id d_order order_date order_date d_order customer_id cust_id d_order net_amount amount Here apply the authorization on “cust_id” Property Type to filter the orders of particular customers. If the same Property Type is used at other places, authorization will be applied on those entities also. In case you do not want to apply the authorization at all entities or apply the authorization at only one place, then extend the base property type and create a new Property Type. Variables Supported: $Variable Constants Syntax: const1, const2 In case if authorization is applied on more than one property or multiple value in one property. Below is the behaviour: AND Operator: If authorization is applied on multiple properties in the same BO with different property types, all parameters will be ANDed. Example1: There are two properties in d_order entity customer and sales_person both have different property types. If authorization is applied on both, this will be ANDed. OR Operator: Used a property type with multiple entity properties in the same entity, all parameters will be ORed. (Reuse property type within entity). At the same time it will be ANDed with other parameters. Example2: There are two properties in d_order entity customer and vendor both have the same property type, in this case both parameters will be ORed. IN Operator: If Multi values qualified for one property, all values will be considered with IN operator. Example3: Authorization is set on state field in d_order entity and multiple values passed at runtime, in this case all values will be passed with IN operator. If authorization to be applied on field A for one Order Type and field B for other order type? Translation: multilocal? This is to facilitate multilingual options for label text. Length suggestion on translatable text. Formation: Multi language setting. This is a global setting and not part of Property Type. Available options: Second language Only a second language.

Entity relation is to allow one entity to relate with another entity qualified by entity property. Relation has a unique name within the Entity. Association: An association is a structural relationship which connects one entity with another. Given an association between two entities, can navigate from one entity to the other entity and vice versa. Association relations can be across BOs. By default each relation is of type Association if it is not marked as Aggregated or Primary. Example1: d_order_item(source) d_material_master(Related) Create a relation to show the material description, LOB, or other property of material. Example2: d_order_item(source) d_order(Related) If you want to navigate from order Item to order header. Define a relation between Item as Source and Header as Related entity. Aggregated Relation: Aggregation is a type of association where two entities(tables) are tightly bound. In some cases we might come across “whole-part” relationships between two Entities, in which one entity is a part of another entity. Such a relationship is known as an aggregation. An aggregation relationship can be described in simple words as "an object of one class can own or access the objects of another class." If a parent is deleted/archive, all other parts associated with it are deleted. Aggregate relations can be across BOs. Primary Relation: This is a special kind of aggregate relation within BO boundary. All entities in a BO are navigable from root entity once unidirectional and only once. Below are the use cases of primary relation: Message processing Key mapping Find Parent Example: d_order ( root entity) d_order_item d_order_conditions Here d_order is the root entity and the other two are child entities in Order BO. Hence relation has to be defined between these entities. Create a relation on d_order entity with d_order_item of type “Primary” and query property is “order_id”. Create a relation on d_order_item entity with d_order_conditions of type “Primary” and query property are “order_id” and “order_item”. Define Relationship: Let’s create a relation between two entities using Procify Data Studio. To create a relation go to the source entity where you want a relation with another entity. Provide a unique Relation name. JOIN is constructed based on the defined relation. Relation Name: unique within an Entity. Relation names and Property names can’t be the same. “Parent” and “Attachments” are reserved keywords. Related Entity: name of Entity with relation to be defined. Type of relation: Aggregate/Primary. If not selected any, by default it is association type. Query Type: - To be removed from Editor UI Relation Query : Select relation query ID from list. Cardinality: - (0:n, 0:1, 1:1, 1:n). User has to select the correct cardinality for the relation. No defaulting in Editor. Add 0:1 cardinality. In case if 0:1 include in Join and if 0:n provide separate query in VH. No validation on 1:1 and 1:n cardinalities from BOL side. Description: describe the relation here in short. Relation Property: Relation Property ID: unique within Entity. Source Property ID: Variables supported- Entity property ID and constants(number, single/double quote) comma separated. Source Property ID can be used multiple times. Related Property ID: it is entity property ID if query type is Runtime and query property ID if query type is Modeled. Entity Name +Property ID in case of Runtime query. Can’t repeat within one relation. Related Entity property ID: new readonly column. Fetch from the selected query. Relation can be defined between two entities: Both Persistent Both Transient One Persistent and one Transient Variables supported: Source Property ID Entity property ID Constant: multi value $VARIABLE Target Property ID Entity/Query property ID Call fetch on relation for business logic in UI and Rules. Syntax: <relation_name>.fetch().

Class: EntityProxyBase.ts getEntityName() either Returns Entity Name. Example: entityProxy.getEntityName(); getParent():Promise<EntityProxyBase>- to be removed. This will come as a relation. Parent and Attachments both will be supported as relations. Returns Promise and resolve with Entity Proxy representing parent if parent exists for the entity. Example: entityProxy.getParent(); getRoot():Promise<EntityProxyBase>- to be removed. This will come as a relation. Parent and Attachments both will be supported as relations. Returns Promise and resolve with Entity Proxy representing parent if parent exists for the entity. Example: entityProxy.getParent(); delete() :Promise<void> This deletes the entity, all the primary children also will be deleted recursively till the leaf node, removes from the entity set it belongs to. If a new entity this will be simply discarded, else and delete action is performed on DB/batch and the registered rules will be executed for ON_DELETE. All cascade deletions will go as one message per BO. This will mark is_deleted flag TRUE on message exchange so that it is deleted from server and other devices. Is_delete flag from all entities to be removed? Var entityProxy = event.getObject(); entityProxy.delete(); archive() :Promise<void> Archiving can be done only on root entities and it will include all its primary children recursively. Send a message to hard delete in all endpoints. Event for archive to be provided. Application to write logic if any reference for that object in other BO. For example if material is archived then it should check this material in all open orders and deliveries. Not supported in offline mode. Example: entityInstance.archive(); syncService() - To be discussed Controlling the data flow to endpoints. refresh(deepRefresh: boolean): Promise Reset the entity back to the DB state. This is applicable only on the current query object. Remove the entity from writeset and reset all the dirty state. Behaviour will be as per the network mode. Refresh on a new entity will behave like revert and mark is_deleted. deepRefresh: Possible values: TRUE/FALSE Deep refresh is applicable on Aggregate relation. By default deepRefresh is FALSE. What is the behaviour in preferred online? Syntax: <proxyInstance>.refresh() UI: entityProxy.refresh(); Rule: Var entityProxy = event.getObject(); entityProxy.refresh(); from(): Promise<FromEntity> ‘from’ state of an entity is captured during the entity load. It returns the current loaded state of that object. FromObject will have only the properties of current entity, that means to get the from state of a child relation entity you have to navigate till that entity object and call from. It returns FromEntity object. Transient properties, Relations and APIs are not accessible. Syntax: <entityInstance>.from Example: order.from().then(function(returnObj){ Var orderID = returnObj.order_id; ........... }); order.ites[0].from().then(function(returnObj){...........}) order.items[0].pricing_condition[0].from().then(function(returnObj){ …… }) executeCreateNewRule() is deprecated and use executeCreateFromTemplate() executeCreateFromTemplate():Promise<any> Executes the rules registered for creating New Entity. Internally it is called by Framework on create in case passing true to second param in EntitySet#newEntity() will result in calling Create Template Rules, but also it can be called explicitly by application in case additional information is passed to the entity. Method available only on newly created objects. Calling this method on other EntityProxy will end up with error. Create New Event: ['ON_CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE'] manual usage : entity.executeCreateFromTemplate() will trigger execution of ON_CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE event subscriptions. This can be used in Rule and Controller both. Syntax: <entityInstance>.executeCreateFromTemplate(); entity.executeCreateFromTemplate().then(function () { entity.s_status = 'NEW_FROM_SO'; resolve(entity); }).catch(reject); toString(): String This returns a valid Stringified JSON object of an entity. entityInstance.toString(); convertTo(objectType, es, executeCPM, insertTo): Promise objectType: object type to which entity needs to be converted es : the es to which the entity belongs to; executeCPM : execute the CPM rules for the newly created object. TRUE/FALSE insertTo: the position to which the proxy to be inserted. Converts the Entity to given object type. Interconversion is supported for the same or different entity. If the entity does not have object type the instance will be converted to default and the parameter value for object type passed will be ignored. This removes the primary keys. Can overwrite any property value. • Object Type: Convert in same entity with diff object type. Entity to Entity • Single Deep To be discussed again and finalize. Field mapping eg: <entityInstance>.convertTo(objectType, es, executeCPM, insertTo); target_object_type = objES[0].target_object_type; logistics.convertTo(target_object_type, newGRQI.getEntitySet(), true).then(function (entity) { entity.ref_id = logistics.logistics_id; entity.s_action = 'DRAFT'; entity.assign_employee = null; entity.legacy_id = logistics.ref_id; msg = logistics.logistics_id + '(' + logistics.s_status + ') Saved successfully'; resolve(msg); }).catch(function (error) { reject(new Error('Error in GR creation...!')); }); dirtyState : DirtyState Only for internal use. Returns the dirty state of the entity. • NEW : Entity is new and no set has happened NOT_MODIFIED: Entity is not dirty NOT_MODIFIED_IN_WRITESET : in writeset but not modified, but one one of the children is modified or created MODIFIED_IN_WRITESET : modified and in writeset NEW_IN_WRITESET : New entity present in writeset DELETE : Deleted and in writeset hasModified(): boolean is deprecated use isDirty instead isDirty: boolean isNew: boolean isDeleted: boolean isLoaded: boolean isDirty: Returns true if the entity is in a dirty state(New, Modified, Deleted), otherwise false. isNew: This will returns true if record is new in the entity and not yet saved to DB, else false; isDeleted: Returns true if the object is deleted, otherwise false. isLoaded: Example: entityInstance.isDirty; entityInstance.isNew; After creating an order if one new line item is added in the order. entityInstance.isDeleted; entityInstance.isLoaded; setLocalChange(value:boolean = false) To be used in exceptional cases when we want to modify the entity locally offline and save but do not want the message to be sent to the server for processing. Need to be called on the root entity of BO. this is an instance specific other instances are unaffected. For online calls or on server it is ignored. Example: entityInstance.setLocalChange(true); getErr() : StatusMessage To be discussed. If you set the code, FW will try to get the corresponding error information maintained in metadata and auto fill the message and type, if you set the message or type, this will take priority. Returns back you the StatusMessage object. StatusMessage: { code: message: Type: } config Returns the config object for the current object, based on object type and brand. This property is only present if has config is marked in the entity. Example: entity.config.fetch(); Is fetch() required here? statusConfig Returns the status config object for the current object, based on status. This property is present only if status is marked. Example: entity.statusConfig.fetch(); Is fetch() required here? moveToArchive() : Promise This is to move the BO data from transaction table to archive table. • Allowed only on root entity. Check if any dependent entity data is present. First archive dependent entity and then this. Example: entityInstance.moveToArchive(); archiveLocal() Remove the BO from local DB. No update to the server. Example: entityInstance.archiveLocal();

A Rule is a function that is to be executed after another function has finished executing. Rules are written by Developer as per the application business logic. Rules can be subscribed with either Entity or Query. Define the Rule: Define a rule with below inputs Rule ID - unique ID across all entities. Class - file name Mime Type: Java or JS Description Recommended to Define the rules on the root entity of BO. Each Rule returns a promise. Promise should be resolved or rejected based on the application scenario. Example: resolve the promise if updated successfully and reject in case of any error. var handleEvent = function (event) { return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) { var order = event.getObject(); if (order.s_action === 'SO_APPROVE') { try { //do something resolve(); } catch (Error) { reject(Error); } }); }; Subscribe Rule: You can subscribe to the Rule for any Entity which can be executed based on the Event type assigned. Rule subscription is part of kloIDE. To subscribe a Rule you need to provide below details. Exit(Rule) ID: Select existing rule on BO, General, All or create a new rule. Exit Class: file name. Defaulted from rule definition for existing rule. Mime Type: Java or JS. Defaulted from rule definition for existing rule. BO Event Subscription ID: auto generated? Event Type: Entity ON_CREATE CREATE_NEW_FROM_TEMPLATE : execute only if executeCreateFromTemplate() method called from application. ON_UPDATE : execute only on update entity. ON_DELETE : execute only on delete entity. BEFORE_MAPPING AFTER_MAPPING Some additional Event types on Root Entity(BO) ON_SUCCESS : execute only after the successful transaction of a BO. ON_ERROR : execute only if the transaction failed for a BO. ENDPOINT_RESOLVER : this is to get all the endpoints to push the MW message. This gets called on every create/update/delete of a BO. Object Group: Thi is optional and If Object Group is not specified, it will get called for all objects of that entity. Channel Type: there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule. All Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON CLIENT Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON SERVER Endpoint/Device to Server/Client---NETWORK CONTEXT SWITCH Klarion Server to Klarion Offline Server Klarion Server to Klarion Server Legacy to Klarion Server Sequence No: Decides in what sequence Rule to be executed. In case multiple Rules subscribed, sequence of rule execution is followed. All positive numbers(1-n) excepted. If sequence no. is the same for 2 rules : should not allow from IDE. Same rule can be subscribed multiple times with different Channel types. Execution sequence of rule: If any change in DataSet of an Entity at any level of BO. All Entities which are on top as per BO definition(sequence of entities) are set to WriteSet till Root entity which we call dirty object. Rule will be executed for all dirty objects one by one. Each record in an entity invokes the Rule. Execution is from Leaf Entity(of BO) Rule to Root Entity Rule for all WriteSet. First call all rules of Lowest level( Leaf Entity in a BO) Entity. If multiple BO changes are there in one WriteSet, first execute the rules of lowest level entity in all BOs then next up… then next up At the same level rule execution is as per sequence number( 1 is top priority). Execute rule based on Channel Type Again jump to Child entity Rule if any modification in parent entity Rule. Same rule subscribed multiple times? Control Transaction in rule: Cancel Transaction Refresh Changeset : This cancels the full transaction and refreshes the Changeset/Writeset. Stop Exit chain only for current entity Instance Stop Exit chain only for current BO instance Eliminate the object from writeset (refresh entity/BO using refresh(deepRefresh)) : if new entity? Eliminate the BO from writeset (refresh BO) Flush Changeset (commit) : intermediate commit How to write a Rule: define(["require", "exports"], function (require, exports) { Load other file in Rule definition: define(["require", "exports", "./H_Order"], function (require, exports, orderUtility) { Event Context: Get current entity or query info using Event context. var handleEvent = function (event) var order = event.getObject(); Require in Rule: require is used to load the Rule file. All the files used in this flavor come from this flavor or from the inheritance hierarchy, so any file you need to load can be required in the context of this flavor. That basically means all the required paths are relative to the current flavor and does not go out or over the flavor. So flavor or version will never be a part of the required paths. In order to load any file which is written in compatible with require/define (amd), you can use require([<relative path to file without extension>],function(dependency1, dependecy2...){ //code goes here. }); The folder structure is as follows: Flavor / Version / Js / Css / Controller / View / … Any file u need from the same folder will have “./<filename>” and any files from another folder will have filename “../<foldername>/<filename>” Require can take array of dependencies and the call back will have those many object loaded and resolved as part of dependencies Writing a file to be in compatible with require/define define([“require”,”exports”,<relative path to file without extension>],function(require,exports,dependency1, dependecy2...){ //code goes here. exports.<export name> = reference; }); Export: exports the handleEvent function which is used by kloBase. exports.handleEvent = handleEvent; Promise has to be either Resolved or Reject based on business logic. Multiple functions in a Rule: Rule API’s: EventContext event.getObject(): EntityProxyBase | KloQuery Return the current object/instance of either Query or Entity based on the context in which rules are invoked. Using this object you can access the properties of Entity or Query. To get the current state of the object, call orderObj.from which returns the current state of this entity in DB. This can be used to compare the saved value with the changed one. var handleEvent = function (event) { var orderObj= event.getObject(); var order_status = orderObj.s_status; //do something } getEventType(): EventType Returns the event type for which the rule is invoked for. If the same Rule is used in multiple subscriptions, you can decide based on event type if business logic differs like Create or Update or Delete. Event types are: • ON_CREATE CREATE_NEW_FROM_TEMPLATE ON_UPDATE ON_DELETE BEFORE_MAPPING AFTER_MAPPING ON_SUCCESS ON_ERROR ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event.getEventType(); getValuebag(): any Return the valuebag instance available that is valid over all rule chain for current Transaction or request. Can be accessed in other rules also. It's a JS object with a key as string and value can be any. Example: Get: event.getValuebag(); Set: event.valuebag[‘key’] = value; getObjectInfo(): any Is this required at the application side? Returns the metadata of current object(Entity or Query) for which the rule has been invoked event.getObjectInfo() flush(): Promise<any> Flush current transaction with immediate commit. This method should be only used in case of a requirement that needs an explicit db persistence. The objects which have already completed the rule execution, will be persisted to the db. event.flush() cancelTransaction(): Promise<any> This method will mark the transaction to be cancelled and resolves immediately after the current rule execution is completed skipping the database persistence and refresh the Changeset. event.cancelTransaction() stopRuleChainForCurrentEntity() This skips rule chain(subsequent rules) execution for the current entity and will immediately go for the next object in the dirty set. Data will be committed to the database for the entity rules skipped. event.stopRuleChainForCurrentEntity() stopRuleChainForBO() This skips rule chain execution for the current BO and will immediately go for the next object in a dirty set. This can be called only on root entity or any entity. event.stopRuleChainForCurrentEntity() config.fetch() Returns config values of an object. This returns only one record for a given object type. order.config.fetch() getLocalStorage getEventInfo addToCurrentTransaction getLocalStorage [CLIENT ONLY API] getLocalStorage() returns an instance of KloLocalStorage. getEventInfo getEventInfo(): returns the current subscription metadata for which the rule has been invoked for. addToCurrentTransaction addToCurrentTransaction(IPersist) : add a new Query object to the current transaction. addEndpoint(endpointid, endpointType) To add an endpoint through the rules, use this API endpointType: BP, USER or ENDPOINT Returns: instance of EndPointBean [Java Class] ADM APIs initADM(): initializes the java class com.maventic.klarion.user.AdmUser and sets the required objects in context. getAdminBp: returns and instance of com.maventic.klarion.tenant.AdminBp Or null, Example: event.getAdminBp(); getUserModel getUserModel(): return the instance of java class CockpitUserModel. initADM() has to be called before using this API. getUserSetup getUserSetup(): return the instance of java class AdmUser. initADM() has to be called before using this API. Rule Sample Code: define(["require", "exports", "./H_Order"], function (require, exports, orderUtility) { // - <ACTION> ON ORDER CANCEL var handleEvent = function (event) { // Updating Items once the header status is changed to cancelled. // making cancel qty to order qty ,pending and approved to zero. return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) { debugger; event.log("*****************ON UPDATE U_SO_cancel*****************"); var order = event.getObject(); if (order.s_action === 'SO_CANCEL') { try { order.s_status = orderUtility.STATUS.CANCELLED; updateItem(order).then(function () { resolve(); }); } catch (Error) { reject(Error); } } else { resolve(); } }); }; var updateItem = function (oOrder) { return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) { oOrder.order_item.fetch().then(function () { var oItem = oOrder.order_item; for (var i = 0; i < oItem.length; i++) { oItem[i].cancel_qty = oItem[i].order_qty; oItem[i].pending_qty = 0; oItem[i].approved_qty = 0; } resolve(); }); }); }; exports.handleEvent = handleEvent; });

Configuration is the manner in which components are arranged to make up the system or application. Configuration controls or changes the behaviour of the application. Possible set of configuration for an entity by which the process flow or behaviour is controlled. Configuration can decide the behaviour of UI, Some Validations, Object flow, etc Works when an entity is marked with has_config to true and configuration entity properties are maintained. Configuration is Object Type based. In case if no object type applicable to an Entity, default Object Type is -1. Entity configuration is framework controlled and values are filled through kloTuner. Metadata definition for configuration entity is provided through Procify Data Studio. config as a relation on runtime entity is provided automatically by framework when has_config is read true. entityObject.config will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for this entity with respect to the current object this holds. If no object type is found / has object type is false, framework will try to find a default configuration with -1 as the default object type. If no configuration is found, returns an empty object. Steps for configuration: Mark the entity(d_order) as “Has Config” in Procify Data Studio. Framework creates a Configuration Entity. It has is_config true and calculated from the entityname by replacing the first character to ‘c’. For example the main Entity is ‘d_order’ then configuration Entity gets created with the name of ‘c_order’. Add the properties in Procify Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create a database table. One Entity has only one Config table with multiple configuration values for different Object types. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Procify Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This help consultants to change the confuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Application behaviour can be changed either on UI or in APIs/Backend based on the configured value. For Example, Sales Order has few configurations like: Credit Limit Check Free Goods Order Approval Order Close Manual header discount Manual Item discount Default Division Pricing Procedure ATP Check Expected Delivery Days Auto Back Order Group Order Part Delivery Allowed

While adding a line item in order, order ID gets filled from header automatically. Aggregation: This is to populate the key in the entity which is not part of the same BO. Separate metadata input required if key mapping to be supported in aggregation relation. Or API to be provided. Association: ? EntitySet is a collection of Entity objects. KloEntitySet extends Array prototype. KloEntitySet have three behavior. Query result: direct result of query execution. Part of primary relation: by accessing primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet. Part of non Primary relation: by accessing non primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet. Deprecated**:** add(obj, position,executeCreateRules) use newEntityP instead Deprecated**:** newEntity(insertAt: number=0, executeCPMRules: boolean=false, underlyingObject: {}={}) use newEntityP instead newEntityP(insertAt: number=0, executeCreateRules?:boolean=false, EntityJson?: string | Entity) promise<Entity> Creates a new entity and returns after CreateRule execution(if the second parameter executeCreateRules is TRUE). insertTo parameter specifies the position(starts at 0) on a new entity in the entity set. Default value is zero. executeCreateRules parameter specifies if Create Rule to be executed inline. Default is false. Returns Promise and resolves with new Entity Object. EntityJson parameter allows to following: • add a valid JSON Representation of Entity or Entity object itself to the Entityset. Object representation can be partial. Like {objecttype:0, Brand:’A’} If a Valid JSON is passed, if a deep structure Enityset will create an entity out of it including the primary relations recursively and adds to the corresponding Entityset. This call will resolve with the top level entity object. If the entity Object is passed it is used as a template and the copy is made with a new primary key. If added on Query result KLoEntitySet than parent primary keys needs to be explicitly filled by developer. During the commit of a transaction if the parent keys are missing or the wrong transaction will fail. If added on primary relation KLoEntitySet than parent primary keys are auto filled in the returned entity. Non Primary relation KLoEntitySet does not support New Entity use Add instead. Middleware allows set of configuration on its functionalities.

This method allows to attach a new message processor, A message processor is a class which intakes a downloaded message and builds the BO structure out of it and persist these BO/Entity. When middleware starts processing the downloaded message from server, based on the download process count, messages are read and the message processor callback is invoked with the messages, Now then the MessageProcessor class is responsible to deal with the message and resolve when the message is processed or reject in case of error so that middleware can continue processing the next message and handle error on the current message. By default Klarion BOL will attach a MessageProcessor class to handle the V4 middleware messages, in case the message processing has to be changed, attach a new MessageProcessor and encapsulate the logic to it only the expected return is a Promise and resolve or reject Ex. mw.attachMessageProcessor(function(messages){ return new MessageProcessor().process(messages);})

Allows to attach convertor callbacks, which has to be called before BEFORE_ADD_TO_UPLOAD_Q BEFORE_PUSH_TO_SERVER_Q AFTER_PULL_FROM_SERVER_Q AFTER_LOAD_FROM_DOWNLOAD_Q These callbacks are called with the message object which can be morphed according to the application logic and the resultant message is considered by the framework. Each callback is expected to return the morphed message, or a Promise and resolves with morphed message. Each call back can get array of messages, call back should be able to handle this. Ex: mw.attachConverter(AFTER_PULL_FROM_SERVER_Q,function(messages){ //manipulate and resolve or return data here }) Dependent Entity: Maintain dependent entity while subscribing endpoint resolver. This will be send with WM message under Dependent[ ] section. Any entity is allowed. Relation is not mandatory.

kloudBase supports a rich set of network modes. Two most frequent network modes are online and offline. OnLine network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) communicating with server for every need. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. If Screen needs to show open Orders, kloBO will go to the server to get the data for Open Order and give it to UI for display. Similarly all the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. Application stores the relevant data locally and keeps the local cache and server data updated as and when finds the connectivity. Browser and installed mobile app both are offline capable. Cached Online network mode refers to the capability of client communicating with server for every need but speedup the interaction by suggesting data from local cache. Commit Online network mode refers to the capability of client serving the data from local cache but save always goes thru online and also modifies local cache. SAP Online refers to the capability of all the transaction goes to SAP via gateway server. SAP Cached Online

Collection of Object Types is Object Group. Screen usage Object Group which defines the behaviour of particular screen/object. Object types of similar kind of behavior and going to be used in one screen has to be bundled in one Object Group. Object Group to Object Type mapping(m:n): One object type can be part of multiple Object Groups. One screen can have only one Object group. Constants for Object Group? Abbreviation : define object group abbreviation like ‘i’ for invoice and ‘o’ for order. This abbreviation can be used in ID series as prefix or some other cases where you want to differentiate the object. Usage: Screen Rule execution Example: Object groups in Order: Sales Order Purchase Order Stock Transport Order

Object Type defines the possible behaviour of an BO/Entity. Object type has a unique key and description. Object type key is unique across all entities and can not be reused across entities. One entity can store multiple objects data if behavior of the objects are different then define multiple object types. Work when has_object_type is marked TRUE for an entity. Do not add any Entity property to add object type field this will be taken care by kloBase based on the Object type flag on Entity level. Possible object types for an entity has to be defined at design time and maintain via kloIDE. Data type is int(11). Max value is 2147483648. Supports merging based on uses relation. s_object_type holds the object type key. Descriptions are part of value help definition. Constants for Object Type. If the object type is false for an entity than -1 is reserved value. Abbreviation : define object type abbreviation like ‘i’ for invoice and ‘o’ for order. This abbreviation can be used in ID series as prefix. Syntax: $objecttype.abr Variable to be used: Constants $VARIABLE Object Group to Object Type Object Type to abbreviation Object Type to Object Type text Display Messages: Object type description supports translatable description use as substitute in title, message, etc with $objecttype.dec. Define language dependent text to support multilocal. Create Entity: while creating an Entity, Object Type has an important role to load the configuration, assign ID from ID series, Rule to be executed, VH to be loaded. Tuner: configurations are maintained on object type to control the behaviour of the application. For more details please visit the Config section. Rule subscription: rules are subscribed on Entity and Object Type. ID Series: ID series can be defined on object type or common for all object types. Value Help/F4: Object conversion mapping: Status: Custom Status: Middleware message processing can be controlled in endpoint resolver. Create operation(in UI-action or Rule) decide which object type to be used. From UI you can pass only the Object types which are part of the Object Group of that screen. UI elements behaviour can be defined like editable, visibility, mandatory, etc. Not supported: Authorization is not applied on object type. For example there are different types of orders. Object types in Order can be defined like: Normal Order Emergency/Fast Track Order

In today's modern world omni channel application supporting multiple form factors and tolerance to network is a must. To support the diversity of device/hardware, OS, Servers, Clouds etc.. we end up creating one application multiple times. For any business application underlying data is a back bone. Unlike old 3 tier application architecture KloudBase promotes micro service with stateless models. This architecture gives tremendous portability and infinite scalability to meet modern needs. With in built klobroker it also enables distributed computing hence multiple system owners can easily exchange their data among themselves to form the network. kloBO refers to mid tier in kloudBase architecture. It is based on the meta model. It accelerates the application development by providing configurability, override, run anywhere ( browser, android app, iphone app, windows mobile app). Developers can write the business rules in JavaScript and based on the deployment model kloBO runs it. kloBO is stateless hence provides infinite scalability and redundancy. kloBO also provides the authorization for security. kloBO consists of a few core objects like Entity, Query, Rule, Transaction, Value Help and configuration etc. Query as name refers are similar to database query. It is used for fetching data from a database. To understand it better let’s go with example I have an entity ( table) called “d_order”. It has multiple columns including a column named “state”. I want to fetch all the record where state == “open” In db term I will write sql as “Select * from d_order WHERE state = ‘open’” and execute to get the desired result. Query also does the same with a few value added services like it gives the ability to fetch the data for offline applications similar to online application. Abstracts the multiple syntax of Odata, SQl, Json etc. so the programmer can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short hand optimization like pagination column select. Security features like authorization etc.. For general purpose understanding, we can see it like below. Following mapping only helps to kick start with assumptions. Db Table: Entity definition Db Table’s Column: Entity Property definition Data type of column: property type with domain Business logic: Rule Commit: Transaction.save Rollback: Transaction.refresh Db SQL query: kloQuery Execute Query: kloQuery.executeP() Result of SQL execution: EntitySet behaves as array of entity Row of sql result: entity Value of column in a result row: entity’s property We can also visualize kloBO as ORM each entity represents a class capable of saving it’s own data, entity properties acts as class member rules acts as methods. Behavior of kloBO varies as per environment. Given the same model ( meta model for application) behavior of query when it is executed ui ( device or browser) are different compared to when it is executed by kloRule as business logic. Let’s see the working example for Order Object. Simple example of reading and writing Data define( abc) Var Orderid = “1234” Var qMan = kloUIQueryManager.getInstance(); Var q = qMan.getEntityQuery(“d_order”); Q.orderid = myOrderID; q.executeP().then((es)=>{ If (es.length >0){ Var ord = es[0]; Ord.qty = Ord.qty +1 Tr. save().then(()=>{ console.log() }); } });

The Status of an object represents the current state of a particular object. Possible status of transactional objects is maintained in a meta model using kloIDE which has Key and Description. Based on the current status of the object screen behavior can be controlled like Visibility, Read-only, Actions, other behavioural decisions, etc. Work when has_status is marked true for an Entity. s_status column is created in all the entities where Has Status is marked as True which holds the status key. Supports merging based on uses relation. To understand Status usage let's take an example. There is an Order placed on any online web portal. Order has the status like Order Placed Dispatched Delivered Canceled Returned Here the first three status are sequential but order can be canceled only with the status “Order Placed”, “Dispatched”. Also “Dispatched” and “Delivered” status can be changed by Delivery Boy or Backend team but “Canceled” status can be set by Customer, Supplier Backend team and Customer Care Executive. Status Profile Status Types: None Single Multi valued Custom status Customization of status as per account/rollout Works when has status is marked true for an entity Possible mapping between status as per implementation is maintained in m_status_custom table as metadata Supports merging based on uses relation. Used in the implementation phase. s_status_custom holds the value of custom status key Description, icon or additional properties will be part of value help definition. Object type will have -1 if the entity does not have object types.

On server physical data may need to be hard partitioned across a set of people. Normally in a multi organization scenario each establishment owns a tenant. Each tenant has a unique end point id assigned.One tenant can also host the data for multiple organizations.

Every attempt to create, update, or delete an entity takes place in the context of a transaction. A single transaction can include any number of such operations. To maintain the consistency of the data, the transaction ensures that all of the operations it contains are applied to KloBase Datastore as a unit or, if any of the operations fails, that none of them are applied. Furthermore, all strongly-consistent reads (ancestor queries or gets) performed within the same transaction observe a consistent snapshot of the data. Auto replace dirty object in query. Merage of result. Intermixing across flavor, version, network more etc? Deprecated: TransactionManager::getTransaction(txnName: string): Transaction use Transaction.getInstance(txnName: string) instead. static getInstance(txnName: string) Returns the Transaction Object. Creates new if it does not exist, otherwise returns the current named one. Transaction.getInstance(); add(txnObject: KloQuery): Transaction Adds the query object into transaction. Any object returned from this query will participate in this transaction. If query not added explicitly in transaction becomes part of default transaction. Why do we need this here?? Need in case of separate transaction. Move to Transaction section baseController:: getTransaction(transaction_name(optional) : string, bAddToController: boolean ): TransactionManager @parameter: transaction_name - this is name of the transaction. @parameter: bAddToController - flag either to add to controller model transaction. This is optional. Default value is true. A transaction is a sequence of operations performed (using one or more Query statements) on a database as a single logical unit of work. The effects of all the Query statements in a transaction can be either all committed (applied to the database) or all rolled back (undone from the database). In a Controller, Model is defined and has a name. Transaction can share the same name or could be different. In case if you need an additional transaction to perform some task in between the main transaction, create the transaction with parameter myTransactionName. oController.getTransaction(myTransactionName); To understand the Transaction concept, let’s see there is a scenario of “create delivery from an order”. In this case there are below three operations to be performed: • Create delivery Reserve the stock Update order All these operations should be either success or fail but together. Commit the transaction if all success or roll back if any one of them failed. Commit Transaction. Clear Transaction Examples: //Get transaction by name and add. oController.getTransaction(myTransactionName).then(function (Transaction) { oController.getQueryP('d_logistics', "E", oController)then(function (oQueryInstance) { oController.addToTranscation(oQuery, oController); or Transaction.add(oQueryInstance); oQueryInstance.executeP(); resolve(oQueryInstance); } } hasDirtyObjects(): boolean Returns TRUE if any object in current transaction is dirty, else FALSE. Example: var transaction = oController.transaction; transaction.hasDirtyObjects() clear(): boolean Removes the object added to transaction validate() Performs as save on all the operations except DB Commit. commit(): Promise<any> Commit has to be invoked when you need to persist with the changes in DB. getStatus(): string Returns transaction status hasDirtyObjects():boolean Returns true if txn objects contain at least one dirty object.

In Application, ID/key is frequently used to store the related data. In the user interface descriptive explanation is required. To achieve it, the ID/key is represented by other single/ multiple data from the related table. Value help is also used to supply the choices available to fill ( combo, dropdown, auto complete) as selection data. Value help can impose the restriction for accepting the input value only from valid set. Value Help (VH) is independent reusable object hence as a best practice always check the existing VHs for reuse before creating the new one. While creating a new one always categorize with entity name so later others can find it easily for reuse. It should be named . Value help Type: Define Value Help: Value Help Name(32 char): unique id across all flavors. Space is not allowed. Entity Name Object Type Query Saved Query VH Transaction VH Language Dependent Config Config Language Dependent System Fields Query Type Runtime Modeled Native Description(255 char) Restrict Value Life Cycle On Session On View Dependent Live Change Parameter: query ID? Scope Dependent Key Display Text: can give multiple values? Icon Query Property change Live Change Threshold Data Sync Query ID Naming convention: Length: 32 char Starts with ‘vh_’ Assign VH: Usage: Provide users with a set of possible values or suggestion items. Show text in UI. VH Design: Associating VH: Entity <>----> Entity Property ----> Property Type -----> VH Query <>----> Query Property -----> Property Type -----> VH VH can be used independently in UI and inside kloRule. Provide users with a set of possible values or suggestion items. Value help is provided by either by an entity or generic, hence it is grouped by an entity. Example: material master can provide a value help that gives material_id and material_description and can be used at multiple places like sales order or in procurement. Property type captures the value help id used for this entity property. Value help definition will be captured separately. One VH ID can be used at multiple places. Goes with offline preferred approach.
TYPES OF VALUE HELPS The type of ValueHelp to be used can be selected under object_type in BOL_EDITOR**. **The Following valueHelps are supported :

Queries are used to read the data from the table, so these queries can be used in valueHelps as well. On Selection of object type, query type has to be selected, it could be one of the following : Runtime Query Native Query Modeled Query On Selection of Runtime Query, query id is has to be set from the existing BO/Entity Names.. On Selection of Native, query Id has to be set from the existing Native queries. On Selection of Modeled, query Id has to be set from the existing Modeled queries. App developer designes a query. Query id is provided as a part of value help definition, which will return a set of values, which will be used as suggestion items. BOL will simply fire the query to get the data. Key, Display Text and Dependents has to be set based on the query type selected. Key & Display Text: Key and Display Text values can vary based on the query type selected. If Runtime Query is selected it contains the entity properties from the selected Entity Name. If Modeled query or Native Query is selected it contains the list of entity properties of the **return Entity **of the selected Query. Dependents : Dependents values can vary based on the query type selected. If the Modeled query or Native query is selected it contains a list of query properties based on the selected query . If Runtime Query is selected it contains a list of entity properties from the selected Entity/BO represented as EntityName.PropertyId. Example: Let’s assume the valueHelp is grouped under “d_material “ Entity which has material_id and material_description as two properties The Key is set to material_id and Display Text is set to material_description. Both Key and Display Text values can be displayed to the user concurrently or just Display Text can be showed and key is set internally. In The above Image Key is IN and Display Text is India. Dependent Example : Let's assume there are two comboBoxes which contains Country, State In The query, we will create one query properties country and create the query as SELECT * FROM States WHERE country =:country And assign the dependent field as country. We will take the country from the first comboBox and fire the Query which gets required Data. *Multiple Dependent Properties are Not supported. If Multiple Dependent Properties are required we can fire EntityQuery with multiple where conditions natively and assign the model explicitly.

After which we have to select the saved query id. And for savedquery as well the key, Display Text and Dependent fields are enabled and works the same way they did for query these can be referred from here. [new table in txn db or same variant based table]) Option on the query to save saved search user specific. Apply the where conditions based on a saved search on the Query Variant based and user based how to ? two tables and get the record merged from both. In initial sync. Queries directly Save option on Query will save to … Apply saved search (id). Internally lookup the saved search metadata and apply where conditions. Constants supported ${$Variables

Every Entity is associated with system properties like s_object_type,s_status and s_brand each of these are in turn associated with there own description, icon etc. Hence these system fields can be used as valuehelps. The values for these are stored in the metadata tables ex: object_type Entity name description 101 so_hdr header System fields like s_object_type,s_status and s_brand can have its on description and icon provided as a part of definition The usage of these values (l_satus_ivon,l_status,l_object_type) etc are provided by framework as valuehelps. (to be continued) SEMANTICS When an entity property has value help (property type holds a value hep id), then a new property with name [<property_name>_vh] will be provided by framework. This property will hold icon : returns icon value provided description : returns description suggetionItems : returns set of suggestion items These properties are bindable to sap ui5 controls and can be used in Rules also While using, make sure it is loaded completely, since this can go for a lazy load. <property_name>_vh.fetch().then(function(){ //ensures that the values are loaded. }) Fetch will return a promise. Fetch has to be used if value help is accessed other than in sap ui5 bindings. Example: For material_id: material_id_vh will return { icon:””, description:””, suggestionItems:[] }

ID series are used for populating the IDs/ Key in the entity’s property by kloBO. If an application wants to allocate the ID self, either it should not assign the ID series or marked it as none. kloBO will allocate the ID on the first read of the ID.

ID Series are customizable in application during configuration hence it supports override or selection of id series based on Brand and Object Type. Application can maintain multiple entries of ID Series ( Entity, Property, [Object Type], [Brand] -> ID Series). Most accurate matching ID Series definition is picked by kloBase for further processing based on precedence first to object type next to brand. For example, the “Order” Object has maintained the following. ID series “order_base_series” with no Brand and no Object type ID series “order_b1_series” with “B1” Brand and no Object type ID series “order_ot1_series” with no Brand and no “1” Object type ID series “order_b1_ot1_series” with “B1” Brand and “1” Object type Object type abbreviation? $objecttype.abr If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 1 then order_b1_ot1_series definition will be picked for processing . If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 2 then order_b1_series definition will be picked for processing . If the order instance in question belongs to B2 and object type 3 then order_base_series definition will be picked for processing .
