The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

Create Blank Page:​ Step 1 - Select the Add icon to create a Blank Page To create a new page click on the Add icon from the top toolbar. Three options will be shown, from those options select ‘Create Blank Page’. After selecting the option a popup will be displayed. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image585.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image577.png) Step 2 - Fill the popup to create a new page In the popup, provide the ID and name/title for the new page. After providing the details, click on the Submit button. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image362.png) Note: Newly created pages will be updated in the database only after saving. To save click on the save icon at the top toolbar (right side of the edit action button). Properties Usage Description Description for the page. leadentity Coming Soon docid The ID/text will be displayed along with the title (bindable). icon If value is provided, the icon will be displayed in front of the title. navbyquery In case user is navigating from a different page to the current page with passing the QP (Query Parameters) in navTo, then this field is mandatory to filter the data based on the query properties passed Example: {“sourcePath”: “search”} navbykey In case user is navigating from a different page to the current page with passing the D (entity unique key) in navTo, then this field is mandatory to set that particular entity’s index as active. Example: {“sourcePath”: “list”} Pip enabled If marked as true, picture-in-picture(PIP) mode will be enabled for the page. screencontainerdefault Default page Layout ID for the page can be provided here. screencontainerdesktop The page layout ID for the desktop can be provided here. screencontainermobile Page Layout ID for mobile can be provided here. screencontainertab Page Layout ID for the tab can be provided here screenid Not an editable field, displays the page ID. title The page name will be filled here, it will be the title for the page. Create Page from Wizard:​ Step 1 - Select App and click on the Edit button ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image627.png) Step 2 - Page selection Click on the add icon dropdown and select “Create a page from wizard”. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image651.png) Step 2 - Provide page information ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image60.png) Once the wizard popup is displayed, provide the screen information. Select the Data Source and check whether Page ID, Page Title, Menu Text, Icon, or Menu Group is pre filled or not. Page Id, Page Title & Manu Text should be prefilled and will be Entity`s description or entity`s ID. Select the Data source (entity or query) by clicking on the vh icon, and give page ID and Page title and Menu Information. By default, the entity id will be Page Title. Page Id should be unique in the particular app, if we are creating more than one pages with the same entity, the Page Id will be auto incremented by 01 as a suffix. Menu Group will come from the app header. We can provide a menu text and can select a group and icon to be displayed there from the Choose button . It will update the page to the selected menu group. Menu Icon will come from Entity’s icon or default icon will come. Also we can allow operations by clicking on the icons provided: ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image38.png) This shows the options to perform CRUD in the main entity. These icons are for Add, Edit, Delete, Multi Delete, Download Excel operations respectively. By default all these icons are selected. We can deselect them by simply clicking on the icons. Click on Next. Step 3 - Select the required section, relation, type, template, position and actions. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image184.jpg) The screen is displaying different requirements to select for all section types of each relation. Relation: It shows the return entity name along with the relationId of the entity. Section: It shows the type of section of the corresponding relations. Type: It shows the screentype of the section that will be created using the relationid. Display options: It shows the different templates of the screentype. It depends on the Type selected for the section. Position: It shows the position of the sections in the application. Eg: If a relation has the Position as dialog, then it will appear as a dialog whenever navigation happens to the section. Required Actions: It shows the option to perform CRUD in the corresponding section created from the relation. We can select the relation required from the checkboxes displayed on the left most of the screen. NOTE: A 1:1 relation can be added only as a Detail section and is supported with Form and Card screen types. The section can be placed as a Section or Subsection on the page.Template Id is supported as Read Only and Inline Editable Section type can be selected from the drop down for different sections (search, list and detail). ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image590.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image600.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image586.png) For List type of section, we can edit the template from the dropdown (Read Only, Inline Edit or Popup Edit) We can specify the position for sections as section(tab) or subscreen or dialog. Actions can be provided to each section type by selecting the icons from required actions.(These are selected by default). The relations have a DND (Drag-and-drop) feature, if we are changing the sequence then the sections will also be generated accordingly. Template tab will not be there for wizard dialog. The detail screen for all child entities will be opened in a popup. Template types:​ Read Only It is non-editable. We will get an edit button for the detail tab only, not for relation list tabs. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image276.jpg) ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image569.png) Inline Edit We will get the Edit button for the selected tab in the relation list. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image621.png) Popup Edit We will get an edit button in each row of data. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image507.png) Click on Next at the bottom of the screen. Step 4 - Specify the availability of fields on screen ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image253.png) On navigating to the screen. all the properties of the lead entity & the selected relations will appear. All the properties will be selected for the detail section(if Detail is selected) & first 5 properties excluding the primary keys will be selected for the list(if List is selected). Select the required properties for the transnodes. Here, availability of fields can be specified on screen by clicking on the respective checkboxes for different sections (Search, List and Detail). On selecting the navigation icon, it will create a link for the property or field in the list to navigate to the detail section. (Only one can be selected.) DND (Drag and Drop) features are available for the fields. The sequence will be arranged accordingly on the screen. If we are selecting any property in the search, it will be automatically selected in list and detail. If we are selecting any property in the list, it will be automatically selected in detail. At least one primary key must be selected. (Selected by default) Primary key selection is not mandatory in the search section. NOTE: In the image, we have selected properties for d_no_header. In the same way you can select related entities (d_no_users, d_no_tasks, d_no_item) properties. To select properties for related entities, click on that entity and select its properties. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image80.png) The buttons are to go back to the previous screen, save as draft, save, and for discarding the page created respectively. On click of the save button, the page will be created and saved. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image561.png) On click of the Preview button, the page will be created but will not be saved. On Click of the Discard button the page will not be created and dialog will be closed ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image634.png) Now after specifying all required fields, click on Save button. This will create and save a new page. Note: For list nodes, at least one primary key needs to be selected. After clicking on save, the page created from wizard will look similar to the image below. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image268.jpg) NOTE: Now we can do necessary changes from the Editor or can update the page from wizard also. The relation section name is taken from relation id ,hence the relation sections are created with similar name incremented by 01 as suffix Refer to this document for the tree hierarchy In desktop view, the list screen will look like this as shown below: ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image138.png) After navigating to detail: ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image168.jpg) Screens will be created for mobile view also. It's PageArea screentype will be Tiles and section screenType will be card in mobile view: ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image328.png) Button Configurations in screen:​ Buttons will be added separately for separate tabs and it will be based on the display options. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image276.jpg) Buttons will appear at the top right corner. Save and Cancel buttons will be visible only in edit mode. If we want to switch between tabs without saving, it will show a popup. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image256.png) Either edit or save button will be shown always. Scroll will start after the edit and save buttons. On selecting the multi delete button while page creation, it will allow you to select multiple items and delete at a time in the grid. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image657.png) If the multi select delete button is not selected, then the delete button will not be visible on the list type of section. Grid behaviour in the Relation Transnode​ On click of the link in the relation list, it opens up the Popup in the same mode as that of the screen mode. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image398.png) ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image255.jpg) On click of the PopupEdit button of the grid of type Popup Edit grid, opens up the popup in the edit mode if the current screen mode is not in either create mode or edit mode.The next and previous buttons can be used to see the next and previous items details. With the click of the OK button, data modified will be saved and the popup will be closed. On click of the Cancel button, the refreshTransnode api will be called which will call refreshP BOL API on the transnode data. (i.e., Changes will be reverted ) and the popup will be closed. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image510.png) ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image224.jpg) On click of the Add button in the toolbar, the popup opens in the Create mode. With a click of the OK button, data will not be saved, as the previous mode is in create mode. On click of the Cancel button, the refrestTransnode api is called the refreshP BOL API on the transnode data and the popup will be closed. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image470.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image456.png) Change in Page Data model Structure​ Now in the Page Data Model, there is no option to move entity properties from unused to used and transnodes will come in the hierarchy of the respective folded path. Note: If a parent transnode is getting deleted, then its respective child will be deleted as well. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image696.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image691.png) Tags​ During wizard page creation, a default tag will be created to navigate to the detail page, this default tag can be used for deep link navigation. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image62.png) Update Page from Wizard: ​ Developers can modify the screen created from Wizard using the Update Page From Wizard option. All the elements selected during the creation of the screen will be auto-selected in the Update Page From Wizard. Example: Sequencing, adding, delete of properties/sections/layouts can be done using Update Page From Wizard. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image373.png) It will reopen the wizard popup with all provided screen information. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image277.jpg) Cardinality update when screen is created from wizard​ If we are creating a page from wizard and it has relations with any particular cardinality. After page creation, if we are changing its cardinality from Data Studio,it will not be reflected on the UI automatically. We have to delete the transnodes manually and have to create them again. For Example: If the user is creating a wizard with 1:n relation and after creation, the cardinality of the relation will be changed to 1::1 from the Data Studio and tries to update the page from wizard, before that the user have to delete the transnodes manually and have to recreate it again. Deletion of a section or control​ If we are deleting a section from Page Builder, it will be updated on wizard also: In the same way it will work for other sections. If we delete any property from the Page Builder, it will be deselected from the wizard popup also. Anything we are changing from Page Builder, it will be reflected in the wizard popup. In the screen we are deleting data from the parent entity, then it will delete all the entries from the child entity also. Make a copy of the page:​ Step 1: Click on ‘Make a Copy of Page’ Step 2: After clicking on ‘Make a copy of page’ the below screen appears with all the details filled already. If you want then you can modify the detail as well. Step 3: Click on the submit button and the current page will be copied to the provided app. Note: The above example was making a copy of a particular page in the same app. What if we are copying a page in a different app and that app doesn’t have the associated entity? If we are doing so then the Page Builder sends an alert message (“Entities/Queries are not found in the app. Do you still want to continue?”) Note: If we click on OK then the particular screen will get copied in the target app without a pagedata model. And if the target app contains the associated entity then the screen will render with all data.

The Page area is the next level in the page hierarchy after the Page Layout. Page areas are embedded with the pagelayout. The detail of the page Area that needs to be rendered for the page area will be maintained in the Page Layout’s Layout Data section. As the page area also has layouting types, supported layouting types are object page Layout, tab, goto, stack, grid layout, and splitter layout. Layout type will be maintained in the screetype property of the Page Layout.

PageLayout is the topmost layer embedded with the page. At runtime, only one pageLayout will be picked based on the device type. The detail of which pageLayout needs to be picked is maintained in the page’s properties (screencontainerdefault, screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screenontainertab). If the property for a specific device type is not maintained then the default pageLayout will be rendered. Example: If the page is being loaded on the desktop, and the screencontainerdesktop property is not maintained (empty) then the pageLayout ID maintained in the screencontainerdefault property will be rendered. Layouting can be also possible using a pageLayout. Supporting layouts are Grid Layout Default Dialog Fit To Area Flexible Column (Deprecated, Use Two Column Pagelayout Instead) Horizontal Splitter Object Page Stack Sticky Tab Tiles Vertical Splitter. Two Column Layout will be maintained in the screetype property of the Page Layout.

CardList​ Screentype cardlist is generally a sap.m.Table with one column. CardList Config​ Config properties are used to set the behaviour of the cardList. Refer to this link to learn more about cardlist config properties. Adding config to a cardList section Step 1: Right-click by selecting the cardlist section. Step 2: Click New and select and click on Config. Step 3: CardList config will be added for the section. Note: If we are adding config properties, the value of the properties should not be empty. Card:​ A screen-type card is a single CSS grid that can hold a single entity. **Note:**On adding checkbox type of control for card or cardlist screen type, dsrc property should not be maintained, otherwise it will show labels along with the checkbox.To bind with a data source, we can use the ‘selected’ property. Map:​ A screen-type map is used to display the locations on the map screen. For how to use it you can refer to this document. Note: for loading the map in full hkloControls 7.0eight, place the section inside the page area of type ‘fit to Area’, and also add the layout property ‘autoHeight’ as true. Adding config to a Map section: Refer to the same steps as mentioned in the Cardlist or grid. Calendar:​ A calendar is a set of working and non-working days specified for a particular time interval. This includes holidays and special periods underlying the organisation’s calendar. For how to use it you can refer to this document. Adding config to Calendar section: Refer to the same steps as mentioned in the Cardlist or grid. Multi Calendar:​ Displays rows with appointments for different entities (such as persons or teams) for the selected time interval. For how to use it you can refer to this document. Adding config to Multi Calendar section: Refer to the same steps as mentioned in the Cardlist or grid. Form​ Screen Type form is generally a simple ui5 form. Note: If you want to customise/configure form then with the following way we can do that: Step 1: Add config to the form type section: click on the form type subscreen click on ‘New’ and then click on ‘add config’ : In the Page Builder, the F4 value help for the columnSpan property displays options "All" and "None". All: Displays all available entries without filtering. None: No filtering criteria applied, showing all possible values. Step 2: Now add the ‘density’ property to the ‘form config’. NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION density string default Specifies whether the form needs to be displayed in default or compact mode Step 3: Now add value to the property. It has two values: compact and default. In compact mode, the labels take the entire column width and shift above the controls. In default mode, the labels appear beside its control. Form in compact mode: Form in default mode: Grid​ Screen Type grid is generally a sap. ui.Table. Grid Config​ Config properties are used to set the behaviour of the grid. Refer to this link to learn more about grid config properties. Note: If we are adding config properties, then the value of the properties should not be empty. Adding config to a grid section Step 1: Right-click by selecting the grid section. Step 2: Click New and select and click on Config. Step 3: Grid config will be added for the section. Note: If we are adding config properties, then the value of the properties should not be empty. Timeline​ A timeline is a screen type of section that is used for showing the timeline of any order/process. A common use case is to provide information about changes to an object, or events related to an object. Timeline Config​ Config properties are used to set the behaviour of the timeline. Refer below table to learn more about timeline config properties. Add Config to a Timeline section​ Step 1: Add config to the Timeline type section: Right-click on the timeline type subscreen then click on ‘New’ and then click on ‘add config’. Step 2: Timeline config will be added for the section. config for Note: If we are adding config properties, then the value of the properties should not be empty. NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION displayShape string Circle Specifies whether the shape of the timeline will be a circle or shape. displaySize string XS Specifies the size of the timeline. backgroundColor string Accent6 This property specifies the background color of the timeline. Tree​ The Tree Screen Type is designed to represent hierarchical data in a structured manner. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organisational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets. Implementation: Data Preparation:​ To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure. Here’s a sample JSON array: [{ "key_01": "value_1", "key_02": "value_2", "key_03": "value_3", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_11", "key_02": "value_22", "key_03": "value_33", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_111", "key_02": "value_222", "key_03": "value_333", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_1111", "key_02": "value_2222", "key_03": "value_3333", }] }] }] }] JSON Structure Each object represents a node in the tree. The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes. Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship. We will store the data in other type transnode. Screen:​ Step 1: Create one pageArea with screentype, fit_to_area and a section with screentype, tree. In the section layout, add one property autoHeight as true. This ensures that the section dynamically adjusts its height based on the content displayed. Step 2: Create an other type transnode. Step 3: Add Controls for Data Binding Create controls within the section for each key in your JSON data (key_01, key_02, key_03). Bind the section to the other type transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data. Ensure that each control is correctly bound to the corresponding key in the JSON structure. The page selection drop-down is used to select the page. The page dropdown will list all the pages available for the app that have been selected. Note:This drop-down will be visible only when the app is selected.

The Where Used list can be accessed from the context menu of the following elements: Page Page Area Section Transnode To open the Where Used dialog: Right-click on the required element (Page, Page Area, Section, or Transnode). The context menu is displayed. Select Show Where Used from the menu. The Where Used dialog opens, displaying all references for the selected element. When clicking on Show Where Used from the context menu, a Where Used dialog box opens. This dialog displays all references to the selected item within the current application. Dialog Layout​ The Where Used dialog is divided into two sections: **Left Panel (Tree View) ** Displays a hierarchical list of all references for the selected item. **Right Panel (Details View) ** Shows detailed information for the reference selected in the left panel. Selecting an entry in the tree view updates the details shown in the right panel. Supported Elements​ The Where Used feature is available for the following elements: Pages Page Areas Sections Transnodes Reference Checks by Element Type​ **Pages ** The system checks for references in: Application menus Home pages Other pages (including embedded sections and tags) Associated files (controllers, utils) Navigation events within the current page (for example, navTo events) **Page Areas ** The system checks for references in: Associated files(controllers, utils) NavTo Events, layouts in other pages and the current page **Transnodes ** The system checks for references in: Binded data paths Associated files(controllers, utils)

The Where Used dialog allows direct navigation to referenced application objects. In the left tree section, a Navigate button is displayed for application-level objects. When you click this button: A new tab opens automatically. The relevant tool or editor is loaded. The referenced object is preselected and highlighted in the opened tool.

Enable permissions for all entities of the application and provide only necessary permissions for the users. Avoid providing all permissions, even if it is an admin user. Only provide permissions which should be intended for that particular user. If permission is used for restricting an action, always make sure the prevention is done also from the server-side. documents.t: When an entity is created, CRUD permissions are enabled by default. These permissions are available to the TESTER role by default. The permissions are grouped under the default flavor-level permission group: flv_master_grp. Whenever a new flavor is created, the flv_master_grp group is automatically created for that flavor. You can verify these settings under Page Builder → Permission Designer → Permission Groups tab. Select flv_master_grp, then open the Entity Permissions tab to view all CRUD permissions. Refer Permissions - User Guide for detailed explanations. 11.2. Flavor Master Permission(Permissions by default) When a new flavor is created, a master permission group named flv_master_grp is generated by default. This group initially contains only the “TESTER” role by default. To assign default permissions to any additional roles, add them to the flv_master_grp. Within this group, there is a custom permission called flv_master_perm. Any group having the flv_master_perm permission automatically inherits all permissions, regardless of what is configured in the Entity Permissions tab. The flv_master_perm is not exclusive to the flv_master_grp; it can be used in other groups as well, and the behaviour will be the same. Upon entity creation, permissions are automatically assigned to the flv_master_grp for that entity. To disable the impact of flv_master_grp permissions, simply remove all roles from that group. 11.3. Developer permissions Users with the “DEVELOPER” system role have all permissions by default, irrespective of entity-specific configurations.

documents.t: By default, all roles assigned under Flavor Master Permission have full access to all entities and menus within a flavor. If you need to override the default permissions or implement custom Access Management, follow one of the approaches below. Option 1: Modify Permissions for an Existing Role​ Remove the role from default permissions (permission group) for whom permission changes are required. Create a new permission group with: Entity-specific access (e.g., restrict Create, Update, or Delete) Menu-specific access (e.g., hide or allow certain menus) Assign the newly created permission to the role. Option 2: Create New Roles and Permissions​ Create a new role based on your access requirements. Define a new permission group with limited or customized access. Assign the newly created permission to the role. Remove the role from the old permission group (default permissions) and assign the new permission group. Note: Flavor Master Permission provides full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access to all entities by default when assigned. Custom permissions are required to restrict or control access.

documents.t: Entity permissions are used to restrict CRUD operations by users for an entity. For every entity, entity CRUD permissions are auto generated by a system based on Permission flags maintained by the developer at an entity level using the Data Studio in the Authorization section except for the download access (It is enabled for all entities). Entity CRUD flags For each flag 1 permissions will be created for example, d_no_hdr=CR_ACC - Can Create Notifications, d_no_hdr=UP_ACC - Can Update Notifications, d_no_hdr=DL_ACC - Can Delete Notifications, d_no_hdr=RD_ACC - Can Read Notifications. d_no_hdr=DW_ACC - Can Download Notifications as Excel. If an entity is managed by external systems like SAP and it is available in Procify only for reporting purposes then the developer can disable the Create, Update and Delete for this entity. Then the system will only generate d_no_hdr=RD_ACC permission.

Step 4 : Go back to the Permission Designer menu in Page Builder. Go to the Permission Groups Section. And create a permission group Step 5 : Go to the Permissions tab and add the newly created permission. Step 6 : Go to the Roles tab and add the desired roles to which menu should be visible. Step 7 : Assign the application to a user with one of the roles. And the user assigned with the roles used in permission groups will get the menu. And others will not.

documents.t: Permission groups are groups of permissions. They can be used to club permissions together so they can be assigned to appropriate users. Furthermore, admin can manipulate the permissions assigned to users in runtime by changing the permissions present in permission groups & assignments of permission groups to users. For more information on how to manage permission groups in runtime. Runtime permission group and permission changes can be done via Permission Group screen in Security & Permissions.

documents.t: SN Steps 1 Boleditor permissions for entity All (CRUD)permissions are enabled for an entity when created 2 Configuring permission via permission groups screen. Create permission groups and add required permissions in the permission group. Assign the permission group to the appropriate application role. Once done, test the application in development by performing the restricted operations by users with & without permissions. In addition to this, permissions can be assigned to the menu via Menu Builder to control their visibility based on the users’ permissions. 3 Transport the application to QA / PROD. Once the application is transported to QA / PROD, the permission groups & permissions will be filled in the runtime. After rollout, for existing users of the application, the permission groups will be auto assigned based on their roles. If new users are onboarded, the permission groups will be assigned during their first registration. 4 Managing permission groups in runtime (On-demand) Tool Reference : Permission groups that are configured in DEV cannot be modified. Permissions cannot be added / removed in those permission groups. They can only be enabled & disabled. Similarly for permission groups that are assigned automatically to users based on roles also cannot be unassigned, but can be marked disabled. But, new permission groups can be created and permission can be added to those groups by admin. Those admin created groups can be assigned to users.

documents.t: When a CRUD operation is performed on an entity and access restriction is enabled on that operation, the system checks if the user has permission to perform that operation. If the user doesn’t have permission, the request will be rejected before executing any server side callbacks. If the user has permission, then the request will be processed further. In the DEV landscapes the permission can be assigned via the Permission Designer screen in Page Builder & Controlled in QA / PROD system via Role Permissions screen in Security & Permissions. Explain further below in the document. Each CRUD permission allows performing a specific operation, Read - Read permission allows the user to fire a query to that entity. This is validated on the server side. Create - Create permission provides the assigned access user to create entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side. Update - Update permission provides the assigned user access to update existing entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side. Delete - Delete permission provides the assigned user access to delete existing entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side. Download - Download permission is a template permission and doesn’t come with any validation by default. It controls the download excel button visibility in wizard created screens. Similarly in case of online query fired from client also, the query will be rejected if sufficient permissions are not found. Incase a query from entity A inner joins entity B. The user executing the query is expected to have permissions for both entity A & entity B. Consider a modelled query belongs to entity A, and it has inner join to entity B.The cases are as follows, The user has permission to A & B - The query will be executed and the result set will be returned as usual. The user doesn’t have permission to A / B - The query will be rejected at entry point and no server side query callbacks will be executed. The user has permission to read B, but not A - The query will be rejected at entry point and no server side query callbacks will be executed. The user has permission to read A, but not B - The query will be rejected while parsing the query, but before query callback will get executed. Middleware messages are also validated against the permission of the user who created the message. If the user who generated that message doesn’t have required permissions, the message will fail to process and will be moved to error q. This is not applicable for CRUD operation performed inside the server. Once the request reaches the server, and is validated, any further CRUD operations performed in the rules are not validated. Similarly for any server side triggered activities i.e. CRUD performed in the scheduler, appservices will not be restricted.

documents.t: Permission groups, their permissions and assigned roles can be changed in the ongoing versions. When the newer version is transported. During the transport, the permission groups & permissions in the groups of the newer version will be copied to runtime, overriding the older version configuration. All the users who got upgraded to the new version will get permission groups assigned based on their application role and the users permissions will be adjusted based on their new permission groups. In case of minor version deployment, where there are users who are running on older versions, Permission groups assignment will not be changed for those users. Permission adjustments will not be triggered for those users i.e. If new permissions were added to an existing group / removed from the existing group in dev, will not reflect. Permissions will be adjusted when there is a change detected in the application assignment that is relevant to permissions i.e. version upgrade, role changes, application assignment removal, admin changing assignment / permission group permissions ..etc.

documents.t: To check whether a user has specific permissions (CRUD or custom) in code, use the permission APIs available on the KloTransaction object. 1. Checking CRUD Permissions​ Use the following method to check if a user has permission to perform a Create, Read, Update, or Delete operation on an entity: hasCRUDPermission( entityName: string, crudAccessType: ENTITY_OPR_TYPE, r_user_id?: string, r_flavor?: string ): Promise<boolean> entityName: Name of the entity. crudAccessType: The operation to check. r_user_id (optional): The user ID to check permission for. Defaults to the user of the current transaction. r_flavor (optional): Flavor context, if applicable. Defaults to the flavor of the current transaction. Note : If permission is not enabled in that entity, but checked via the API, it will return true. 2. Checking Custom Permissions​ Use the following method to check a specific custom permission by its ID: hasPermission( permissionId: string, r_user_id?: string, r_flavor?: string ): Promise<boolean> permissionId: The ID of the custom permission to check. Other parameters are the same as in hasCRUDPermission. Environment Support​ Both APIs can be used in client-side and server-side environments. If r_user_id or r_flavor is not provided, they default to the user and flavor of the current transaction. Note : Performing any validation on the client side doesn’t provide protection against requests directly made to the server. For any security validation, make sure to add the validation on the server side.

Permissions is a feature provided to control the access to application resources. By default an application user can access any entity of the application and perform CRUD operation if enabled. To control the access, CRUD permissions can be enabled at entity level and appropriate permissions can be granted to selected users.

The "Permission Designer" screen has been added under the Page Builder menu. This screen lets you create and manage permissions, permission groups, and assign roles and permissions to each group while developing an app. Permissions are used to permit access to contents of the Application. Permissions can only be created/Generated in the DEV environment The permissions are owning app specific and will inherit to child Apps. There are two types of permissions, CRUD Permissions: Entity permissions are used to restrict CRUD operations by users for an entity. CUSTOM Permissions: Developers can maintain the custom permissions using the permission master screen and use it for controlling menu and home page visibility. Permissions can also be used in application logic to make decisions based on whether the current user has the particular permissions or not.
Entity CRUD : Basics understanding of CRUD activities performed on entities. Application roles : Roles which are used for vieniable.
The Page Builder_klotouch app is required to be assigned to the user to get access to this feature.
The cockpit app is required to be assigned to the user to get access to this feature.

The "Role Permissions" screen has been added under the Security & Permissions menu. This screen lets you create and manage their own permissions groups, and assign users and permissions to each group. Permissions are used to permit who can access what content of the Application. Permissions can only be created/Generated in the DEV environment The permissions are owning app specific and will inherit to child Apps. There are two types of permissions, CRUD Permissions: Entity permissions are used to restrict CRUD operations by users for an entity. CUSTOM Permissions: Developers can maintain the custom permissions using the permission master screen and use it for controlling menu and home page visibility. Permissions can also be used in application logic to make decisions based on whether the current user has the particular permissions or not.

Two actions are required to be added in the KloSectionToolbar (showViewSelection and pivotModellerButton). Once the above actions are added during the design time, the modeller button and view selection will appear in the toolbar of the table during runtime. In Runtime, on click of the modeller button, as shown in the above screenshot, Pivot Modeller opens. If the report is selected from the selection view of the modeller, it will be available and selected automatically. The details can be seen in the left section. If no report is selected when the modeller has opened, it will look like the following image: Pivot Modeller Sections - In the left section, respective report details are shown: During design time, only one report can be modelled in a single instance whereas during runtime, users can work on multiple reports in a single instance. Report listed above the properties are shown only in runtime. On the right side, two list is available i.e Report List and Properties List

It contains the reports created by the user during runtime i.e. Transactional Reports, as well as the reports created during design time i.e. Metadata reports. Metadata reports are locked, users can not modify them. They can only select the report to see the output on their pivot table. This list has four actions i.e. Create, Delete, Copy, Rename on a report. Create - On click of the create button, a blank report gets created with a default name as GUID (GUID, in general, signifies a unique ID). Copy - On click of copy, it copies the selected report with a default name as GUID. Delete - On clicking the delete button, the selected report gets deleted. Rename - This can be achieved by opening the right-click context menu over a report item. On the right click, the report also will be selected and details will be reflected on the left section. All those actions of reports will be saved on close of the modeller.

This list is visible at both runtime and design time. It contains all the properties of the entity in the transnode which is bound with the table/grid. There is a fuzzy search provided in the toolbar of the property list. Here the properties have a drag and drop option. They can be dragged and dropped to the following lists - Rows, Columns, Preprocessors, Chart (Series and Category dropdowns only).

This is the left section of the modeller. It contains five panels : Preprocessor Rows Columns Chart Setting Preprocessors -​ To add preprocessors, properties can either be dragged/dropped from the Property list, Rows, Columns list or the add button itself. Properties can be dragged and dropped in the preprocessor list. Selecting a function will show data showing that kind of value, YEAR: will show values in each Year.(2023,2024) MONTH: will show value in each Month(Jan, Feb,.., Dec) MONTH_YEAR : will show value in each Month with Year (Jan 2023, feb 2023, Jan 2024,feb 2024). DATE: will show value in each Date(1 to 31) DAY: will show value in each Day.(Monday - Sunday) DD_MM_YYYY: will show value in the DD-MM-YYYY format (24-05-2024) ROUNDOFF: will show rounded values such as, if 24.5- value will be shown as 25 CUSTOM: isn’t working Currently Mapping: Mapping can be used to show a different value for a particular value. Rows -​ To add rows, properties can either be dragged/dropped from the Property list, Pre-processor, Columns list or the add button itself. Rows Details - It contains three icons for sorting i.e. No Sort, Ascending, Descending. There is a button - to show more/less, to expand and collapse the advanced fields. The user can paste the icon uri from the sapIcons in the rows section as shown below:(Currently value help is not shown.) Style doesn’t work as for now Columns -​ To add columns, properties can either be dragged/dropped from Property list, Preprocessor, Rows list or the add button itself. Column Details - It contains three icons for sorting i.e. No Sort, Ascending, Descending and two icons for showing Total and Total Percentage. There is a button - to show more/less, to expand and collapse the advanced fields. The figure above shows advanced column options. The column header title is the grouped pivot columns title. The pivot property is the entity property on which the data is pivoted. The aggregate function is the aggregate function of the columns. The default value is count. The aggregate position is the position of the Total column. The possible values are Show Explicit, Show in Tree, Don’t Show. The above figure show the aggregate position: Show Explicit The above figure shows the aggregate position: Show In Tree Chart -​ The chart panel itself contains a switch button, which defines where the Chart is required for the selected report that you are working on. Chart Details - In the chart section, two dropdowns are droppable i.e. Series and Category. Category (x-axis) - Properties which are added in the Rows, among them one can be added in category by either drag/drop or by selecting from the dropdown. Series - Properties which are added in the Columns, can be added in Series multi-dropdown, either by drag/drop or by selecting from the multi-dropdown. There is a toggle button in the header of the chart section. It Enables the Chart view in the view selection field of the KloSectionToolbar. An entry with a label of the report with __chart is made in the viewSelectionDield. Once you select the chart we get the view as shown below: You can further configure the chart with the help of options available in the chart section of the KloPivotModeller. Options are available to enable the zoom of the chart. To enable micro charts there is an option zoom. Colors of the chart can be changed by using the Colors property Colors e.g: {"type":"ColorSet", "list": ["#FF5733", "#33FF57", "#3357FF", "#FF33FF"]} Or {"type":"ColorSet", "step": 5 } Fore more detail check KloChart User Guide Setting -​ Setting Detail - There is a settings section at the bottom of the left container of KloPivotModeller. The toggle button shown above enables the grand total row for the report. The other options rename the grandTotal row and column title. Section Toolbar Properties Three new bindable properties are available on Section Toolbar. They control pivot execution behaviour and link or text rendering — set them in the Properties panel during design time. Property Type Default Description PivotExecutionMode string "client" Controls where pivot aggregation runs. "client" — computed in the browser. "server" — SQL generated by PivotQueryGenerator and run on the database. Switch to "server" for large datasets to avoid browser memory pressure. PivotValuesAsLinks boolean true When true, pivot cell values are rendered as clickable links. The destination of each link is determined by the application's navigation configuration. Set to false to render plain text values. PivotValuesAsLinksScope string "both" Limits where the link rendering is active. "designTime" — links appear only in the designer. "runTime" — links appear only at runtime. "both" — links appear in both contexts. Only takes effect when PivotValuesAsLinks is true.

documents.t: Write the app with its app version and then select the action to either Publish or Validate app. Dropdown will be shown when the page is opened from the menu. On pressing enter or comma it takes the string as an entry. Even if enter or comma is not pressed, on submit it will take the string as an entry. For Publish​ Choose the Build Type from the given option to Publish the App. Publish action will show the response for that flavor as shown below. And status can be checked using the Refresh button provided below App details. Dependencies changes Suggestion​ On click of submit option for publishing a suggestion popup will be shown to the users in case there are any changes detected in the provided apps dependencies. The popup will not be shown incase of no changes detected. These suggestions are determined based upon calculating the time difference between the last metadata save and the last publish time, if the last metadata save time is latest then the dependent app will be considered for suggestions. Actions Apply suggestions - will include the suggestion apps to the publish list Continue with selected apps - will skip the suggestions and continue with the user provided apps list Cancel - will close the popup & publish will not be triggered. The Build History screen allows users to view and filter logs related to various app builds.Refer for more details-Build History Screen ** ** Single or multiple apps can be published. Before Publish, it will validate all the selected apps. If validation fails for any of the flavors, no apps will be published. Selected apps will be published only when all the apps will be validated and there will be no errors. If some of the apps are already IN-QUEUE and Publish is triggered for the same apps again. The completed apps will go to publish again but for IN-QUEUE apps one message will be shown that some of the apps are already IN-QUEUE. Validation failed scenario during publish​ Before initiating the build, all flavors are validated. If any application has a validation error, the build will be blocked and an error list will be displayed, as shown in the screenshot below: However, if a flavor contains only warnings or informational messages, a dialog box will appear, allowing the user to choose whether to view the messages or proceed with the build as shown in the screenshot below: If the user selects Show Logs, it will show all the info as: Else if user selects Proceed with build, the flavor will be published. documents.t: In order to build the application using the URL directly (in case login is not working), the URL should be as below. Replace the placeholders with values as per your requirement. https://<your_domain>/p6/<your_landscape>/closedmodules/<app_util_ver>/buildandvalidate.html?appName=<AppNames>&action=<Action>&environment=<Environment> Place holder Description your_domain E.g.: dev.procify31.com your_landscape E.g.: CTOOLS_DEV app_util_ver E.g.: app_util_6-0-13 AppNames E.g: sample_app7637_2-0-1 Action Following actions are possible“publish” Use this action if you want to Build the application“validate” Use this action if you want to validate the application and see the errors. Environment: dev OR prod.(if action is publish) Note: In case you want to build multiple applications, specify the same separated by comma ‘,’ Example: https://dev.procify31.com/p6/CTOOLS_DEV/closedmodules/app_util_6-0-13/buildandvalidate.html?appName=sample_app7637_2-0-1,bol_test_1,tpr_test_6-0-3&action=publish&environment=dev It will ask for credentials if the url is directly entered. Note: During the build process, it is mandatory for the parent app to be built first, followed by the child app. However, if the users do not follow this build sequence, the app sequence will be automatically corrected during the build even if the user uses the app utility screen or build url.

This document helps the Application Team find the exact source of a query fired from a Procify application, optimize that query, trace the generated SQL, and use the relevant framework (FW) APIs efficiently. Details about Covers: locating the query source, query optimization techniques, enabling sufficient logging to inspect the generated query, and using FW APIs (e.g. addEndpoint) optimally.

Access to Procify Data Studio for the app/flavor under investigation. A working Private Node checkout of the application source (see the Private Node Setup guide). Access to Design Studio → Query Console (formerly SQL Executor). Access to Google Cloud Logging for the environment under investigation.

Not Applicable — the methods in this guide (Where Used List, Network Initiator, Private Node search, query logging) are built-in platform capabilities and do not require separate enablement. The optional logging flags are listed under Configurations below and Google Cloud Logging guide.
documents.s: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Open Procify Data Studio and select the App/Flavor that owns the entity or query in question. In the entity/query tree, locate the Entity, Query, Property, Value Help, or Event Exit you want to trace. Open the “Where Used List” option for that object. It lists every screen, query, rule, or event exit that references it, along with the property type / value help used where applicable. Use this list to narrow down which module(s)/screen(s) could be responsible for firing the query, before checking Network calls or code.
documents.s: A. Finding the source of a query — Where Used List (Procify Data Studio)
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Open the application in Chrome and press F12 (or right-click → Inspect) to open DevTools. Switch to the Network tab, make sure recording is on, and clear existing entries for a clean trace. Reproduce the action in the application so the request fires. Find the relevant XHR/Fetch request (filter by “Fetch/XHR”). Click the request, then open the “Initiator” tab — it shows the call stack (exact file and line) that issued the request. Click any frame in the Initiator stack to jump to that source line in the Sources panel.
documents.s: B. Finding the source of a query — Chrome Network Initiator
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Set up / start your Private Node for the flavor in question. Open the application’s source checkout in VS Code, e.g. the src folder under the flavor’s workspace. In the Explorer, right-click the src folder → Find in Folder. Search for the query ID / entity ID / property name. Use “Match Whole Word” to avoid false positives. Review every places where this query/entity is used
documents.s: C. Finding the source of a query — Private Node (Find in Folder)
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Paste the query definition and surrounding code into an AI assistant (Recommended : Claude AI with Procify Knowledge Assistant) and ask for unnecessary joins, unused columns, and missing filters/indexes. Never paste real customer data or credentials. Apply setPartialSelect([...]) to return only the needed entity properties. Set setLoadAll(false) unless full-row data is genuinely required. Apply setLimit(n) Push filters into the query (setColumnFilter) instead of filtering in code afterward. Important: Expand All and an INNER JOIN on the same relation are not supported together — confirm which is configured before removing either. Re-run the optimized query in the Query Console and compare row counts / execution time. Query Console- User Guide Re-run the screen end-to-end on Private Node and capture a before/after timing as evidence.

documents.t: SN Steps 1 Call addEndpoint once per Business Object, not once per child entity — it already sends the full BO tree by default. 2 Leave onlydirtyobject at its default (true) to send only changed children; set false only when every child must be included. 3 Leave onlyRootEntity at its default (false) so children are included automatically. 4 Consolidate repeated addEndpoint calls against the same BO’s children into one call.
documents.s: E. Using addEndpoint and other apis efficiently
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: The following flags and settings control how much query/transaction detail is captured for debugging, without needing extra code. Parameter Description txn.enableStackTrace Boolean on the transaction (default false). Set true to record a stack trace of all activities of the transaction, including queries executed. Switch off again once captured. enableQueryStats Framework-internal flag (default true) driving query statistics collection. Do not disable unless instructed by platform engineering. "enableReqDump": true (klarion.json) Captures full incoming request payloads into the req_dump folder. Disabled by default. Turn off again after the investigation — req_dump folders have previously grown to multiple GB when left on. Select Distinct (Query → Detail) Set loadAll = true only when true column-level distinctness is required; otherwise leave Select Distinct off.

setPartialSelect(entityPropertyNames: string[]): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description entityPropertyNames Array of return-entity property IDs to select, instead of every property on the return entity.
setLoadAll(val: boolean): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description val Whether to load all fields of the return entity at execution time. Set false to skip properties/relations not required.
setLimit(limitValue: number): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description limitValue Maximum number of records to fetch — use for pagination on list/search screens.
setExpandAll(relations: string): string Parameter Description relations Comma-separated relation IDs to expand. Not supported together with an INNER JOIN on the same relation.

addEndpoint(endpoint, type, channel, object?, onlydirtyobject?, onlyRootEntity?): EndPointBean Parameter Description endpoint Endpoint ID(s) to notify — meaning depends on type (BP_USER, ENDPOINT, USER). type EndpointType — determines how endpoint is interpreted. channel ChannelType filter on qualifying endpoints (default DEVICE). object The KloEntity whose full BO tree is sent. Defaults to the event object. onlydirtyobject Default true — only dirty child entities are included. Set false to force all children. onlyRootEntity Default false — children already included. Set true to send the root entity alone. Note: A single addEndpoint call already messages the root entity and its (dirty) children — avoid a separate call per child entity.

getExecutedQuery(queryid, saveQueryObj, flavor?): Promise<KloEntitySet<KloEntity>> Parameter Description queryid Query name or entity name. saveQueryObj Saved query parameters to apply. flavor Optional — flavor to resolve the query/entity from.

The sql_executor_6-0-1 or later versions of the App should be assigned to the user to access the Query Console. Note: Query Console can only be run in Public Node and is available in the Development environment only.

The Query Console tool enables users to validate and run complex SQL SELECT queries, displaying the results in an organized table format. It also supports the use of EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE for query analysis and optimization insights. Output records are listed immediately after execution. Results can be downloaded as an Excel file with a single click for easy sharing or further analysis. Only SELECT-style queries are permitted. Note: DML/DDL keywords (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, etc.) are automatically blocked and will be cleared from the screen.

1. Select Page Builder header from the menu 2. Select "Query Console" menu item to navigate to the SQL Executer application 3. Use the app selection dropdown to select your application 4. Click "Execute" to execute the query 8. Use the splitter to expand the result section 9. Use the horizontal scrollbar to navigate through all the table columns 10. Click "Download" to download the results in a xlsx file

In the Data Studio, when a user is working on any particular entity/query/value help then that object will be locked. Hence, other users will be restricted to modify the locked objects. Those objects will be unlocked as soon as the user clicks on the save button. If the user forgets to click on save and log off, in the meantime if someone wants to modify that object, then they can use the Unlock entity page to unlock the locked object.
Step 1: Select the Design Studio menu header. Step 2: Click the Record Lock Manager menu item.
Users can search for any particular object with the object name (Example: d_no_items, q_notifications) in that particular app.
Assigned apps for the users will be listed in the dropdown, users can select the app in which they want to unlock an entity.
With a click of the unlock button, the selected objects from the list will be unlocked.
With a click of the Refresh button, the list of entities of selected apps is refreshed.

Columns Description Object Name It will list the names of the objects(entity, query, value help) that have been locked for the selected app. Object Type It will display the type of the objects(Entity / Query / Value Help). Lock State It will show the current state of the object. Locked By It will show the user ID by whom the object has been locked. Locked On It will show the entity-locked date and time

To unlock an object follow the below steps: Step 1: Select the app from the dropdown. Step 2: Select the objects Step 3: Click on the unlock button. On clicking on unlock the selected objects will be unlocked and a success message toast will be shown.
The cockpit app is required to be assigned to the user to get access to this feature.

When using getResult / setResult on the server side for row wise authorized entities, make sure not to send back non authorized data. The data set on to the query using setResults are directly returned as query results, no more filtration is applied. When changing callback from client side to server side always consider row wise authorization if involved. Avoid logging sensitive data. Native query doesn’t support row wise authorization, so don’t select sensitive data via native query. Use “me” token only if all users of applications can access the data, else don’t use me token, use a different access key and add User Access Keys in callback. ValueHelp where row wise authorization is turned off should not have any sensitive data as key or description. The data based on which User Access Keys are generated, should be protected. For example : If Access to issues is based on projects assigned, then, only authorized users should be able to assign or un-assign projects. Query fired on server side will not have row wise authorization / permission applied on it. To apply row wise authorization on server side queries, use applyRowWiseAuthorization.

The feature is for restricting unauthorized access. Only implement on entities with sensitive data. For non-sensitive data, consider using query filtrations. In the User Access Keys callback, make sure to batch queries based on user, as it can be called for 1 - many users.

In the Data Studio, open the Access Management tab. Turn on the row-wise authorization flag for the entity, then click ‘+’ to add a token template. Developers can add more than one template if needed. Tokens are generated based on the application's code in the entity.ts file and the data available in that entity. Refer Row wise authorization - User Guide for detailed explanations. Columns Description ID Stores the access ID (Primary Key). Access key Stores the access key used as a prefix for the tokens. Property Stores the property ID used to create tokens based on those properties. Access Token Navigation Navigates to the Data Access Rules screen to display the generated tokens.

documents.t: How does Row-wise authorization work ? Row wise authorization works by filtering records on the server level by matching tokens (strings that are used to create a mapping) between user and data. A simple illustration like: Entity Data: data1 -> [token1, token2] data2 -> [token2, token3] data3 -> [token4, token5] User tokens: user1 -> [token1] -> [data1] user2 -> [token1, token2] -> [data1, data2] user3 -> [token3, token4] -> [data2, data3] user4 -> [] -> [] Consider an entity ENT_A, where row wise authorization is enabled, and each record in ENT_A has a set of tokens assigned to it. Consider user USER_A, who has a set of tokens for that entity assigned to him. When USER_A fires a query, he will get only the records in the entity ENT_A which have at least of the tokens that USER_A has. Eg : Consider entity d_no_hdr S.no k_notif_id work_center plant Access Tokens 1 10005154 ELEC 2000 wc=elec pl=2000 2 M10236914 CIVIL 2000 wc=civil pl=2000 3 M10236913 AIW 2000 wc=aiw pl=2000 4 10005141 AIW 2000 wc=aiw pl=2000 5 10005140 CIVIL 2000 wc=civil pl=2000 6 10005142 CIVIL 2002 wc=civil pl=2002 In the above example we have two tokens assigned for each record of data, as listed in the access token column. Now consider a set of users and the token assigned to the users as listed below. User Id Access Tokens asset_manager_01 wc=aiw elec_manager_01 wc=elec plant_head_01 pl=2000 elec_civil_user_01 wc=elec wc=civil Now when query is fired by, asset_manager_01, record 3rd & 4th will be returned as the user has only wc=aiw token assigned to him and only the 3rd & 4th record have the wc=aiw tokens. elec_manager_01, has token wc=elec, so records 1st will be returned as that is the only record with token wc=elec. plant_head_01, has token pl=2000, so all records from 1-5 will be returned as all those records have token pl=2000. elec_civil_user_01, has tokens wc=elec, wc=civil, so, records 1,2,5,6 will be returned. As record 1 has token wc=elec and record 2,5,6 has token wc=civil.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: Step 1 : Enable row wise authorization on the entity via Data Studio. Step 2 : Create an access token template, enter a readable ID and Key (can be the same). Step 3 : Click on the property expand icon, click on + - add property, and select the property with which you want to control data access. Step 4 : Save the entity. You will see a dialog asking to recalculate the access token. (This dialog won’t be shown if the entity was newly created). Click OK. Step 5 : After recalculation is done, another dialog will appear to build the flavor (This dialog won’t be shown if the entity was newly created). Build the flavor. Step 6 : Add some data in the Data Studio. And make sure to fill the property used for row wise authorization. (Optional if data is already present.) Step 7 : Click on the navigate icon in the access token. It will navigate to the Data Access Rules screen in the Workspace Hub (Workspace Hub should be assigned to the user). In the Data Access Rules screen, check the generated Data Access Keys. For each record where the access token property is not null, a token should be generated. Now we have successfully generated the Data Access Keys. Now, we have to generate matching User Access Keys to provide access. Step 8 : Now we have to add access tokens to users based on what data they should have access to. Go to the Workspace Hub and create some roles in the application. Step 9 : Create entity.ts file for the row wise authorized entity. And add a method as shown below and correct the logic to match your application requirement. Fire query to application entities, if access is dependent upon application data. Copy this code to a temporary file for clearer view. import { d_invoice as d_invoice_gen } from "invoice_management/entity_gen/d_invoice"; import { KloTransaction } from "kloBo/KloTransaction"; import { AccessTokenHelper, EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType } from "kloBo/KloEntity"; export class d_invoice extends d_invoice_gen { static async getAccessTokensForUsers(txn: KloTransaction, flavor: string, version: string, userAppRoleMap: { [user_id: string]: string }, accessTokenHelper: AccessTokenHelper): Promise<EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType> { let userIdList = Object.keys(userAppRoleMap); let accessTokensMap: EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType = {}; debugger; for (let user_id of userIdList) { /** * Building the EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType map. * { * user_id1 : { * access_token: [ token1, token2 ] * }, * user_id2 : { * access_token: [ token3, token4 ] * } * } */ if (!accessTokensMap[user_id]) accessTokensMap[user_id] = { access_tokens: [] }; if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "FINANCE_VIEWER") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push( await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken( "status" /** ID from access token screen - not the property*/, { status: "approved", } /** Object with property : value for properties used in access token.*/ ) ); } else if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "CREATOR") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push(await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "draft" })); } else if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "APPROVER") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push(await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "pending" })); } else if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "AUDITOR") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push(await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "paid" }), await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "approved" })); } } return accessTokensMap; } } Note : This example considers a use where each role has access to a set of data, but cases where the User Access Keys should be generated based on application data are also possible. Step 10 : Go to the User Data Access in the Security & Permissions and click on re-calculate, select flavor, entity name and click recalculate. Once done, it should generate access tokens for all the users who the application is assigned, based on the logic. (No token will be generated if the application is not assigned with an Application Role). This method can be debugged by triggering re-calculate from private node registration. Step 11 : Now assign the application to some user, and configure based on the logic written in the getAccessTokensForUsers callback. After assigning the flavor, a token should be generated for the user based on the callback logic. Step 12 : Create a screen with the entity and add it to the menu, and build the flavor. Step 13 : Register with the assigned user. Only the data that has access to should be listed. Thus row wise authorization can be configured.

documents.t: Access token template can be defined in the entity metadata via bol-editor, Look into quickstart for step wise guidance*.* For each record of the entity all templates will be used to generate access tokens. A template can be defined with access key and access properties. The access key is a custom string and can contain alpha numeric characters. The access properties are a list of properties which should be added to build the token. The access token will be constructed as explained below. Structure : {access key}={property 1’s value}#{property 2’s value},... The generated access token will start with access key with an equal (“=”) symbol, followed by entity property(s) in the sequence mentioned in access properties separated by comma (“#”). For example : Consider the above example of d_no_hdr where there are properties work_center, planner_group, is_flagged & plant, We have created token templates as explained below, Access key : wc. Access properties : work_center. Access key : pg_pl. Access properties : planner_group & plant (In same seq.) Access key : flagged. Access properties : is_flagged. Access tokens will be generated as described below, work_center planner_group plant is_flagged access tokens ELEC PG01 2000 true wc=elec pg_pl=pg01#2000 flagged=1 MECH PG02 2000 false wc=mech pg_pl=pg02#2000 flagged=0 CIVIL PG01 2001 false wc=elec pg_pl=pg01#2001 flagged=0 In case of null values, if all the access properties have null values, then access tokens will not be generated. If any one of the properties has value, access token will be generated with null in place of other properties’ values. For eg: Consider same set of tokens as explained for above example with this new set of data work_center planner_group plant is_flagged access tokens null PG01 2000 true pg_pl=pg01#2000 flagged=1 wc token is not generated as work center is null MECH null 2000 false wc=mech pg_pl=null#2000 flagged=0 Since planner_group is null, access token is generated as pg_pl=null#2000 CIVIL null null false wc=elec flagged=0 pg_pl access token is not generated as both planner_group and plant are null. Note : Boolean properties will return false even if the field is not filled (is null). But, since the underlying data is null, access tokens generation will consider it as null and won’t generate tokens. So, if required, add the default value as false to generate a token.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: In the Entity file the onAccessTokenCalculate method can be overridden and application logic for manipulating the Data Access Keys can be written. This method will be called whenever the access token is getting calculated / re-calculated. public async onAccessTokenCalculate(tokenHandler: TokenHandler): Promise<void> The method will be invoked with the tokenHandler instance as the first parameter. tokenHandler public async onAccessTokenCalculate(tokenHandler: TokenHandler): Promise<void> { let existingTokens = await tokenHandler.getTokenArray(); let watchers = await this.txn.getExecutedQuery("d_watchers", { selectclause: ["user_id"] }); for(let watcher of watchers){ existingTokens.push("WATCHER:" +watcher.user_id); } return null; } 4.6.2.1. How to debug?​ This method can be debugged in a private server similar to how rules are debugged. To trigger this, kindly check the following section on when tokens will be recalculated.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: Data Access Keys will get calculated when it has to be filled / corrected. It is triggered when, A new record is getting created. In existing records, any of the access properties are getting modified. recalculateAccessTokens is called by application logic to manually trigger access token recalculation on an existing record. Recalculate is triggered from the Data Access Rules screen. (Will not trigger debugging in private nodes.)
documents.s: 4.7. When Data Access Keys gets calculated.

documents.t: As explained in previous sections, row wise authorization on child entities will be applied based on the root entity, so that if a user has access to the root object, they will have access to all the child objects of those root objects. But, the access token templates can be added to child entities. The access tokens generated by the child objects will be added to the root object. For example : Consider example similar to before : S.no k_notif_id work_center plant Access Tokens 1 10005154 ELEC 2000 wc=elec pl=2000 assign=user001 assign=user002 For that notification, d_no_user is a child entity which says, which are users are this assigned to, And an access token template is added with access key as "assign” and access property as user_id S.no k_notif_id user_id 1 10005154 user001 2 10005154 user002 Now, due to two d_no_user entries for that notification, access tokens of assign=user001 and assign=user002 are assigned to the notification. This can be used to provide notification access to the involved users.

documents.t: On multiple occasions the Data Access Keys have to be completely re-calculated. Such as The entity callback logic for generation of tokens (onAccessTokenCalculate) is changed. New access token templates are added / existing ones are modified. Primary keys of the entity are changed. The changes (2) & (3) are detected by FW and will be prompted to re-calculate from the Data Studio. So, the recalculate access tokens button is provided in boleditor to trigger when application developers want to recalculate the access tokens.

documents.t: User Access Keys are stored in the user access table maintained by FW. An application callback in the entity file will be called for collecting the access tokens for that entity in that flavor. User Access Keys assignment has the following important fields. User ID Flavor Entityname Type Access token USER001 o2c d_o2c_employee ROW_AUTH emp=user001 This implies any access token assigned to a user is specific to entity and flavor. So, the application developer has to provide a list of access tokens for each user for each row wise enabled entity for each flavor. The parameters and expected return type is explained below.

documents.t: This callback has to be overridden in the entity file. It is a static method. public static getAccessTokensForUsers(ring, version: txn: KloTransaction, flavor: ststring, userAppRoleMap: {[user_id:string]: string}, accessTokenHelper: AccessTokenHelper): Promise<EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType> This method will be called, When the application is transported to FW, User Access Keys will be recalculated for all the upgraded users. When an application is newly assigned to some users. When recalculateUserAccessToken is triggered by application logic. When recalculateUserAccessToken is triggered from the User Data Access screen. Params : txn - Application transaction. flavor - Application flavor version - Application version userAppRoleMap - Map of users, with key as users & value as application role with which they were assigned. Expected return type: Map of users and their tokens. With Key as User ID and value as JSON Object with { access_tokens?: string[]; org_accesses?: OrgConfig[] } as value. { [user_id: string]: { access_tokens?: string[]; org_accesses?: OrgConfig[] } }; For example : { "USER001": { access_tokens: [ "wc=ELEC", "pl=2000" ] }, "USER002": { access_tokens: [ "wc=MECH", "pl=2002" ] }, } Considering only USER001 & USER002 came in the userAppRoleMap for access token recalculation. Note : Here in all the places user id refers to the FW stored user's id. It is application responsibility to map between application user id and FW user id. Make sure you have written the implementation in the root entity and not in any child entities. If a user is not assigned with an application role i.e. only assigned as DEVELOPER / MANAGER, this callback will not be called for that user.

documents.t: For debugging User Access Keys callback in the entity file, Workspace Hub flavor should be assigned to the user, and the application that Developer is working on should be assigned as Manager. Step 1 : Set-up private nodes and check out the flavor in which the entity callback is written. Compile the application files. Step 2 : Register in browser and navigate to Security & Permissions menu, User Data Access Screen. If this menu is not visible, make sure the Workspace Hub flavor is assigned to your user. Step 3 : Start the private node in debugger-mode and place debuggers inside the entity file, getAccessTokensForUsers method. Step 4 : Go back to the browser, and click on the recalculate button, select the flavor, select the entity that you want to debug, and click Re-calculate. Now the debugger should reach the private node, you can debug the method. If the debugger is not getting attached / not getting triggered, try adding an inline debugger in code. Note : After 1-2 mins the request will fail from the UI and the returned access tokens will not be added to the User Access Keys list. So, after debugging, re-trigger without debugging to generate correctly. Make sure users are assigned with an application role. If not assigned with the application role, the user will be sent for access token generation.
