documents.t: 4.10.3.1 “Me” ($USER) Tokens​ By default, all the users are internally provided the access token me=${userid} for all queries they are firing on row wise authorized entities. Consider the below example. Entity d_so_hdr, where access to the sales order (entry) should be provided to the user ID filled in the responsible field. An access token template should be created with, access key as “me” and property as “responsible”. S.no k_notif_id responsible description Access Tokens 1 SO10001001 MM0672 Sales order 1 me=mm0672 2 SO10001002 MM0472 Sales order 2 me=mm0472 And the users MM0672 & MM0472, don't need explicit User Access Keys assigned to them via the callback. But, when the query is fired by MM0672, the first record will be returned, as that record has “me=mm0672” access token assigned to it and the user MM0672 by default is provided with the me=mm0672 token by Framework. 4.10.3.2. How to configure a “me” token for an entity ?​ Step 1 : Go to the entity in Data Studio and navigate to Access Management, and click on Edit Step 2 : Add an access token template by clicking the button in the row wise authorization section. Provide any id of your desire, in the access key, provide the value - me. And select the property where the user_id of the user who access should be provided is filled. After saving, the editor will prompt to recalculate access tokens, click on OK. After recalculation is complete. Click on the navigate button to check the recalculated access tokens. Search again to get all the tokens present in the entity. Step 3 : Login with one of the users, and navigate to the application screen which uses this entity, whose user_id is present in the access token field. Or create a record and check. The records where the current logged in user_id is filled should be visible to the user. When an access token is generated with me=${user_id}, no changes in the User Access Keys callback (getAccessTokensForUsers) for providing access to users. Note : me token provides access without User Access Keys logic. Thus, it is generic and cannot be controlled on user level. So, if restriction is mandatory on user level, DON’T USE “ME” TOKEN, generate own tokens with that field and handle assigning only to require users in the User Access Keys callback (getAccessTokensForUsers). 4.10.3.3. “ * ” (All data access) Tokens​ When a user has * - ( asterisk with no space in the front / back ) access token assigned to them. All the data in the entity will be accessible to that user i.e. row wise authorization will not be applied when the user fires a query of that entity. So, to provide all data access for that entity return * in the access token array. Eg : { "USER001": { access_tokens: [ "*" // This provides all data access to USER001 ] }, "USER002": { access_tokens: [ "wc=MECH", "pl=2002" ] }, }
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: Org hierarchy is a feature by which access to data can be provided based on the hierarchy of users in the organization.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: Users can be grouped based on management hierarchy and access can be provided relative to the user’s position in the hierarchy. Org structure can be defined with a tree structure (org tree), built of org units as elements of tree. An org unit can have only one parent, but multiple org units can have the same parent. (Strictly tree) Users can be assigned to org units. One user can be assigned to multiple org units. When assigning a user to an org unit, the user will be assigned with a designation (Will be used for access management, explained below).
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: Placing the user in an organisational structure alone will not provide any extra access. Org auth config should be assigned to the user (in User Access), if he/she should get access to other users’ access in the same org unit or org unit relative to theirs. (Eg : Manager needs access to all data in the child org units). The scope of org authorization is defined using two flags: includePeers. If true, provides access to all the users’ access tokens in the same org unit as the target user. includeChildren. If true, provides access to all the users’ access tokens in the org unit below the target users’ org units. Both can be used together. In the org units that are collected based on the above mentioned flags, users can be included or excluded based on designation. As explained below. considerDesignations : Token from users with the list of designation mentioned will be only taken. ignoreDesignations : Token from users whose designation is not in the list of designation mentioned will be only taken. Only one of the above can be used. Both are not supported. Consider userA, he is present in org unit teamGlue with a designation Bottle, and there are other members in org unit teamGlue, whose data access you want to share with userA. Data can be maintained as follows, User id entityname flavor type Access token userA targetEntity targetFlavor Org auth { includePeers: true } Now we have a member in the org unit teamGlue, userR with designation : approver, whose data we don’t want to share with userA. User id entityname flavor type Access token userA targetEntity targetFlavor Org auth { includePeers: true, ignoreDesignations : approver } Now we have the org unit teamPaper and teamPhoto, who are child org units of teamGlue. And we want userA to be able to access data of all users of org unit teamPaper and teamPhoto also. User id entityname flavor type Access token userA targetEntity targetFlavor Org auth { includeColleagues: true, ignoreDesignation: approver, includeChildren: true } 4.11.2.1. How to add org config to users ?​ In the User Access Keys callback refer, along with the access_token for each user, org_access can also be provided in the returned object. Eg : { "USER001": { access_tokens: [ "wc=ELEC", "pl=2000" ], org_accesses: [ { include_children: true, }, { include_peers: true, ignore_designations: ["SUPERVISOR"] } ] }, "USER002": { access_tokens: [ "wc=MECH", "pl=2002" ], org_accesses: [ { include_children: true, consider_designations: ["TECHNICIAN"] } ] }, }
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: An entity is secured with row-wise authorization, meaning users can only see rows assigned or accessible to them. However, there are cases where users may need to see all rows in the value help suggestion items. This requirement is addressed with the "Ignore Row-wise Auth" toggle. Key Highlights:​ Ignore Row-wise Auth toggle allows users to view all rows in the value help suggestions. This does not completely bypass authorization; only properties used in the value help are visible. Other properties will be undefined or null, ensuring sensitive data remains protected. Sensitive properties involved in row-wise authorization should NOT be included in the value help when this toggle is enabled. How It Works:​ Enabling row-wise authorization automatically assigns a query to the value help (VH). This query is applied across all value helps in the entity that have the "Ignore Row-wise Auth" toggle enabled. When the toggle is disabled, the query is removed. Users must then assign their own query or entity to the value help. In this mode, only authorized rows are visible in the suggestion items.
documents.s: 4.13. Value help behavior with ROW wise authentication

documents.t: By default, when a query is executed from server-side logic—such as Create/Update/Delete rules, schedulers, app service logic, or beforeQuery / afterQuery callbacks—it does not apply row-wise authorization automatically. To enable row-wise filters in such cases, use the following API available on the KloQuery or KloQueryForRule instance: applyRowWiseAuthorization(userIdToImpersonate?: string): Promise<void>
documents.s: 4.14.1. Applying Row-wise Authorization in Server-side Queries
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Row wise authorization/How to use the feature

documents.t: userIdToImpersonate (optional): Pass the user ID whose row-level access you want to apply. If not provided, it will default to $SYSTEM.userID. For system-level operations (like schedulers or unauthorized app services), you must explicitly provide a user ID. Calling this API without a user ID in these cases will throw an error. Client-side Restriction: This API cannot be used for queries executed on the client side. This restriction ensures that unauthorized data is not exposed to the client, maintaining security.

In the past, the framework has provided the application with screen lifecycle events like onScreenEnter, onModelCreate, onTranscationEnter, onAfterTransactionEnter, onTranscationExit, onModelDestroy, and onScreenExit. But in the applications which run with version 6.0 or higher, the above-mentioned events are removed and new events have been introduced.
onPageInit onPageModelReady onPageEnter onPageExit onPageDestroy

onPageInit This event will be called as soon as the controller is loaded. The transaction, model and UI are yet to be created for this controller when this event is called. This event will be called only once. onPageModelReady This event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the Data is not set to the model yet. From this event, the developer can call the skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then he/she should be responsible for setting the data in the model. This event will also be called once. onPageEnter This event will be called whenever the screen enters the visible area using navigation (Both front and back navigation). If the navigation is within the same screen, this event will not be triggered. This event will be called after the data is set(if the model preparation is not skipped) to the model. onPageExit This event will be called in the source screen whenever the developer navigates to a different screen. The developer can call cancelNavigation API which will cancel the navigation. onPageDestroy This event is called when the screen is destroyed. Destruction of the screen is initiated only during back navigation. This event will be called only once. All the events hold a read-only object as a parameter which holds information such as if the screen is initialized or not, if the navigation to the screen is from an external source or not, navigation parameters and source screen ID from where the navigation is triggered.

API Name setAttachmentP of attachment qualifier Parameter 1 File Blob Parameter 2 File name Parameter Description File Blob blob object of the attachment that needs to be uploaded file_name Name of the file with extension Example: report.pdf
documents.s: Server Side Attachment Upload — API Details

documents.t: The following BOL API methods are available on any entity property with the attachment qualifier. In server-side callbacks they are called on the property through this, for example this.attach where attach is the property name.

setAttachmentP(fileBlob, fileName): Promise<void> Parameters​ fileBlob (Blob): Blob object of the attachment to upload. fileName (string): Name of the file, including the extension. Example: report.pdf Returns​ Promise<void>: resolves once the file is uploaded to the attachment property. Description​ Uploads a file to the attachment qualifier property. It supports uploads from both server side and client side. On the server side, generate the report (PDF, CSV and so on), convert it to a Blob object and pass it to this method. Example​ const pdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save(); const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" }); const fileName = `order_${this.order_id || "new"}_${Date.now()}.pdf`; await this.attach.setAttachmentP(blob, fileName);

getAttachmentServerLoadP(): Promise<Uint8Array> Returns​ Promise<Uint8Array>: content of the file currently stored in the attachment property. The value is empty when no attachment exists. Description​ Loads the existing attachment from the server so that it can be read or modified in a server-side callback. To save the changes, upload the modified file again with setAttachmentP. Example​ const existingAttachment = await this.attach.getAttachmentServerLoadP(); if (!existingAttachment) { throw new Error("No attachment found to update"); } const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.load(existingAttachment); // modify the PDF, then upload it again const modifiedBlob = new Blob([await pdfDoc.save()], { type: "application/pdf" }); await this.attach.setAttachmentP(modifiedBlob, "order_updated.pdf");

SN Steps 1 From the server side callback function, we can generate the reports[pdf, csv etc] and convert it to blob object and upload it via setAttachmentP API. Below code snippet, imports pdf-lib and generates the pdf , convert to blob object and uploads it via setAttachmentP API // Import pdf-lib for server-side PDF generation const { PDFDocument, rgb } = require("pdf-lib"); // Create a new PDF document const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.create(); const page = pdfDoc.addPage([595, 842]); // Add content to the PDF page.drawText("ORDER DOCUMENT", { x: 50, y: 800, size: 18, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText("=".repeat(80), { x: 50, y: 780, size: 8, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Order ID: ${this.order_id || "N/A"}`, { x: 50, y: 750, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Order Description: ${this.order_desc || "N/A"}`, { x: 50, y: 730, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Created Date: ${new Date().toLocaleDateString()}`, { x: 50, y: 700, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Created Time: ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}`, { x: 50, y: 680, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); // Save the PDF to bytes const pdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save(); // Create a Blob object from PDF bytes (required by setAttachmentP) const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" }); // Set file name const fileName = `order_${this.order_id || "new"}_${Date.now()}.pdf`; // Upload the PDF using setAttachmentP await this.attach.setAttachmentP(blob, fileName);
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Server Side Attachment Upload/How to use the feature

documents.t: SN Steps 1 From the server side callback function, We can retrieve the previously generated PDF reports and modify them. Below code snippet, that retrieves the pdf, modified it and uploads it via setAttachmentP API // Import pdf-lib for server-side PDF modification const { PDFDocument, rgb } = require("pdf-lib"); // Load the existing attachment from server (returns Uint8Array) const existingAttachment = await this.attach.getAttachmentServerLoadP(); if (!existingAttachment) { throw new Error("No attachment found to update"); } // Load the existing PDF document directly from Uint8Array const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.load(existingAttachment); // Get the first page (or add a new page if needed) const pages = pdfDoc.getPages(); const firstPage = pages[0]; // Add updated/modified content to the PDF firstPage.drawText("*** UPDATED ***", { x: 50, y: 650, size: 14, color: rgb(1, 0, 0), // Red color to indicate update }); firstPage.drawText(`Last Modified: ${new Date().toLocaleString()}`, { x: 50, y: 630, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 1), // Blue color }); firstPage.drawText(`Modified Order Description: ${this.order_desc || "N/A"} - MODIFIED`, { x: 50, y: 610, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); // Save the modified PDF to bytes const modifiedPdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save(); // Create a Blob object from modified PDF bytes const modifiedBlob = new Blob([modifiedPdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" }); // Generate updated file name const updatedFileName = `order_${this.order_id || "new"}_updated_${Date.now()}.pdf`; // Upload the modified PDF using setAttachmentP await this.attach.setAttachmentP(modifiedBlob, updatedFileName);

Server-Side Debugging (Windows/Linux) - User Guide Date of Issue: 28/03/2024 Version: 7.0 Target Audience: Developers
The System should have Chrome installed. Access to the required HTTP port number, host address and UUID for debugging.

For Server Debugging in the server, a ticket needs to be raised to the Infra team in Jira with the below information in the case of local/AWS servers. Reason for debugging and ticket no of the issue if exists. Timeline for debugging. In the case of customer servers, send a mail to the customer team to enable the http debugging port in the firewall. After providing the above information, approval from Piyush is required in the case of local/AWS servers. Once Approval is provided, the Infra will provide the access to debugging http port i.e. opening the http debugging port in the firewall in case of local/aws servers and the Customer team will allow the port for customer servers after taking the necessary approvals from their teams. Infra Team → AWS servers Infra Team → Local Servers Customer Team → Customer servers Note: AWS DEV Server debugging is possible only within the Jump server(AWS).

Step 1: Start the landscape-specific Bol Node server with the below command: [Take the help of the Infra Team to start the BOL Node] F:\Klarion 6.0\BOL_NODE> node --inspect=0.0.0.0:9229 --max-old-space-size=2048 --unhandled-rejections=none closedmodules/kloBolServer_6-0/kloIDE/kloBolServerIndex.js servingLandscapes=APPS Details are given below: Elements Descriptions F:\Klarion 6.0\BOL_NODE This is the Bolnode path (public node path). --inspect=0.0.0.0:9229 This port 9229 for remote debugging. --max-old-space-size This is used for specifying the heap size. closedmodules/kloBolServer_6-0/kloIDE/kloBolServerIndex.js the entry point to the node application to start. servingLandscapes=APPS (APPS – Landscape Name ) provide the landscape name which you need to debug. When the --inspect switch is put, a Node.js process looks for a debugging client. By default, it will look at the host and port 127.0.0.1:9229. Each process is also assigned a unique UUID. Inspector clients must know and specify the host address, port number, and UUID to connect. A full URL will look something like: ws://127.0.0.1:9229/0f2c936f-b1cd-4ac9-aab3-f63b0f33d55e If the debugger is bound to a public IP address, or 0.0.0.0, any clients that can reach your IP address will be able to connect to the debugger without any restriction and will be able to run arbitrary codes. Note: By default, node --inspect binds to 127.0.0.1. You explicitly need to provide a public IP address or 0.0.0.0, etc., if you intend to allow external connections to the debugger. Once the server is started with the above configurations mentioned, then connect to the system and open Chrome & follow the below instructions for debugging the BOLNODE server. Step 3: In the Chrome search bar, type “chrome://inspect” Step 4: In DevTools > Devices select “Open dedicated DevTools For Node” Step 5: In the new tab that will be opened in a new window, select “Add Connection”. Step 6: We will put the Server IP address and the Debugging Port No. in the Network address field and Add the same. Step 7: Refresh the page once more to find the target node.

Slow queries are the queries that take a longer time to load during execution. The loading time is more than the average required time. The slow query log can be used to find queries that take a long time to execute and are therefore candidates for optimisation.
documents.s: What is a Slow Query log?
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Slow Query Log/What is a Slow Query log

documents.t: Queries can be fetched in a log file or server console. Note: One can get log access from the Infra team. This image identifies the BOLServer log file. The following statement will be printed in the code rendition space if SQL execution is taking more than the average time (up to or over a minute): “logger.error("Query Execution is taking more than a minute, Query : "<+ sql>); logger.error("Bindings : "+ JSON.stringify<params>);” <sql> here depicts the actual SQL that has taken more than a minute to execute. <params> Here are the arguments supplied to the above SQL.

documents.t: Query statistics help developers boost the performance of the application/server by providing useful information on queries that are to be executed on the server. Query stats contain a list of queries and the number of times they are executed on the server within a given period. It also provides information like the maximum or minimum time taken by the queries. Application developers can find the query statistics data in the query_stats table in the transaction DB. documents.t: In the UWL (Universal Work List) notification screen, if the Workflow contains user tasks, those tasks will be shown on the screen. It mainly has 2 screens, Approver and Requester. The approver (Pending Approvals) can see and take necessary actions (those actions are defined in the workflow during design time) by reviewing the tasks. In the Requester (My Submissions) screen, whatever tasks have been created or assigned will reflect, and the users can see the update of the task on this screen.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/UWL Notification Guide/Introduction To UWL Notification

documents.t: The user should be assigned to uwl to access this app.

Step 1: In the application menu, go to My Workspace. Step 2: Under the Admin Tool you will find Approver and Requester. Click on the Pending Approvals screen. The Pending Approvals screen will open as shown below: Advanced Search : Advanced search has few fields(Task ID, Workflow ID, Initiator, Priority and Due IN), Based on the value provided it will filter the list data. Navigate to detail :- When we click on one of the tasks from the list, it opens the details page where detailed information on the task is shown along with the task history, if any. The approver can take necessary actions based on the conditions by clicking on the Action Button on the top right side of the detail screen. Assign Button : Approver can also assign this task to another actor. The elements on the approver screen have been explained below: Elements Description Task This is the description of the task provided in Workflow. Lead Entity Instance ID A reference ID of the entity object. Priority It shows the importance of a particular task. Raised By Refers to the initiator of the Workflow. Status Status shows the process of the task (ex: in progress, end). Due Deadline before which approver has to take an action. Remarks Refers to the response of the Approver while taking Action. Action Action (Approve/Reject etc) taken by the Approver upon one’s task/request.

Step 1: In the application menu, go to My Workspace. Step 2: Under the Admin Tool you will find Approver and Requester. Click on the Requester screen. The Requester screen will open as shown below: Advanced Search : Advanced search has few fields(Task ID, Workflow ID, Initiator, Priority and Due IN), Based on the value provided it will filter the list data. When we click on one of the tasks from the list, it opens the details page where a piece of detailed information on the task is shown along with the task history. Note: Here we won't get any action button as this screen is for the requesters' view only. The elements on the requester screen have been explained below: Elements Description Task This is the description of the task provided in Workflow. Lead Entity Instance ID A reference ID of the Entity object. Priority It shows the importance of a particular task. Raised By Refers to the initiator of the Workflow. Status Status shows the process of the task (ex: in progress, end). Remarks Refers to the response of the Approver while taking Action. Due Deadline before which the approver has to take the action. Note: No action buttons as the Requester can only see the updates of the task.

The Task status tabs can be seen on the top left corner of the screen for Approver. OPEN: The Open tab refers to the tasks for which actions are pending and status are in progress. The approver can see the tasks and take necessary actions in this tab. HISTORY: The History tab refers to the tasks for which actions have already been taken and the status for these tasks has been closed. History shows 3 months of data on the tasks. Here, we can also see the remark's end time and end action of a particular task. ESCALATED: Tasks shown in the escalated tab refer to the tasks that have crossed their deadlines. As the actions were supposed to be done before the deadline. The Task status tabs can be seen on the top left corner of the screen for Requester. OPEN: The Open tab refers to the tasks for which actions are pending and status are in progress. The approver can see the tasks and take necessary actions in this tab. HISTORY: The History tab refers to the tasks for which actions have already been taken and the status for these tasks has been closed. History shows 3 months of data on the tasks. Here, we can also see the remark's end time and end action of a particular task. SUBSTITUTED: In this tab, the task of the substituted approver will be displayed.

Step 1: Click on ( ) the action button from the list screen or click on () the action button from the detail screen. It will get disabled after taking one action. Step 2: A popup will show, where one can write their responses to the task and take necessary actions. The popup is shown below: Note : remarks is mandatory for all actions Step 3: Upon taking one action, on success, a popup message will appear as if the following action was successful or it will show an error message projecting the error.

The Mass Update ( ) button is available on the Approver list screen. Upon clicking the mass update button the same action popup will appear, showing the necessary actions that are required to be taken for the selected tasks. But the tasks have to be in the same Workflow and their following actions should match for mass update, mass updation will fail. Step 1: To Mass Update, we need to select one or more tasks. Step 2: After selecting the tasks we can click on the mass update button. First, it will check the necessary conditions internally. Once the conditions are satisfactory, the action popup will show up. Or else the mass update will fail. Note : remarks is mandatory for all actions Step 3: Upon clicking the action and giving approver remarks for the selected tasks, the user remarks and user action will be the same. After completing the mass update, it will show a popup displaying the requests that have been updated or that have failed with the reason for failure. So, one can see the tasks that have been updated and the tasks that have failed. 3.6 Task Timeline Process In the detail section, process section we will able to see the timeline progress of the task 3.7 Navigating to UWL page via navTo If application want to navigate the user to the UWL page, they use use the navTo API with the following navTo parameters S Approval Page : p_app_screen_1 Requester Page : p_request_screen_1 F uwl SS Approval Page Open tab : “pa_open” History tab : ‘pa_history’ Escalated : ‘pa_escalated’ Requester Page Open Tab:’pa_portal_open’ History Tab:’pa_portal_history’ Substituted Tab : ‘pa_portal_escalated’ AD Using the AD parameter they can pass the queryParameters to filter the data while navigating {queryParams:{priority : ‘1’,wfid: } }

The Approver can see the requests/tasks and decide on the necessary actions to be taken for the tasks accordingly. The Requester, on the other hand, can see the updates or actions taken on the tasks or requests. For Example: If a requester applies for a leave give the reason for the leave and the duration of the leave. Whoever is the approver for the request will see the request verify the reason and take necessary actions (like Approved or Rejected). The same way the UWL screen works but it can have different workflows.
API name: createTable Method: GET

There are four levels of schema update, the parameters guide for each level type is mentioned below: Flavor Level​ This is for updating all the tables of one/multiple flavors. Mandatory Parameters: update_level, landscape, fv_list, consider Optional params: log_required, force_uncompatible, is_config { //@mandatory update_level: "flavor", //@mandatory landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */ //@mandatory consider: "table",/* "table" or "index" */ //@mandatory fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], /* multiple flavors are also allowed but the sequence has to be maintained properly (parent,child)*/ //@optional log_required: false,/* true or false*/ //@optional force_uncompatible: false,/* true or false*/ //@optional is_config: false,/* true or false. If true, then it considers config entities(Metadata DB) */ } Entity Level​ This is for updating the table of only one entity. Mandatory Parameters: update_level, landscape, fv_list, entity_name Optional params: log_required, force_uncompatible, give_diff, is_config { //@mandatory update_level: "entity", //@mandatory landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */ //@mandatory entity_name: "d_no_header",/* entity name */ //@mandatory consider: "table",/* table or index*/ //@mandatory fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], /* pass only one belonging flavor in the array */ //@optional log_required: "FALSE",/* "TRUE" or "FALSE" */ //@optional force_uncompatible: false,/* true or false*/ //@optional give_diff: false,/* true or false- This will return the difference between metadata and table in DB*/ //@optional is_config: false,/* true or false- This flag indicates whether the selected entity is config or not*/ } Index Level​ This is for updating only one index in the table. Mandatory Parameters: update_level, landscape, fv_list, index_name Optional params: log_required { //@mandatory update_level: "index", //@mandatory landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */ //@mandatory index_name: "index123",/* index id */ //@mandatory consider: "index", //@mandatory fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], /* pass only one belonging flavor in the array */ //@optional log_required: false,/* true or false*/ } Landscape Level​ This is for updating all the tables of a landscape. Mandatory Parameters: update_level, landscape, consider Optional params: log_required, force_uncompatible, drop_extra, is_config { //@mandatory update_level: "landscape", //@mandatory landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */ //@mandatory consider: "table",/* "table" or "index" */ //@optional log_required: false,/* true or false*/ //@optional force_uncompatible: false,/* true or false*/ //@optional drop_extra: false/* true or false*/ //@optional is_config: false,/* true or false. If true, then it considers config entities(Metadata DB) */ }

Table and Index can not be processed at a time. The ‘consider’ flag has to be either ‘table’ or ‘index’. For dropping additional tables and columns which are not used, createTable api has to be called at the landscape level and the drop_extra flag has to be ‘TRUE’. API doesn't delete the tables/columns, it only returns the deleted SQL statements. force_uncompatible flag is for updating the column domain/length forcefully. It may result in data truncation. Use it wisely. The primary key change is allowed only in owning flavor. Domain, length, and precision change are not allowed in non-owning flavors. Entity scp (Scope/Persists on) needs to be maintained for creating table in server as well as in the client. If the scp is marked both it will create table in client and server side. scp marked as client-only, will create a table in client and scp server-only will create a table in server DB. After changing the scp of the entity for server-side the changes will reflect no build will be required but in client to reflect the changes build is required. Compatible changes are mentioned in the sheet, this list may change in future if required

Note: This API should be triggered, whenever there is an inconsistency between the entity metadata and the actual table in the DB. Also, in case of unexpected error from UpdateSchema/Validation of an entity through Data Studio. Please run the below script in the console: Kindly mention the domain, landscape, flavor, and entity accordingly. If “is_config” is false, then it fixes the transaction table of the entity, else it fixes the status/config table of the entity in metadata DB. Entity level fix (()=>{ //Maintain the DOMAIN, LANDSCAPE and params accordingly const DOMAIN = 'dev.procify38.com'; const LANDSCAPE = 'tools_dev6'; let params = { landscape: LANDSCAPE, fix_level: 'entity', fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], entity_name: 'd_no_header', is_config: false, // true or false } const fixSchemaURL = `https://${DOMAIN}/node/${LANDSCAPE}/core_fw_6-0/fixSchemaDef?meta=${encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(params))}`; window.open(fixSchemaURL, '_blank'); })() App-level fix (It fixes all the entities inside the app) (()=>{ let baseUrl = 'https://maven90.com/node/\<tools_dev>/core_fw_6-0/fixSchemaDef'; let params = { fix_level: 'flavor', landscape: '<tools_dev>', fv_list: [{fl:'<eam>',ver:'<1>'}], is_config: false, // true or false } let finalUrl = baseUrl + "?meta=" + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(params)); window.open(finalUrl, '_blank'); })()

documents.t: App Dependencies is an Admin Tool that helps in managing the hierarchy of the applications. App Inheritance is another cool feature of the procify which helps to improve the productivity and integrity of the application by packaging the development into relevant screens and objects and then using Inheritance which works similarly to object-oriented inheritance. This tool manages the inheritance and sequence of the applications used or inherited. The App Dependencies screen has different sections Apps List: This section of the editor will list all the apps available in the landscape along with their version. App Detail: The details of the selected app from the app list will be displayed in this section. Versions: The versions table will list all the available versions of the selected app.

For creating a new app use the Workspace Hub application. Column Header Description App app name in fvid( aid_appName_version) format. Version version of the app. Network Mode App mode/network mode of that app version. Apply Changes Refer to the below section.
Apply change can be used to cleanup duplicate metadata from child App/ inheriting app
Use the Workspace Hub application for new version creation.

The used Apps/Inherited Apps(Parent app) of the selected app version will be listed here. Column Header Description Used Fv’s App name in FVid format Sequence Sequence of the used FVs based on which the app will be inherited

Step 1: Click on the application (these will be child applications) from the apps list you want to inherit from another application (you inherit from the parent app). Step 2: Click on the edit button which is placed in the right corner of the screen. Step 3: Under the Used FVs section, click on the Plus(+) button. It will show a list of applications to select from. Step 4: Choose the parent application that you want to inherit from the list. Now, it will show in the Used FVs section. Step 5: Click on the Save button in the right corner of the screen. Step 6: After completing Save, click on the Generate App Sequence button to update the sequence for inherited apps. The process will be complete. Now Publish the child application from the Workspace Hub.

Export App will download metadata of any given app version(eg. Myapp 6-0-1) in the form of a zip. The exported metadata zip file can now be uploaded/imported to any other application (eg. yourapp 6-0-4). The metadata contains all of your developments like screens, entities, menu homepage etc. (except the files like controllers, util, entity file, query file etc.)

Fill in the input fields on the Export App Page and then click on the Export button. Suppose we have an app, 5-moast4_ui-1; then the following will be the details: Account ID: 5 2. Flavor ID: moast4_ui 3. **Version ID: 1 **After this wait for a pop-up that indicates download has started.

Import App can be used to upload/import any application metadata from any server/system of Procify. Refer to export sections. To import an app the following inputs are mandatory. Upload Export zip: Exported zip with the correct name like 5-flavor_name-1.zip. Importing Account: Account-id. Importing App: App with a version like app_name-1. After filling out all fields click on import and then wait for a response we can also check the status of importing data by clicking on the check status button to ensure the task is completed or not.

documents.t: Upgrade and Transport application is used to EXPORT metadata of any application version and IMPORT onto any other application version. It also helps in merging two apps' metadata into one. App inheritance is another powerful feature which is a part of this application, that allows users to manage the application hierarchy. Read more about App Dependencies here
account_1 flavor should be assigned to you.

App compare allows you to compare two Apps metadata(eg. Screens, entities. etc..) and pick/merge what you want from App1 and App2 then generate a 3rd App. The output of the App comparison is a new zip of metadata which can be imported to any app and that will have all screens, entities etc.. chosen in app comparison. To compare any two applications, export metadata of the apps using Export App and upload them on the compare screens SET1 and SET2 click on compare. System will display what objects are contained in SET1(App1) and SET2(App2)

To compare among two app versions, the compare screen requires two sets of exported app zip files as input. After comparison, the screen gives an object-wise difference. The following difference status is shown on the screen. Only in set-1 Only in set-2 Same (matches in both) Different After comparison, one can change the metadata and merge it into one app, then download the merged zip. The Downloaded merge zip can be imported into the Import App page to get the merged metadata in the application.

A Workflow is defined as a sequence of tasks that processes a set of data through a specific path from initiation to completion. It helps users to manage business processes efficiently. Workflows are useful for processes that include several people, a sequence of tasks and coordination between different objects.

This is a tool which allows users to create workflows for entities of a particular app, which get executed during runtime based on the action taken on the entity i.e. Create/Update/Delete. To perform a complex business process such as ‘Employee Onboarding’, involves going through different steps. Users can define those steps in the workflow in the form of tasks and manage the sequence by connecting them.

The user should be assigned to mf to access this app. The user should be assigned to uwl to access this app. The workflow_admin flavor is no longer required, so users should be assigned only the mf flavor.
In the DEV environment, mf should be assigned as TESTER. In the QA and PROD environments, mf should be assigned as WF_ADMIN.
mf(Workflow Designer) First the user should be assigned to mf to access this app. mf(Workflow Designer)

Step 1: Navigate to the Design Studio menu, go to the Workflow Designer. The screen will open as shown below: Users can select the apps, entities and create workflows for selected entities of an app. Example:
Purpose: To design and set up a new workflow from scratch. Use Case: When a user wants to define a custom process flow based on unique requirements or business rules.

Purpose: To duplicate an existing workflow and make adjustments as needed. Use Case: Useful when you want to create a similar workflow without starting from scratch. Once the edit mode is set, the save and revert option will be displayed to make the changes in your work flow.

Header details can be seen by clicking anywhere on the graph except shapes and connectors. Elements Description Detail This is the building block of a workflow. It comes in various kinds of shapes and its details i.e. rectangular, diamond, circle etc. Model Models also have to be defined at the header level. This contains the definition of the $ variables i.e. ($D, $Q). These variables are used in the events and connectors for data processing based on the use case of workflow. Actor Actors have to be defined at the header level, which can further be assigned to any user task. Groups Groups can be defined at the header level, which can contain the details of group id and its description according to user needs. Used Notification Sends a notification to administrators or designated approvers when their action is required in the workflow.
There are different types of tasks:
This is the entry point of the workflow, where the execution flow starts.

This kind of task contains an Actor, who is responsible for taking action in the business process. Note: The task description is required as it will be used to navigate to the detail screen in mobile view in the My Tasks screen.

Join indicates the dependency between other tasks. This task is used when the process has to move forward only after the completion of a few user tasks. In technical terms, all the predecessor tasks of the Join tasks have to be completed before moving forward.
This is also a normal task but gets executed when the timer expires.
This task can be added only with User Tasks. This is used for multiple reminders to the assigned user.
This is a diamond-shaped task used for conditional/decision-making Need syntax for condition task .

This is the end of the workflow. Whenever the execution flow reaches the end task shape, the workflow ends. NOTE: We can send notifications/emails/sms through various tasks. Events can be attached to all kinds of tasks. It depends on the use case and the workflow design that leads to what and where of the specific things.
These are normal tasks, used for sending email/sms/notifications and processing/updating the data.
Tasks contain the following elements:
This is only for user tasks. All the actions defined for the user task, are shown in the UWL screen along with the task For adding actions for the user define task, priority is mandatory .

There are 3 different types of events: HOOK Event : Task_onStart, Task_onProcessing, Task_onEnd Hooks can be added in the event tab of the task. Used to manipulate the $expressions by providing a left & right expression, on occurrence of the lifecycle event of the task execution. ACTION Event: onAction Action events can be added in the action tab of the task. This is also used for assignment operations of $expressions but on occurrence of action taken by the user through UWL. SCHEDULE Event: Task_onDeadline, Task_onEscalation, Task_onReminder Schedule events can be added in User Task, if deadline,reminder,escalation are provided. On occurrence of these events through the scheduler, expression evaluation and assignment occurs based on process data provided. All of these hooks can be called as methods of the Workflow class, where developers can write their own logic. Following standard has to be followed: In the process column, the left side input is the path defined in the model, where the correct value will be evaluated and assigned. The right-side input can be a direct value or expression.

Hooks can be configured similarly to the Event tab.Instead of assigning values, hooks are used to trigger notifications (such as SMS or email).Based on the template selected and the recipients specified, a notification is automatically sent when the hook condition is met. Click the Detail button next to the Template VH to view or edit the notification template configuration.

This tab Displays all outgoing connectors from a specific task in the workflow.Each connector defines the next step in the workflow based on the user's action at the source task.The connectors typically represent different outcomes like approve/reject, ensuring that the process transitions correctly depending on user decisions.

To trigger a workflow, an entity action, such as onCreate, onUpdate, or onDelete must be specified in the condition. The expression field is optional. If an expression is provided, it must evaluate to true for the workflow to be initiated.

Actors are placeholders defined in the workflow as expression variables. At runtime, these expressions are evaluated and resolved to actual users, who will then perform the tasks assigned to them. The Actor tab is available at the workflow header level. To access it, click anywhere on the canvas except on shapes or connectors. Note: All actors used in the workflow must first be maintained in the mwfa_actor_resolver table to ensure proper resolution during execution. A task can be assigned to multiple users, and actor mappings are scoped to an application. See section 3.2.9.5. All those actors have to be defined here and can be further assigned to user tasks as mentioned in the below screenshot.

The Model List is available at the workflow header level. Only $D (Data) and $Q (Query) type variables can be defined here.These variables can be used in expressions across the workflow, including in: events/notifications/connectors.

This is a user-defined variable, which can be defined in the model tab of the workflow header.It completely depends on the use case of the workflow, and how many $D variables are required. For instance, let's say the user has defined the variable $D>/hasApproved variable in the model section.Users can use this variable wherever expression is allowed, let it be task hooks or connectors or email/sms/notification templates. Example: The defined variable is used in the connector. However, the value of this variable has to be either assigned through an event.

This is a query variable which can be defined in the model. Workflow internally calls entity query with the given parameters. The resulting entity can be then available in the variable. e.g. - {$Q>/fetchTeamBudget} in any expression returns a single entity object.

$E is predefined, hence the user cannot re-assign its value in the runtime. This contains the lead entity, upon which workflow is getting executed. Users can access and assign values to the entity property in the following manner:
This is a system variable and cannot be declared by the user in the model. $S contains certain utilities. For example - At any point {$S>/now} in an expression, returns the current timestamp in ms.

The group is available in the header section of the workflow. This is a root entity and workflows can be mapped with groups. Individual groups can be mapped with different types of tasks in the same workflow.
This list is available in the header section of the workflow. Users can see the list of all the notifications used in the workflow.
Mf must be assigned.

Before proceeding with UWL, a mf must be assigned. Once assigned, the Workflow Participants section under the Workflow Manager will display a list of responsible actors along with their resolved user details and user IDs. The Workflow Manager can manage these actors by adding new ones, editing existing entries, or removing them from the workflow as needed. Tasks can be assigned to multiple users. Actor mappings are scoped to an application.

The Active Workflows screen provides a Workflow Status Diagram of the workflow that has been created. This visual display allows users to view the workflow’s structure and progression, but it is view-only and cannot be edited from this screen. This diagram shows the current status of a workflow instance.The shapes marked indicates; green -> Executed Yellow -> Pending Red -> Suspended, Failed, Expired The Failed and Expired states are new. A workflow that fails moves to Failed, and a workflow whose deadline expires moves to Expired. Admins can also cancel running instances. See section 3.2.9. In addition to the diagram, the evaluated results of $D variables are also shown: Once the workflow is checked and verified, it can be moved to the UWL (Universal Workflow List) for further processing or execution.

UWL must be assigned. The UWL (Universal Work List) is a modifiable notification screen that displays tasks from the user tasks list. It reflects the tasks assigned to users and allows them to manage and process those tasks efficiently. Navigate to My Workspace and then choose My Submissions to view the task details for the workflow created. In the My Tasks screen, you will find options such as Open, History, and Substituted, which allow you to view the list of requests submitted for the actors' approval. These options provide a comprehensive view of the task statuses,remarks and their history. Navigate to My Workspace and select My Submissions to approve or reject a created workflow . For actors, the workflow tasks will be displayed in the My Tasks section, where you can review each task and take appropriate action such as approval or rejection.
When a workflow fails, it now moves to a Failed state and the failure reason is recorded.
When a deadline expires, the workflow moves to a new Expired state.
Unexpected errors in scheduled steps are retried automatically. The retry count configurable.
Admins can cancel running workflow instances. The details of the cancellation, such as the reason for cancellation, are captured. An onCancel() hook is available to applications.
For automation of complex workflows within the organisation.

WorkflowServices gives a supported API with the same rules as UWL (flavor scoping, user scope, group-candidate tasks). Typical use: a custom screen or service that shows a user’s pending approvals, lets them approve or reject, and tracks their submitted requests, without embedding the UWL screen.

The ticket doesn’t give signatures, so the calls below are illustrative only. Argument names and shapes are assumed. Check the JSDoc in WorkflowServices.ts for the real ones. ts const wf = WorkflowServices.gI("myFlavor", txn);  Method Used for Example gI(flavor, txn) Start here. Gets the service scoped to your flavor. const wf = WorkflowServices.gI("myFlavor", txn); getTasksP A full worklist (open plus others) with filters await wf.getTasksP({ priority: "High" }) getOpenTasksP A “Pending approvals” tab or badge count await wf.getOpenTasksP({}) getEscalatedTasksP An “Escalated / overdue” tab await wf.getEscalatedTasksP({}) getHistoryTasksP A “Completed tasks” history view await wf.getHistoryTasksP({ deadlineFrom: "2026-10-01" }) getTaskP A task detail page await wf.getTaskP(taskid) getFilterOptionsP Filling filter dropdowns (workflow, priority) await wf.getFilterOptionsP() getMySubmissionsP A “My requests” list await wf.getMySubmissionsP({}) getMySubmissionInstanceP Opening one of my requests to see its status await wf.getMySubmissionInstanceP(instanceId) getWfInstanceP A progress tracker showing the steps of a workflow await wf.getWfInstanceP(instanceId) getTaskActionsP Showing the right buttons (Approve, Reject) await wf.getTaskActionsP(taskid) executeActionP Running the button click await wf.executeActionP(taskid, "APPROVE", comment) getSubstituteActorsP Filling the “Reassign to” user picker await wf.getSubstituteActorsP(taskid) substituteTaskP Delegating a task, such as when on leave await wf.substituteTaskP(taskid, newActor)
documents.s: What each method is for, with example usage

documents.t: gI(...) gets the service. getOpenTasksP shows the pending list. The user opens a task, and getTaskP plus getTaskActionsP load its details and buttons. The user clicks Approve, and executeActionP runs it. The user can instead delegate: getSubstituteActorsP, then substituteTaskP.

documents.t: Step 1: Go to the Apps tab of the App Collections detail screen. Step 2: Click on the Edit button. Step 3: Click on the Add button. Step 4: A pop-up will appear. Select the apps and click on the Add button present at the bottom. Only apps having the same auth code as the app group and assigned as manager role to the logged in user can be added. The app will be successfully added in the details section. Step 5: You will have the option to specify: Update Type: It specifies how the app will be installed. Regular: It installs the registered app normally for the user and creates initial sync, table generation, etc On-Demand: It helps to assign the app to the user but the user has to install the app through the Developer Page. Default: It is the same as regular installation type which helps the user to assign the app directly with table creation. Upgrade Type: It specifies how the app will be upgraded. Immediate: It upgrades the app with an immediate notification where the user will have the option of the OK button and it upgrades the app. Postpondable: It upgrades the app with an optional notification where the user will have the option of the OK and Cancel buttons and it will install the app later on. Role: specifies via which role the application will be assigned to the users of that group. Supported Channel: It specifies that the application assigned to the user group will be for browser, device or both. You can toggle the buttons according to your needs. Step 6: Click on the Save button. Note: When displaying individual apps within App Collections: Non-MANAGER roles: Only the latest added version of an app is retained in the group. Older versions with the same major and minor version are removed upon new addition. MANAGER role: All added versions of the app are retained, even if they share the same major and minor version. This ensures that MANAGER roles can track version history, while non-MANAGER roles only reflect the latest active version. documents.t: When a new user is created in the Workspace Hub, that user will be automatically assigned to an Auth Code named “Common” Note: If your user is old, you might not be assigned to this Auth Code.

Step 1: In the Auth Configuration you will find unique groups which will consist of specific groups of users. Click on the Add button. Step 2: In the details section, create an Auth code for your group and save it. Step 3: Next go to the Users section and add users with the help of the Add button. Step 4: Select the users you want to add to your newly created group. Step 5: Save the process. Note: Please add your account (Manager) as well in the Users section otherwise the group will not reflect. For example: Here the demo test is my user name. Hence my account needs to be added to this group. Users present in any auth code group can see users, App Collections and User Collections having the same auth code.

Using User group and App group: usage of using user group and App Collections and mapping them is the best policy, Instead of assigning in the apps screen. Example: Imagine an organization having 100 users to whom we need to assign two apps. Without User Collections and App Collections: to add users we have to select 100 users to assign for each role to assign and viceversa for removal of users. It needs more effort. With User Collections and App Collections: to add users add apps into the App Collections with all the roles, add 100 users into User Collections. Map the user group with the app group and for removal just remove apps from App Collections. It needs less effort. Mapping user group and App Collections : go to App Collections tab in user group detail and add app group to the user group or go to user group tab in any app group and add user group. How to maintain Hierarchy of users? : User with tester access need to be assigned to the tester role Users with development access need to be assigned to the development role. Users with manager access need to be assigned to a manager role. If a user is assigned to all the roles, application roles will take precedence over developer role and manager role. In application role precedence will be taken based upon role_precedence.

Each user can be provided with a designation or role. Step 1: In the Apps section, once an App is created click on the app ID from the app list. Step 2: Go to the Roles & Users tab, and click the Edit button. Step 3: Go to the application roles’ section toolbar and click on the “+” Button, a new row will appear in the grid table. Step 4: Add the role ID and description and click Save. It has 2 buttons: Configure - It will navigate to Design Studio → Permission Modeler and load that flavor data. Cancel - It will simply close the dialog. User Assignment​ Users can be assigned to apps via roles. The roles can be as follows: Application Roles: These are mainly custom-created roles meant for the users who will use the application. Tester is the default role provided by the framework. System Roles: These are the default roles provided by Framework. It will be Developer: Users assigned as developers can create entities and relations in the particular app. Manager: Users assigned as managers can create new apps and assign users to those apps.

Important: There are a few things we need to know about App Versioning. The App versions are written in 6-0-1(Major-Minor-Patch). Here, 6 is referred to as Major 0 is referred to as Minor and, 1 is referred to as Patch When the patch is changed while versioning, the roles & users are automatically copied from the previous version to the recent version. If the minor or major is changed then the users will not get copied from the previous version to the new version. While creating a new version the patch number automatically changes, but when you want to create the app branch click on the branch button and it will create a branch with the latest version like major-minor+B-patch ,Note: When any new or hot fixes are made a new version should be created for that and an update should be taken for the same. All flavors within a single application hierarchy must use the same FW version to ensure compatibility and consistency. If any application in the hierarchy (that has dependencies with other flavors) requires a FW version upgrade, all associated flavors within that hierarchy must also be updated to the same new FW version. Example: If em4_6-0-1 plans to upgrade to a newer FW version (e.g., 6-1-0), then every other flavor under the same hierarchy must be versioned accordingly and updated to use 6-1-0. However, independent flavors that do not belong to this hierarchy are not required to update their FW version.

documents.t: The endpoint is used to check and manage account log-in. Whenever any new user registers in the application, a new endpoint ID is created against that account. This can be checked in the endpoint section. The Endpoint table consists of the following information: Attributes Description Endpoint ID It is a unique ID generated each time an account logs in Login ID This is the ID of the user. Channel Type This implies the channel or mode via which the user has logged in. It can be via a browser or device. Status Once a user does fresh registration they become a New user and then when they log in again the status becomes Active for them. Also if any user is Deboarded from the console it reflects here. Remark It gives remarks relevant to the endpoint. When you click on any particular endpoint ID on the screen, it will open a detailed screen for that Endpoint ID. In this detail screen, there are two sections: Details About There is also a Deboard action button available on the right-hand side of the screen in case a user needs to be removed. Under Details, All the information regarding the user of the endpoint will be present as shown in the image below: The About section, consists of App Name, Role ID and version. The app name shows the number of apps that have been assigned to the user, for that particular Endpoint. Role ID puts forth the role this user is playing against each app and the Version shows the version, framework and Build Number. Note : To check the user activity, click on the check login history button. It will get navigated to a new screen to show logs of user login activity.

documents.t: Workspace Hub menu will be visible for Users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN. Step 1: Go to the menu options and select Workspace Hub. Step 2: The Workspace Hub contains the following screens. Under the menu header, App Lifecycle users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN wIll find Auth Configuration and Custom Domains menus. Under the menu header,App Lifecycle users who are assigned SUPERADMIN and not as any application role wIll find the App Authorisation menu. First, we will look into the menus under the menu header Workspace Hub. AccountDetails - For overviewing the account details of the user and modifying it. Account Name : Account Name are the basic details of the customer for which the account is created. Account Type: Account Type are the basic details of the customer for which the account is created. Valid Till: Valid till are the subscription period of the account which has been created for the customer. Valid From: Valid from are the subscription period of the account which has been created for the customer. User Management - The User screen lists the users who are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration whose accounts have been created under current landscape.We can check the details of the users, the User Collections one is assigned , the endpoints and apps assigned. Need help?: Need help is the help and support section in an Workspace Hub that includes options for contacting customer support, such as phone numbers or email details, and links to important documents like Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, and Logo sections. You can also find details on sales inquiries or account management contacts. App Management - The Apps screen lists the Apps that are created in the current landscape for which logged in user has MANAGER access . Apps help create new apps, assign users based on roles to the app, and add language and FAQ Keys. use show External checkbox to show/hide external apps (default hide). Use ShowExternal to see external apps assigned to the user as manager. User ShowAll to see all the versions of apps assigned to the user as manager. User Collections - The User Group screen lists the User Collections who are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration and have been created under the current landscape. A User Group is the section where a group of users using the same application are listed. User Collections are of two types : 1. Individual user group which is created by default for every user. By default individual User Collections are hidden, use show Individual checkbox if needed. Individual User Collections are needed to automatically assign newly created apps to the logged in user. 2. Group user group which was manually created. These groups of users can be assigned to an app group. App Collections - The App Group screen lists the App Collections which are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration and have been created under the current landscape. The App Group is used to create groups that will consist of apps which fall under a particular project or that fall under a particular user. App Collections are of two types: 1. Individual App group which is created by default during every new , major and minor App creation. By default individual App Collections are hidden, use show Individual checkbox if needed. Individual App Collections are used to assign newly created apps to the logged in user. 2. Group App group which was manually created. One can also add User Collections to the App Collections. Login Sessions - Whenever any account is registered in the application, a new endpoint ID gets created against that account. It can be checked in the endpoint section. Now, we have three menus under the menu header App Lifecycle. Let us delve in to know what each does. Auth Configuration - Here we will find the available Auth Configuration that are available in this tool and under this we can add or remove users according to our requirements. Auth Configuration are used to segregate users, apps , User Collections ,App Collections. It works as authorisation to particular users for apps, users, App Collections and User Collections. Custom Domains - Custom Domains is a URL Development for redirecting a short url to its long url version. This process is done to make the URLs convenient for the end user's understanding. Short URLs improve the user experience by being easier to type out. AI User Quota - AI User quota is a screen that will store the AI seat allocation details for the users. It consists of seat id clicking on which it will navigate to the AI conversation history screen. This screen is only visible to app admins. AI Conversation History - AI conversation history is a screen that has detailed information about the prompts and the corresponding responses that are given by user/’s using particular seats. This screen is only visible to app admins. Now, we have a menu under the menu header App Lifecycle**.** Let us delve in to know what each does. App Authorisation - In this section, the accounts of the current or existing users will be shown and the users can assign or remove apps as and when required. Note:​ After saving in the Users, User Collections and App Collections screen a popup will be shown indicating that Permission has been triggered and can be checked in the Permission Logs screen. User can go to Permission Logs screen in App Lifecycle

1.15.1.1. Business Requirement​ Application configuration wizard is to create a new application in the system by taking the necessary information, an application can also be created by taking a reference of an existing application. 1.15.1.2. Prerequisites​ All configuration tables in the system. The Application wizard and its components in the system. 1.15.1.3.Process Flow​ Path : Wizards → Application Wizard Tcode : /MVN/APP_WIZARD Report : /MVN/RP_APP_WIZARD Execute the Tcode or use Menu to open the wizard. It enters the start page of the wizard as shown below. Wizard steps​ Please read the guidelines provided in each step of the wizard carefully before proceeding with the execution of that step. Name and Integration parameters​ This step is for setting up the application configuration. Input Purpose Possible values Application-Version App and version of the newly created app. Eg:eam-1 Integration Mode Integration mode of app Online/ Offline Integration Type Integration type of app File/Gateway/PI or PO Reference From All Informations will be copied from the reference app to the newly creating app Existing App name and version Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step. Connection parameter​ This step is to provide the Connection parameters of the application. Input Purpose Possible values Gateway/PI URL URL of gateway or PI Gateway RFC Gateway RFC name Inbound folder Inbound folder path Outbound folder Outbound folder path Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step. Token parameter​ This step is to configure the token parameter of the application for the provided gateway information. Input Purpose Possible values Token URL Token url Username User name of the URL access Password Password of the URL access SSL ID SSL ID of the connection Proxy Proxy RFC: Gateway to SAP Gateway to SAP RFC Once all token parameters are provided, click the ‘TEST’ icon to verify the connection. This will display the connection status as shown below. Click on continue to move to the next step. Middleware parameter​ Modify the default middleware parameter values in this step according to the requirements, then click continue to proceed to the next page. Click the ‘Del’ icon in the table to remove parameters. Message parameter​ Edit the default message parameters in this step based on the requirement and click on continue to move on to the next page. Copy other configurations​ This step involves selecting the configurations to be copied to the new app if a reference app is available. kloBroker is a broker between tenants, clients, and external systems. It enables communication via messaging and queues. kloBroker runs on the master node in the kloSystem. There can be multiple instances, one per kloLandscape. This dialog allows the user to modify klobroker fields such as mw_msg_pick, mw required, notif required, bol enabled, fcm server key, base path, external file size, holding time, notif interval, notif threshold, interval, queue size, threshold, queue creation class, max message per file, SQL batch size, notif pick size and file parallel count. This dialog also allows CRUD on klobroker external fields which contain endpointid, type, destination host, destination port, destination protocol, user ID, password, and destination path. Description for the above fields are as follows: Fields Description MW Msg Pick This implies the number of messages middleware can pick from the tenant_q table. MW Required This implies whether middleware is required or not. Notif Required Server will send push notifications to the device. It will push all notifications to one table(ma_notification_queue). FCM Server Key To sync the message from the server to the device, fcm_server_key is mandatory. Base Path SAP will put files in this folder and the server will pick files. External File Size Size of the external files Notif Interval It will check in the queue at intervals whether the messages are present or not. Notif threshold The Maximum number of notifications the server will pick. Interval For how much time the DB needs to be checked, the Server will check whether the file is available or not in the sap in the folder and if the file is available then it will process or it will not. Threshold The number of messages the server will hold at a time. Notif pick size The number of notifications it can pick at a time

User Id User Id provided by SAP for the url. Password Password provided by SAP for the url. Destination Path When the type is a folder, then we specify a path here. Note :​ File processing. When processing SAP messages by file, txn_user_id has to be maintained in KloBroker configuration, or else, the generated messages will go to error q without user in transaction. The user ID maintained should have required application, row wise authorization(If required), permissions assigned.

A calendar is a set of working and non-working days specified for a particular time interval. This includes holidays and special periods underlying the organisation’s calendar. We have two types of calendars: 1. Calendar 2. Team Calendar
Displays a calendar of a single entity (such as a person, or resource) for the selected time interval.

NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION appointmentCreate boolean false Determines either user can create appointments on hold and drag. calendarView string week Defines the type of calendar view based on time. Ex. “week”, “month”, “WorkWeek” etc. CalendarView appointmentStartDate UI5Date or JavaScript Date object null Takes the binding for appointment aggregation’s start date. appointmentEndDate UI5Date or JavaScript Date object null Takes the binding for appointment aggregation’s end date. appointmentTitle string “” Title of the appointment. detail appointmentText string “” Text of the appointment. detail appointmentType sap.ui.unified.CalendarDayType Type01 Colour of the appointments. detail specialDates string Entityset transnode path. specialStartDate UI5 Date/ JS Date Path of start date from Special dates entityset. specialEndDate UI5 Date/ JS Date Path of end date from Special dates entityset. specialDateType sap.ui.unified.CalendarDayType Background colour of special date. details specialDateSecondaryType sap.ui.unified.CalendarDayType Secondary Background colour of special date. details appointmentIcon sap.ui.core.Icon null Icon for appointments. detail enabled boolean true Determines if the calendar should be enabled or disabled. showAppointmentDetail boolean true controls visibility of appointment detail on click of an appointment in calendar

KloAttach control is used to capture, record, upload and display the media.
Properties Type Doc

For using the KloAttach control using Page Builder, developers need to have a qualifier of type attachment. Then developers need to select the section in which KloAttach is needed. After selecting the section click and then new -> Controls. Provide the ID to the control and type KloAttach in the control field. Bind the value property of the control with the attachment qualifier type property of your entity. Developers also can drag the qualifier property from the trans node and drop over the section in which they want to use KloAttach control; the control generator will automatically predict the KloAttach control. NOTE: Please note that video recording in IQOO doesn’t work for unsupported codec with the Blob generated from MediaRecorder API. There are 4 modes in KloAttach control: Preview: In this mode Image control will be there with camera control. Users can capture and upload attachments. This mode will also display the captured and uploaded attachment. This is also the default mode of the KloAttach control. w/o preview: In this mode, users can capture and upload all the valid types of media but a preview will not be available. Compact fileUpload: In this mode file upload icon will be there. Users can upload all valid media. fileUpload: In this mode upload icon with the input field will be there. Users can upload all valid media. If developers want to change the mode of the control then add the mode property in control and choose the mode from the f4 of the mode property.Two new properties, `maxFileSizeAttachment` and `showFileSizeRestriction`, along with their validations, have been added for all four modes in the KloAttach control. A text display shows users the file size limit and supported file types (if enabled). Preview mode: If the enabled property of control is false then the camera button will be hidden. The image of the attachment is clickable. On click, it will open in full size in a dialog. With the click of the camera button, a dialog will appear with a live stream. By default, captured image/video will be of quality SD. But this can be configured using control’s property quality This button is used to open the flashlight of the camera. This button will close the camera. This button will open the file uploader. With the click of this button, the image will get captured. This button will switch the mode of the camera. On clicking the icon the camera & video buttons will get switched. Like On a click of this button video recording will start. With the click of this button video recording will stop. After capturing the image the dialog will look like below: On click, the image editing dialog will open with editing options. For knowing more about editing options see the KloFeedBack control. On click, the captured photo will be saved. On click, the dialog will get closed without saving the image. W/O Preview mode: In this mode, only the camera button will be visible. The only difference between review and w/o preview mode is that in w/o preview mode attachments will not be displayed. File upload mode: In this mode file upload button with a text field will be displayed. On click of the file upload button, the system's file explorer will open and the user can select the attachment and upload. The name of the selected attachment will be shown in the text field. Preview of the attachment is not available in this mode. Compact file upload mode: In this mode, only the file upload button will be visible. On click of the file upload button, the system's file explorer will open and the user can select the attachment and upload. Preview of the attachment is not available in this mode.

Developers are also able to change the preview preference of the KloAttach control. For using thumbnails the developer needs to enable the isThumbnailEnabled property in the IAttachment qualifier from the Data Studio. By default, KloAttach will display the original images and videos. Developers can change the preview preference by using the previewPreference property of the KloAttach control. There are 3 types of preview preference are available: Only Thumbnail 2. Only Real 3. On clicking Real This property is applicable only in preview mode. If "Only Thumbnail" then always the thumbnail will be displayed. If 'Only Real' then always a real image will be displayed. If 'On click Real' then a thumbnail will be displayed and on click of an image real image will come into frame. The difference between thumbnails and real images is their size & quality. Thumbnails will have low-quality images & smaller in size as compared to the original images. Developers are also able to change the WaterMark of the KloAttach control. By default, waterMark will not be displayed in the original images and videos. The developer has to mark the watermark property as true to enable that. There are a total of 5 watermark properties: - waterMark Watermark Position Watermark Size Watermark Type Watermark Config The developer can use these properties to change the size, position and type of watermark. If the developer wants to customize the watermark according to his preference, they should use the Watermark config:- In waterMarkConfig, add json Like:- { waterMarkPosition: "top_left", waterMarkColor: 'white', waterMarkSize: 'M', waterMarkType: ['geolocation', 'user', 'Text','Logo'], waterMarkText: 'Solution', waterMarkLogo: 'closedmodules/kloTouch_5/media/logo.png' } if you want to test the logo, the logo should be present in the location specified or you should change it to the current location Default watermark w/o any configuration. Note:- The watermark will only appear on the captured images/videos, it will not appear on uploaded images/videos.

A media type (also known as a Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions or MIME type) indicates the nature and format of a document, file, or assortment of bytes. Mode should be file_upload. mimeType can be an array of strings containing the required mime types . For specific file types(“file_upload”, “compact_file_upload” mode) pass the MIME type array. MIME types are listed in Mime Type Data. Note: There is another property fileType that will accept the file extensions in the format [“pdf”, “xlsx”, “txt”]. This property handles the mimetype of the control automatically. If fileType is provided, then the mimeType property will be ignored. For filetypes “vsd” and “vsdx”, some browser do not have the internal mimetypes maintained. You can use [“vsd”, “*”] in the fileType property for these files.
